name: AI-assisted bug hunt in Apache Lucene

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter NRT
bugs.title: openIfChanged returns null and isCurrent stays true after a flush when the only changes are doc-values updates
bugs.summary: You open an NRT reader, update a doc-values field (or soft-delete through updateDocValues), and then call flush, a no-op forceMerge(1), or open readers with writeAllDeletes=true. You expect DirectoryReader.openIfChanged(reader, writer) to return a reader that sees the change. Instead it returns null and reader.isCurrent is true, so SearcherManager keeps the stale searcher, and hasUncommittedChanges can also return false while updates are uncommitted.

bugs.area: index / doc-values updates
bugs.title: deleteDocuments(Query) on a doc-values field is evaluated against stale values when doc-values updates are pending
bugs.summary: You update a doc-values field and then delete documents with a query on that field before the updates are written. You expect the delete to see the updated values. Instead delete-by-query is resolved against the written values, and inside a packet deletes run before doc-values updates, so the wrong documents are deleted or kept.

bugs.area: codecs / doc values
bugs.title: Doc-values range queries with a skip index return wrong hits when a segment's values span more than Long.MAX_VALUE
bugs.summary: You index numeric doc values with a skip index (NumericDocValuesField.indexedField) where one segment's values span more than Long.MAX_VALUE, and run a doc-values range query. You expect the same hits as 10.5.2. Instead the encoded-domain bound transform wraps: 100k random latitudes queried for [45, 90] gave 0 hits instead of 25,157, 64-bit hashes gave 2 instead of 49,931, and some cases add wrong hits.

bugs.area: join / block join (ToParentBlockJoinQuery.BlockJoinBulkScorer) x search / BooleanQuery MUST_NOT bulk scoring (ReqExclBulkScorer, #16669)
bugs.title: A MUST_NOT clause next to a scoring ToParentBlockJoinQuery is checked against child documents instead of parents, so excluded parents are returned, and the search throws when a parent/child block straddles a 4096-doc window
bugs.summary: You index parent/child blocks and search BooleanQuery(MUST ToParentBlockJoinQuery(skill:java, parentsFilter, ScoreMode.Avg), MUST_NOT status:hidden), expecting only the parents that are not hidden, which is what count of the same query and ScoreMode.None return. Instead, on main the hidden parent p2 comes back for Avg, Max, Min and Total ([p1, p2] instead of [p1]); a MUST_NOT clause that matches only child documents (MUST_NOT skill:java) removes both parents ( instead of [p1, p2]); and in a 6,000-doc segment where a block straddles doc 4096 the search throws AssertionError in ReqExclBulkScorer$WindowBits.get with -ea and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (index -1) with -da. The cause is that since #16669 ReqExclBulkScorer folds the MUST_NOT matches of each 4096-doc window into a bit set that it passes to the required clause as acceptDocs, and the join's BlockJoinBulkScorer forwards that acceptDocs unchanged to its child scorer (ToParentBlockJoinQuery.java:541), so the exclusions are tested on child doc IDs, some of them below the window, and never on the parents it collects.

bugs.area: search / vector similarity queries and the query cache
bugs.title: Vector similarity queries report isCacheable == true although their per-segment result depends on live docs, the search timeout and the filter, so a shared query cache serves one reader's or one search's result to another
bugs.summary: You search with a vector similarity (threshold) query, for example FloatVectorSimilarityQuery, in a non-scoring context such as IndexSearcher#count or ConstantScoreQuery, with a query cache that several readers or searchers share (the IndexSearcher default in 9.10.0-10.5.2). You expect every reader and every search to get the hits it gets without the cache. Instead the cache hands one reader's or one search's per-segment result to another: an older point-in-time reader misses a document that only a newer reader has deleted (99 hits instead of 100), a search without a timeout gets the empty result of an earlier timed-out search (0 instead of 100), and with a filter on an updated doc-values field a newer reader gets a document that no longer matches the filter (100 instead of 99).

bugs.area: search / multi-term queries
bugs.title: Doc-values-rewritten multi-term queries are invisible to QueryVisitor, so they escape the nested clause limit and the query-cache RAM budget
bugs.summary: You run a query tree whose leaves are multi-term queries rewritten with MultiTermQuery.DOC_VALUES_REWRITE (or SortedSetDocValuesField/SortedDocValuesField.newSlowSetQuery) under IndexSearcher's maxClauseCount. You expect IndexSearcher.rewrite to count each such leaf toward the nested clause limit, and an LRUQueryCache to account for the terms a cached query holds. Instead MultiTermQueryDocValuesWrapper.visit calls visitor.getSubVisitor(FILTER, query) and throws the result away, so each leaf counts as 0: with maxClauseCount=8 a query with 10 such leaves raises no TooManyNestedClauses, and a cached 50,000-term TermInSetQuery that holds 966,712 bytes is accounted as 200 bytes; search results stay correct.
bugs.affected_versions: every release since 8.6.0, branch_10_6 and main [read]

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter merge
bugs.title: With index sorting and a parent field, deleting only a block's parent makes every later merge fail
bugs.summary: You use index sorting with a parent field and document blocks, and delete only the parent document of a block. You expect later merges to work. Instead MultiSorter finds no parent for the orphaned child (nextSetBit returns NO_MORE_DOCS), every later merge of that segment throws (an EOFException with the default codec on a file-system directory, IndexOutOfBoundsException on ByteBuffersDirectory), the writer closes tragically and uncommitted documents are lost.
bugs.introduced_commit: #12829 (df6bd25ce44 on main; backport 0aa88910ca9) introduced the parent field

bugs.area: search / HNSW
bugs.title: HNSW merge-time graph reuse can leave the entry node with no neighbours, dropping kNN recall to zero
bugs.summary: You delete a cluster of documents around the HNSW entry node and merge, for example with forceMerge(1), so the merge reuses and repairs the biggest segment's graph. You expect kNN recall to stay about the same. Instead the repair cannot reconnect an entry node that lost every neighbour, every search starts at that isolated node and returns only it (recall@10 0.906 to 0.000 in the repro), and CheckIndex reports no problem.

bugs.area: analysis / StandardTokenizer and the other JFlex-generated scanners (zzRefill in both Lucene JFlex skeletons)
bugs.title: StandardAnalyzer and the other JFlex-generated scanners (StandardTokenizer, UAX29URLEmailTokenizer, ClassicTokenizer, WikipediaTokenizer, HTMLStripCharFilter) silently index no tokens for a text value that ends in an unpaired high surrogate, such as a string cut inside an emoji; values longer than the scan buffer lose or split their last buffer window
bugs.summary: You index a text field with StandardAnalyzer at default settings, and the value ends in an unpaired high surrogate, for example 'hello world' followed by U+D83D, which is what cutting a Java String inside an emoji, or decoding the JSON escape \ud83d, produces. You expect hello and world to be indexed and end to report the input length as the final offset, as happens when the same lone surrogate sits mid-text and as Lucene 7.6.0 did. Instead the scanner's refill reads the whole text, looks one char ahead for the missing low surrogate, hits end of input and reports 'no new input', so the scanner ends the stream without scanning what it just read: no tokens, final offset 0, and the document does not match title:hello; values longer than the 255-char buffer lose or split their last window instead.

bugs.area: index / FieldInfos and segment metadata strings (DataOutput#writeString in.fnm, segments_N and.si)
bugs.title: Two field names that differ only in an unpaired surrogate are written to disk as the same U+FFFD name, so IndexWriter commits an index that DirectoryReader and a new IndexWriter refuse to open (on main also colliding field attribute keys and commit user-data keys)
bugs.summary: You add a document with two field names that differ only in an unpaired surrogate, for example 'f\uD800' and 'f\uFFFD' (or two different lone surrogates in the same position), and commit; addDocument and commit return normally, as IndexWriter documents that malformed UTF-16 is silently replaced with U+FFFD, and you expect the committed index to open. Instead DataOutput#writeString writes both names as the same bytes ('f' + U+FFFD), so DirectoryReader.open and a new IndexWriter throw IllegalArgumentException 'duplicate field names: 0 and 1 have: f\uFFFD' for the whole index, and CheckIndex can only recover it by dropping the whole segment. On main the same happens for two colliding field attribute keys or commit user-data keys ('duplicate key'), and a lone-surrogate index-sort field name is stored in its U+FFFD form, so a new IndexWriter with the same sort is refused.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter deletes (deleteDocuments, DocumentsWriterDeleteQueue array nodes, per-thread delete slices)
bugs.title: IndexWriter.deleteDocuments(Term...) and deleteDocuments(Query...) keep the caller's array without copying it, so documents still buffered in RAM are deleted by whatever the array holds when the per-thread writer later applies the delete (at its next addDocument or flush): a caller that refills or clears its array after the call returned keeps documents it deleted and deletes documents no call named, silently and also after commit (since 4.0.0)
bugs.summary: You pass a Term or Query to IndexWriter.deleteDocuments, the call returns its sequence number, and you then reuse the array, for example refill it with the next batch of ids; the delete should mean the terms or queries the array held at the call, as it already does for documents in flushed segments. IndexWriter hands the array itself to its delete queue, and each per-thread writer reads it only later, at its next addDocument or flush, so documents still buffered in RAM are deleted by the array's new contents. In the repro, deleting {flushed1, buffered1} and then refilling the same array with {flushed2, buffered2} and deleting again leaves buffered1 alive after commit, and reassigning the slot of a one-element Query after the call keeps 'delete-me' and deletes 'keep', which no delete call named; no exception is thrown.

bugs.area: core / index write path (delete-by-query: FrozenBufferedUpdates.applyQueryDeletes) x core / search and queries (reader-dependent rewrites)
bugs.title: IndexWriter.deleteDocuments(Query) and updateDocuments(Query,...) rewrite the query separately on each segment, so reader-dependent queries (kNN, the default FuzzyQuery and other top-N term rewrites, CommonTermsQuery, MoreLikeThisQuery, score ranges) delete a set that depends on the segment layout and differs from what IndexSearcher.search returns
bugs.summary: You call IndexWriter.deleteDocuments(query) (or updateDocuments(query, docs)) on an index with two or more segments and expect it to delete the documents IndexSearcher.search(query) returns, since the javadoc says it 'Deletes the document(s) matching any of the provided queries'. Instead the writer rewrites the query on a separate one-segment IndexSearcher for each segment, so top-k, top-N term expansion and index statistics are computed per segment: a kNN query with k=2 deletes up to 2 documents per segment (4 on two segments), a default FuzzyQuery deletes 60 documents where search finds 50, and MoreLikeThisQuery or a score-range predicate deletes none of the documents search returns. With the same documents committed in one segment before the delete, the delete equals the search result, so the segment layout alone decides what is deleted, and the result is permanent once committed.
bugs.introduced_commit: 5b113c8af63c (LUCENE-1194 / #2271, 'add IndexWriter.deleteDocuments(Query)', svn r634219, Subversion era, no PR) [read]. The first implementation already resolved a delete query per segment: DocumentsWriter.applyDeletes did 'IndexSearcher searcher = new IndexSearcher(reader); Weight weight = query.weight(searcher)' for each SegmentReader (DocumentsWriter.java:2794-2801 at the commit), and Query.weight starts with searcher.rewrite(this). Every later rewrite of the resolution code kept the per-segment searcher: LUCENE-2680 / LUCENE-1076 (BufferedDeletes, BufferedDeletesStream, 3.1/3.2), QueryWrapperFilter per segment (3.3-5.2.1), 5d16b973962 (LUCENE-6688 / #7746, 2015, new IndexSearcher(readerContext.reader)), 58105a203a1 (LUCENE-7868 / #8919, 2017, FrozenBufferedUpdates) and 798d3510341 (LUCENE-8242 / #9289, 2018, explicit searcher.rewrite + createWeight). On main the lines are FrozenBufferedUpdates.java:397-400 (git blame -w -M -C: 397-398 from 5d16b973962, 399-400 from 798d3510341). Not a regression: the bug is as old as the API; what changed over time is only which stock queries expose it.

bugs.summary: You index 10 documents with vectors, delete the nearest one (d0) by its id term, commit, then call deleteDocuments(new KnnFloatVectorQuery(field, target, 1)) and expect it to delete the nearest remaining document, d1, which is what an NRT search at that point returns. Instead nothing more is deleted: IndexWriter runs delete queries on its internal pooled SegmentReader, whose live docs are not refreshed after deletes, so the kNN query still sees d0 as live and picks it again (also after an NRT reopen, or with both deletes in one session). Likewise, while the documents are still buffered, a document added after the kNN delete can take the top slot inside the flushed segment and is then cut by the delete's docID limit, so the delete removes nothing.

bugs.area: search / concurrency
bugs.title: IndexSearcher#count hangs forever when Weight#count throws, for example on a query timeout, on a segment split into intra-segment partitions
bugs.summary: You search with an executor and intra-segment partitions (IndexSearcher.slices(..., allowSegmentPartitions=true)) and call IndexSearcher#count, and the first partition of a segment to arrive throws from Weight#count, for example the ExitingReaderException of a stock ExitableDirectoryReader timeout. You expect the exception to propagate, as TaskExecutor#invokeAll promises. Instead TotalHitCountCollectorManager completes the segment's shared future only on success or CollectionTerminatedException, so the other partitions wait in an unbounded get and the call never returns (with no test hooks, 124/200 and 176/200 calls hung on main, 44/50 on 10.5.2).

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter frozen update packets vs. merge carry-over (forceApply, commitMergedDeletesAndUpdates, BufferedUpdatesStream)
bugs.title: IndexWriter.forceApply marks a re-resolving update packet finished outside the IndexWriter lock when its re-iteration matches no segment, so a merge that commits in that gap skips the packet's already-resolved doc-values updates and nobody applies them again: an acknowledged updateNumericDocValue/updateDocValues is lost and softUpdateDocument leaves two live versions of the document, also after commit (since 7.0.0)
bugs.summary: You update a document's doc-values field (updateNumericDocValue, updateDocValues) or replace a document with softUpdateDocument while background merges run; IndexWriter returns a sequence number, so every later NRT reader and commit should show the change. If the update packet must re-resolve because a merge committed meanwhile and that merge's result was dropped as fully deleted, IndexWriter.forceApply finds no segment left, leaves the IndexWriter lock and only then marks the packet finished; a second merge that commits in that gap treats the packet as still running, skips its already-resolved update on the merged-away segment, and nobody applies it again. The update is silently lost (id 3 keeps value 30 instead of 7, also after commit and reopen), and with softUpdateDocument the old version is never soft-deleted, so two live versions of one document remain.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter doc-values update write path (ReadersAndUpdates.writeFieldUpdates, the checkpoint after writeReaderPool, IndexFileDeleter reference counts)
bugs.title: An IOException late in a doc-values update write leaves IndexWriter open but inconsistent: published update files are never checkpointed and get deleted while still referenced, and a failed pooled-reader re-open silently drops the update
bugs.summary: You update a doc-values field (updateNumericDocValue, updateBinaryDocValue, or a soft delete) and open an NRT reader, flush or commit, and the doc-values update write throws a non-tragic IOException after the new files were already published into the segment's SegmentCommitInfo (re-opening the writer's pooled segment reader fails, or a second segment's update write in the same batch fails); the writer stays open (isOpen true, no tragic exception) and you keep using it. You expect the acknowledged update to reach the next NRT reader and commit, and every file the writer's SegmentInfos references to stay on disk, as in 6.x and as the since-deleted test testNoLostDeletesOrUpdates required. Instead the writer skips its IndexFileDeleter checkpoint and keeps a stale pooled reader whose pending update was already pruned: in releases (and on main with maxDocValuesOverlays=0) the next update rewrites the column from that stale reader and a later commit succeeds with the update reverted (doc 0 = 0 instead of 100, no exception), while with overlays (main's default) or on the partial-batch path the writer later deletes the published files and NRT opens or commits fail with NoSuchFileException.

bugs.area: index / DocumentsWriter full flush (DocumentsWriterFlushControl.abortFullFlushes, blockedFlushes) and the error paths of IndexWriter.getReader and prepareCommit
bugs.title: A non-tragic exception during an NRT reopen or commit full flush aborts the DWPTs other threads filled during that flush, silently losing acknowledged documents and updates while the writer stays open
bugs.summary: One thread opens an NRT reader from the IndexWriter (or commits) while other threads keep indexing, and the reopen or commit fails after its flush with an ordinary, non-tragic exception, for example an I/O error while opening a segment file; the writer stays open and the other threads' updateDocument and addDocument calls returned normally with sequence numbers. You expect those changes in the next commit, whose sequence number covers them, and updateDocument to stay atomic. Instead Lucene discards the per-thread buffers that filled up and were parked during the failed full flush, so the added documents never reach the index, and the update keeps only its delete, so the updated document disappears entirely.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter full flush (DocumentsWriter.flushAllThreads naked-delete freeze, DocumentsWriterDeleteQueue.close)
bugs.title: An Error (in practice an OutOfMemoryError) while an NRT reopen or commit that has no buffered documents freezes the buffered deletes and doc-values updates is replaced by IllegalStateException("Can't close queue unless all changes are applied") from the finally of DocumentsWriter.flushAllThreads, so IndexWriter stays open instead of closing itself and its next commit silently drops those acknowledged deletes and updates (with -ea an AssertionError replaces the Error; every release since 8.2.0)
bugs.summary: You commit documents id:1 and id:2, call deleteDocuments(id:1) and updateNumericDocValue(id:2, dv, 22) (both return sequence numbers), and then open an NRT reader from the writer or call commit with no documents buffered, and an OutOfMemoryError strikes while the writer freezes those two buffered changes; the IndexWriter javadoc says the writer closes itself after an Error, so you expect to see the Error and a closed writer (or, if the writer stays usable, a later commit that contains both changes). Instead the finally of DocumentsWriter.flushAllThreads closes the delete queue that the flush has already swapped out, and its close throws IllegalStateException("Can't close queue unless all changes are applied"), which replaces the Error; IndexWriter does not treat that as tragic and stays open, the old queue with both changes is abandoned, and the next commit returns -1 with id:1 still live and dv(id:2) still 2. With -ea an AssertionError ('Can not replace a full flush queue if the queue is not closed') replaces the Error instead, and since 10.0.0 it closes the writer.

bugs.area: search / phrase queries (ExactPhraseMatcher maxFreq and merged impacts, PhraseScorer TOP_SCORES pruning)
bugs.title: Exact PhraseQuery/MultiPhraseQuery: when the first query term occurs twice at one document position, the phrase freq exceeds the maxFreq/impacts bound, so Scorer#getMaxScore is below score and TOP_SCORES search drops the best hit
bugs.summary: You index text with an analyzer that can put the first word of a phrase twice at one position (for example KeywordRepeatFilter plus a stemmer, or index-time synonyms queried through QueryBuilder) and run an exact phrase search with IndexSearcher#search(q, n); you expect the same top hits as scoring every match. ExactPhraseMatcher counts such a phrase occurrence once per copy of the first word, so the document's phrase freq is 2, but the bound it reports for skipping work (maxFreq and the block impacts behind getMaxScore) is the smallest term freq, 1. Once more than 1000 hits are counted the searcher skips documents whose real score is competitive: in the repro search(q, 1) returns doc 0 although exhaustive scoring ranks doc 1100 first, with no error.

bugs.area: suggest / document (NRT) suggester (NRTSuggester.getMaxTopNSearcherQueueSize via SuggestIndexSearcher and CompletionQuery; Util.TopNSearcher queue depth)
bugs.title: NRTSuggester returns too few or wrongly ranked suggestions in a segment with only a few deleted documents, because its deleted-document queue slack (long)(topN / liveDocsRatio) rounds back down to topN
bugs.summary: You index suggestions with SuggestField, delete one document or update it (which deletes the old version), and ask SuggestIndexSearcher.suggest for the top n completions; you expect the top n live completions, because NRTSuggester enlarges its bounded search queue 'to account for the filtered out suggestions' of deleted documents. With few deletions that enlargement, (long)(topN / liveDocsRatio), rounds back down to topN (for one deletion in ten documents, (long)(1 / 0.9) = 1), so a deleted completion that takes a result slot is thrown away and nothing replaces it: with abc_0, the best of abc_0..abc_9 in one segment, deleted, suggest('abc_', 1) returns instead of [abc_1], and after updateDocument lowers the best entry's weight from 1000 to 1, suggest(num=1) returns that entry at weight 1 instead of the live entry at weight 999. Deleting more documents (5 of 10) gives the queue enough room and the same lookup works.

bugs.area: facet / DrillSideways (sequential DrillSidewaysScorer, drill-down-advance strategy, two-phase drill-down dimensions)
bugs.title: Sequential DrillSideways skips the two-phase matches check of the second-cheapest drill-down dimension on segments without deletions, so documents that fail that dimension but are in its approximation are returned as drill-down hits and counted in the facets (released since 5.3.0)
bugs.summary: You run DrillSideways without an executor on a DrillDownQuery with two or more dimensions, one of which is a two-phase query such as a distance or range drill-down with a fast-match query or a PhraseQuery, and expect the hits to match every dimension and each dimension's sideways counts to cover the documents that match all the other dimensions. Instead, on a segment with no deleted documents, when that dimension is the second-cheapest by approximation cost and the base query is broad, DrillSidewaysScorer never calls its TwoPhaseIterator#matches, because the condition 'acceptDocs == null || acceptDocs.get(docID) && (dc.twoPhase == null || dc.twoPhase.matches)' parses as 'acceptDocs == null || (get && matches)'. So every document in that dimension's approximation (inside the bounding box but outside the radius, the phrase words in another order) is treated as matching it, returned as a hit and counted in the facets, while concurrent DrillSideways and plain boolean queries on the same searcher give the correct sets.

bugs.area: facet / DrillSideways (sequential query-first scoring: score mode of the base weight and the scorable handed to the hit collector)
bugs.title: Sequential DrillSideways lets a TOP_SCORES hit collector prune the shared base query, so drill-sideways facet counts silently miss matching documents
bugs.summary: You run a sequential DrillSideways search (no executor) with a filter-style base query drilled down to color=red, and pass a TopScoreDocCollectorManager with a finite total-hits threshold (10 in the repro, or IndexSearcher's default 1000) as the hit collector through search(DrillDownQuery, CollectorManager, List). You expect the drill-sideways counts for color to include every document that matches the base query (75 in the repro), as the same search does with an exhaustive hit collector or with the concurrent DrillSideways. Instead the counts are silently too low (11, or 1001 instead of 2250 at threshold 1000): the base query is scored with the hit collector's TOP_SCORES mode and its scorer is handed to the hit collector, whose min-competitive-score updates make the shared base iteration skip documents that the sideways collectors then never see; the top hits are correct.
bugs.introduced_commit: 61f8517000b3af74c0b079e4a5fa81eb870b1c35 (LUCENE-10030, issue #11069, PR #217 by gtroitskiy, merged by gsmiller: lazy score for near-miss documents in DrillSidewaysScorer.doQueryFirstScoring); branch_8x backport apache/lucene-solr#2542 = c7210e494e165b66673000df6ae43a32702800cf [exec]. The change handed the hit collector ScoreCachingWrappingScorer(baseScorer), which forwards setMinCompetitiveScore to the base scorer, instead of the private ScoreAndDoc scorable whose setMinCompetitiveScore was the Scorable no-op. Older preconditions [read]: the base weight takes the caller's score mode since LUCENE-4100 (4fc5a872ded, 2017-12-07, 8.0.0), and ConstantScoreScorer empties its iterator under TOP_SCORES once minScore > score since LUCENE-8464 (b4449c73e4c, 2018-11-08, 8.0.0). Behaviour-preserving follow-ups: e44636c2808 (LUCENE-10036, #226) and f527eb3b12d (#12407).

bugs.area: util / automaton
bugs.title: RegExp no longer parses an escaped range start such as [\.-z] as a range
bugs.summary: You write a RegexpQuery or RegExp whose character class starts a range with an escaped character, such as [\.-z]. You expect it to match the range from '.' to 'z', as in 10.1 and java.util.regex. Instead, since 10.2.0, it is parsed as the three characters '.', '-' and 'z', so the query silently matches different terms.

bugs.area: queryparser / SimpleQueryParser (near operator: consumePhrase phrase slop)
bugs.title: SimpleQueryParser drops the '+', '|', quote or '(' typed directly after a phrase slop, so "a b"~2+c parses as phrase OR c and "a b"~2|c (default operator AND) as phrase AND c
bugs.summary: You parse "a b"~2+c with SimpleQueryParser and expect what its javadoc defines, the near query AND c, just as "a b"~2 +c and "a b"+c parse. Instead the parser skips the character right after the slop digits, so the '+' is lost and you get phrase OR c (on an index with the documents 'a b' and 'c' it matches 2 documents instead of 0); the same happens to '|' ("a b"~2|c becomes AND under default MUST), to a quote ("a b"~2"c d" becomes the phrase OR c OR d) and to '(' ("a b"~2(c+d) loses its group). The cause is an off-by-one in consumePhrase: parseFuzziness already stops on the delimiter that ends the slop, and the unconditional '++state.index' that was written to step over the closing quote then skips that delimiter.

bugs.area: queryparser / flexible StandardQueryParser (processor pipeline order: WildcardQueryNodeProcessor runs before MultiFieldQueryNodeProcessor)
bugs.title: StandardQueryParser with setMultiFields normalizes field-less prefix and wildcard terms with field null, before the multi-field expansion, so per-field analyzers are ignored for them (and a PerFieldAnalyzerWrapper over Map.of throws NullPointerException)
bugs.summary: You give StandardQueryParser a PerFieldAnalyzerWrapper (WhitespaceAnalyzer by default, StandardAnalyzer for 'title'), call setMultiFields({title}) and parse 'Luc*' with no field, expecting what the javadoc promises: the clause expanded over the multi fields, i.e. the same query as 'title:Luc*', which becomes title:luc* and finds the document titled 'Lucene'. Instead the pipeline normalizes the prefix in WildcardQueryNodeProcessor before MultiFieldQueryNodeProcessor has set the field, so Analyzer#normalize is called with field null (the wrapper's default analyzer), the query becomes title:Luc* and finds nothing, while plain, fuzzy, regexp and range clauses in the same setup are normalized with the expanded field. If the per-field map is a Map.of, the null lookup makes parse throw NullPointerException for every field-less prefix or wildcard clause.
bugs.introduced_commit: e92a38af90d12e51390b4307ccbe0c24ac7b6b4e (master): LUCENE-7355 'Add Analyzer#normalize and use it in query parsers' by @jpountz (now apache/lucene#8409; a JIRA patch, no PR) [read]. It removed LowercaseExpandedTermsQueryNodeProcessor, which ran after MultiFieldQueryNodeProcessor and lower-cased field-independently, and added Analyzer#normalize(fqn.getFieldAsString,...) to WildcardQueryNodeProcessor, the first processor of the pipeline; the calls it added to the fuzzy, regexp and range processors run after the expansion. The pipeline order itself dates from 6f66858572c (2010) and was harmless until then. The 6.x backport 7c2e7a0fb80 (6.2.0) did not touch the flexible parser. Not commit-bisected (2016 sources not built)

bugs.area: document / geo shape fields (ShapeField triangle encoding; LatLonShape and XYShape CONTAINS queries)
bugs.title: ShapeField.encodeTriangle puts the wrong edge flag on the first edge when it flips a clockwise triangle, so LatLonShape and XYShape CONTAINS queries return wrong hits
bugs.summary: You index a polygon with LatLonShape or XYShape and run a CONTAINS query that asks whether the polygon fully contains a box (or another query shape); you expect a match exactly when the box lies inside the polygon. When ShapeField.encodeTriangle turns one of the polygon's clockwise tessellation triangles counter-clockwise, it swaps two vertices but gives the new first edge the 'belongs to the polygon boundary' flag of the wrong old edge, so a real boundary edge can lose its flag and an internal diagonal can gain one. CONTAINS then silently says yes for boxes that stick out of the polygon (in one executed case a box 99.9998% outside it) and no for boxes well inside it.

bugs.area: geo / shape queries (Polygon2D intersectsLine/intersectsTriangle; LatLonShape and XYShape INTERSECTS and DISJOINT with a query polygon that has holes)
bugs.title: Polygon2D.intersectsLine/intersectsTriangle never test the query polygon's hole edges, so LatLonShape/XYShape INTERSECTS misses, and DISJOINT matches, a line or polygon whose vertices all lie in holes but which crosses the polygon between them
bugs.summary: You index a line or polygon with LatLonShape or XYShape and search with a query polygon that has holes, for example a region with two lakes cut out; a line from one lake to the other crosses the land between them, so INTERSECTS should return it and DISJOINT should not. Polygon2D.intersectsLine/intersectsTriangle report an intersection only when a vertex of the indexed shape is inside the polygon (holes excluded) or one of its edges crosses the outer ring; they never test the hole edges, so when every vertex lies in a hole the shape counts as not intersecting. The query returns the wrong documents with no error (repro: the square [0,10]^2 with holes [1,3]x[4,6] and [7,9]x[4,6]; of the line (2,5)-(8,5), the box [2,8]x[4.5,5.5] and the point (5,5), INTERSECTS returns only the point and DISJOINT returns the line and the box).

bugs.area: queries / intervals (Intervals.notContainedBy: NotContainedByIntervalsSource disjunction rewrite, LUCENE-8477)
bugs.title: Intervals.notContainedBy(small, or(B1, B2)) returns small intervals that lie inside B1 or B2, because the default disjunction rewrite turns it into an OR of per-clause filters
bugs.summary: You index 'i love new york', 'york city is big' and 'york is here' and search notContainedBy(york, or(phrase(new, york), phrase(york, city))), meaning 'york that is not part of new york or york city'; you expect only the third document, which is what or(false,...) and the nested form notContainedBy(notContainedBy(york, 'new york'), 'york city') return. Instead all three documents match: the default disjunction rewrite (LUCENE-8477) pulls the OR out of the excluded operand and builds or(NOT_CONTAINED_BY(york, 'new york'), NOT_CONTAINED_BY(york, 'york city')), which computes 'not inside B1 or not inside B2' where the javadoc promises 'not inside (B1 or B2)'. So adding a clause to the exclusion adds hits: notContainedBy(a, or(phrase(c, a), b)) matches 'c a' although notContainedBy(a, phrase(c, a)) does not.

bugs.area: queries / intervals (overlap filters Intervals.overlapping / nonOverlapping / notWithin vs the LUCENE-8477 disjunction rewrite that containedBy and within apply to their reference)
bugs.title: Intervals.overlapping, nonOverlapping and notWithin read a disjunctive reference through the minimized or, while containedBy and within test every alternative, so for the reference or(york, "new york") the same interval is reported both within and not within n positions of it, and containedBy(new, ref) matches 'new york' where overlapping(new, ref) does not
bugs.summary: You index 'visit new york' and run within(visit, 1, R) and notWithin(visit, 1, R) with R = or(york, "new york"), and you expect exactly one of them to return 'visit', because the javadoc defines notWithin as the intervals that do not appear within n positions of the reference. Instead both return the same interval [0,0]: within is built on containedBy, which pulls the or apart (LUCENE-8477) and sees 'new york' right next to 'visit', while notWithin, overlapping and nonOverlapping read the default or as one minimized source, which drops 'new york' because that interval contains 'york'. In the same way containedBy(new, R) matches 'new york' but overlapping(new, R) does not, and maxgaps(0, overlapping(new, R)) does match, because the nested form does pull the reference apart.

bugs.area: queries / intervals (NotContainingIntervalsSource, Intervals.notContaining)
bugs.title: Intervals.notContaining drops minuend intervals that a subtrahend interval overlaps on the right edge or encloses, though they contain no subtrahend interval
bugs.summary: You search with Intervals.notContaining(minuend, subtrahend), for example notContaining(phrase(a,b), phrase(b,c)) on the text 'a b c', or notContaining(term york, phrase(new,york)) on 'new york'. You expect the minuend interval back, because the javadoc says notContaining 'Returns intervals from the minuend that do not contain intervals of the subtrahend', and 'a b' does not contain 'b c' (and one position cannot contain two). Instead the iterator keeps a minuend interval only if the next subtrahend interval starts after its end, so both queries return no interval and the document is not a hit, while the mirror-image overlap on the left edge (notContaining(phrase(b,c), phrase(a,b))) is kept.

bugs.area: queries / span queries (per-document lockstep of the ContainSpans subclasses in SpanContainingQuery and SpanWithinQuery)
bugs.title: SpanContainingQuery and SpanWithinQuery miss documents and spans when the little query's spans end out of order (for example a SpanOrQuery of a longer near clause and a shorter clause that can occur inside it): their single forward pass tests only the current little span (containing) or never goes back to a big span it skipped (within), so a later, shorter little span inside a big span is never tried
bugs.summary: You index 'a b a' and search with SpanContainingQuery(big = SpanNear([a, b], slop 0), little = SpanOr(SpanNear([a, a], slop 5), b)): the big span 'a b' at [0,2) contains the little span 'b' at [1,2), so you expect a hit, and SpanWithinQuery with the same pair should match too. Instead both return nothing, because the little spans arrive sorted by start as [0,3) and then [1,2) (their ends go down, which the Spans contract allows), and each query's single forward pass gives up after testing only the longer little span [0,3): containing moves on to the next big span, within moves the big iterator past [0,2) and never comes back. The same happens in a sentence-scoped search for '(apple NEAR/5 pie) OR cake' on 'bos apple cake eos bos pie eos' (the 'cake' sentence is missed only because 'apple... pie' crosses into the next sentence), so adding a word to a document or an OR alternative to the query can remove a hit; nothing extra is ever returned.

bugs.title: ToParentBlockJoinSortField treats a parent as having a missing child value whenever its block holds any document outside childFilter, even if every document has the sort field (regression in 10.5.0)
bugs.summary: You index blocks with two kinds of non-parent documents, for example P1 = [type:a s=y n=40, type:b s=x n=7, parent P1] and P2 = [type:a s=d n=10, parent P2], and sort the parents of a ToParentBlockJoinQuery with new ToParentBlockJoinSortField("s", STRING, false, parents, childFilter type:a), expecting 'P2=d P1=y', which is what Lucene 10.4.0 returns. bugs.title: Document suggester with skipDuplicates=true and an index-time synonym returns fewer than n distinct suggestions (n=2 drops one that n=3 returns), because Util.TopNSearcher drops its queue before the last result although acceptPartialPath can still reject that path, and NRTSuggester sizes the queue from entries per analyzed form, which ignores synonym graph paths
bugs.summary: You index suggestions through a CompletionAnalyzer with an index-time synonym (b => xb, keeping the original, so 'a b' is indexed as 'a b' and 'a xb'), add a second suggestion 'a xc', and call SuggestIndexSearcher.suggest(prefix 'a', 2, skipDuplicates=true); you expect the two distinct suggestions [a b/10, a xc/3], which n=3 does return. Instead you get only [a b/10]: Util.TopNSearcher sets its queue to null for the last result when maxQueueDepth == topN, assuming the last path always completes, but the duplicate filter (acceptPartialPath) rejects that path when it reaches 'a xb', so the sibling arc that leads to 'a xc' is never queued and the search ends early (called directly, TopNSearcher even reports isComplete=true for such a search). NRTSuggester makes the queue that small because it counts entries sharing one analyzed form, not the analyzed paths per suggestion that its javadoc describes, so a synonym never enlarges it; with two synonyms (b => {xb, yb}) the duplicate paths fill the queue and both n=2 and n=3 lose a suggestion even with the shortcut removed.

bugs.title: TSTLookup.store/load writes each tree node's split char with DataOutput.writeString, so the two surrogate halves of an emoji or CJK Extension B character come back as U+FFFD: after load, get and lookups whose prefix runs through such a character silently find nothing, and some neighbouring BMP keys are lost too (every release since 4.7.0)

Instead lookup('𠮷', true, 5) returns instead of [𠮷野家/5] and get('𠮷野家') returns null after the reload, because TSTLookup keeps one tree node per UTF-16 code unit, writeRecursively writes each node's split char with DataOutput.writeString of a one-char String, and a lone surrogate has no UTF-8 form, so it is written and reloaded as U+FFFD and the tree's char comparisons then take the wrong branches. bugs.summary: You wrap an ordinary query, for example a TermQuery, in RescoreTopNQuery to re-score its matches with a DoubleValuesSource and keep the best n, on an index where some matching documents are deleted but not yet merged away. bugs.title: RescoreTopNQuery builds its inner Weight with ScoreMode.COMPLETE_NO_SCORES, so a values source that needs scores (DoubleValuesSource.SCORES, an expression using _score) reads 0 instead of the inner query's score
bugs.summary: You wrap a query in RescoreTopNQuery and re-score its matches with a values source that uses the query's own score, for example DoubleValuesSource.SCORES or an expression such as _score * popularity, keeping the best n. bugs.area: search / BlendedTermQuery cross-field statistics blending
bugs.title: Cross-field BlendedTermQuery gives a sparse field's term a docFreq above that field's docCount, so matches score negative (and since 10.3 are dropped from top-k), and a field with no indexed terms makes search throw NullPointerException
bugs.summary: You build a BlendedTermQuery for "lucene" on the fields title and keywords, as its javadoc suggests for cross-field search, over an index where two titles contain "lucene" and only one document has a keywords field at all. You expect every matching document back with a non-negative score, and a field that no document has yet to simply match nothing. Instead the query gives keywords:lucene the largest docFreq of all its terms (2) although only 1 document has the keywords field, so BM25's idf turns negative and that document scores -0.10 and is ranked last, since 10.3 it is missing from search(q, 10) when it sits in a segment of its own (count(q) = 3, 2 hits returned), and when no document has the keywords field yet, search throws NullPointerException.

bugs.area: misc / similarities (SweetSpotSimilarity) with core impacts-based TOP_SCORES pruning
bugs.title: SweetSpotSimilarity with a length plateau (setLengthNormFactors with min >= 2) breaks Similarity's norm-monotonicity contract, so default top-k search silently misses the best hits
bugs.summary: You score a field with SweetSpotSimilarity and setLengthNormFactors(10, 20, 0.5f), index mostly 10-term fields plus some shorter ones, and run searcher.search(new TermQuery(new Term("f", "t")), 10) on a term with more than 1,000 matches, expecting the same top hits as an exhaustive search. Instead a 10-term document that contains the term twice (score 1.414) is missing and a document that contains it once (score 1.0) comes first. Below the plateau a 2-term field scores lower than a 10-term field although its norm is smaller, which breaks the rule that a greater norm never scores higher; the postings writer relies on that rule, keeps only the short field's (freq, norm) pair for the block, advertises a block maximum of 0.471, and top-k search skips the block.

bugs.area: search / CombinedFieldQuery (BM25F) max-score bound under dynamic pruning (CombinedFieldScorer.getMaxScore as used by MaxScoreBulkScorer)
bugs.title: CombinedFieldQuery computes its max score as score(+Infinity, 1), which is NaN under AxiomaticF2LOG/F2EXP, so top-k pruning silently drops the best hits
bugs.summary: You score a query with CombinedFieldQuery under the core AxiomaticF2LOG (or AxiomaticF2EXP) similarity, which the class javadoc counts as compatible because it keeps the default computeNorm, put it in a BooleanQuery next to another scoring clause such as a TermQuery, and expect IndexSearcher#search(q, 10) to return the same top hits as an exhaustive search. CombinedFieldScorer reports score(Float.POSITIVE_INFINITY, 1) as its max score, although SimScorer#score requires a finite freq and documents score(Float.MAX_VALUE, 1) as the bound; for the F2 similarities that is Inf/Inf = NaN, and MaxScoreBulkScorer, for which NaN is never below the minimum competitive score, then makes the other clause required. Documents that match only the CombinedFieldQuery are skipped: in a 3000-document index the default search returns doc 0 (score 2.1975672) as the top hit instead of doc 2000 (6.383921), and the upstream oracle CheckHits.checkTopScores fails.

bugs.area: search / similarities (IndriDirichletSimilarity constructors and the LMSimilarity collection model)
bugs.title: IndriDirichletSimilarity(float mu) uses LMSimilarity's default (cf+1)/(|C|+1) collection model instead of IndriCollectionModel (cf/|C|), so new IndriDirichletSimilarity(2000f) scores differently from new IndriDirichletSimilarity although both print the same name
bugs.summary: You install new IndriDirichletSimilarity(2000f) and expect the same similarity as new IndriDirichletSimilarity, which is documented as using 'the default mu value of 2000', and Indri's Dirichlet smoothing log((tf + mu*cf/|C|)/(|D| + mu)) for any mu. Instead the mu-only constructor passes no collection model, so its implicit super installs LMSimilarity's DefaultCollectionModel, (cf+1)/(|C|+1), while only the no-argument constructor installs the class's own IndriCollectionModel, cf/|C|. On a 25-token index the term 'president' (cf 3) scores -1.871553 instead of -2.119101 in the same document, although both instances print 'LM IndriDirichlet(2000.000000)'.

bugs.area: search / IndriAndQuery (IndriDisjunctionScorer iteration over two-phase clauses)
bugs.title: IndriAndQuery returns documents that match none of its clauses when a clause uses two-phase iteration (PhraseQuery, doc-values range queries), because IndriDisjunctionScorer iterates the clauses' approximations and never calls TwoPhaseIterator.matches
bugs.summary: You build an IndriAndQuery from SHOULD clauses, for example the phrase "a b" plus the term c, or a doc-values range n in [1, 10] plus the term c, and expect the documents that match at least one clause, as its javadoc ('matches documents matching combinations of subqueries') says. Instead it also returns documents that are only cheap candidates of the phrase or range clause: 'b a' (both terms, no phrase) in the phrase case and the documents with n=50 and n=100 in the range case, and count agrees with the wrong hits (3 instead of 2, and 4 instead of 2, in the 4-document repro). IndriDisjunctionScorer walks the approximations of its two-phase clauses and never runs their exact matches check; a segment where only one clause has a scorer is exact, so the same document can be rejected in one segment and returned in another.

bugs.area: search / score fusion (LogOddsFusionQuery: LogOddsFusionWeight#scorerSupplier)
bugs.title: LogOddsFusionQuery returns the raw clause score in segments where only one clause has a scorer, so identical documents score differently depending on their segment and explain disagrees with the score
bugs.summary: You combine two or more probability clauses (for example a BayesianScoreQuery over BM25 and a kNN query) with LogOddsFusionQuery and search an index that has more than one segment. You expect every document to get the documented fused score, sigmoid(n^alpha * mean of the gated log-odds over all n clauses), which is also what explain reports, whichever segment holds the document. Instead, in a segment where only one clause has a scorer, the query hands back that clause's own scorer unchanged, so documents there get the raw clause score: in the repro two documents with identical content score 0.6386912 and 0.5532073, while explain reports 0.6386912 for both.

bugs.area: monitor / presearcher (RegexpQueryHandler custom query handler)
bugs.title: Monitor with RegexpQueryHandler silently misses matching RegexpQuery queries, because the handler indexes each one under a fragment of its pattern text (for example 'cat|dog', 'colou' or '?mail') that matching terms do not contain
bugs.summary: You build a Monitor whose presearcher uses RegexpQueryHandler, register ordinary regexp queries such as /cat|dog/, /colou*r/ or /e.?mail/, and match documents containing 'dog', 'color' or 'email'. You expect Monitor.match to report each query, because the regexp matches the document and the presearcher may only skip queries that cannot match. Instead the handler indexes each query under a piece of its pattern text cut only at '.', '*' and '?' ('cat|dog', 'colou', '?mail'), no document term contains that piece, so the query is never run and the match is silently lost.

bugs.area: monitor / presearcher (RegexpQueryHandler document-side ngram filter SuffixingNGramTokenFilter)
bugs.title: Monitor with RegexpQueryHandler silently misses regexp matches on any short token that contains a supplementary character (an emoji, a CJK Extension B ideograph, a Gothic or Adlam letter), because SuffixingNGramTokenFilter emits no ngrams for that token
bugs.summary: You build a Monitor whose presearcher uses RegexpQueryHandler, register the query /hel.*/ and match a document whose text is 'hello😀' (WhitespaceAnalyzer, one token). You expect a match, because the regexp matches that token and the presearcher may only skip queries that cannot match. Instead SuffixingNGramTokenFilter, which should emit every substring of the token with the suffix 'XX' so that the query's index term 'helXX' is found, starts its gram size at the token's UTF-16 length (7) but checks it against the token's code-point count (6), gives up on the token without emitting a single ngram, and the query is silently never run.

bugs.area: monitor / query index updates (WritableQueryIndex.commitWithoutNotify and populateQueryCache, reached through both Monitor.register overloads and ConcurrentQueryLoader)
bugs.title: Monitor.register with the same query id twice in one call keeps both versions in the query index, so the query matches a mix of both versions, and after a reopen a persistent Monitor runs the older version while getQuery returns the newer one
bugs.summary: You register query id q twice in one call, monitor.register(List.of(new MonitorQuery("q", apple OR banana), new MonitorQuery("q", cherry))), as an application might when it applies a batch of query edits, and expect q to behave like one version, as it does when the two entries are registered in separate calls (the newer replaces the older). Instead the query index keeps both versions: q is reported for documents containing banana or cherry, a set that neither version matches, and getDisjunctCount is 3 for a one-clause query. With a persistent Monitor (q = apple, then q = cherry, in one call) the newer version runs until the Monitor is reopened, and from then on the older version apple runs instead while getQuery("q") still returns cherry.

bugs.area: monitor / query index updates (WritableQueryIndex.commitWithoutNotify failure atomicity, reached through both Monitor.register overloads)
bugs.title: A Monitor.register call that IndexWriter rejects is not rolled back: the earlier versions of the queries in the call are deleted at the next commit or close, and until then getQuery and match disagree
bugs.summary: You update stored queries with Monitor.register and IndexWriter rejects one of the new query documents, for example register(q2 = f:y) where q2 carries a 40,000-byte value in a TermFilteredPresearcher filter field, so register throws IllegalArgumentException. You expect the queries of the call to keep their old versions, as they do when the Monitor rejects a query before writing and as IndexWriter.updateDocuments would guarantee for each id. Instead the Monitor has already queued the deletion of the old version of every query id in the call and switched its in-memory cache to the new versions: right away q2 matches nothing although getQuery("q2") still returns f:b, and the next unrelated register or deleteById, or close of a persistent Monitor, deletes the old versions for good (register(q2 rejected, q1 valid), then close and reopen, leaves neither q1 nor q2).

bugs.area: monitor / query index updates (WritableQueryIndex.deleteQueries and clear versus commitWithoutNotify, reached through Monitor.deleteById, Monitor.clear and Monitor.register)
bugs.title: Monitor.deleteById and Monitor.clear issue their IndexWriter delete outside the commit lock, so a delete or clear that runs while register is indexing a decomposed query leaves that query partly indexed: it stays registered but silently stops matching what its deleted parts match, also after a reopen
bugs.summary: One thread registers query q = a OR b OR c, which the Monitor indexes as three parts, one per clause, while another thread calls monitor.deleteById("q") or monitor.clear; you expect the two calls to take effect in some order, so that afterwards q is either fully registered or gone. Instead the delete goes to the IndexWriter without the commit lock that register holds, lands between register's per-part addDocument calls and removes only the parts already added. q is still reported as registered with its full query, getDisjunctCount is 2, and a document that contains only 'a' no longer matches, also after the Monitor is closed and reopened.

bugs.area: monitor / query index updates versus matching (WritableQueryIndex.commitWithoutNotify versus search, reached through Monitor.register and Monitor.match)
bugs.title: Monitor.match running while Monitor.register re-registers the same query id can silently miss that query, because register puts the new version's cache entries into the live cache map before the new index documents are committed and the query index searcher is refreshed
bugs.summary: Query q = apple OR banana is registered in a Monitor; one thread re-registers q as cherry OR apple while another thread matches a document that contains apple. You expect the match to report q, because both versions of q match the document and every serial order of the two calls reports it. Instead the match can return no queries: register has already replaced the cache entry q_0 with the new first clause (cherry) while the searcher still holds the old index documents, so the old document for apple resolves to the cherry clause, which does not match, and the new apple clause is not searchable yet; once register returns, the same match reports q again.

bugs.area: search / intra-segment concurrency (index / TermStates lazy per-leaf lookup)
bugs.title: TermStates#get hands a lazily looked-up TermState to the other partitions of the same segment without safe publication, so under intra-segment concurrency a partition can read docFreq or file pointers still at 0 and a non-scoring term or phrase query silently misses matches (executed on aarch64)
bugs.summary: You search with an IndexSearcher that splits one segment into several partitions (the documented intra-segment concurrency) and count a non-scoring PhraseQuery, expecting the same count as a sequential search (500). Instead, on aarch64 about once per 10^5 to 10^6 searches the count is 437, 438 or 375 with no error: all partitions share one lazily filled TermStates, and TermStates#get stores each freshly cloned TermState into a plain array slot that the other partitions read with plain loads, so a partition can see the object before its fields (docFreq 0, sometimes a zero docStartFP or posStartFP) and gets an empty or garbage postings list for its doc range. Publishing the slot with a release store and reading it with acquire loads removes the failure in every test (0 in 1.2M end-to-end searches, 0 in 122.9M root-cause lookups).

bugs.title: MoreLikeThisQuery ignores its moreLikeFields and searches only fieldName, so the XML parser's <LikeThisQuery fieldNames="a,b"> searches only the first field (documents similar through the other fields are silently missed, every release since 6.1.0)
bugs.summary: You build a MoreLikeThisQuery for the text 'zebra quokka' with moreLikeFields {title, body} (or parse <LikeThisQuery fieldNames="title,body">zebra quokka</LikeThisQuery>) on an index where those words occur only in body, and expect the documents whose body contains them, because the javadoc says moreLikeFields are the 'fields used for similarity measure' and the XML DTD calls fieldNames a 'Comma delimited list of field names'. Up to 6.0.1 each word went to the listed field with the highest document frequency; LUCENE-6954 (6.1) made MoreLikeThis's Reader path use only the field it is given, and MoreLikeThisQuery, which uses that path, was never adapted.

bugs.area: replicator / NRT segment replication (CopyJob.transferAndCancel, ReplicaNode.newNRTPoint)
bugs.title: After a primary change, an NRT replica keeps a file it already copied from the old primary when the new primary's file has the same name, matching by name only, so the replica serves and commits the wrong documents with CheckIndex clean
bugs.summary: You run Lucene's NRT segment replication with failover: replica A is promoted to primary (a higher primaryGen) while replica B is still copying an NRT point from the old primary and has already finished one of its files, for example _1_1.liv. You expect B, once it has installed the new primary's NRT point, to search exactly the new primary's documents, because the module discards pre-copied data on a primary change and treats two files as the same only if name, header and footer match. Instead CopyJob._transferAndCancel keeps the old primary's finished temp file because the new primary's file has the same name, so B, at the new primary's version, shows [a0, b1] instead of [a0, a1], commits that state, and CheckIndex reports the index clean.

bugs.area: index / index sorting at merge time (IndexSorter.FloatSorter/DoubleSorter merge keys, MultiSorter) -> search / TopFieldCollector index-sort early termination
bugs.title: Merging segments of an index sorted by a FLOAT or DOUBLE field misplaces a NaN whose sign bit is set, so the merged segment violates its declared index sort (CheckIndex at level 2 or higher reports it) and sorted searches that terminate early on the index sort return wrong top hits
bugs.summary: You configure IndexWriterConfig#setIndexSort with a FLOAT (or DOUBLE) SortField over a FloatDocValuesField (DoubleDocValuesField), index a document whose value is a NaN with the sign bit set, for example the run-time negation of a NaN, and expect every flushed and merged segment to follow the sort, in which Float.compare puts every NaN after +Infinity. Flush gets this right, but a merge orders documents by NumericUtils.sortableFloatBits of the raw stored bits, which ranks that NaN below -Infinity, so the merged segment follows neither order: segments {3, 1, NaN} and {2, 0.5} sorted descending merge to [2.0, 0.5, NaN, 3.0, 1.0]. CheckIndex at level 2 or higher reports the segment as unsorted, and a top-1 search sorted by the index sort returns 2.0 instead of NaN, and 2.0 instead of 3.0 for a query that does not match the NaN document.

bugs.area: index / index sorting at merge time (IndexSorter.IntSorter merge keys, MultiSorter) -> search / TopFieldCollector index-sort early termination
bugs.title: With an INT index sort, merges order documents by the full 64-bit doc value while flush, sorted search and CheckIndex use its low 32 bits, so merging a value outside the int range writes a segment that violates its declared index sort (CheckIndex at level 2 or higher rejects it) and sorted searches that terminate early on the index sort return wrong top hits (a regression in 8.2.0)
bugs.summary: You configure an index sort on SortField("s", SortField.Type.INT), index documents with NumericDocValuesField("s", value), one of them with a value that does not fit in an int (for example 2^32, whose int value is 0), and let segments merge, expecting the merged segment to be sorted the way a flushed segment of the same documents is. Flush (IntSorter#getDocComparator), the search-time IntComparator and CheckIndex all compare (int) of the value, but the merge key (IntSorter#getComparableProviders) is the full long, so forceMerge(1) of the segments [a = 2^32] and [b = 1, c = 2] writes the order b, c, a instead of a, b, c. CheckIndex (level 2 or higher) then reports 'segment has indexSort=<int: "s"> but docID=1 sorts after docID=2' and a top-1 search sorted by the index sort returns b instead of a, while before the merge the same index is clean and returns a.

bugs.area: search / FieldExistsQuery count
bugs.title: FieldExistsQuery#count undercounts documents whose norms-free text field analyzes to no tokens but still has a doc value, so IndexSearcher#count is too low
bugs.summary: You index a text field with norms turned off together with a doc-values field of the same name, some document's text analyzes to no tokens (for example an empty string), and you call IndexSearcher#count(new FieldExistsQuery(field)). You expect the count to equal the number of documents the query returns, because the query matches every document that has a doc value. Instead, on a segment without deletions, Weight#count returns Terms#getDocCount, which counts only documents with at least one term, so the count is 1 for 2 hits, or 0 for 1 hit when no document in the segment has a term.

bugs.area: index / soft deletes
bugs.title: Removing a document's soft-delete value brings a hard-deleted document back
bugs.summary: With a soft-deletes field configured, you hard-delete a document and then clear its soft-delete value. You expect the document to stay deleted. Instead PendingSoftDeletes.applySoftDeletes sets its live bit again, so it becomes visible; softDelCount can reach -1, which wedges the writer and gives a corrupt commit or merge.
bugs.affected_versions: 7.4.0, 8.11.4, 9.12.3, 10.5.2, main [exec]; 7.3.1 has no soft deletes

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter construction from a near-real-time reader (ReaderPool pre-enrollment, PendingSoftDeletes reader constructor, soft-deletes accounting)
bugs.title: With a soft-deletes field configured, an IndexWriter opened from a near-real-time reader's IndexCommit (IndexWriterConfig#setIndexCommit) counts the reader's deletions again, so its next commit can drop a segment that still has live documents, write a commit that cannot be opened, or turn a soft delete into a hard delete (since 7.4.0)
bugs.summary: You configure a soft-deletes field, soft-delete one document (for example with an ordinary softUpdateDocument), open a near-real-time reader, close the writer, and open a new IndexWriter from that reader with setIndexCommit(nrtReader.getIndexCommit), as the setIndexCommit javadoc documents. You expect the new writer to start from the reader's point in time and commit every document, with the soft delete still soft. Instead it counts each deletion the reader sees again (a committed soft delete three times, an uncommitted hard delete twice), so its next commit drops a 3-document segment that has 2 live documents, writes a 2-document commit that DirectoryReader.open rejects with 'invalid deletion count: 3 vs maxDoc=2', or hard-deletes the soft-deleted document, and a later forceMerge can silently attach one document's terms to another document's stored fields.

It added IndexWriterConfig#setSoftDeletesField and the PendingSoftDeletes(field, reader, info) constructor, and made the writer-from-reader pre-enrollment (LUCENE-6524, #7582, 5.3.0) call it; that constructor seeds both its soft count and its hard-delete tracker from the reader's soft-applied live docs [exec]. Three later 7.4 development commits made the effects worse before the first release: LUCENE-8253 (#9300, aeac55a6029, 2018-04-16) removed a reset that had hidden the double-counted hard delete; LUCENE-8290 (#9337, 8fdd3d7584b, 2018-05-02, bisected) started dropping segments that look fully deleted; LUCENE-8341 (#9388, 21f03a49532, committed 2018-06-04) recorded softDelCount in SegmentCommitInfo, so a committed soft delete is counted a third time and the -ea assertion fires [exec].

bugs.area: util / BKD points
bugs.title: PointInSetQuery silently misses most matches on selectively indexed points (fewer index dimensions than data dimensions)
bugs.summary: You index a point field with more data dimensions than index dimensions (FieldType.setDimensions(d, 1, bytes), selective indexing) and run a PointInSetQuery (newSetQuery) on it. You expect every document whose indexed value is in the set to match. Instead BKDWriter sorts leaves by a data dimension and the query's forward-only visitor skips matches: 189,088 of 207,884 expected hits (91%) were missed in the repro, and a 3-dim/2-index-dim field returned 0 hits instead of 2.

bugs.area: search / points queries (PointInSetQuery segment early exit)
bugs.title: Multi-dimensional PointInSetQuery skips segments that contain matching points, because its segment early exit uses the lexicographically first and last set points as per-dimension bounds
bugs.summary: You subclass PointInSetQuery for a 2-D point field, as Lucene's own tests do, and search for the set {(0,1), (1,0)} in an index whose segment holds one document at (1,0). You expect that document to match, as it does for the one-point set {(1,0)}. Instead, since 10.3.0 the query keeps the first and last set points in sorted order, (0,1) and (1,0), as if they were the set's per-dimension minimum and maximum, concludes from dimension 1 (1 is above the segment's maximum 0) that the segment cannot match, and skips it, so count is 0 with no error; adding a point to a set can thus remove hits.

bugs.area: search / sorting (NumericComparator doc-values-skipper pruning for FLOAT/DOUBLE)
bugs.title: A FLOAT or DOUBLE sort on a NUMERIC doc-values field with a skip index and no points silently returns wrong or missing top hits when values have the sign bit set (negative values, or -0.0 with a tie-break sort): skipper pruning compares sortable-encoded bounds with the raw IEEE-bit block min/max
bugs.summary: You store float or double values as raw IEEE bits in a single-valued NUMERIC doc-values field with a skip index and no points (for example NumericDocValuesField.indexedField("f", Float.floatToRawIntBits(v)), the layout of Lucene's own skip-index sort test) and sort on it with SortField.Type.FLOAT or DOUBLE. You expect the same hits as on the same values without a skip index, lowest value first. Instead, with 10,000 docs holding 0, -1,..., -9999 and a TermQuery that matches all of them, the ascending top 3 is [-8191, -8190, -8189] instead of [-9999, -9998, -9997] and a descending searchAfter(-9000) returns no hits, because the pruning compares bounds in NumericUtils sortable order with skipper block min/max in raw-bit order, and the two orders disagree for values with the sign bit set.

bugs.area: document / point query factories (BinaryPoint, PointRangeQuery)
bugs.title: BinaryPoint.newExactQuery and the one-dimensional newRangeQuery keep the caller's byte as the query bounds (BinaryPoint.pack returns the caller's array for one dimension), while the same factory packs a private copy for two or more dimensions, so a caller that refills its buffer silently changes queries it already built
bugs.summary: You write a one-dimensional binary key into a scratch byte, build BinaryPoint.newExactQuery(field, scratch), write the next key into the same array, build a second query and OR the two; you expect each query to match the key it was built for, as BinaryPoint's two-dimension range queries and its one-value newSetQuery do. Instead both queries now mean the second key (they compare equal and print the same bounds) and the OR finds 1 document instead of 2; likewise a one-dimensional newRangeQuery whose lo/hi arrays the caller overwrites afterwards matches 0 documents instead of the range it was built for. BinaryPoint.pack returns new BytesRef(point[0]), a wrapper over the caller's array, when there is one dimension, and PointRangeQuery stores that array as its bounds, so matching, equals, hashCode and toString read whatever the caller's array holds at the time.
bugs.introduced_commit: e1a1dbfabcc9 (LUCENE-7117/LUCENE-7118 'Remove multidimensional arrays from PointRangeQuery', Robert Muir (rmuir), migrated as apache/lucene#8172 and #8173; JIRA era, no pull request; committed the same day on branch_6_0 as d8c4e6977b0e, the copy in 6.0.0, and on branch_6x as 51b109620be7) [read]: it made BinaryPoint.newRangeQuery(String, byte, byte) pass pack(lowerValue).bytes and pack(upperValue).bytes to PointRangeQuery, so two or more dimensions get a private packed array while one dimension keeps the caller's array through pack's shortcut 'if (point.length == 1) return new BytesRef(point[0])', which LUCENE-6881 (f12cb52a3b8, 2015-11-08) had written for the field constructor (Field documents its byte values as not copied). In the unreleased code between LUCENE-7045 (099e0311398, 2016-02-23) and this commit the query kept the caller's byte for every dimension count, so no released version ever copied the one-dimension bounds. The lines are unchanged on main apart from the 2020 reformat (2d6ad2fee6d, LUCENE-9570)

bugs.area: search / IndexSearcher timeout reporting for vector queries (AbstractKnnVectorQuery rewrite, AbstractVectorSimilarityQuery scorerSupplier)
bugs.title: kNN and vector-similarity searches that hit the IndexSearcher timeout before collecting any hit return 0 hits with IndexSearcher.timedOut == false, so the timed-out search looks like a search without matches
bugs.summary: You set a timeout with IndexSearcher#setTimeout and run a kNN query (KnnFloatVectorQuery or KnnByteVectorQuery) or an approximate FloatVectorSimilarityQuery/ByteVectorSimilarityQuery, and the timeout fires before the vector search has found its first hit. You expect what a TermQuery gives under the same timeout: 0 hits with IndexSearcher#timedOut == true, the documented signal ('Returns true if any search hit the timeout') that the answer is incomplete. Instead the search returns 0 hits, TotalHits '0 hits' (EQUAL_TO) and timedOut == false, so the timed-out search cannot be told apart from a search that has no matches; IndexSearcher#count of a kNN query behaves the same way.

bugs.area: search / vector similarity-threshold queries (ExplicitVectorSimilarityCollector with the exhaustive scan and the HNSW graph search)
bugs.title: FloatVectorSimilarityQuery and ByteVectorSimilarityQuery with traversalSimilarity == resultSimilarity (the 3- and 4-argument constructors: the plain ones in 9.10.0-10.4.0, the deprecated Explicit classes in 10.5.2 and main) silently drop documents whose similarity is exactly resultSimilarity, because the collector's minCompetitiveSimilarity rises to the inclusive threshold and every searcher treats an equal score as not competitive
bugs.summary: You index vectors with the default codec and run FloatVectorSimilarityQuery.Explicit(field, target, 1.0f) on main or 10.5.2 (the plain FloatVectorSimilarityQuery(field, target, 1.0f) on 9.10.0-10.4.0), which sets traversalSimilarity = resultSimilarity, to find every exact copy of target under EUCLIDEAN, and you expect every document with similarity >= 1.0, as collect ('similarity >= resultSimilarity'), explain ('Score above threshold') and the query's own exact fallback all count them. Instead only the first copy comes back: a 65-vector segment with copies at doc 0 and doc 64 returns [0] and count 1, the same query with a MatchAllDocsQuery filter returns [0, 64], a 4,000-vector HNSW segment returns 1 of its 12 copies, and a traversalSimilarity one ulp lower returns all of them (byte vectors at an exact 0.5 behave the same). Once a hit at the threshold is collected, ExplicitVectorSimilarityCollector.minCompetitiveSimilarity = min(traversalSimilarity, maxSimilarity) equals the inclusive result threshold, and both the exhaustive scan (a 64-vector batch is collected only if its best score > minCompetitiveSimilarity) and the graph search (score >= nextUp(minCompetitiveSimilarity)) treat an equal score as not competitive; the one-line fix returns min(nextDown(traversalSimilarity), maxSimilarity).
bugs.introduced_commit: cd195980ecbcb45e19ce9465854fed0b6be79ea7 on main (GITHUB#12679 'Add support for similarity-based vector searches' by kaivalnp, merged 2023-12-11) and its branch_9x backport 8089b8c9d3374dc4d451a4280daae85e0b139b84, first released in 9.10.0 [read]: the new collector kept similarity >= resultSimilarity but reported min(traversalSimilarity, maxSimilarity) as minCompetitiveSimilarity, and the 3/4-argument constructors passed resultSimilarity as traversalSimilarity (a default the author proposed in the PR on 2023-11-30), while #12770 (e1ce1d692ca4, merged 2023-11-07 during that review, released in 9.9.0) had already made HnswGraphSearcher's level-0 neighbour test strict ('>'), so the code was defective the day it merged. Not adapted when #15021 (0421a8de771e, 10.4.0) added the exhaustive-scan batch gate 'max > minCompetitiveSimilarity', and #14963 (4a7c9c2780b, 10.4.0) stopped building graphs for small segments, so that gate became the normal path for them. Gone in 10.5.0 (#15784, be2af1e7b43: the plain constructors use the adaptive collector) and restored verbatim in 10.5.2 by #16654 (bc9adc96cc58 on main, 2026-09-13; backport #16671 5caef2a1fda9) as the deprecated ExplicitVectorSimilarityCollector behind [Byte|Float]VectorSimilarityQuery.Explicit [read]

bugs.area: index / FilterCodecReader reader lifecycle (IndexReader reference counting)
bugs.title: Closing a FilterCodecReader runs the wrapped reader's close hook directly (in.doClose instead of in.close), so a DirectoryReader that still uses that segment silently finds 0 hits, and its own close later releases the segment a second time and throws
bugs.summary: You wrap a segment of an open DirectoryReader in a FilterCodecReader (for example to pass it to IndexWriter.addIndexes), take the usual extra reference with incRef, and close the wrapper, expecting the DirectoryReader to keep working, because the IndexReader javadoc says a reader 'will not really be closed until decRef has been called for all outstanding references' and FilterLeafReader behaves exactly that way. Instead FilterCodecReader.doClose calls the wrapped reader's internal close hook (in.doClose) rather than releasing a reference (in.close), so the segment's files are closed while the DirectoryReader still uses it: a TermQuery that matched 1 document now finds 0 with no error, reading stored fields throws AlreadyClosedException, and closing the DirectoryReader later releases the same resources a second time and throws.

It added 'doClose { in.doClose; }' together with TestFilterCodecReader#testDeclaredMethodsOverridden, a reflective test that requires FilterCodecReader to override every CodecReader method; before it FilterCodecReader inherited CodecReader#doClose, which never touches the delegate [read]

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter merge-time reordering (OneMerge#reorder guard; misc BPReorderingMergePolicy)
bugs.title: Reordering merges (BPReorderingMergePolicy) silently break document blocks written before Lucene 9.9, because IndexWriter's reorder guard reads the unrecorded LeafMetaData#hasBlocks flag as 'no blocks'
bugs.summary: You have an index with document blocks (children followed by their parent, added with IndexWriter#addDocuments) that was written by Lucene 9.8 or earlier, open it with a current Lucene, and force-merge it through BPReorderingMergePolicy. You expect the merge to leave the blocks alone, because since 9.11 IndexWriter lets a merge reorder documents only when there are no blocks or a parent field identifies them, and such an old index cannot have a parent field. Instead the guard trusts LeafMetaData#hasBlocks, which was never recorded before 9.9 and reads false for those segments, so the reorderer renumbers the documents one by one and interleaves the blocks, with no exception and a clean CheckIndex, while the same documents written by 9.9.2 are left intact.
bugs.introduced_commit: 4a3f4cfe9745 on main and 2e503b657549 on branch_9x (#13128 'Make OneMerge#reorder preserve blocks', by jpountz), which added today's guard hasBlocksButNoParentField = anyMatch(LeafMetaData::hasBlocks) && (some leaf has no parent field) [read]. The reorder hook itself came earlier with #12622 ('Add a merge policy wrapper that performs recursive graph bisection on merge', jpountz; 6b1538b33136 on branch_9x, f7cab1645017 on main), which called OneMerge#reorder with no block check at all, so the pre-9.9 damage starts there [exec]. The 'not recorded before 9.9.0' caveat of hasBlocks comes from #12685 (s1monw; 26043819a5b1 on branch_9x, 6677109ee608 on main), four months before the guard. No commit-level bisect: release-level runs plus git ancestry pin both boundaries

bugs.area: search / FieldExistsQuery and index / FieldInfos field-schema consistency on Lucene-8-created indexes (SegmentInfos per-segment open gate, #14607)
bugs.title: Since 10.4.0 Lucene opens indexes created by Lucene 8 once Lucene 9 has rewritten every segment, but without Lucene 9's field-consistency leniency for them (LUCENE-10518), so FieldExistsQuery returns documents that lack the doc value (or throws) and IndexWriter refuses the index
bugs.summary: You have an index first created by Lucene 8 that Lucene 9 later rewrote completely (every live segment is 9.x), in which a field is indexed in every document but has a doc value in only some (Lucene 9 allowed that only for such 8.x-created indexes), and you open it with Lucene 10.4.0 or later, which accepts it since #14607. You expect FieldExistsQuery on that field to return only the documents with the doc value, as Lucene 9.12.3 does and Lucene 9's own TestFieldExistsQuery#testOldIndices asserts, and IndexWriter to open whatever DirectoryReader.open accepts. Instead, once the documents share a segment FieldExistsQuery silently rewrites to MatchAllDocsQuery and also returns the document without the doc value (hits [d1, d2] instead of [d1], count 2 instead of 1), while they sit in separate segments it throws IllegalStateException, and IndexWriter and FieldInfos.getMergedFieldInfos throw IllegalArgumentException 'cannot change field "my_field" from doc values type=BINARY to inconsistent doc values type=NONE'.

bugs.area: index / addIndexes reorder path: SlowCompositeCodecReaderWrapper merged vector values (MergedDocIterator) over SortingCodecReader inputs
bugs.title: SlowCompositeCodecReaderWrapper's merged vector iterator numbers ordinals by position and ignores each input's own index, so addIndexes of two or more SortingCodecReader inputs through a reordering merge policy writes vectors onto the wrong documents
bugs.summary: You re-sort two or more segments with SortingCodecReader and pass them to one IndexWriter.addIndexes(CodecReader...) call on a writer that has no index sort but uses a merge policy that reorders addIndexes merges, such as BPReorderingMergePolicy (an identity OneMerge#reorder is enough), and you expect every document to keep the vector it was indexed with, as it does without the reorder. Instead the merged view that IndexWriter builds for the reorder (SlowCompositeCodecReaderWrapper) numbers vectors by iteration position, while each SortingCodecReader input reports and reads vectors by its original ordinal, so in each input the k-th document in sorted order is written with the vector at original ordinal k. Nothing throws, with or without assertions, CheckIndex reports the new index clean, and kNN search then scores documents by other documents' vectors, in an executed probe including the vector of a document deleted before the call.
