bugs.area: codecs / quantized vector formats merge (Lucene104 scalar-quantized, Lucene102 binary-quantized) with index / addIndexes through SlowCodecReaderWrapper and memory / MemoryIndex
bugs.title: Merging into a Lucene104 scalar-quantized FLOAT32 vector field that does not use COSINE centers the merge source's own vector arrays in place, so IndexWriter.addIndexes changes a source that keeps its arrays (MemoryIndex, FloatVectorValues.fromFloats) and can store wrong full-precision vectors or wrong quantized codes
bugs.summary: You index a FLOAT32 field with Lucene104ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and EUCLIDEAN, DOT_PRODUCT or MAXIMUM_INNER_PRODUCT by calling IndexWriter.addIndexes(SlowCodecReaderWrapper.wrap(...)) on a MemoryIndex, or on a FilterLeafReader that serves new vectors from your own list through FloatVectorValues.fromFloats, and you expect the merge only to read its source, as it does for COSINE fields and for the older Lucene99 scalar-quantized formats. Instead the quantizer subtracts the merged centroid from the source's own arrays: afterwards the MemoryIndex vector {1,2,3,4} reads back as {0,0,0,0} when it is the only vector, and as {1.5,0.75,-2,1.5} when merged together with a second source holding {-2,0.5,7,1}, a second addIndexes of it stores that centered vector as the full-precision vector, and your list holds centered vectors. When two documents share one float in a single addIndexes, the second is quantized from the already-centered array, so it scores 0.160 against 0.066 for its identical copies (exact 0.066) and ranks first.

bugs.area: queryparser / classic QueryParser and MultiFieldQueryParser (QueryParser.jj MultiTerm run grouping, QueryParserBase.addClause conjunction step)
bugs.title: Classic QueryParser with the default splitOnWhitespace=false: since #16446 an AND/OR that directly follows a token the analyzer drops (such as a stopword) binds to the whole preceding run of plain terms instead of the last term, so typing the stopword changes which documents match (unreleased regression on main and branch_10_6)
bugs.summary: You parse 'apple banana the AND cherry' with the classic QueryParser at its default settings and an analyzer that drops 'the', and expect the same query as for 'apple banana AND cherry', namely body:apple +body:banana +body:cherry, which is what Lucene 10.5.2 returns and what main returns with splitOnWhitespace=true. On main you get +(body:apple body:banana) +body:cherry, so a document containing only 'apple cherry' now matches; with the AND default operator, 'apple banana the OR cherry' becomes (+body:apple +body:banana) body:cherry instead of +body:apple body:banana body:cherry, so a document with only 'cherry' matches and one with only 'apple' no longer does. The cause is #16446, which now adds the analysed run 'apple banana' as one clause: the stopword yields no clause, so the following conjunction's 'make the preceding clause required (or optional)' step in addClause changes the whole run instead of 'banana'.

bugs.area: search / index-sort range-query shortcuts (Sort.getPrimarySortField; SortedNumericDocValuesRangeQuery, SortedSetDocValuesRangeQuery, IndexSortSortedNumericDocValuesRangeQuery)
bugs.title: Sort.getPrimarySortField (new in 10.6.0, #16424) skips an index-sort field that the reader's FieldInfos do not list, or whose skip index holds a single value, even when that field still orders the documents (a FilterLeafReader hides it but keeps the index sort, or a BinarySortField derives its key from other fields), so doc-values range queries on the next sort field, LongField.newRangeQuery included, return wrong hits or throw
bugs.summary: You sort an index by two fields, say (c, f), and then either read it through a FilterLeafReader that hides c from FieldInfos but, like every FilterLeafReader by default, still reports the index sort (c, f) in getMetaData, or sort by a BinarySortField subclass whose key is derived from another doc-values field, as its javadoc allows; a doc-values range query on f should still match exactly the documents whose f is in the range, as it does on 10.5.2. On main and the 10.6.0 release candidate, Sort.getPrimarySortField (added by #16424) finds no FieldInfo for c (or for the BinarySortField's own name), concludes that sorting by it 'has no effect', and returns f as the primary sort, so the range queries' index-sort shortcuts binary-search a segment that is not ordered by f. The result: most ranges miss matching documents and some return documents outside the range (43 of 55 ranges wrong in an independent test; f:[1 TO 3] returns 0 hits instead of 2), and LongField.newRangeQuery can throw IllegalArgumentException 'minDoc must be < maxDoc'.

bugs.area: analysis / Thai (ThaiTokenizer#incrementWord user-dictionary loop and re-anchor, GITHUB#16722; ThaiTokenizerFactory 'dictionary')
bugs.title: ThaiTokenizer with a user dictionary silently drops the vowel or tone marks that follow a dictionary word ending inside a character cluster (with {แม่น}, 'แม่น้ำ' (river) is tokenized as just [แม่น] (accurate)), because the match is accepted at a non-boundary and the remainder, which now starts with a mark, is skipped
bugs.summary: You configure ThaiTokenizer with a user dictionary that contains an ordinary short word such as แม่น ('accurate') or ผล ('result') and expect it to change only where words split. Instead, when the dictionary word is followed in the text by a combining vowel or tone mark, as in แม่น้ำ ('river') or ผลิต ('produce'), the tokenizer cuts the character cluster and throws the mark away: แม่น้ำ becomes the single token แม่น, and ผลิต becomes [ผล, ต]. Because queries are analyzed the same way, a search for แม่น้ำ also matches documents that only contain แม่น, with no error.

bugs.area: search / similarities: StableTflSimilarity with SynonymQuery and CombinedFieldQuery
bugs.title: StableTflSimilarity scores SynonymQuery and CombinedFieldQuery with the length of a placeholder term string ('synonym pseudo-term', 19 code points, or 'pseudo_term', 11), not the length of the query terms
bugs.summary: You set StableTflSimilarity on the searcher, whose javadoc derives a term's rarity from the length |t| of the query term, and you search with a SynonymQuery (for example the one QueryBuilder builds when a synonym filter stacks 'dog' and 'dogs' at one position) or with a CombinedFieldQuery. You expect the real query terms' length to be used, so that SynonymQuery{ab, cd} on a document that contains 'ab' once scores like TermQuery(ab), and a one-field CombinedFieldQuery scores like a TermQuery on a copy field. Instead both queries hand the similarity a fixed placeholder term ('synonym pseudo-term', 19 code points; 'pseudo_term', 11 code points), so every synonym group is scored as an almost maximally rare 19-character term and every combined-field term as an 11-character one: SynonymQuery{ab, cd} scores 1.4050181 instead of 1.3490043, and in 200-token documents the group {dog, dogs} scores 2.13x TermQuery(dog) and outranks a document that matches 'elephant'.

bugs.area: search / SynonymQuery pseudo-term statistics (SynonymWeight; reached through QueryBuilder with stock synonym parsers)
bugs.title: SynonymQuery with a repeated term adds that term's totalTermFreq once per copy, so the pseudo-term statistics it gives the Similarity can exceed the field's sumTotalTermFreq (AssertionError in SimilarityBase with -ea, scores from impossible statistics with -da)
bugs.summary: You search with a SynonymQuery that contains the same term more than once, built with SynonymQuery.Builder or produced by QueryBuilder when a synonym rule's entries coincide after analysis (the rule 'résumé, resume, cv' with ASCII folding gives Synonym(f:cv f:resume f:resume) for the query 'resume'), and expect the pseudo-term statistics it hands to the Similarity to stay within the field's totals, which TermStats lists as 'always true' (totalTermFreq <= sumTotalTermFreq of the field). Instead SynonymWeight takes the largest docFreq of the terms but adds the repeated term's totalTermFreq once per copy: on a field with the documents 'a' and 'a b' (sumTotalTermFreq 4), SynonymQuery(a, a) passes totalTermFreq 6. With assertions enabled every SimilarityBase similarity throws AssertionError from fillBasicStats when the Weight is built; with assertions disabled they score from impossible statistics, for example LM Dirichlet uses a collection probability P(t|C) of 1.17 for SynonymQuery(x, x, x) where TermQuery(x) uses 0.5.

bugs.area: misc / BP merge-time reordering
bugs.title: Merges through BPReorderingMergePolicy with BpVectorReorderer break document blocks even when a parent field is configured
bugs.summary: You index documents in blocks (children followed by their parent) with IndexWriterConfig#setParentField, and use BPReorderingMergePolicy with a BpVectorReorderer over a float vector field. You expect merges to keep every block together with its parent last, because IndexWriter only lets a merge reorder documents when the parent field identifies the blocks, and setParentField promises that IndexWriter does not alter the order of a block. Instead BpVectorReorderer moves each document on its own and puts every document without a vector after all documents with one, so the merged segment's blocks are silently scrambled and ToParentBlockJoinQuery joins children to the wrong parent (59 of 60 children in one run), with no exception and with assertions on or off.

bugs.area: queries / FunctionScoreQuery block-max pruning (#16431)
bugs.title: FunctionScoreQuery's block-max bound multiplies by the wrapped query's no-score max score (0 for a TermQuery), so a BooleanQuery that contains it can drop the true top hits
bugs.summary: You index a popularity field with a skip index (NumericDocValuesField.indexedField("popularity", v)) and search BooleanQuery(SHOULD FunctionScoreQuery(TermQuery(body:a), DoubleValuesSource.fromLongField("popularity")), SHOULD TermQuery(body:b)) for the top hit, expecting the same hit as an exhaustive search, because the function query scores each matching document by its popularity value. Instead, with 5,000 documents that all match body:a, where only doc 4999 has popularity 100 (all others 1) and only doc 0 matches body:b, TOP_SCORES and the plain IndexSearcher.search(q, 1) return doc 0 (score 4.69) instead of doc 4999 (score 100). The cause is that the scorer's getMaxScore returns innerMaxScore * valueMaxScore * boost, where innerMaxScore is the max score of the wrapped TermQuery, which FunctionScoreQuery itself weighted without scores (so it reports 0), although score is value * boost and never reads the wrapped score; every block therefore reports a bound of 0, and MaxScoreBulkScorer stops scoring documents that only the function clause makes competitive.

bugs.title: tryDeleteDocument / tryUpdateDocValue running while commit flushes returns a sequence number above the commit's, yet its change is in that commit

bugs.area: index / DirectoryReader reopen with doc-values updates (generation numbers reused across writer sessions)
bugs.title: A reopened reader returns the doc values of a discarded writer session or commit when a later writer session reuses the same doc-values generation number
bugs.summary: You keep a reader open while a writer session updates doc values and then ends without committing (rollback, or close with commitOnClose=false), or while a writer opened on an older commit with setIndexCommit discards the newer commit; a later writer session updates doc values of the same segment and commits, and you reopen the old reader with DirectoryReader.openIfChanged. bugs.area: index / IndexWriter tryDeleteDocument (dropDeletedSegment, change accounting)
bugs.title: If tryDeleteDocument removes a segment's last live document and closing that segment's pooled reader throws, IndexWriter stays open but never counts the change, so NRT readers hide the document while commit and close keep it

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter deleteAll (change accounting on the exception path, ReaderPool.dropAll)
bugs.title: If closing a pooled segment reader throws inside IndexWriter.deleteAll, the segments are already cleared but the change is never counted: the writer stays open and its NRT readers show an empty index, yet hasUncommittedChanges is false and commit and close keep every document, until a later unrelated commit silently applies the failed deleteAll
bugs.summary: You commit two documents, open and close an NRT reader (so the writer keeps pooled segment readers), and call deleteAll; closing one of the pooled readers throws (for example a core ClosedListener your cache registered throws its declared IOException, or closing a file fails), so deleteAll throws an IOException and the writer stays open. You expect the writer to stay self-consistent: what its NRT readers show is what commit persists, and hasUncommittedChanges reports the pending change. Instead deleteAll has already removed every segment but skipped counting the change, so new NRT readers show 0 documents while hasUncommittedChanges is false, commit returns -1 and writes nothing, close keeps both documents on disk, and the next unrelated addDocument plus commit silently applies the deleteAll that failed.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter deleteAll versus a concurrent segment flush (DocumentsWriter.lockAndAbortAll, flush-ticket queue)
bugs.title: IndexWriter.deleteAll misses a segment flush that another thread is already running, so documents added before deleteAll survive it and are committed
bugs.summary: Several threads index into one IndexWriter, and one of them is in the middle of writing its full in-memory buffer out as a new segment when another thread calls deleteAll. You expect deleteAll to drop every buffered document and every segment, like opening a new IndexWriter with OpenMode.CREATE, so the next commit is empty: every document was added with a smaller sequence number than deleteAll's, and some of those addDocument calls had already returned before deleteAll was called. Instead deleteAll returns without waiting for that segment to be published, the flushing thread then adds it to the freshly cleared index, and its documents survive deleteAll into the commit, still carrying the old field schema.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter forced merge (forceMerge wait loop, mergeExceptions and mergeGen, tragic events)
bugs.title: IndexWriter.forceMerge(n) can return normally with more than n segments when a merge that was already pending or running at the call fails: forceMerge adopts that merge without updating its mergeGen, so addMergeException drops the failure, and the tragic event is published only after mergeFinish has woken the waiting forceMerge
bugs.summary: You call forceMerge(1) while a background merge started by an earlier commit or flush (or by forceMerge's own flush) is still pending or running, and that merge fails, for example because the disk is full. You expect forceMerge to throw, as it does ('background merge hit exception') when the failing merge is one it registered itself. Instead it can return normally with the index still unmerged (2 segments, or 9 with the default TieredMergePolicy): the adopted merge keeps its old mergeGen, so its failure is dropped, and the tragic event that closes the writer is published only after mergeFinish has woken the waiting call.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter doc-values updates (BinaryDocValuesFieldUpdates value buffer, FrozenBufferedUpdates apply, applyUpdatesPacket tragic close)
bugs.title: A binary doc-values update whose term matches many documents copies its value once per matched document into one int-sized buffer when it is applied, so at 2^31 bytes in one segment (about 2^30 for the first update of a field in a packet) commit throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (AssertionError with -ea) and IndexWriter closes itself, losing the update and every uncommitted document (every release since 4.8.0)
bugs.summary: You commit 2,100 documents that share the term group:g, add one more document, call updateBinaryDocValue(group:g, field, a 1 MiB value) once and commit; the javadoc sets no size limit and says the value replaces the value of all affected documents, and the resulting 2.1 GB of binary doc values is an index Lucene can hold (a build with the fix sketch commits it). Instead, applying the update appends a full copy of the value for every matched document to one int-addressed BytesRefBuilder, which overflows at 2^31 bytes: commit throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (with -ea, AssertionError 'size must be positive (got -2147483648): likely integer overflow?'), IndexWriter treats it as a tragic event and closes itself, and both the update and the extra uncommitted document are gone. On 7.7.0 and later a lone update fails at half that size (1,100 documents x 1 MiB) because of the linked bug that applies the first update of a field twice, and ordinary value sizes suffice too (530,000 documents x 4 KiB).

bugs.area: core / index (ParallelLeafReader stored fields x StoredFieldsWriter.MergeVisitor, on addIndexes and wrapForMerge copies)
bugs.title: Copying a ParallelLeafReader into an index (IndexWriter.addIndexes over SlowCodecReaderWrapper, or a merge whose OneMerge.wrapForMerge returns one) silently stores a later sub-reader's stored fields under another field's name: ParallelLeafReader.storedFields lets each sub-reader visit with its own FieldInfo numbers while getFieldInfos renumbers the fields, and StoredFieldsWriter.MergeVisitor skips its remap-by-name step when the numbers look aligned
bugs.summary: You build two indexes in lockstep, as ParallelLeafReader requires (index A stores title='Lucene in Action', index B stores price='42'), wrap them in a ParallelLeafReader, which itself returns both fields correctly, and copy it into a new index with IndexWriter.addIndexes(SlowCodecReaderWrapper.wrap(reader)), expecting the copy to hold title and price. Instead the copy holds title='Lucene in Action' and title='42' and no price field, with no error and a clean CheckIndex: storedFields lets B report price with B's own field number 0, the parallel reader's getFieldInfos numbers price 1, and because the target's merged numbers equal the parallel reader's, the stored-fields merge skips its remap-by-name step and writes the value under number 0, which is title. A merge whose OneMerge.wrapForMerge adds a parallel index with stored fields behind each segment goes wrong the same way (a 'summary' value stored as a second 'id').

Instead the visarga branch copies the next character before the loop has folded it and never revisits the copy, so নিঃশব্দ becomes নিশসব্দ (SHA SA) and নিঃষব্দ becomes নিষসব্দ (SSA SA): the three spellings give three different terms, and a document written with one of them is not found by a query written with another, with no error.

bugs.title: StandardTokenizer (StandardAnalyzer's tokenizer) and UAX29URLEmailTokenizer misapply the UAX #29 Hebrew quote rules WB7a-WB7c next to other word characters: a Hebrew letter + ASCII apostrophe swallows a following digit or underscore (BET'2 is one term), an ASCII apostrophe after a Hebrew letter that ends a mid-word chain is dropped (HE.SHIN' -> HE.SHIN), and a word with an ASCII quotation mark between Hebrew letters is split when it also contains a mid-word '.', ':' or quote (ALEF.TSADI"LAMED, TAV"ALEF.BET)
bugs.summary: You index Hebrew text with the stock StandardAnalyzer, whose StandardTokenizer says it implements the UAX #29 word-break rules, among them WB7a-WB7c, which keep an ASCII apostrophe after a Hebrew letter (BET') and an ASCII quotation mark between two Hebrew letters (TAV"ALEF) inside a word, and you expect them to combine with the other rules as the annex and ICU do: BET'2 gives [BET', 2], HE.SHIN' gives [HE.SHIN'], and TAV"ALEF.BET and ALEF.TSADI"LAMED are single words. Instead the grammar writes 'Hebrew letter + quote' as a separate piece that may be glued to any following piece but cannot continue a letter chain, so BET'2 becomes one term (a search for 2 misses the document), HE.SHIN' loses the apostrophe, and the quoted words are split into [TAV"ALEF, BET] and [ALEF.TSADI, LAMED]. StandardTokenizer and UAX29URLEmailTokenizer behave the same, with no error.

bugs.area: analysis-common / ASCIIFoldingFilter mapping table (foldToASCII switch)
bugs.title: ASCIIFoldingFilter folds six letters to the ASCII letter of the opposite case (ǥ U+01E5 and ǧ U+01E7 to 'G', insular ꞅ U+A785 to 'S' and Ꞅ U+A784 to 's', Ɐ U+2C6F to 'a', Ꜿ U+A73E to 'c'; stretched ʗ U+0297 to 'C' is contested), so a LowerCaseFilter-then-ASCIIFoldingFilter chain indexes 'naǧib' as 'naGib' and the ASCII query 'nagib' finds nothing
bugs.summary: You index and search through a chain that lower-cases and then applies ASCIIFoldingFilter, documented to convert characters 'into their ASCII equivalents', and you type queries in plain ASCII. You expect 'naǧib' and 'NAǦIB' to be indexed as 'nagib', just as 'ağa' becomes 'aga'; instead six entries of the 1,242-entry folding table sit in the output group of the opposite case (ǥ and ǧ in 'G', ꞅ in 'S', Ꞅ in 's', Ɐ in 'a', Ꜿ in 'c', plus the contested ʗ in 'C'), so the term is 'naGib' and the query 'nagib' finds nothing. Each of the six lines carries a source comment that names the other case (for example [LATIN SMALL LETTER G WITH CARON] inside the 'G' group), and the fix is to move these case labels into the group of their own case.

bugs.area: analysis / QueryAutoStopWordAnalyzer (analysis-common query package; AnalyzerWrapper reuse strategy, Analyzer.ReuseStrategy)
bugs.title: QueryAutoStopWordAnalyzer inherits its delegate's reuse strategy although its analysis chain differs per field, so with a stock delegate (GLOBAL_REUSE_STRATEGY) the chain built for the first field a thread analyses is reused for every other field: one field's stop words drop another field's query terms and a field's own stop words are kept (since 4.5.0)
bugs.summary: You wrap a stock analyzer such as StandardAnalyzer in QueryAutoStopWordAnalyzer, which computes a separate set of very common words (stop words) for each field from the index, and use that one analyzer for queries on several fields. You expect each field to lose only its own stop words, as the class's per-field design and its upstream test testNoFieldNamePollution say ('Filter should not prevent stopwords in one field being used in another'). Instead the analyzer reuses the analysis chain it built for the first field it analysed on the thread, so a word that is common in one field is removed from queries on another field (MultiFieldQueryParser parses 'boring' to an empty query instead of variedField:boring), and in the other order a field's own stop words stay in.

bugs.area: analysis-smartcn / language analyzers (SmartChineseAnalyzer normalization: Analyzer#normalize vs the width and case folding inside HMMChineseTokenizer's SegTokenFilter, used by the query parsers for multi-term queries)
bugs.title: SmartChineseAnalyzer.normalize only lower-cases, but indexing folds full-width Latin letters and digits to half-width (in the tokenizer's SegTokenFilter), so full-width prefix, wildcard, regexp, range and fuzzy terms from the query parsers miss documents that the same word as a term query finds
bugs.summary: You index the text '我们使用Ｌｕｃｅｎｅ' (or '我们使用Lucene') with the stock SmartChineseAnalyzer and search with the classic QueryParser: the term query 'Ｌｕｃｅｎｅ' and the half-width prefix 'Luc*' find the document, so you expect the full-width prefix 'Ｌｕｃ*' to find it too. Instead it finds 0 documents, with no error: the tokenizer's SegTokenFilter folds full-width Latin letters and digits to half-width and lower-cases A-Z, so the index holds 'lucen', but SmartChineseAnalyzer.normalize, which the query parsers apply to prefix, wildcard, regexp, range and fuzzy terms, is only a LowerCaseFilter, so the query term stays full-width ('ｌｕｃ*'). Likewise Analyzer.normalize returns 'ａｂｃ' for 'ＡＢＣ' and '１２３' for '１２３' (the index holds 'abc' and '123') and 'é' for 'É' (the index keeps 'É').

bugs.title: HTMLStripCharFilter (since 10.5.0) treats a start tag whose name only begins with script, style or br (<scripts>, <style-guide>, <stylesheet>, <brand>) as a script, style or br tag, so it silently drops all text after it up to the next </script> or </style> (often to the end of the value) and misapplies escapedTags to such names
bugs.summary:
You strip '<scripts>hello</scripts> world' (or '<style-guide>hello</style-guide> world') with HTMLStripCharFilter and expect '
hello
 world', which is what Lucene 10.4.0 gives and what main gives for the same shape with any other name, such as '<scrapes>'. Since 10.5.0 the output is empty: the start-tag rules for script and style no longer require a delimiter after the name, so the longer name is taken for a <script> or <style> tag and everything up to the next literal </script> or </style>, here the end of the input, is dropped (for '<stylesheet>hello</stylesheet> world' a StandardTokenizer after the filter emits no token at all). With escapedTags={brand}, '<brand>Acme</brand>' likewise comes out as '
Acme</brand>' instead of unchanged.

bugs.area: analysis-common / wikipedia: WikipediaTokenizer (JFlex grammar lexical states, WikipediaTokenizerImpl.jflex)
bugs.title: WikipediaTokenizer silently drops Chinese and Japanese text inside wiki markup (links, categories, headings, bold/italics, templates, citations, external-link labels): its grammar has a CJ token rule only for plain text, and every markup state matches ALPHANUM only
bugs.summary: You tokenize Chinese or Japanese wiki text with WikipediaTokenizer, for example '[[日本]]', '[[Category:日本]]', '== 日本 ==' or "x '''東京''' y", and expect the text inside the markup to become tokens, as it does for Latin and Korean text in the same markup ('[[Japan]]', '[[한국]]') and for Chinese/Japanese plain text ('日本' gives 日|<CJ> and 本|<CJ>). Instead every Chinese/Japanese character inside markup is skipped without an error: '[[日本]]', '[[Category:日本]]', '== 日本 ==' and '<ref>日本</ref>' give no token at all, '[http://example.org 日本]' gives only the URL, and "x '''東京''' y" gives x and y, with y typed bold. The cause is the grammar: its only CJ token rule is for plain text (WikipediaTokenizerImpl.jflex:201), while all nine markup lexical states have a token rule for ALPHANUM only and ignore every other character (:219-309), and the CJ character class is disjoint from ALPHANUM.

bugs.area: analysis-common / wikipedia: WikipediaTokenizer (JFlex grammar character classes, WikipediaTokenizerImpl.jflex LETTER/DIGIT macros)
bugs.title: WikipediaTokenizer silently drops letters and digits from plain text that Unicode 3.0 already had (µ in '5 µm', ª/º in '1ª'/'2º', fullwidth digits and letters, ligatures such as ﬁ, Yi syllables, Arabic presentation forms; 2,083 BMP code points that ClassicTokenizer keeps) because its LETTER and DIGIT macros are hard-coded 2008 range lists
bugs.summary: You tokenize ordinary plain text with WikipediaTokenizer, for example '5 µm', '1ª edición 2º piso', '２０２６ year', 'ﬁle' or the Yi text 'ꀀꀁ', and expect every letter and digit to end up in a token, as it does with ClassicTokenizer (whose grammar is also pinned to Unicode 3.0) and StandardTokenizer. Instead WikipediaTokenizer skips these characters without an error: '5 µm' gives [5, m], '1ª 2º' gives [1, 2], 'ﬁle' gives [le], and '２０２６', 'ＡＢＣ' and 'ꀀꀁ' give no token; an exhaustive check of the BMP finds 2,083 letters and digits that ClassicTokenizer keeps and WikipediaTokenizer drops. The cause is the grammar: ALPHANUM is built from LETTER and DIGIT macros that are fixed range lists copied in 2008 (WikipediaTokenizerImpl.jflex:154,:156), which miss U+00AA, U+00B5, U+00BA and every letter or digit from U+2000 up to the halfwidth forms outside the CJ and Korean ranges, so these characters fall into the '[^]' ignore rule (:216); StandardTokenizer had the same lists and replaced them with [:letter:]/[:digit:] in 2.4 (LUCENE-1126), but the WikipediaTokenizer copy was never updated.

Instead it gets [the, quick, foxes, jumped]: the sink replays each token with restoreState but never calls clearAttributes, and the KeywordAttribute that only the sink's chain added is not in the tee's captured states, so once 'quick' is marked as a keyword every later token stays marked and is not stemmed. Nothing is thrown; a query for stemmed:fox finds nothing.

bugs.area: analysis / nori UserDictionary (right context id of user nouns, used by the Viterbi connection costs)
bugs.title: Nori UserDictionary picks a user noun's right context id (last syllable with a final consonant, without one, or not Hangul) from the last character of the whole entry line instead of the noun, so a trailing space or an inline comment ('학교 # memo') changes how the word after the noun is analysed
bugs.summary: You load a nori user dictionary whose line for the noun 학교 ('school') ends with a space, or carries an inline comment as in '학교 # memo' (the parser deletes '#' to the end of the line but keeps the space before it), and expect the same analysis as with the plain line '학교', because the parser splits the line on whitespace and gets the same noun with no segmentation. Instead UserDictionary.java:94 takes the noun's right context id, which tells the tokenizer whether the noun's last syllable ends in a consonant, from the last character of the whole line, here the space, so the noun gets the generic id and the word after it is analysed differently: on 9.12.3 '학교이' gives 이/VCP with '학교' but 이/J with '학교 ', and KoreanAnalyzer turns '학교가방을 샀다' into [학교][가방][사] with '학교' but [학교][방][사] with '학교 ', losing the term 가방 ('bag'). The two line forms disagree in every release from 7.4.0 to 10.5.2 and on main (main: '학교이' gives 이/JKS vs 이/VCP, '사람이나' gives [사람] vs [사람][이]), and a shorter segmentation such as '세종시 세종' takes the id from 종 (final consonant) instead of 시 (none) in the same way.

bugs.title: Kuromoji UserDictionary loads entries whose whitespace makes the stored segment lengths disagree with the surface form (a half-width space inside the surface, a tab between segments, a space after a comma), so JapaneseTokenizer later emits a term that starts with a space and drops the entry's last character, throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, or emits an empty token
bugs.summary: You add the entry 'ソニー ミュージック,ソニー ミュージック,ソニー ミュージック,カスタム名詞' (a name written with a half-width space) to a Kuromoji user dictionary and expect it either to be rejected when the dictionary loads, as LUCENE-8933 promises for segmentations that do not match the surface form ('This change avoids unexpected runtime exceptions or behaviours', MIGRATE.md), or to give tokens that cover ソニー ミュージック. Instead it loads, and JapaneseTokenizer emits ソニー[0,3) and ' ミュージッ'[3,9): one term starts with a space and the final ク is in no token, because the load-time check compares the two columns with all whitespace removed, while the stored segment lengths come from splitting the segmentation on ' ' only and the dictionary key keeps its whitespace. Two related entry shapes also load: a tab between segments (日本<TAB>経済 新聞) makes incrementToken throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException 'arraycopy: last source index 7 out of bounds for char[6]', the exact LUCENE-8933 symptom, and a space after each comma gives an empty token [0,0) (an AssertionError with -ea).

bugs.area: analysis-common / compound (HyphenationTree, HyphenationCompoundWordTokenFilter)
bugs.title: HyphenationTree.hyphenate does not shift its added start and end points past leading characters that are in none of the grammar's character classes, so HyphenationCompoundWordTokenFilter misses the subwords of tokens such as 3zimmerwohnung or "zimmerwohnung (the same word with a trailing quote decomposes)
bugs.summary: You index text through HyphenationCompoundWordTokenFilter with a hyphenation grammar and the dictionary {zimmer, wohnung}, and expect '3zimmerwohnung' (one StandardTokenizer token) or '"zimmerwohnung' (WhitespaceTokenizer) to add the subwords zimmer and wohnung, as 'zimmerwohnung' and 'zimmerwohnung"' (trailing quote) do. Instead no subword is added: HyphenationTree.hyphenate skips the leading characters that are in no character class and shifts its inner hyphenation points past them, but it adds the start and end points unshifted (0 and the letter count), so '3zimmerwohnung' gets [0, 7, 13] instead of [1, 7, 14] and every candidate slice either starts on the '3' or loses the final letter. With two or more such characters the points are not even ascending ('!!abcde' gives [0, 6, 5]), and nothing throws.

bugs.area: analysis-common / compound hyphenation (TernaryTree insert and compact via HyphenationTree.loadPatterns and HyphenationCompoundWordTokenFilter)
bugs.title: Hyphenation grammars whose TernaryTree key array grows past 65,535 chars load without error but silently lose or corrupt patterns, because TernaryTree stores key-array offsets in 16-bit chars (the Norwegian OFFO grammars the Lucene docs point to: nb/nn 1,158 of 27,448 patterns wrong, 1.2 no.xml 309 of 26,017)
bugs.summary: You load a well-formed FOP-format hyphenation grammar with HyphenationCompoundWordTokenFilter.getHyphenationTree (or HyphenationTree.loadPatterns, or the factory's hyphenator file) and expect findPattern to return every pattern's values afterwards, or an exception if the grammar does not fit. For a grammar whose stored key tails pass 65,535 chars, such as the Norwegian nb.xml from the OFFO download the Lucene docs link to (27,448 patterns, 52,404 nodes), loading succeeds but 1,158 patterns return wrong values (1,111 are not found at all), and with the OFFO 1.2 Norwegian grammar real words such as 'forfatter' are hyphenated and decompounded differently. The cause: TernaryTree keeps the offset of each key tail in its key array in a 16-bit char (lo[p] = (char) kv.alloc(len + 1), TernaryTree.java:151, and (char) k in compact at:408/:410) without a range check, so past 65,535 the offset wraps and the new tail is written over an earlier one; grammars past 65,535 nodes fail with StackOverflowError instead, the part that Apache FOP's open FOP-2569 already reports.

The commit added the compound/hyphenation package copied from Apache FOP (the class javadoc says so), with the char-typed pointers and the (char) casts of key-array offsets; the 33-comment LUCENE-1166 discussion does not mention the pointer width or any size limit. bugs.area: analysis / UAX29URLEmailTokenizer JFlex URL rules (path segments of http(s), scheme-less, ftp and file URLs; analysis-common)
bugs.title: UAX29URLEmailTokenizer ends a URL token at the first $ + ! * ' or, in the URL path, although both RFCs its grammar cites allow these characters there, so URLs such as https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) or http://example.com/a+b/c are split
bugs.summary: You run text such as 'see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) now' or 'http://example.com/a+b/c' through UAX29URLEmailTokenizer, whose javadoc says URLs are 'tokenized according to the relevant RFCs', and expect each URL as one <URL> token, because RFC 3986 (sub-delims are allowed in path segments) and RFC 1738 (its 'safe' and 'extra' characters are allowed in hsegment and fsegment) both allow $ + ! * ' and, in a path. Instead the <URL> token stops right before the first such character ('https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_', then 'programming_language' as a word; 'http://example.com/a', then 'b' and 'c'), because the grammar's two path-segment rules use RFC 3986's narrow 'unreserved' set inside rules shaped after RFC 1738, so these characters are rejected under either RFC. The same characters in the query, fragment or userinfo stay inside the URL token, and nothing reports an error.

bugs.area: analysis / pattern tokenizers (analysis-common: SimplePatternTokenizer, SimplePatternSplitTokenizer and their simplePattern / simplePatternSplit factories)
bugs.title: SimplePatternTokenizer and SimplePatternSplitTokenizer stop scanning when a non-matching lookahead reaches the end of the input, so later tokens are dropped (or later separators ignored)
bugs.summary: You tokenize 'say "hello world' with SimplePatternTokenizer and the pattern "[^"]*"|[a-z]+ (a quoted string or a word) and expect [say, hello, world], because the javadoc says the longest match at each start point is the next token and the class otherwise skips one character and tries again (PatternTokenizer with the same regex gives these three tokens). Instead you get only [say]: the lookahead from the unclosed quote runs to the end of the input without ever matching, and that end-of-input branch ends tokenization instead of retrying at the next character, so 'hello' and 'world' are never indexed (minimal case: abc|b on 'ab' gives instead of [b]). SimplePatternSplitTokenizer has the same branch and emits the whole rest as one token: separator <[^>]*>|+ on 'x < y' gives [x, '< y'] instead of String.split's [x, <, y]; nothing throws.

bugs.area: analysis / icu (ICUFoldingFilter UTR#30 folding data: the hand-written 'Rule: verbatim' Cyrillic block of DiacriticFolding.txt, compiled into utr30.nrm)
bugs.title: ICUFoldingFilter folds the Tajik/Abkhaz letter CHE WITH DESCENDER (ҷ U+04B7, Ҷ U+04B6) to the different letter ABKHASIAN CHE (ҽ U+04BD) instead of to CHE (ч U+0447), so Tajik text is not found by the same words typed with plain ч
bugs.summary: You index Tajik text such as 'Ҷумҳурии Тоҷикистон' with ICUFoldingFilter, whose javadoc lists 'Diacritic removal (including stroke, hook, descender)', and expect the same words typed without the Tajik letters, 'Чумхурии Точикистон', to find it, as they do for ҳ, қ and the other WITH DESCENDER letters. Instead the hand-copied line '04B7>04BC' in DiacriticFolding.txt maps CHE WITH DESCENDER to ABKHASIAN CHE, so ҷ and Ҷ are indexed as ҽ while the query's ч stays ч, and the query gets 0 hits. In Abkhaz, which uses ҷ, ҽ and ҿ as three separate letters, all three fold to ҽ and match each other.

bugs.summary: You tokenize the Korean word U+D55C U+AD6D U+C5B4 ('Korean language') with the default ICUTokenizer, once as is, once with an invisible soft hyphen (U+00AD) after its second syllable and once with a combining mark after each syllable, and expect the word to be indexed every time, because ICUTokenizer 'Breaks text into words according to UAX #29' (ICUTokenizer.java:31), whose rule WB4 attaches Extend and Format characters to the preceding letter, and StandardTokenizer indeed keeps U+D55C U+AD6D U+00AD U+C5B4 as one <HANGUL> token. bugs.title: SharedTermsUniformSplit merges silently drop the postings of fields that a source segment stored under another postings format or another shared-terms group (after a per-field postings mapping change, or addIndexes from an index with another mapping), because STUniformSplitTermsWriter.merge reads only the shared-terms block of the first field with terms in each source segment

bugs.area: core / codecs: term vectors (TermVectorsWriter.addAllDocVectors merge copier; Lucene90 compressing term-vector writer and reader), reached through IndexWriter.addIndexes(CodecReader)
bugs.title: addIndexes(CodecReader) from a reader whose term vectors list a field with zero terms writes a term-vector chunk that the default codec cannot read back, and every later merge that re-encodes the segment closes the IndexWriter
bugs.summary: You copy an index with IndexWriter.addIndexes(CodecReader...) through a reader that removes some terms consistently from the postings and the term vectors (CheckIndex at its strictest level accepts this reader), so one document's term-vector field is left with zero terms. You expect the new segment to read back and merge like any other, as the postings do (the postings writer simply drops the emptied field). Instead the default term-vector format writes per-field AvgCharsPerTerm floats that its own reader does not expect, so when the emptied field stores offsets the other documents of the chunk throw 'offset 0 is invalid' on read, and because the reader lists the emptied field but returns null for it, the next merge that re-encodes the segment fails with 'Wrong number of values added' and closes the IndexWriter, on every retry.

bugs.area: misc / BP merge-time reordering (BPIndexReorderer with document blocks)
bugs.title: BPIndexReorderer assumes every segment ends with a parent document: once a segment ends with child documents that have no parent after them, each BP reordering merge in which that segment comes last throws and closes the IndexWriter
bugs.summary: You index document blocks with IndexWriterConfig#setParentField, merge through BPReorderingMergePolicy with a BPIndexReorderer, and a segment ends up ending with child documents that have no parent after them, for example because you deleted or updated only the parent of its last block and a merge dropped it, or because IndexWriter rejected a block at one of its children (with the documented IllegalArgumentException) just before a flush. You expect later merges to work: IndexWriter accepted every call, CheckIndex calls the index clean and a plain merge of the same segment succeeds. Instead BPIndexReorderer, which assumes the merged view ends with a parent, runs past the end of its arrays in the next reordering merge in which that segment comes last (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException with assertions off, AssertionError with them on), and IndexWriter closes with a tragic exception, loses uncommitted changes and fails the same way after every reopen.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter document blocks (parent field) and merges
bugs.title: A document block rejected at a child can be flushed as a fully deleted segment without the parent field; if the merge policy keeps it (SoftDeletesRetentionMergePolicy can), merges that combine it only with segments without multi-document blocks throw 'expected parent doc field... across all segments' and close IndexWriter, again after every reopen
bugs.summary: You set IndexWriterConfig#setParentField (no index sort) and a merge policy that keeps fully deleted segments, such as SoftDeletesRetentionMergePolicy, and IndexWriter rejects a document block at a child with a documented non-aborting exception (for example a term longer than MAX_TERM_LENGTH) while that block is the only content of its in-memory segment, for example the first thing indexed after a commit. You expect the rejection to leave a consistent index that keeps merging, as the addDocument javadoc promises ('if an Exception is hit... the index will be consistent'). bugs.title: IndexUpgrader's command line and default constructors use a bare IndexWriterConfig, so upgrading a sorted index silently and permanently removes its index sort (the application's sorted IndexWriter then refuses to open the index), and an index with a parent field or a soft-deletes field cannot be upgraded at all

bugs.area: suggest / document suggester (CompletionFieldsConsumer type check at flush and merge; core flush and merge abort paths)
bugs.title: Mixing SuggestField and ContextSuggestField under one field name is accepted by addDocument and rejected only when the completion postings are written at flush or merge, where the IllegalArgumentException is tragic: the IndexWriter closes and loses every uncommitted document, and two cleanly committed segments of the two types make every merge that combines them close the writer again, also in a new writer (released since 5.3.0)
bugs.summary: You index a SuggestField document and a ContextSuggestField document under the same field name; addDocument accepts both, and the suggest module's design (LUCENE-6459) says such a mix is rejected with an IllegalArgumentException, so you expect an input error that leaves the writer and your other documents alone. Instead the type is compared only in CompletionFieldsConsumer while postings are written, so the IllegalArgumentException 'single field name has mixed types' fires inside flush or merge, where IndexWriter treats every exception as tragic: the writer closes and drops every uncommitted document. If the two types landed in different segments, both commit cleanly, but every merge that combines them closes the writer, also in any new writer, until you delete all documents of one type.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter doc-values updates with index sorting (BinarySortField, custom IndexSorter)
bugs.title: IndexWriter accepts doc-values updates of a field that a custom index-sort key reads (such as a BinarySortField subclass that derives its key from another doc-values field), so the segment keeps its old order while still declaring the index sort: CheckIndex rejects it, sorted searches that terminate early return wrong top hits, and merges carry the disorder forward
bugs.summary: You configure an index sort with a BinarySortField subclass whose key is derived from another doc-values field (sort by the numeric field price, ties broken by the binary field sku, declared on sku), index a(5), b(7), c(8), and then change c's price to 1 with updateNumericDocValue; you expect the writer either to reject the update, as it rejects an update of sku itself ('cannot update docvalues field involved in the index sort'), or to keep the segment sorted. Instead the update is accepted, the segment stays in the order a, b, c while still declaring the sort, CheckIndex reports 'segment has indexSort=<binary: "sku"> but docID=1 sorts after docID=2', and a top-1 search sorted by the index sort returns a instead of c because it stops at the first non-competitive document. The cause is that IndexWriterConfig#setIndexSort protects only the SortField#getField names, while a custom index sort may read any field.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter merge soft-delete accounting (mergeMiddle carry-over of soft deletes x OneMerge#wrapForMerge, OneMergeWrappingMergePolicy, SoftDeletesRetentionMergePolicy)
bugs.title: With a soft-deletes field configured, IndexWriter's merge assumes OneMerge#wrapForMerge only revives documents: for each merged segment without hard deletes, every live document that a merge wrapper hides (which the javadoc allows) lowers the new segment's soft-delete count by one, so the merge throws 'invalid softDelCount=-1' when nothing is revived, and under SoftDeletesRetentionMergePolicy commits a too-low count (numDocs and IndexSearcher#count over-count, CheckIndex rejects it, later merges of it throw); regression since 7.7.0 (LUCENE-8569)
bugs.summary: You set IndexWriterConfig#setSoftDeletesField and a merge policy whose OneMerge#wrapForMerge hides expired documents (its javadoc says a wrapper may 'add/remove fields or documents'), index two segments without hard deletes, and call forceMerge(1); you expect the merge to drop the expired document and succeed, as the same merge does without a soft-deletes field, or with one when the segment happens to hold a hard delete. Instead IndexWriter derives the carried-over soft deletes as getSoftDelCount - wrappedReader.numDeletedDocs, which counts each hidden live document as a dropped soft delete, so the count comes out -1 and the merge throws IllegalArgumentException 'invalid softDelCount=-1 (maxDoc=2)'. With SoftDeletesRetentionMergePolicy on top (one retained soft-deleted document) the merge silently commits softDelCount=0, so numDocs and IndexSearcher#count report 3 where 2 documents are live, CheckIndex reports 'actual soft deletes: 1 but expected: 0', and after the retention window the next merge of that segment throws 'invalid softDelCount=-1 (maxDoc=3)'.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter addIndexes(CodecReader...) accounting (reserveDocs, addIndexesReaderMerge soft-delete count) x MergePolicy#findMerges(CodecReader...) / OneMerge#wrapForMerge
bugs.title: addIndexes(CodecReader...) takes the reserved document count and the new segment's soft-delete count from the readers before OneMerge#wrapForMerge, so a merge whose wrapper removes documents over-reserves documents and, with soft deletes, commits a wrong soft-delete count that can drop live documents or corrupt a later merge (since 9.9.0)
bugs.summary: You install a merge policy whose findMerges(CodecReader...) returns a OneMerge whose wrapForMerge removes documents (its javadoc allows this: 'add/remove fields or documents'), for example to drop soft-deleted or expired documents while importing, and call IndexWriter.addIndexes(CodecReader...); you expect the writer to account for the documents the merge actually wrote, as the regular merge path does. Instead addIndexes reserves the live-document count of the unwrapped readers, so getPendingNumDocs stays too high for the rest of the writer session, and with soft deletes it stores the unwrapped readers' soft-delete count in the new segment, so DocStats.numDocs under-counts and CheckIndex (level 2 and up) reports 'actual soft deletes: 0 but expected: 1'. With assertions off, later operations then build on that wrong count: a live document can vanish from the committed index, and a later ordinary forceMerge can merge two documents into one doc ID (a search for one returns the other) or fail with CorruptIndexException.

bugs.area: search / CachingCollector first-pass caching (CachingCollector, CachingCollectorManager)
bugs.title: CachingCollector and CachingCollectorManager report isCached true (no overflow) but hold only the hits their wrapped first-pass collector let through (TOP_SCORES pruning, early leaf termination, skipped leaves), so replay silently feeds the second pass fewer matches than re-running the query
bugs.summary: You run a query once through a CachingCollector or CachingCollectorManager that wraps a first-pass collector, see isCached return true (the cache did not overflow), and replay the cached hits into a second collector, expecting the same result as running that collector on the query, which is what the javadocs and the grouping docs offer ('without re-running the query', 'hold all hits'). Instead the cache holds only the hits the first-pass collector let through: TopScoreDocCollectorManager(10, 1000), the IndexSearcher#search(Query, int) default, prunes non-competitive hits (even when the score-caching variant tells the searcher it needs COMPLETE), an index-order TopFieldCollector stops each segment early, and TotalHitCountCollector skips whole segments it can count from index statistics. In the repro, replaying into a hit counter sees 1001, 2 and 0 of 5000 matching documents, with no error.

bugs.area: facet / sampling (RandomSamplingFacetsCollector.createManager reduce, FacetsCollectorManager.reduceMatchingDocs)
bugs.title: RandomSamplingFacetsCollector.createManager samples the hits twice when a search has more than one slice: the reduce reads each slice's already-sampled getMatchingDocs as its original hits, so the sample is far too small and every amortized facet count is biased low (regression from #13542, 10.0.0 onward)
bugs.summary: You count facets on a sample of a large result set with RandomSamplingFacetsCollector.createManager(sampleSize, seed) on an IndexSearcher that has an executor, and expect what a one-slice search gives: about sampleSize sampled hits, taken at the rate sampleSize / totalHits that getSamplingRate reports, so that amortizeFacetCounts estimates the real counts. Instead, with two or more slices the reduce fills the reduced collector's original hits from FacetsCollectorManager.reduceMatchingDocs, which calls each slice collector's getMatchingDocs, the accessor RandomSamplingFacetsCollector overrides to return that slice's sample; the reduced collector then samples those samples again. The sample shrinks to about sampleSize^2 x numSlices / totalHits and every amortized count is low by the per-slice ratio, with no error: 2 segments of 1,024 matching docs with sampleSize 128 and one slice per segment give 16 sampled hits and an amortized count of 256 instead of 128 and 2,048, and default slicing on 2 segments of 262,144 docs with sampleSize 4,096 gives 64 sampled hits and 8,192 instead of 4,096 and 524,288.

bugs.area: facet / range facet counts (LongRangeCounter multi-valued path, exclusive and overlapping counters)
bugs.title: Multi-valued range facet counts drop matches when a document's values do not arrive in ascending order (custom MultiLongValuesSource/MultiDoubleValuesSource, or raw-bit doubles with two or more negative values): LongRangeCounter.addMultiValued assumes sorted values
bugs.summary: You compute range facet counts over a multi-valued source, for example the distances from the user to each of a document's locations computed by your own MultiDoubleValuesSource, or doubles stored as raw bits in a SortedNumeric field and read with fromDoubleField or the DoubleRangeFacetCounts(String,...) constructor. You expect each range to count every document that has at least one value in it, which is exactly what the range's own drill-down query finds. Instead, when a document's values arrive in descending order (a custom source in its natural order, or raw-bit doubles whenever the document has two or more negative values), the counter skips every later value that sorts below an interval it already counted for that document, so a document with distances {3.0, 0.5} is missing from '< 1 km' and '< 2 km'.

bugs.area: facet / sampling (RandomSamplingFacetsCollector: sampling rate vs bin size in amortizeFacetCounts and getSamplingRate)
bugs.title: RandomSamplingFacetsCollector samples one hit per (int) (1 / samplingRate) hits but amortizes by the untruncated samplingRate, so amortized facet counts are up to 2x too high (1999 hits with sampleSize 1000: every hit is sampled, yet every count is doubled)
bugs.summary: You sample facet counts with RandomSamplingFacetsCollector and sampleSize 1000 on a query with 1999 hits, call amortizeFacetCounts to scale the sampled counts back up, and expect estimates of the true counts; here the sample happens to contain every hit, so the right answer is the exact counts 667/666/666. Instead you get 1333/1331/1331 and a dimension total of 3996 for 1999 hits, with no error: the collector computes samplingRate = 1000 / 1999 = 0.50025 but samples one hit per bin of (int) (1 / samplingRate) = 1 hit, and it amortizes, and reports through getSamplingRate, with the untruncated rate. In general the counts are too high by totalHits / (sampleSize * binSize), between 1 and 2, worst just below twice the sample size.

bugs.area: facet / taxonomy association facets (TaxonomyFacetFloatAssociations value-source path, FloatTaxonomyFacets#updateValueFromRollup count roll-up)
bugs.title: TaxonomyFacetFloatAssociations with a DoubleValuesSource reports a too-high LabelAndValue.count for every label that has matching documents below it in a hierarchical dimension, because FloatTaxonomyFacets rolls the counts up again at every ancestor level (values are right; every release since 9.11.0)
bugs.summary: You index documents with a FacetField in a dimension declared hierarchical (FacetsConfig.setHierarchical("d", true)), for example d/a/x with weight 7 and d/a/y with weight 2, and sum a per-document DoubleValuesSource per label with TaxonomyFacetFloatAssociations; you expect label a under d to report value 9 and count 2, the 'Number of occurrences for this label' that FastTaxonomyFacetCounts reports for the same hits. Instead getTopChildren and getAllChildren report a (9.0) with count 4, because FloatTaxonomyFacets#updateValueFromRollup first calls super.updateValueFromRollup, which rolls up the counts of the whole sub-tree, and then its own rollup(childOrdinal), which calls updateValueFromRollup again for every descendant, so the sub-tree counts are added once more at each ancestor level. Values and leaf counts are right; only LabelAndValue.count of labels with descendants is inflated, and the deeper the tree, the larger the overcount.

bugs.area: grouping / GroupSelector score needs (FirstPass, SecondPass/TopGroups, AllGroups, AllGroupHeads collector score modes)
bugs.title: Grouping collectors never ask for scores on behalf of their group selector, so DoubleRangeGroupSelector or LongRangeGroupSelector over a score-dependent source (e.g. DoubleValuesSource.SCORES) groups every hit by the placeholder score of a non-scoring search (0 in every repro) when no sort or reducer needs scores, or when AllGroups/AllGroupHeads runs alone (since 8.6.0)
bugs.summary: You group hits into score ranges, for example with new DoubleRangeGroupSelector(DoubleValuesSource.SCORES, new DoubleRangeFactory(0, 1, 10)), and sort the groups by a field, expecting each hit in the range of its own score, which is what the same search returns with the default relevance group sort (three ranges, [1,2) = {0, 3}, [2,3) = {1}, [3,4) = {2, 4}, in the repro). Instead GroupingSearch returns one empty group [0,1) (LongRangeGroupSelector: LongRange(0, 1)), and AllGroupsCollectorManager on its own reports one range instead of three, because the grouping collectors take their ScoreMode only from their sorts or reducer, so the query runs without scores and the selector, which reads the collector's Scorable through DoubleValuesSource.fromScorer, sees the placeholder score 0 for every hit. GroupSelector has no way to say that it needs scores; a GroupSelector#needsScores hook (true for the range selectors when their source needs scores), ORed into the four collectors' score modes, fixes it.

bugs.title: SortedSetDocValues faceting builds its facet tree from the byte order of the encoded paths, so a label or dimension name that equals a sibling's name followed by a character below U+001F (TAB, CR, LF, or the U+001E that FacetsConfig writes when it escapes U+001E/U+001F) moves a label's children under that sibling, or drops a whole dimension or one of its labels

Instead it returns null and the leaf 'shoes<TAB>' reports red=1: the encoded paths sort by byte, a character below the path delimiter U+001F places 'shoes<TAB>' between 'shoes' and 'shoes U+001F red', and the reader state infers parent, child and sibling links only from the order of consecutive ordinals. The same happens for a label that contains U+001F or U+001E (FacetsConfig escapes both with U+001E), and dimension names such as 'd' next to 'd<TAB>' make dimension d disappear or, for a flat multiValued + requireDimCount dimension, lose one label, all with no error.

bugs.title: DirectoryTaxonomyWriter indexes a facet label that contains an unpaired surrogate a second time, under a new ordinal, once its writer cache has been filled from the taxonomy index, because the cache compares the label's Java string while the index stores its UTF-8 term with the surrogate replaced by U+FFFD; the taxonomy then holds two categories with one path and facet counts for that value are split
bugs.summary: You add a facet value with an unpaired surrogate, for example FacetField("dim", "x\uD83D") built from a string cut inside an emoji, in one writer session and the same value again in a later session, with the default DirectoryTaxonomyWriter; you expect the existing ordinal back, as TaxonomyWriter.addCategory promises, and one facet entry with count 2. Instead, once the second session has filled its cache from the index (after 11 new categories by default), the cached key is the stored form "x\uFFFD", the original string misses, the writer trusts its now complete cache and indexes the label again (ordinal 14 instead of 2), so the facet result shows x\uFFFD (1) twice. The duplicate stays in the taxonomy for good; within one fresh session the writer likewise gives "x\uD83D" and "x\uFFFD" ordinals 2 and 3, although the taxonomy reader resolves both to 2.

bugs.title: Taxonomy Facets#getTopDims returns another dimension's children, childCount and value under a multi-valued dimension's name, because replacing the bottom of the top-dims queue updates dim and value but not dimOrd (released since 9.2.0)

bugs.area: facet / sampling (RandomSamplingFacetsCollector.amortizeFacetCounts x FacetsConfig drill-down term indexing)
bugs.title: RandomSamplingFacetsCollector.amortizeFacetCounts caps each amortized label count at the docFreq of the label's drill-down term, so with a non-default FacetsConfig DrillDownTermsIndexing (NONE on any dimension, or FULL_PATH_ONLY / DIMENSION_AND_FULL_PATH on a hierarchical dimension) it silently returns 0, or a value below the true count
bugs.summary: You sample facet counts with RandomSamplingFacetsCollector on a dimension whose FacetsConfig skips drill-down terms (DrillDownTermsIndexing NONE, or FULL_PATH_ONLY / DIMENSION_AND_FULL_PATH on a hierarchical dimension), call amortizeFacetCounts to scale the sampled counts up to estimates of the full counts, and expect what the default indexing gives: about sampled / samplingRate per label, capped by the label's real count. Instead each label is capped at reader.docFreq of its drill-down term, which these modes do not index at all (docFreq 0) or index only for the documents whose full path is that label, so a label seen 15 times in a 10% sample comes back as 0 and a label on 1000 documents comes back as 500. Nothing fails, and in the same FacetResult the amortized dimension total (for example 1000) no longer matches its children (all 0).

bugs.area: core / search collectors (PositiveScoresOnlyCollector; FilterCollector scoreMode and setWeight forwarding; TotalHitCountCollector Weight#count shortcut)
bugs.title: PositiveScoresOnlyCollector inherits its wrapped collector's scoreMode and setWeight, so a wrapped sort-by-field TopFieldCollector or TotalHitCountCollector silently gets the wrong hits or count instead of exactly the hits that score > 0 (score-mode leg since 5.1.0, count leg since 9.3.0)
bugs.summary: You wrap a collector in PositiveScoresOnlyCollector, whose javadoc says it 'makes sure only documents with scores > 0 are collected' and which Collector's overview says 'wraps any other Collector', and expect the wrapped collector to see exactly the matches that score > 0: in the repro 6 hits for the TermQuery g:y with a TopFieldCollector sorted by a field, and counts 0 for (f:x)^0 and 6 for (g:y)^2 OR (f:x)^0 with a TotalHitCountCollector. Instead the sort-by-field collector receives 0 hits and the counter reports 12 for both queries, because PositiveScoresOnlyCollector, which reads scorer.score itself, inherits two FilterCollector hooks: scoreMode reports the wrapped collector's no-score mode, so the search builds scorers without scores and the > 0 test reads placeholder values (0 for TermQuery, so real hits are dropped; a constant positive value for FunctionScoreQuery over MatchAllDocsQuery, so zero-score hits get through), and setWeight hands the wrapped TotalHitCountCollector the Weight, so it counts whole segments with Weight#count and never goes through the filter. Overriding scoreMode to return COMPLETE when the wrapped collector needs no scores, and passing on a Weight whose count returns -1 (or not forwarding setWeight at all), fixes both.

bugs.title: DoubleDocValuesStats and SortedDoubleDocValuesStats (lucene/misc) start max at Double.MIN_VALUE, the smallest positive double, so max returns 4.9E-324 instead of the real maximum whenever every collected value is <= 0 (and min returns Double.MAX_VALUE when every value is +Infinity)
bugs.summary: You collect statistics for a double doc-values field with DocValuesStats.DoubleDocValuesStats (or SortedDoubleDocValuesStats) and expect max to be the largest collected value; the javadoc calls it 'the maximum value of the field' and leaves it undefined only when count is zero. bugs.area: classification / k-NN classifiers and BooleanPerceptronClassifier (training query)
bugs.title: KNearestNeighborClassifier, KNearestFuzzyClassifier, KNearestNeighborDocumentClassifier and BooleanPerceptronClassifier add their documented training filter query (and the class-field restriction) as scoring Occur.MUST clauses, so a training query that filters out nothing changes the k-NN class scores and can flip the assigned class, the nearest neighbours or the learned perceptron model (released since 4.6.0)
bugs.summary: You index three labelled documents ('aa bb' as Y, 'aa' as X, 'aa' as X), build KNearestNeighborClassifier with k = 3 once with no training query and once with MatchAllDocsQuery (the parameter is documented as 'a Query to eventually filter the docs used for training the classifier', and this one removes nothing), and expect the same answer for 'aa bb bb'. Instead the answer flips from Y (class scores Y 0.333, X 0.309) to X (X 0.417, Y 0.333), because the training query and the class-field WildcardQuery are added as scoring Occur.MUST clauses, so their scores are added to every neighbour's MoreLikeThis score before each vote is weighted by score / maxScore; a training query whose score differs between documents, such as TermQuery(split:train) on a text field every document has, even replaces the nearest neighbour (k = 1: 'aa', class X, becomes 'aa bb', class Y). KNearestFuzzyClassifier and KNearestNeighborDocumentClassifier return different class scores in the same way, and BooleanPerceptronClassifier, which trains in the score order of the same kind of query, learns a different model ('aa' answers true instead of false).

bugs.area: classification / BooleanPerceptronClassifier (batched training)
bugs.title: BooleanPerceptronClassifier with batchSize > 1 can silently lose the weight updates of misclassified training documents: the weight FST is rebuilt only when a misclassified document sits at a multiple of batchSize and never after the last batch, and updates inside a batch are computed from the last FST build and overwrite each other, so the trained model is wrong (released since 5.0.0)
bugs.summary: You index two training documents labelled false, 'bb' and 'aa aa', train BooleanPerceptronClassifier with bias 1.5 and batchSize 2, and expect assignClass('aa aa') = false, which is what batchSize 1 gives on the same data and what both an online and a mini-batch perceptron give. Instead it returns true (score 0.81): the update for the misclassified 'aa aa' (batch position 1) is written only to the pending weight map, because the FST that holds the weights is rebuilt only when a misclassified document sits at a position that is a multiple of batchSize, and the constructor ends by clearing that map without a final rebuild. Updates inside a batch are also computed from the last FST build and overwrite each other, so with batchSize 10 and three training documents 'aa' labelled false only the first update is applied and the model still answers true.

The issue's only attachment, LUCENE-4818.patch (March 2013), had no batching: it read the pending weight from the map and rebuilt the FST after every update, so batching and the stale read arrived in the commit. It reached a release through the branch_5x creation backport 55594bad9b0 (LUCENE-5944, 2014-09-18). Instead the entry is used verbatim as the name of a field called 'text^2', which does not exist, so that field adds no terms to the query: with one text field assignClass returns null and getClasses an empty list, and with several fields the boosted one is silently ignored. The sibling KNearestNeighborClassifier, whose javadoc has the same sentence, parses the boost and classifies normally.

bugs.area: classification / SimpleNaiveBayesClassifier (training query; copies in SimpleNaiveBayesDocumentClassifier and CachingNaiveBayesClassifier)
bugs.title: SimpleNaiveBayesClassifier applies its documented training query only to the per-word counts: the class prior and the likelihood denominators are computed over the whole index, so labelled documents outside the training set can decide the class (released since 4.6.0; same pattern in SimpleNaiveBayesDocumentClassifier and CachingNaiveBayesClassifier)
bugs.summary: You index four training documents marked split:train (fruit: 'apple', 'pear', 'plum'; vehicle: 'car') and ten more vehicle documents marked split:other, build SimpleNaiveBayesClassifier with the training query split:train and classify 'apple', expecting what the same classifier trained on an index holding only the four training documents answers: fruit (0.811), with prior P(fruit) = 3/4. Instead it answers vehicle (P(fruit) = 0.445), and for an empty input, which only the prior decides, it gives P(fruit) = 3/14, the whole-index share. The query is ANDed only into the per-word counts (getWordFreqForClass); the prior (docFreq(class) / Terms.getDocCount) and the likelihood denominator (average unique terms per document x docFreq(class) + that document count) ignore it, because countDocsWithClass applies the query only in a getDocCount == -1 fallback that current codecs never take.

Present since the feature was created, not a regression: git log -L lists 8 later commits on calculateLogPrior/docCount and 10 on getTextTermFreqForClass (2012-2021), none of which applies the query. Related: 173daaedefe (LUCENE-5466, 2014) moved the query assignment in train so that the fallback count sees it.

bugs.area: classification / BooleanPerceptronClassifier (weights FST)
bugs.title: BooleanPerceptronClassifier adds its term weights to its FST in Java String (UTF-16) order instead of the UTF-8 byte order the FST requires, so a text field with a term starting with a supplementary character (such as an emoji) and a term starting with a character in U+E000..U+FFFF (such as a fullwidth letter) makes training throw AssertionError with -ea and, with -da, silently loses term weights (in some term layouts all of them) or throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (released since 5.0.0)
bugs.summary: You index two documents, 'P P P' labelled true and 'N' labelled false, where P is U+F900 (a CJK compatibility ideograph) and N is U+1D400 (mathematical bold capital A), train BooleanPerceptronClassifier with the default bias (the average term frequency, here 2), and expect assignClass(P) = (true, 0.393), which is what the same corpus gives with ASCII terms or with ordinary CJK ideographs. Instead the constructor throws AssertionError 'inputs are added out of order lastInput=[f0 9d 90 80] vs input=[ef a4 80]' with -ea, and with -da assignClass(P) returns (false, 0.632) because P's weight can no longer be found in the FST. The classifier keeps its weights in a ConcurrentSkipListMap<String, Double>, whose String order (UTF-16 code units) puts U+1D400 (D835 DC00) before U+F900, and adds their UTF-8 encodings in that order to an FSTCompiler that requires UTF-8 byte order (EF before F0) and checks it only with an assert.

bugs.area: classification / BM25NBClassifier (assignClass and getClasses)
bugs.title: BM25NBClassifier scores a class that has no live, training-query-matching document as if it had probability 1 (log prior 0 and log-likelihood 0), so with few classes it outranks the trained classes and is assigned although it has no training data (released since 7.0.0)
bugs.summary: You index four training documents labelled fruit ('apple banana', 'apple pear') or vehicle ('car truck', 'car bus') plus one document labelled heldout that your training query split:train excludes, build BM25NBClassifier with that query and classify 'apple', expecting fruit, which is what the classifier answers when the heldout document is absent. Instead assignClass returns heldout (getClasses: heldout 0.568, fruit 0.273, vehicle 0.159), and the same happens with no training query when every document of a label is deleted but its segment is not yet merged ('apple' -> gone 0.681). BM25NBClassifier makes every term of the class field a candidate class (MultiTerms.getTerms), and for a class with no live, query-matching document both of its searches find no hit, so calculateLogPrior falls back to 0 and getTermProbForClass to 1 (log 0): the class scores exactly 0, while each trained class sums log(top BM25 score) over the prior and every input token, which is negative whenever those scores are below 1.

bugs.area: classification / utils: DatasetSplitter (split, test/cv/training assignment loop)
bugs.title: DatasetSplitter puts at most about half of each class into the test index, whatever testRatio is
bugs.summary: You split an index with new DatasetSplitter(0.8, 0).split(...) to put 80% of the documents into the test index. You expect about 8 of every 10 documents of each class in the test index, as crossValidationRatio 0.8 gives 8 of 10 in the cross-validation index. Instead the test index gets only 5 of 10 and training gets the other 5, because the loop lets a document into the test index only when its running counter b is even (DatasetSplitter.java:153, 'if (b % 2 == 0 && tc < testSize)'), so at most every other document can be a test document, with no error.

bugs.area: spatial3d / Geo3DPoint shape queries (PointInShapeIntersectVisitor per-document test against GeoStandardCircle and other cap-shaped boundaries)
bugs.title: Geo3DPoint distance queries with a radius below about 1 km silently return wrong results in both directions: each document's decoded point lies a few millimetres off the planet surface and is tested against a circle plane nearly tangent to the surface, so a 10 m query misses documents at its own centre and matches documents about 100 m away
bugs.summary: You index locations as Geo3DPoint on the default WGS84 model and run Geo3DPoint.newDistanceQuery with a small radius, say 10 m, expecting the points within 10 m (the javadoc allows up to 0.5% error). Instead the query misses about half of the points inside the radius, even a document located exactly at the query centre, and returns points about 100 m away, while LatLonPoint gives the right answer on the same data. The cause is that each document's stored x/y/z is decoded to a point a few millimetres off the planet surface, and that point is tested against the circle's cutting plane, which for a small circle meets the surface at a grazing angle and turns millimetres into 100-190 m.
bugs.introduced_commit: 31b17203f2c (branch_5x, svn r1700887, first released in 5.4.0) and 03e5bcfa739 (trunk, svn r1700883, first released in 6.0.0), the same change: LUCENE-6699 'add geo3d + BKD for fast, accurate earth-surface point-in-shape queries' (apache/lucene#7757, companion LUCENE-6759 = #7817), committed by mikemccand on 2015-09-02, no GitHub pull request (SVN era). bugs.area: spatial3d / geom path membership (GeoStandardPath end caps; Geo3DPoint.newPathQuery, Geo3DDocValuesField.newPathSort)
bugs.title: On WGS84, geo3d path end caps are shifted toward the equator, so Geo3DPoint.newPathQuery and Geo3DDocValuesField.newPathSort miss documents just beyond a poleward path end (sort value +Infinity) and match documents tens of km beyond an equatorward end
bugs.summary: You run Geo3DPoint.newPathQuery (or Geo3DDocValuesField.newPathSort) on WGS84 with a north-south path, for example from (44N,20E) to (45N,20E), and expect it to match the points within pathWidthMeters of the path, with round end caps of that radius around the first and last points, as it does on PlanetModel.SPHERE. Instead both end caps are shifted about 21 km toward the equator: with pathWidthMeters 20000 the query misses documents 12 and 16 km beyond the north end (sort value +Infinity), and with pathWidthMeters 1000 it matches documents 10 to 40 km south of the first point (sort values 10006 to 40034 m). The end-cap plane (GeoStandardPath.CutoffSingleCircleSegmentEndpoint, built by CircleSegmentEndpoint through the two segment corners with its normal inside the origin-containing cutoff plane) points along the end point's geocentric direction, which on an ellipsoid is not the surface normal there, so the cap circle is centred equatorward of the end point.

bugs.area: spatial3d / Geo3DDocValuesField sort comparators (Geo3DPointDistanceComparator, Geo3DPointOutsideDistanceComparator; all seven Geo3D sort factories)
bugs.title: Geo3D distance sorts read a document's doc values twice in any segment where some document has two or more points, so top-N and searchAfter results come back in the wrong order with another document's distance as the sort value (even a filtered-out or deleted document's), or the search throws EOFException (every release since 7.0.0)
bugs.summary: You index documents with Geo3DDocValuesField, at least one of them with two or more points (the javadoc allows this and says the closest one is used), and ask for the top 2 hits sorted by Geo3DDocValuesField.newDistanceSort; you expect the head of the full sorted order, each hit carrying its own closest distance. Instead the top 2 come back in the wrong order and a hit reports the distance of the next document, because the comparator reads the document's values once in compareBottom (or compareTop) and again in copy without re-positioning the SortedNumericDocValues iterator, which its javadoc forbids ('Do not call this more than docValueCount times'), so the second read takes the following document's values or runs past the end of the data and throws EOFException. The same happens with searchAfter paging and all seven Geo3D sort factories, and because document order decides which value is read, a hit can report the distance of a document that a filter, a live-docs wrapper or a delete hides from the search.

bugs.area: spatial3d / Geo3D distance sort comparator (Geo3DPointDistanceComparator.compareBottom bounds shortcut; Geo3DDocValuesField.newDistanceSort and newPathSort)
bugs.title: Geo3D distance and path sorts (Geo3DDocValuesField.newDistanceSort, newPathSort) skip the secondary SortField for hits outside the shape's bounding box once the queue bottom is +Infinity, so top-N keeps the earliest out-of-radius documents in doc order instead of the first N of the sorted order (released since 6.1.0)
bugs.summary: You sort a query with Sort(Geo3DDocValuesField.newDistanceSort(field, lat, lon, maxRadiusMeters, planet), secondary SortField) and expect search(q, n, sort) to return the first n hits of the sorted order: every hit outside the radius reports distance +Infinity (like a document without the field), so the secondary field should order them. Instead, five documents at latitude 60 sorted around (0,0) with a 1,000 km radius and a secondary 'tie' key descending give top 2 = [1, 0] although the full order is [4, 3, 2, 1, 0] (WGS84; the same on SPHERE with a 0.2 planet-radius circle; with a sixth document missing the field, [5, 1] instead of [5, 4]), and newPathSort does the same. The cause: once the queue bottom is +Infinity, compareBottom rejects (-1) every later document whose points lie outside the shape's bounding box instead of reporting a tie (0), so the secondary SortField is never consulted.

bugs.area: queries / intervals (Intervals.before, OffsetIntervalsSource PRECEDING)
bugs.title: Intervals.before(source, reference) treats a source interval at position 0 as before a reference interval that also starts at position 0, so for example before(york, york) matches the one-word document 'york'
bugs.summary: You search with Intervals.before(source, reference), for example before(term new, phrase(new, york)) on the text 'new york', or before(term york, term york) on the one-word text 'york'. You expect no match, because the javadoc says before 'Returns intervals from the source that appear before intervals from the reference' and nothing comes before the first word. Instead both documents match: before is built from a helper that places a pseudo-interval one position before each reference match, and for a reference at position 0 the helper clamps that position to 0 instead of producing nothing, so a source at position 0 counts as 'before' it; prepend one unrelated word and the same text correctly stops matching.
