bugs.area: queries / intervals (Intervals.ordered and unorderedNoOverlaps with equal consecutive sub-sources: OrderedIntervalsSource.deduplicate, RepeatingIntervalsSource)
bugs.title: Intervals.ordered(X, X) with two equal sub-sources that span several positions lets the two copies of X overlap, so ordered(phrase(a, a), phrase(a, a)) matches 'a a' and ordered(unordered(a, b), unordered(a, b)) matches 'a b a' (one b), while the same query with an equivalent but unequal second source finds nothing

Instead, because the two arguments are equal, OrderedIntervalsSource.build merges them into a RepeatingIntervalsSource, which joins consecutive intervals of a single sub-iterator without checking that they are disjoint, so ordered(unordered(a, b), unordered(a, b)) matches 'a b a', which has only one b, and ordered(phrase(a, a), phrase(a, a)) matches 'a a'. bugs.area: queries / intervals (Intervals.ordered/unordered with equal sub-sources: RepeatingIntervalsSource, maxgaps)
bugs.title: RepeatingIntervalsSource's iterator computes width with the sign inverted (start - end + 1 per repeated sub-interval), so when Intervals.ordered/unordered repeat a sub-source wider than one position (for example the same phrase twice) gaps is over-reported, maxgaps drops real matches and Weight#matches disagrees with the scorer
bugs.summary: You search with an interval query that repeats a multi-word piece, for example maxgaps(0, ordered(phrase(new, york), phrase(new, york))) on the text 'new york new york', and expect a match because the two phrases sit back to back with no gap. Instead it finds nothing: Lucene turns equal sub-sources into a RepeatingIntervalsSource whose iterator adds start - end + 1 instead of end - start + 1 for each copy, so width is 0 instead of 4, gaps is 4 instead of 0, and maxgaps rejects the interval. The Matches path of the same class uses the right formula, so Weight#matches returns a match for the very document the scorer rejected; repeats of single words are unaffected because their start equals their end.

bugs.area: queries / intervals (RepeatingIntervalsSource.minExtent for ordered/unordered of equal sub-sources; Disjunctions rewrite under phrase/maxgaps)
bugs.title: Intervals.ordered(a, a) and Intervals.unordered(a, a) report minExtent 1, so the default disjunction rewrite under phrase/maxgaps leaves or(ordered(a, a), a) unsplit and phrase(x, or(ordered(a, a), a), c) misses 'x a c'

Instead it finds nothing: ordered(a, a) and unordered(a, a) are built as a RepeatingIntervalsSource whose minExtent returns the minExtent of a single 'a' (1) instead of 2, the rewrite assumes that only single-position sources report 1 and so keeps or(ordered(a, a), a) as one OR, and inside that OR the interval of 'a a' contains the interval of a single 'a' and is minimized away. bugs.area: queries / intervals (a whole ordered/unordered of equal sub-sources nested in another operator: RepeatingIntervalsSource width, Ordered/UnorderedIntervalsSource.deduplicate)
bugs.title: A nested Intervals.ordered(a, a) or unordered(a, a) passes its inner gap up to its parent, so maxgaps(0, ordered(ordered(a, a), a)) misses 'a x a a' while maxgaps(0, ordered(ordered(a, b), a)) matches 'a x b a'
bugs.summary: You nest a repeated pair inside another interval operator, for example ordered(ordered(a, a), a), and filter it with maxgaps(0,...): the IntervalIterator#gaps javadoc counts only the gaps between the parent's immediate sub-intervals, so 'a x a a' (sub-intervals [0,2] and [3,3]) should match, just as maxgaps(0, ordered(ordered(a, b), a)) matches 'a x b a'. Instead, because the two arguments of the inner ordered(a, a) are equal, Lucene builds it as a RepeatingIntervalsSource whose width is the sum of its two copies (2) rather than its span (3), so the parent counts the inner 'x' as its own gap (gaps 1) and maxgaps(0) silently drops the document. The same happens for ordered(unordered(a, a), b), unordered(ordered(a, a), b) and ordered(x, ordered(a, a)), while wrapping the inner pair in a no-op filter such as maxwidth(100,...) brings the hit back.

bugs.area: spatial-extras / spatial4j bridge to spatial3d (Geo3dShapeFactory line-string builder, Geo3dLineStringBuilder.build), reached through the public LineStringBuilder API, the deprecated lineString(List, double), multi-line builders and the Geo3d context's polyshape reader (and the GeoJSON reader when its optional parser is present)
bugs.title: Geo3dShapeFactory passes a line string's buffer distance to spatial3d's GeoPathFactory, which takes radians, without the degrees-to-radians conversion its circle applies, so in the Geo3d spatial context a line buffered by 1 degree is 1 radian (57.3 degrees) wide and buffers above about 1.57 throw
bugs.summary: You use the Geo3d spatial context, build a line from (0,0) to (10,0) with buffer(1), and expect a corridor reaching 1 degree from the line, because spatial4j distances are in the units of x and y (degrees in a geo context) and spatial4j's standard geo context and the same factory's 1-degree circle both say a point at (5, 20) is DISJOINT. Instead the line CONTAINS that point and its bounding box is about [-57.3, 67.3] x [-57.3, 57.3]: Geo3dLineStringBuilder.build hands the buffer straight to GeoPathFactory.makeGeoPath, whose width is an angle in radians, while the factory's circle and Geo3dRectangleShape.getBuffered convert degrees with DEGREES_TO_RADIANS. The same happens when the Geo3d context reads spatial4j's polyshape string for a 1-degree buffered line, and every buffer above about 1.5708 is rejected with 'Cutoff angle out of bounds', so a buffer of 2 degrees cannot be built at all.

bugs.area: spatial-extras / spatial4j bridge to spatial3d (Geo3dShape.relate(Rectangle) and its shared GeoArea-to-SpatialRelation mapping), reached through SpatialOperation IsWithin/Contains on SerializedDVStrategy and CompositeSpatialStrategy, RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy cell traversal over PackedQuadPrefixTree, and any spatial4j relate against ctx.getWorldBounds
bugs.title: Geo3dShape.relate(Rectangle) swaps WITHIN and CONTAINS when the rectangle is not a Geo3d shape (such as ctx.getWorldBounds or a PackedQuadPrefixTree cell), so IsWithin/Contains on stored shapes give the opposite answer and RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy over PackedQuadPrefixTree returns documents far outside the query shape (regression in 7.1.0)
bugs.summary: You use the Geo3d spatial context and relate a Geo3d shape to a spatial4j rectangle that the Geo3d shape factory did not build, for example a 10-degree circle against the context's own ctx.getWorldBounds, or run a SerializedDVStrategy IsWithin(ctx.getWorldBounds) query over that circle, and expect WITHIN (the circle lies inside the world) and one hit. Instead relate returns CONTAINS and the query matches nothing, while Contains(world bounds) matches the circle: Geo3dShape.relate(Rectangle) asks spatial3d how this shape relates to the rectangle but then applies the mapping written for the opposite question (how the other shape relates to this one), so the two nested answers come out swapped, whereas the same box built by the Geo3d factory relates correctly. Lucene builds such rectangles itself, so RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy over PackedQuadPrefixTree, whose cells are plain spatial4j rectangles, treats a cell that contains a small query circle as lying inside the circle and returns every document in that cell, for example a point at (100.3, 37.7) for a half-degree circle at (1, 1).

bugs.area: facet / range drill-down queries (LongRange and DoubleRange ValueSourceQuery and MultiValueSourceQuery) and the query cache
bugs.title: LongRange/DoubleRange#getQuery(fastMatchQuery, valueSource) reports its Weight as cacheable without asking the fast-match query, so after an in-place doc-values update the query cache keeps returning the old matches
bugs.summary: You build a range filter or drill-down with LongRange or DoubleRange#getQuery(fastMatchQuery, valueSource) whose fast-match query reads a doc-values field (for example NumericDocValuesField.newSlowExactQuery("inStock", 1)), run it through a query cache, then change that field for one document in place with IndexWriter#updateNumericDocValue and reopen the reader. You expect the reopened searcher to use the new value, because a query that depends on updated doc values must report itself not cacheable (SegmentCacheable), and the fast-match query alone does. bugs.area: search / phrase queries (SloppyPhraseMatcher Matches support: endPosition/endOffset read after advanceRpts)
bugs.title: For a sloppy PhraseQuery with a repeated term (for example "very very"~1), Weight#matches reports an end position and end offset past the match, at a later occurrence of the repeated term that repeat-collision resolution has already advanced to, so Matches-based highlighting (the default UnifiedHighlighter) marks too much text
bugs.summary: You run a sloppy phrase query that repeats a word, such as "very very"~1, on the text 'very very good very' and ask Weight#matches (or the default UnifiedHighlighter) where it matched; you expect positions 0-1, 'very very'. Lucene reports positions 0-3, 'very very good very', because after finding the match the sloppy matcher moves the second 'very' on to the later occurrence to resolve a collision between the two copies of the term, and endPosition/endOffset are read only afterwards, from that moved state. The reported span is not the window of any valid match (positions 0 and 3 are two moves apart, the slop is 1); the hit itself and its score are correct.

bugs.area: highlighter / original Highlighter, QueryScorer and WeightedSpanTermExtractor (MultiPhraseQuery-to-span conversion)
bugs.title: Classic Highlighter counts the unused positions before a MultiPhraseQuery's first position as gaps, so a phrase that starts at position 1 or later (a leading stop word plus a synonym) is highlighted with extra slop and non-matching pairs get marked
bugs.summary: You search for the quoted phrase "the dogs bark" with an analyzer that removes the stop word 'the' and adds the synonym dog for dogs (QueryParser and QueryBuilder build a MultiPhraseQuery [dogs|dog] at position 1, bark at position 2, slop 0), and highlight the text 'dogs often bark but my dogs bark' with Highlighter and QueryScorer, expecting 'dogs often bark but my dogs bark' (Weight#matches reports only positions 5-6, and the same query starting at position 0, or a PhraseQuery at positions 1 and 2, is highlighted that way). Instead you get 'dogs often bark but my dogs bark', with no error. WeightedSpanTermExtractor counts every empty slot from index 0 up to the last position as a position gap, including the unused slot 0 below the first position, so the phrase becomes an ordered SpanNearQuery with slop 1 instead of 0 (one extra unit per leading slot, also for sloppy phrases), while its PhraseQuery branch measures gaps from the first position.

bugs.title: FastVectorHighlighter drops a match at a position that holds stacked tokens (index-time synonyms, stems) when the token that sorts first there starts a query phrase that does not continue: FieldPhraseList tries only the first stacked token with any query-map entry, so dogs OR "dog house" on 'my dogs' (synonym dog stacked on dogs) highlights nothing (a LUCENE-5538 regression, 4.7.1 on)

bugs.area: join / block join Weight#matches (ParentsChildrenBlockJoinQuery; consumers BooleanWeight#matches, UnifiedHighlighter, Monitor HighlightsMatch)
bugs.title: ParentsChildrenBlockJoinQuery's Weight#matches ignores the join and returns Matches for documents the query does not match (parent documents, children of non-matching parents, children over childLimitPerParent), so as a MUST_NOT clause it strips the Matches and highlights of real hits, and Lucene Monitor's HighlightsMatch matcher reports the wrong documents

bugs.area: queries / span queries Matches API (SpanWeight#matches takes offsets and sub-matches from ContainSpans#collect for SpanWithinQuery; seen through the UnifiedHighlighter and MatchRegionRetriever)
bugs.title: SpanWithinQuery's Weight#matches reports the contained (little) span's positions but the enclosing (big) span's offsets and sub-matches, so Matches-based highlighting (the default UnifiedHighlighter, MatchRegionRetriever) marks the enclosing terms and a field with offsets highlights differently from the same text indexed with positions only
bugs.summary: You index 'ab ac bc' in a field with offsets and ask Weight#matches for SpanWithinQuery(big = SpanNear([ab, bc], slop 1, in order), little = ac); you expect one match, 'ac' at position 1 with offsets [3,5) and sub-matches only inside it, which is what the equivalent Intervals.containedBy(ac, ordered(ab, bc)) reports. Instead the match says positions [1,1] but offsets [0,8) and lists ab@0 and bc@2 as sub-matches, because the offsets and sub-matches come from Spans#collect, which for SpanWithinQuery also collects the enclosing span. So the default UnifiedHighlighter marks 'ab ac bc' instead of 'ab ac bc', and MatchRegionRetriever returns [0,8) on a field with offsets but [3,5) on the same text indexed with positions only; hits and scores are unaffected.

bugs.area: highlighter / original Highlighter, QueryScorer and WeightedSpanTermExtractor (phrase-to-span conversion)
bugs.title: Classic Highlighter turns the position holes of an exact PhraseQuery or MultiPhraseQuery (for example from removed stop words) into SpanNearQuery slop, so it highlights nearby pairs that do not match and can miss the occurrence that does
bugs.summary: You index 'rock roll rock and roll' with a stop-word analyzer, search for the phrase "rock and roll" (QueryParser and QueryBuilder make it rock at position 0 and roll at position 2, slop 0, and Weight#matches reports the only match at positions 2-4), and highlight the hit with Highlighter and QueryScorer, expecting 'rock roll rock and roll'. Instead you get 'rock roll rock and roll', and on 'rock roll roll', which matches only as the first rock plus the last roll, you get 'rock roll roll', with the matching last word unmarked. WeightedSpanTermExtractor turns the phrase's one hole into slop 1 of an ordered SpanNearQuery, which accepts 0 or 1 words between the terms instead of exactly 1 and keeps only the shortest span per start; MultiPhraseQuery has the same conversion, and the UnifiedHighlighter with weight matches turned off reaches it through PhraseHelper.

bugs.area: highlighter / UnifiedHighlighter WEIGHT_MATCHES path (FieldOffsetStrategy) with statistics-dependent query rewrites (CommonTermsQuery, MoreLikeThisQuery)
bugs.title: Default UnifiedHighlighter (WEIGHT_MATCHES) rewrites the query again on its own per-leaf or one-document reader, so statistics-dependent queries such as CommonTermsQuery lose their highlights
bugs.summary: You search with CommonTermsQuery(SHOULD, MUST, 0.5) over 'the' (in 5 of 6 documents) and 'fox' (2 of 6), which the searcher rewrites to +fox the, and highlight the hit 'quick brown fox' with a default UnifiedHighlighter built on that same searcher. You expect 'quick brown fox', which the highlighter returns with WEIGHT_MATCHES off and the legacy Highlighter and FastVectorHighlighter also give. Instead the snippet has no mark, because FieldOffsetStrategy rewrites the query again on the hit's own segment or a one-document view of it, where 'the' counts as rare and becomes required (+the +fox), so the hit no longer matches; the result changes with segment layout alone, and MoreLikeThisQuery with its default minDocFreq rewrites there to an empty query, so its hits are never highlighted.

bugs.area: search / IndriQuery (QueryVisitor traversal of Indri composite queries; consumers: QueryVisitor.termCollector, IndexSearcher's cumulative clause limit, RamUsageEstimator.sizeOf(Query), UnifiedHighlighter)
bugs.title: IndriQuery.visit reports the whole query as a leaf and never visits its clauses, so QueryVisitor.termCollector, UnifiedHighlighter term extraction, IndexSearcher's cumulative clause limit and RamUsageEstimator.sizeOf all ignore an IndriAndQuery's clauses
bugs.summary: You build an IndriAndQuery of ordinary TermQuery clauses, for example f:a and f:b, and inspect it with a QueryVisitor, as term extraction, highlighting, IndexSearcher's clause-count check and the query RAM estimate do. You expect the visitor to reach both clauses, as it does for a BooleanQuery over the same clauses, because Query#visit is documented to 'recurse through the query tree, visiting any child queries'. Instead IndriQuery.visit only calls visitor.visitLeaf(this), so termCollector returns , with maxClauseCount=4 a 51-clause IndriAndQuery and BooleanQuery(IndriAndQuery(3), IndriAndQuery(3)) both run while the same nesting of BooleanQuery clauses throws TooManyClauses, and RamUsageEstimator.sizeOf gives 1,024 bytes for 1,000 clauses against 1,169,024 for the BooleanQuery.

bugs.area: highlighter / matchhighlight (MatchRegionRetriever default offset strategy OffsetsFromTokens for fields indexed without positions; MatchHighlighter on top of it)
bugs.title: MatchRegionRetriever's default OffsetsFromTokens strategy ignores QueryVisitor#consumeTermsMatching, so prefix, wildcard, regexp, term-range and multi-term TermInSetQuery matches on fields without positions get no hit regions
bugs.summary: You index a stored field without positions (one document 'foo bar', IndexOptions DOCS_AND_FREQS, or a StringField), run a PrefixQuery('ba') that matches it, and ask MatchRegionRetriever (or MatchHighlighter) with its default strategies for the hit regions; you expect the region [4,7) for 'bar', which a TermQuery('bar') on the same field, a FuzzyQuery('baz'~1) and the same PrefixQuery on a field with positions all give. Instead the field gets no hit regions at all ({}), although the document is a hit and Weight#matches reports a match on that field. The default strategy for such fields, OffsetsFromTokens, collects the query's terms only through QueryVisitor#consumeTerms, while constant-score multi-term queries report theirs through consumeTermsMatching, so its term set stays empty and no re-analysed token is kept.

It added OffsetsFromTokens with a QueryVisitor that overrides only consumeTerms and made it the default for DOCS and DOCS_AND_FREQS fields; the visitor is unchanged on main apart from reformatting (6faa4f98e04) and refactors (2c1f9381390, 755de5aae33). bugs.area: search / sorting (TopFieldCollector competitive iterator x DenseConjunctionBulkScorer collectRange shortcut)
bugs.title: Since 10.3.0, a field-sorted top-n search whose query fully matches a segment without deletions (MatchAllDocsQuery, a range covering the segment) no longer skips non-competitive documents: the comparator's initial all-docs competitive iterator reports a run to maxDoc through UpdateableDocIdSetIterator.docIDRunEnd, so DenseConjunctionBulkScorer hands the whole segment to the collector in one collectRange call (performance regression; results correct)
bugs.summary: You run a top-10 search sorted on a LONG field with points (or a STRING field with a terms index, or a LONG field with a skip index) with MatchAllDocsQuery over one 100,000-doc segment that has no deletions. You expect Lucene to skip non-competitive documents, as 10.2.2 does for this exact search (about 1,000-1,750 docs collected) and as a TermQuery matching the same docs still does on main (about 8,200). Instead main and every release since 10.3.0 collect all 100,000 docs, because the comparator's competitive iterator starts as all docs and since #14532 reports a run up to maxDoc, so DenseConjunctionBulkScorer collects the whole segment in one collectRange call before the comparator narrows the iterator; the top hits are still correct, only the pruning is lost.

bugs.area: analysis-smartcn / HHMM segmenter bigram dictionary (BigramDictionary.getBigramItemIndex, AbstractDictionary.hash2; reached through SmartChineseAnalyzer and HMMChineseTokenizer)
bugs.title: smartcn: the double-hashing step of BigramDictionary (AbstractDictionary.hash2, an operator-precedence slip) is 0 for some Chinese word + ASCII or Latin-1 punctuation pairs, so each such bigram lookup re-reads one slot 402,136 times (about 0.7 ms instead of about 0.1 us) and SmartChineseAnalyzer analyzes ordinary prose 2-7x slower and text dense in such pairs 67x-174x slower, with unchanged tokens
bugs.summary: You analyze Chinese text written with ASCII punctuation, for example '我们要发展经济和文化,加强法律,增加资金,继续努力,共同进步.', with the default SmartChineseAnalyzer; its bigram dictionary is an open-addressing hash table with double hashing, so you expect each bigram frequency lookup to take a handful of probes and the text to cost about as much as the same sentence with full-width punctuation, which gives the same tokens. Instead AbstractDictionary.hash2 computes ((33h + d) & 0xFF) and then ((33h + d) >> 8), because '+' binds tighter than '&' and '>>' (AbstractDictionary.java:195-196), so the probe step is always in [0, 288] and is 0 for some keys whose last char is below U+0100, such as '对@,' or '文化@,'; when such a key's home slot holds another bigram, BigramDictionary.getBigramItemIndex (BigramDictionary.java:213-233) re-reads that same slot until i reaches PRIME_BIGRAM_LENGTH = 402,137 and then returns 'not found'. The tokens stay correct, but that sentence repeated 100 times takes about 220 ms of CPU instead of about 2.6 ms (85x on main), and 1x with a one-line guard.

bugs.area: search / sorting (TopFieldCollector, relevance-first sort: minimum competitive score at the totalHitsThreshold crossing)
bugs.title: A relevance-first TopFieldCollector (Sort.RELEVANCE or Sort(FIELD_SCORE, tiebreak)) never sets the minimum competitive score when totalHitsThreshold is crossed, so skipping starts only if a later hit is competitive, and the search can score every match (performance regression since 8.7.0; results correct)
bugs.summary: You run IndexSearcher#search(query, 10, Sort.RELEVANCE), or a searchAfter page sorted by Sort(SortField.FIELD_SCORE, tiebreak), on a query with many matches, and expect it to start skipping non-competitive documents once 1,000 hits are counted, as search(query, 10) does and as LUCENE-8507 made relevance-first TopFieldCollector do from 8.0.0 to 8.6.3. Instead TopFieldCollector.countHit flips totalHitsRelation to GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO on the hit that crosses the threshold, before thresholdCheck's EQUAL_TO-guarded updateMinCompetitiveScore call runs, so that call can never take effect and the minimum competitive score is set only when a later hit is competitive; with the best documents first, the relevance-sorted search scores all 10,011 matches where search(query, 10) stops at 1,024, with the same top 10. This is a regression from LUCENE-9449 (8.7.0); results are always correct.

bugs.title: RescoreTopNQuery throws (AssertionError with -ea, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException with -da) instead of matching nothing when its inner query matches no document: rewrite passes an empty top-n list to DocAndScoreQuery.createDocAndScoreQuery, which requires a non-empty one

bugs.title: A kNN query built with a null KnnSearchStrategy, documented as 'the default strategy will be used', throws NullPointerException when a seeded HNSW search runs (SeededKnnVectorQuery, or the optimistic re-entry pass when a segment is re-entered)

bugs.area: join / JoinUtil numeric (point-based) query-time join
bugs.title: JoinUtil's numeric join on Float or Double throws 'values are out of order' when the from side has two or more distinct negative values
bugs.summary: You build JoinUtil.createJoinQuery("fromF", false, "toF", Float.class, fromQuery, searcher, ScoreMode.None) where the from documents store -1 and -2 in a FloatDocValuesField and the to documents index FloatPoint -1, -2 and 3, and expect a query that matches the two to documents with -1 and -2, because the javadoc lists Float and Double as supported numeric types with no sign restriction. Instead createJoinQuery throws IllegalArgumentException 'values are out of order: saw [40 7f ff ff] before [3f ff ff ff]' (that is, -1 before -2; releases before 10.4.0 show an UnsupportedOperationException raised while that message is built), and Double and every scoring ScoreMode fail the same way. The cause is that JoinUtil sorts the collected Float/Double join values as raw IEEE bits in signed-long order, which for negative numbers is the reverse of numeric order, and streams them in that order into PointInSetQuery / PointInSetIncludingScoreQuery, which require strictly ascending points.

bugs.area: highlighter / UnifiedHighlighter passage scoring (PassageScorer match labels)
bugs.title: UnifiedHighlighter throws MaxBytesLengthExceededException when a TermInSetQuery's toString is longer than 32766 bytes (for example 886 UUID-like ids), because PassageScorer groups match labels in a BytesRefHash
bugs.summary: You search with a TermInSetQuery of 886 UUID-shaped ids (or 4,000 short terms) on a field indexed with offsets, get the hit, and call the default UnifiedHighlighter's highlight on that field, expecting the snippet with the matching id in <b>, as the equivalent ConstantScoreQuery over a SHOULD BooleanQuery of the same ids gives. For a multi-term set query the highlighter labels each match with the query's whole toString, which lists every term, and PassageScorer groups those labels in a BytesRefHash, which rejects entries over 32766 bytes; 885 ids (a 32,749-byte toString) still work.

bugs.area: facet / FacetsConfig drill-down term indexing (DrillDownTermsIndexing.NONE in a shared indexFieldName) vs the core per-field schema check (IndexingChain FieldSchema, FieldInfo.verifySameIndexOptions)
bugs.title: A facet dimension set to DrillDownTermsIndexing.NONE that shares its index field ($facets by default) with term-indexing dimensions makes FacetsConfig emit two schemas for that field, so since 9.0.0 IndexWriter rejects documents of one kind once a document of the other kind is indexed, and after a commit until the index is cleared or rebuilt
bugs.summary: You call config.setDrillDownTermsIndexing("rating", NONE), leave every dimension in the default index field $facets, and index one document with only FacetField("rating", "5") and then one with FacetField("author", "Bob"); you expect both to be indexed, as they are on Lucene 8.9 to 8.11 and as they are when rating gets its own index field. FacetsConfig.build gives the first document a doc-values-only $facets (NONE adds no drill-down terms) and the second a $facets with drill-down terms, and since 9.0 Lucene requires one schema per field, so the second addDocument throws IllegalArgumentException 'Inconsistency of field data structures across documents for field [$facets] of doc [1]. index options: expected 'NONE', but it has 'DOCS'' (with taxonomy facets the reverse order fails the same way). After a commit, a new IndexWriter keeps rejecting documents of the other kind ('cannot change field "$facets" from index options=NONE to inconsistent index options=DOCS') until the index is cleared or rebuilt.

bugs.area: suggest / FreeTextSuggester (n-gram model built with ShingleFilter; lookup context counts after analysis holes)
bugs.title: FreeTextSuggester.lookup throws AssertionError (-ea) or NullPointerException (-da) when a word the analyzer removed (a stop word) comes right before the key's last word, because it reads the count of the filler-only context '_', which the n-gram model never stores (lookup('the w') with the default constructor and EnglishAnalyzer)
bugs.summary: You build a FreeTextSuggester with the default constructor and the stock EnglishAnalyzer over 'the wizard of oz' and call lookup('the w'), expecting the suggestion 'wizard': lookup documents only IllegalArgumentException and IllegalStateException, and the upstream tests testEndingHole and testTwoEndingHoles assert results for a stop-word analyzer. Instead lookup throws AssertionError at FreeTextSuggester.java:576 with -ea, or NullPointerException in decodeWeight (:724) with -da: the removed 'the' leaves a hole, so the bigram-level query token is '_ w', which matches the stored shingle '_ wizard', and lookup then reads the count of its context '_', which ShingleFilter never emits and the model therefore never stores. bugs.area: index / vector values iteration (KnnVectorValues.fromDISI) with backward-codecs / Lucene 9.4 sparse byte vector reader
bugs.title: KnnVectorValues.fromDISI's advance leaves index stale, so on Lucene 10 sparse byte vectors in segments written by Lucene 9.4 read back as zeros or as another document's vector
bugs.summary: You open, on Lucene 10, an index whose segment was written by Lucene 9.4.2 with a byte vector field that only some documents have, move the field's iterator to a document with advance(doc) and read vectorValue(iterator.index), which is what ByteKnnVectorFieldSource does, and expect that document's own vector, because DocIndexIterator.index is documented as the ordinal of the current document and DocIdSetIterator.advance must behave like repeated nextDoc calls. Instead every document that has a vector reads as all zeros: the iterator that KnnVectorValues.fromDISI builds, which this one reader returns, counts the ordinal only in nextDoc, and its advance moves to the document without moving the ordinal, so index stays at -1 (the reader then hands back its never-filled buffer); after earlier nextDoc calls, index is an earlier document's ordinal and the read returns that document's vector. Lucene 9.x reads the same index correctly; the defect came with the 10.0 vector-values API change #13779.

Inside the PR, commit d43785d (2024-09-15, 'no default advance; default cost unsupported') replaced the inherited slowAdvance(target) default, which kept the ordinal right, with the forwarding advance after a review comment called the default a possible performance trap [read]. Release-level execution on both sides: 9.12.0 passes (9.x-API variant), 10.0.0 fails

bugs.area: search / vector queries (KnnFloat/Byte/Float16VectorQuery, Float/Byte/Float16VectorSimilarityQuery; join DiversifyingChildren*KnnVectorQuery)
bugs.title: kNN and vector-similarity query constructors keep the caller's query-vector array instead of copying it, so a caller that refills that buffer before the query runs silently changes which documents the query matches and what it is equal to
bugs.summary: You decode a query embedding into a scratch float, build new KnnFloatVectorQuery(field, scratch, k), decode the next embedding into the same array, build a second query and OR the two; you expect each query to search the vector it was built from, as TermQuery does when built from a reused BytesRef. Instead both queries now search the second vector and compare equal, so the OR returns 1 hit instead of 2 (the neighbour of the first vector is lost); the same holds for KnnByteVectorQuery, KnnFloat16VectorQuery, the three vector-similarity queries and the join DiversifyingChildren*KnnVectorQuery classes. The constructors store the caller's array itself (VectorUtil.checkFinite returns its argument) and search, equals and hashCode all read it, although getTargetCopy returns a copy precisely so that callers cannot reach that array.

bugs.area: index / indexing chain (single-term BINARY inversion, norms)
bugs.title: IndexingChain.invertTerm adds 2 to the field length for each single-term (InvertableType.BINARY) value, so untokenized DOCS_AND_FREQS fields with norms get double the norm and a lower BM25 score
bugs.summary: You index one value in an untokenized field whose FieldType has DOCS_AND_FREQS and norms enabled, once through a plain Field (TokenStream inversion) and once through the single-term path (a Field subclass whose invertableType returns BINARY, or an IndexWriter#addBatch BinaryColumn or DictionaryColumn). You expect the same field length and norm, 1 per value, because FieldInvertState#getLength is the 'total number of terms in this field' and a BINARY value is documented as a single value with term frequency one. Instead IndexingChain.invertTerm adds 2 to the length for every value, so the norm is 2 (2k for k values) and the BM25 score of the identical document drops (0.082873434 to 0.058813408 in the repro), while the postings still record freq 1 per value.

bugs.area: memory / MemoryIndex term inversion (custom term frequencies: FeatureField, TermFrequencyAttribute streams, DOCS_AND_CUSTOM_FREQS); reached in-tree through monitor single-document batches
bugs.title: MemoryIndex ignores TermFrequencyAttribute, so FeatureField values and custom term frequencies are indexed as frequency 1 and their postings frequencies, term statistics, norms and scores differ from IndexWriter's (Lucene Monitor's single-document matching included)
bugs.summary: You add a document with FeatureField("features", "pagerank", 10f), or a tokenized DOCS_AND_FREQS field whose TokenStream sets TermFrequencyAttribute (for example DelimitedTermFrequencyTokenFilter on 'a|7'), to a MemoryIndex and expect its postings, statistics and scores to equal those of the same document in a one-document IndexWriter index, as they do for ordinary fields. bugs.area: memory / MemoryIndex term inversion (multi-valued analyzed fields: positions and offsets carried from one value to the next); reached in-tree through monitor single-document batches
bugs.title: MemoryIndex drops the final position increment of each value of a multi-valued field (and the gaps after leading values with no tokens), so phrase and other position queries disagree with IndexWriter, including Lucene Monitor's single-document matching
bugs.summary: You add a document whose text field has two values, 'quick the' and 'fox', to a MemoryIndex with an analyzer that removes the stop word 'the', and expect the positions of a one-document IndexWriter index: IndexWriter keeps the hole the removed trailing 'the' leaves (TokenStream.end reports it as a final position increment), so 'fox' is at position 2 and the phrase "quick fox" does not match. MemoryIndex.storeTerms never adds that final increment, puts 'fox' at position 1 and matches the phrase; the reverse also happens (the input of upstream's TestIndexWriter#testStopwordsPosIncHole matches a phrase on IndexWriter but not on MemoryIndex), and values that produce no tokens before the first token skip the position and offset gaps ([the | quick fox] with gap 100: IndexWriter quick at position 101, offsets 4-9; MemoryIndex position 0, offsets 0-5). Lucene Monitor inherits it: a stored phrase query matches the document when it is matched alone (MemoryIndex path) but not when the same document is in a two-document batch (IndexWriter path).

bugs.area: memory / MemoryIndex lazy per-field read state (sorted terms, points and doc-values preparation, norms)
bugs.title: An unfrozen MemoryIndex does not reset its lazily built per-field state when more values are added to a field after a read, so later searches miss the new terms or points, throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, return unsorted SORTED_NUMERIC values or score with stale norms
bugs.summary: You add a value to a field of a MemoryIndex that is not frozen, search it, add more values to the same field, and search again; you expect the second search to see everything, like a MemoryIndex built from the same adds, because freeze is the only documented point after which no data may be added and adding the same field several times is supported. Instead the field keeps the read state that the first read built lazily and nothing ever resets (the sorted term ids, the point min/max and 1D order, the sorted doc values, the cached norm): a term or IntPoint added later is silently not found (for example IntPoint p=2, search, p=1: newExactQuery(p, 1) no longer matches), SORTED_NUMERIC values come back as 2, 1, the score uses the old norm, or the search throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from the corrupted term dictionary (an AssertionError under -ea for some inputs).

bugs.area: index / stored fields (StoredFieldDataInput: DataInput-backed StoredField values, #14213)
bugs.title: StoredFieldDataInput(ByteArrayDataInput) takes the input's end position as its length, so a ByteArrayDataInput that does not start at position 0 (a slice at a non-zero offset, or a partly read input) silently stores extra trailing bytes, or makes addDocument fail and close IndexWriter
bugs.summary: You add new StoredField(name, new StoredFieldDataInput(new ByteArrayDataInput(bytes, offset, len))) and expect the stored value to be exactly those len bytes, because the record's length is documented as 'the length of the data input'. The convenience constructor copies ByteArrayDataInput.length, which is the end position offset + len, so for an 8-byte slice at offset 4 of a 16-byte array the document stores 12 bytes, the slice plus the next 4, with no error. If fewer bytes than the offset follow the slice, the stored fields writer reads past the array, addDocument throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and IndexWriter closes itself.

bugs.area: core / document: shape doc values (ShapeDocValues reader behind LatLonShapeDocValues / XYShapeDocValues relate and the slow doc-values shape queries; MemoryIndex shape doc-values fields)
bugs.title: ShapeDocValues.relate rewinds to position 0 of the backing array instead of to the BytesRef's offset, so a LatLonShape or XYShape doc value built from a BytesRef slice (offset != 0) silently relates wrongly to queries
bugs.summary: You build a LatLonShape or XYShape doc value from a BytesRef that points into the middle of a larger byte array (offset != 0), for example with LatLonShape.createLatLonShapeDocValues(BytesRef) or as a MemoryIndex field, and expect relate and the doc-values shape queries to answer exactly as for the same bytes at offset 0. bugs.area: facet / facet sets (MatchingFacetSetsCounts.count, a BinaryDocValues consumer; reached through MemoryIndex, custom readers and the backward-codecs Lucene80 BEST_COMPRESSION doc-values producer)
bugs.title: MatchingFacetSetsCounts decodes the facet-set binary doc value from position 0 of BytesRef.bytes instead of BytesRef.offset, so a value that a reader returns as a slice of a larger array is counted from the wrong bytes (silently wrong facet-set counts, or NegativeArraySizeException / ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException)
bugs.summary: You count facet sets with MatchingFacetSetsCounts over a reader that hands back a document's facet-set binary doc value as a BytesRef slice of a larger array (offset != 0), for example a MemoryIndex holding a value that was packed into a shared buffer, and expect the same counts as for a compact copy of the same bytes. Instead count reads the dimension count from bytes[0] and the dimension values from bytes[4..length) of the backing array, ignoring the offset, so the document is counted under whatever bytes start that array: a document whose set is (3,4), stored right after an encoding of (1,2), is counted as (1,2)=1 and (3,4)=0, with no error. When the leading bytes do not decode to a sane dimension count, the MatchingFacetSetsCounts constructor throws NegativeArraySizeException or ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead, while the same value indexed through IndexWriter with the default codec is counted correctly.

bugs.area: join / JoinUtil query-time join (single-valued term and numeric collectors)
bugs.title: JoinUtil's single-valued term and numeric joins treat a 'from' document without a join value as if it had the empty term or the number 0, so they also return the 'to' document whose key is empty or 0 and add the value-less documents' scores to it (since 4.0.0)
bugs.summary: You join orders to customers with JoinUtil.createJoinQuery("customer", false, "id", fromQuery, searcher, scoreMode), or the numeric overload with Integer.class, where fromQuery matches two orders and only one of them has a customer key, and expect only that order's customer back, because the javadoc returns the to-documents that 'have the same terms' as the matching from-documents. Instead the order without a key is collected as if its key were the empty term (term join) or 0 (numeric join), so the customer whose id is "" or 0 is returned too, in every ScoreMode, and a real customer 0 also gets the key-less order's score (Max 5.0 instead of 1.0). bugs.area: join / JoinUtil query-time term join (TermsWithScoreCollector.SV and SV.Avg, ScoreMode Min/Avg)
bugs.title: JoinUtil's single-valued term join forgets a from-document that scored exactly 0, so ScoreMode.Min and ScoreMode.Avg give too-high, order-dependent scores
bugs.summary: You build JoinUtil.createJoinQuery("join", false, "ref", fromQuery, searcher, ScoreMode.Min) where two from-documents share the join value x and fromQuery scores them 0 and 2 (one matches only a FILTER clause), and expect the to-document with ref x to score min(0, 2) = 0, or (0 + 2) / 2 = 1 with ScoreMode.Avg, because the ScoreMode javadoc says 'the min of all child scores' and 'the average of all child scores' and the multi-valued join returns exactly that on the same documents. Which documents match does not change; only scores and ranking are wrong, and they depend on collection order (scores [0, 2] go wrong, [2, 0] come out right).

bugs.area: monitor / query decomposition and match scoring (QueryDecomposer DisjunctionMaxQuery split, ScoringMatch/ExplainingMatch resolve)
bugs.title: Lucene Monitor's ScoringMatch and ExplainingMatch score a registered DisjunctionMaxQuery with a tie-breaker below 1 as the sum of its matching disjuncts instead of max + tieBreaker * others
bugs.summary: You register a DisjunctionMaxQuery such as (title:apple | body:apple) with tie-breaker 0 in a Monitor and match a document that has apple in both fields with ScoringMatch or ExplainingMatch, expecting the score the query itself gives that document: the best field's score plus tie times the others, which is what IndexSearcher returns (0.1798013 in an independent test). In the 'albino elephant' example of DisjunctionMaxQuery's own javadoc, this makes the document with 'albino' in both fields tie with the document that matches both words, which the query is designed to rank higher.

bugs.area: queries / span queries (SpanNotQuery: the exclusion filter in SpanNotWeight#getSpans)
bugs.title: SpanNotQuery with a negative post (or dist) drops every include span that follows the last exclude span in a document, because NO_MORE_POSITIONS - post overflows int
bugs.summary: You index the text 'b a c' and run new SpanNotQuery(a, b, 0, -1), whose javadoc says it keeps the 'a' spans that do not overlap a 'b' and that a negative post only allows some overlap; since 'b' at position 0 overlaps neither 'a', you expect both spans [1,2) and [2,3), exactly as with post = 0. Instead you get only [1,2): once the first 'a' has used up the document's exclude spans, the exclude iterator sits at NO_MORE_POSITIONS (Integer.MAX_VALUE) and SpanNotQuery.java:210 computes Integer.MAX_VALUE - post, which wraps to a negative int for any post < 0, so every later 'a' in the document is rejected. bugs.area: queries / function queries (the ValueSource.fromDoubleValuesSource bridge: its FunctionValues inherits the float default FunctionValues.getRangeScorer that FunctionRangeQuery calls)
bugs.title: FunctionRangeQuery over ValueSource.fromDoubleValuesSource(...) compares bounds and values as floats, not doubles, so double and long ranges silently gain or lose hits near a bound and beyond Float.MAX_VALUE

bugs.area: analysis-common / minhash (MinHashFilter.FixedSizeTreeSet bottom-k set; MinHashFilterFactory 'minHash')
bugs.title: MinHashFilter with hashSetSize >= 2 drops one of the kept lowest hash values when a token repeats while its (hash, bucket) set is full, so the min-hash signature depends on token repeats and order instead of only on the token set ('b a a' keeps 1 of 2 values; 'c a c b' and 'c a b c' give different signatures)
bugs.summary: You analyse 'b a a' with MinHashFilter(hashCount 1, bucketCount 1, hashSetSize 2) and expect the same two min hashes as for 'b a', because the filter keeps 'the N lowest values' of the tokens' hashes (MinHashFilter.java:38-40; hashSetSize is 'the no. of min hashes to keep') and the lowest values of a token set do not change when a token repeats. Instead, FixedSizeTreeSet.add removes the full set's largest value (pollLast) before TreeSet.add finds that the repeated value is already there, so 'b a a' gives one value; a later new token, however large its hash, then fills the free slot ('c a c b' keeps the hashes of c and b, not the true lowest two, c and a), and the same tokens in another order ('c a b c') give yet another signature. In the javadoc's '1 hash and keep the 100 lowest values' setting with 5-word shingles, a 150-word text read twice has the same shingle set as the text read once but a signature of 99 values that misses one of the 100 lowest.

bugs.area: suggest / analyzing infix suggester (AnalyzingInfixSuggester.build failure path; inherited unchanged by BlendedInfixSuggester)
bugs.title: AnalyzingInfixSuggester.build can commit and then throw, and its catch block leaves writer == null, so refresh becomes a no-op: the old suggestions stay served while the directory holds the build that threw, and the next add/update or a reopen silently switches to it (default settings, since 9.2.0)
bugs.summary: You rebuild an AnalyzingInfixSuggester with default settings, build throws an IOException, you call refresh and keep using the instance, and you expect it to serve what its index holds, so that a later add adds exactly one suggestion. Instead build has already committed the new index (closeIndexWriterOnBuild defaults to true) before it opens the SearcherManager on it; when that open fails, the catch block rolls back (which cannot undo the commit), sets writer = null and keeps the old SearcherManager, so refresh is a no-op, lookups serve the old suggestions ([old apple]) while the directory holds the failed build ([new avocado]), and after the next add lookups return [another apricot, new avocado], with the old suggestion gone. A second trigger needs no I/O fault: build first closes, and so commits, a writer that holds an add or update not yet refreshed, and if the rebuild's input then throws, refresh never shows that committed change.

bugs.title: JapaneseCompletionFilter expands a reading into every combination of romaji spellings with no bound, so 24-32 kana (for example 32 x "ン", or 32 x "し" in QUERY mode) throw OutOfMemoryError inside one incrementToken call

bugs.area: index / merge policy (LogMergePolicy.findMerges level window; LogDocMergePolicy, LogByteSizeMergePolicy)
bugs.title: LogMergePolicy.findMerges wraps 'start + mergeFactor' when mergeFactor is Integer.MAX_VALUE (or within about the segment count of it), which setMergeFactor accepts, so commit and flush throw once two size levels exist (every release since 2.3.0)
bugs.summary: You configure LogDocMergePolicy (or LogByteSizeMergePolicy) with setMergeFactor(Integer.MAX_VALUE), which the setter accepts (it rejects only values below 2, and its javadoc recommends large values for batch indexing), bulk-load one large segment, add one document and commit, and expect the commit to succeed with no merge, as it does with Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1. Instead findMerges computes the end of each merge window as 'int end = start + mergeFactor', which wraps negative for every size level that does not start at segment 0, and its minimum-size packing step then calls levels.get(-2147483648), so commit throws IndexOutOfBoundsException (OutOfMemoryError 'Requested array size exceeds VM limit' before 10.2.0). Every later commit and flush of new documents fails the same way until the factor is lowered; on main a 20,000,000-document segment followed by a 1-document flush is enough.

bugs.area: search / kNN vector queries (per-segment collector sizing: AbstractKnnVectorQuery, TopKnnCollectorManager, TopKnnCollector; join DiversifyingNearestChildrenKnnCollectorManager)
bugs.title: kNN vector queries size each segment's result heap from the requested k, not from what the segment can return, so k = Integer.MAX_VALUE throws IllegalArgumentException and k = 2^28 runs out of a 2 GiB heap on a 3-document index (core KnnFloat/KnnByteVectorQuery without a filter: regression in 9.10.0; join DiversifyingChildren*KnnVectorQuery: since 9.8.0)
bugs.summary: You run a KnnFloatVectorQuery with a k larger than the index, for example k = Integer.MAX_VALUE to mean 'all vectors', and expect every vector back, as k = 1000 over 3 vectors gives, and as 9.9.2 gives for any k. Instead each segment's collector is built with a heap sized from k (k + 1 longs on a single-segment index) before the segment's vector count is looked at: k = Integer.MAX_VALUE throws IllegalArgumentException('initialCapacity must be > 0 and < 2147483630; got: 2147483647') from TernaryLongHeap, and k = 2^28 over a 3-document index throws OutOfMemoryError with a 2 GiB heap. Lucene used to cap k at the segment's vector count ('bound k by total number of vectors to prevent oversizing data structures'); a search speed-up change dropped that cap in 9.10.0, and the join DiversifyingChildren*KnnVectorQuery never had it.

bugs.area: index / TieredMergePolicy merge selection (doFindMerges candidate loop; setMaxMergedSegmentMB validation)
bugs.title: TieredMergePolicy.setMaxMergedSegmentMB(0), a value the setter accepts, makes commit, close and forceMergeDeletes throw once a segment has enough deletes: the doFindMerges candidate loop never admits a segment, so the merge candidate is empty (AssertionError with -ea, IndexOutOfBoundsException with -da); a regression since 7.5.0
bugs.summary: You configure the default TieredMergePolicy with setMaxMergedSegmentMB(0), which the setter accepts (it rejects only negative values, with the message 'must be >=0'), delete some documents, and expect commit, close and forceMergeDeletes to succeed, either with no merge or with the singleton merge the class javadoc promises for segments over the maximum ('down to 1 at once, if that one has deletions'), as they do with a 1-byte maximum and as they did on 7.4.0. Instead the candidate loop in doFindMerges requires 'bytesThisMerge < maxMergedSegmentBytes', which is 0 < 0 before the first segment is added, so no segment is ever admitted and the candidate list stays empty. 'assert candidate.size > 0' then fails with -ea, and candidate.get(0) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException ('Index 0 out of bounds for length 0') with -da, out of the writer call.

bugs.area: geo / Tessellator hole elimination (polygon indexing for LatLonShape and XYShape)
bugs.title: Tessellator bridges a hole whose left-most vertex touches an outer-ring edge to a vertex off that edge, so LatLonShape and XYShape index the hole (in some shapes also area outside the polygon) as part of the shape, or reject a valid polygon
bugs.summary: You index a polygon whose hole touches the outer boundary at one corner, which the Tessellator javadoc allows ('Holes may only touch at one vertex'), for example the outer ring (2,0) (1,1) (0,2) (3,3) with the hole (1,1) (1,2) (2,2), and you expect a point inside the hole not to match. To cut the polygon into triangles Lucene first joins the hole to the outer ring with a bridge; when the hole's left-most corner lies on an outer edge, Tessellator.fetchHoleBridge links it to the vertex before that edge instead of the edge's own endpoint, so the bridge runs across the hole. The triangles then cover the hole and an INTERSECTS query for a point in it matches the document with no error, or, for other shapes such as a hole corner touching the middle of an outer edge, the valid polygon is rejected with 'Unable to Tessellate shape'.

bugs.area: geo / Tessellator hole-bridge edge flags (LatLonShape and XYShape CONTAINS queries)
bugs.title: Tessellator flags a hole bridge that lies inside a longer outer-ring edge as an internal edge, so LatLonShape and XYShape CONTAINS queries match boxes that stick out of a valid polygon whose two holes touch the same outer edge

While joining the second hole to the ring, Tessellator.eliminateHole draws a bridge from (5,0) to (2,0) that runs along the outer edge but marks it as an internal edge, because it only compares the bridge with the ring edges next to its two ends, so the indexed triangle loses its 'belongs to the polygon' flag on that piece of the boundary. bugs.area: geo / XYShape point queries (Component2D.pointInTriangle; ShapeField.encodeTriangle orientation for XY)
bugs.title: XYShape point queries can miss a polygon at one of its own vertices: Component2D.pointInTriangle rejects the second vertex (b) of a clockwise triangle, and ShapeField.encodeTriangle makes XY triangles counter-clockwise only on their sortable-int encodings, so a stored triangle can decode clockwise; an INTERSECTS point query at that vertex misses the polygon and DISJOINT returns it (since 8.5.0)
bugs.summary: You index the clockwise triangle (0,1) (1,2) (3,3) as an XYPolygon with XYShape.createIndexableFields and run XYShape.newPointQuery at each of its corners; you expect every corner to match the polygon (INTERSECTS) and none to be DISJOINT from it, as happens for the same triangle moved by (8,8) and for every point of its edges. Instead the INTERSECTS query at (1,2) finds nothing and the DISJOINT query at (1,2) returns the document: ShapeField.encodeTriangle checks the winding on the sortable-int encodings of the floats, which are ordered like the floats but not evenly spaced, so the stored triangle decodes clockwise, and Component2D.pointInTriangle reports the second vertex of a clockwise triangle as outside. The same happens with projected metre-like coordinates, for example at vertex (518885,4395432) of a hexagon whose x range crosses 2^19.

bugs.summary: You index a polygon with LatLonShape or XYShape and search with a polygon or line using INTERSECTS (or DISJOINT); you expect a match only when the two shapes share at least one point. bugs.area: geo / shape queries (Polygon2D containsLine/containsTriangle, LatLonShape and XYShape WITHIN)
bugs.title: Polygon2D.containsLine/containsTriangle accept a segment or triangle whose vertices lie on the boundary of a non-convex polygon even when it passes outside between them, so LatLonShape/XYShape WITHIN queries return false positives
bugs.summary: You index a line or polygon whose corner points lie exactly on the boundary of a non-convex (dented) query polygon, for example a road between two corners of a district, and search for shapes WITHIN that polygon; you expect only shapes that lie inside it. Polygon2D.containsLine/containsTriangle accept a segment or triangle when every vertex is contained, with boundary points counting as inside, and no polygon edge crosses it strictly; that shortcut is only valid for convex polygons, so a segment that cuts across a dent between two boundary points, or a triangle that fills the dent and lies completely outside, is reported as contained. The WITHIN query returns those documents with no error (repro: for the polygon (0,0),(4,0),(4,4),(2,1),(0,4), WITHIN returns the indexed segment (0,4)-(4,4) and the indexed notch triangle (0,4),(4,4),(2,1) although (2,4) and (2,3) are outside the polygon).

bugs.area: geo / shape queries (Polygon2D.withinTriangle; LatLonShape and XYShape CONTAINS with a query polygon that has holes)
bugs.title: LatLonShape/XYShape CONTAINS with a query polygon that has holes returns indexed shapes that do not contain it, because Polygon2D.withinTriangle never tests the query's hole edges

Polygon2D.withinTriangle rejects an indexed triangle only when one of its vertices is inside the query or one of its real (original-shape) edges crosses the query's outer ring; it never tests the query's hole edges, so an edge that starts and ends inside query holes and crosses the land between them goes unnoticed and the shape is returned as CONTAINS, with no error. Repro: query = the square [0,10]^2 with holes [1,3]x[4,6] and [7,9]x[4,6]; doc 0 = the square [-1,11]^2 with a hole [2,8]x[4.5,5.5] (it does not cover the query point (5,5)), doc 1 = the same square without a hole; CONTAINS returns [0, 1] instead of [1] for XYShape and LatLonShape, while a point query at (5,5) correctly returns only doc 1.

bugs.area: core / geo distance queries (GeoUtils.distanceQuerySortKey, shared by LatLonPoint, LatLonDocValuesField and LatLonShape circle queries)
bugs.title: Lat/lon distance queries can drop a point whose distance equals the radius and match a point one ulp beyond it, because GeoUtils.distanceQuerySortKey does not return the largest sort key within the radius (every release since 6.1.0)
bugs.summary: You index points with LatLonPoint (or LatLonDocValuesField or LatLonShape) and run a distance query whose radius is exactly a point's distance from the center as Lucene computes it (SloppyMath.haversinMeters, the same value a distance sort or LatLonPoint.nearest reports), and expect that point to match, because the query matches 'points within the specified distance' and Lucene's own test oracle is haversinMeters(center, point) <= radius; with the radius one ulp smaller you expect it not to match. Instead the point is often missing in the first case and often still matches in the second (each in roughly a fifth to a third of random cases, depending on the points): for example, two points that both the distance sort and haversinMeters put 8154434.476304402 m apart are not matched by any of the three distance queries with exactly that radius. The cause is GeoUtils.distanceQuerySortKey, which turns the radius into a sort-key threshold by binary search: it returns the first key it meets whose distance equals the radius, not the largest such key, so a point on a larger key of the same distance fails 'key <= threshold', and when no key has exactly that distance it returns the smallest key whose distance exceeds the radius.

It replaced the exact per-document check SloppyMath.haversinMeters(...) <= radiusMeters with haversinSortKey(...) <= sortKey(radiusMeters), where sortKey is the binary search that is still GeoUtils.distanceQuerySortKey. bugs.title: XYShape circle queries miss lines and polygons that enter the circle only near its extreme x or y, and can report CONTAINS for a polygon the circle sticks out of, when the centre coordinate is large relative to the radius, because XYRectangle.fromPointDistance rounds the circle's bounding box inward

Instead INTERSECTS finds nothing and DISJOINT matches the document, because XYRectangle.fromPointDistance builds the circle's bounding box as x + nextUp(r) in float, which rounds to nearest (2^23 + 1.3 becomes 2^23 + 1), and since 8.6.0 Circle2D's Cartesian contains rejects every point outside that too-small box before its exact distance test, including the segment's closest point to the centre. bugs.area: spatial3d / geom outside distance (Plane.arcDistance and Plane.linearDistance behind GeoStandardCircle and GeoExactCircle computeOutsideDistance; user-facing Geo3DDocValuesField.newOutsideDistanceSort via Geo3DPointOutsideDistanceComparator)
bugs.title: On WGS84 and other non-spherical planet models, the outside distance from a point to a geo3d circle smaller than about 50 km is +Infinity in most directions (GeoCircle.computeOutsideDistance with the ARC or LINEAR style, and so Geo3DDocValuesField.newOutsideDistanceSort, which then sorts valid documents as if they had no value), because Plane.arcDistance and Plane.linearDistance look for the edge on the line where the circle's plane meets a plane through the origin, the plane normal and the point, and on an ellipsoid that line misses a small circle
bugs.summary: You build a 1 km circle on the default WGS84 planet model (GeoCircleFactory.makeGeoCircle, or Geo3DDocValuesField.newOutsideDistanceSort with maxRadiusMeters 1000) and ask for the outside distance of points 3 km from the centre, expecting about 2 km in every direction (0.0 inside, distance to the edge outside). Instead computeOutsideDistance returns +Infinity at 10 of 12 bearings (only due north and due south are right), and the sort gives most documents outside the circle +Infinity, the value the javadoc reserves for documents missing the field, so they sort last. The cause: Plane.arcDistance and Plane.linearDistance look for the nearest edge point on the line where the circle's plane meets a plane through the origin, the plane normal and the point; on a sphere that line passes through the circle's centre, but on an ellipsoid the circle plane's normal is tilted, the line passes about 21 km from the circle at latitude 40, and for a smaller circle it finds no edge point at all, so the minimum keeps its +Infinity start value.

bugs.area: spatial3d / geom path outside distance (GeoStandardPath segment endpoints; Geo3DDocValuesField.newOutsidePathSort)
bugs.title: GeoStandardPath outside distance measures end caps (and one-point paths) to the end point instead of the cap edge, so values are too large by up to the path half-width and Geo3DDocValuesField.newOutsidePathSort misorders documents
bugs.summary: You build a path with a width (GeoPathFactory.makeGeoPath, or the pathWidthMeters of Geo3DDocValuesField.newOutsidePathSort) and ask for the outside distance of a point beyond one of its ends, expecting 'the distance from a point to the closest outside edge' (GeoOutsideDistance), which is how the same path measures points beside its segments and how GeoCircle measures a circle. Instead you get the distance to the path's end point, i.e. the gap plus up to the half-width: on the unit sphere a point 0.001 rad beyond the end of a path of half-width 0.01 gets 0.011, a one-point path reports 0.011 where the same-size GeoCircle reports 0.001, the value jumps from 0 to about the half-width as a point crosses the end cap's edge, and on WGS84 the outside-path sort ranks a document 1 km beyond the end of a path of half-width 5 km (5992 m) after one 3 km beside it (3067 m). The cause is BaseSegmentEndpoint.outsideDistance, which every endpoint with a width inherits: it measures to the end point itself, which is the edge only for a zero-width path.

bugs.area: spatial3d / geom shape relationships (GeoBaseAreaShape.getRelationship with GeoStandardCircle's single edge point and Plane.intersects' tangency test), reached through the spatial-extras Geo3d spatial4j adapter (Geo3dShape.relate, SpatialOperation IsWithin/Contains, SerializedDVStrategy, CompositeSpatialStrategy)
bugs.title: Geo3d reports two shapes that touch at a single point as nested (WITHIN/CONTAINS) instead of overlapping when the touch point is a circle's one sampled edge point, so IsWithin and Contains spatial queries (SerializedDVStrategy, CompositeSpatialStrategy) return circles that lie mostly outside the query shape
bugs.summary: You create a circle and a box (or a second circle) that touch at exactly one point, for example with the Geo3d spatial context a 20-degree circle centred at latitude 55 and a box whose southern edge is latitude 75, and expect relate to report INTERSECTS (shapes that share a point intersect, and spatial3d may only weaken WITHIN to OVERLAPS, never the reverse). Instead it reports WITHIN or CONTAINS, as if one shape were inside the other: GeoBaseAreaShape.getRelationship infers nesting from sampled edge points plus a plane-intersection test, a standard circle has a single edge point, and when that point lies on the other shape's boundary the 1e-12 membership test counts it as inside while Plane.intersects' one-solution test misses the touch. So SerializedDVStrategy's IsWithin(box) returns the circle although its centre is 20 degrees outside the box, while radius 19.9 or 20.1 degrees gives the correct DISJOINT or INTERSECTS.

bugs.area: spatial3d / geom bounding boxes (GeoBBox.expand in the 13 GeoBBox classes with a longitude range, GeoBBoxFactory.makeGeoBBox); spatial-extras / spatial4j Geo3D context (Geo3dRectangleShape.getBuffered, reached by spatial4j's WKT BUFFER)
bugs.title: GeoBBox.expand clamps a widened longitude bound at +-180 degrees instead of wrapping it across the antimeridian, so expanded geo3d boxes (and Geo3dRectangleShape.getBuffered / WKT BUFFER(ENVELOPE(...)) in a Geo3D spatial context) miss the part beyond the dateline
bugs.summary: You take a geo3d box whose east edge is near the dateline, for example longitudes [2.5, 3.0] radians, and call expand(0.3), or in a Geo3D spatial context you search 'Intersects(BUFFER(ENVELOPE(172, 178, 4, -4), 4))'. You expect each bound to move out by the angle, so the box now crosses the dateline and reaches -2.983 radians (-178 degrees), as the same code already does for a box that crosses the dateline and as spatial4j's own geo rectangle buffer does. Instead expand passes the unwrapped bound 3.3 to GeoBBoxFactory.makeGeoBBox, which clamps it to PI, so the box stops at 180 degrees and a document at (-179.5, 1) is not found (0 hits instead of 1); the west edge and all 13 GeoBBox classes with a longitude range behave the same way.

bugs.area: spatial3d / geom bounding boxes (GeoDegenerateLatitudeZone, which GeoBBoxFactory.makeGeoBBox returns for a box with equal top and bottom latitude spanning all longitudes), reached through Geo3DPoint.newBoxQuery / newShapeQuery and the spatial-extras Geo3D spatial context (Geo3dShape.relate, RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy, CompositeSpatialStrategy)
bugs.title: GeoDegenerateLatitudeZone.isWithin compares z with sin(latitude) at a 1e-10 tolerance instead of using its own planet-model plane, so a zero-height geo3d box spanning all longitudes rejects the points on its own latitude on WGS84 and, on any planet model, can report CONTAINS for areas just below it, which makes Geo3D prefix-tree searches match points tens of degrees away
bugs.summary: You build a geo3d box whose top and bottom latitude are equal and which spans all longitudes, for example GeoBBoxFactory.makeGeoBBox(WGS84, 0.5, 0.5, -PI, PI), and expect it to contain exactly the points on that latitude, as the same line over [-179, 179] degrees does. Its isWithin compares a point's z with sin(latitude), the unit-sphere value, with a 1e-10 tolerance, instead of the planet-model plane that the class builds and uses everywhere else, so on WGS84 it rejects every point on its own latitude (and accepts a parallel about 1.2 km away). On any planet model, including the default sphere of the Geo3D spatial context, the 100x looser tolerance makes getRelationship report that the line CONTAINS a rectangle just below it, so a prefix-tree Intersects query for rect(-180, 180, 45.000000001, 45.000000001) matched 4 points at latitudes 10, 10, 30 and 44 degrees, while the [-179, 179] control matched none.

bugs.area: spatial3d / geom exact-circle outside distance (GeoExactCircle.outsideDistance, reached through GeoCircleFactory.makeExactGeoCircle and GeoOutsideDistance.computeOutsideDistance)
bugs.title: GeoExactCircle.computeOutsideDistance never measures the slice end points where two of its approximation slices meet, so a point outside whose nearest edge point is such a joint gets +Infinity or the distance to the far side of the circle: on WGS84 every point due north or due south of the centre, at any radius; on the sphere a point 0.001 rad due west of a 1e-4 rad exact circle gets 0.0012
bugs.summary: You build an exact circle on the default WGS84 planet model (GeoCircleFactory.makeExactGeoCircle, centre latitude 0.3 and longitude 0.2, radius 0.1 rad, about 637 km, accuracy 1e-6) and ask computeOutsideDistance for a point 0.11 rad due north of the centre, expecting 'the distance from a point to the closest outside edge' (GeoOutsideDistance), about 0.0096. Instead you get +Infinity, and the same for every point due north or due south at any distance; on the unit sphere a point 0.001 rad due west of a 1e-4 rad exact circle gets 0.0012, the distance to the far side of the circle. The cause: GeoExactCircle.outsideDistance takes the minimum of each slice's plane distance bounded to that slice's sector and never measures the slice end points, so when the nearest edge point is a joint between two slices, the point's foot on each neighbouring plane falls just outside its sector, both return +Infinity, and the minimum is +Infinity or a foot on the far side.

bugs.area: spatial-extras / prefix trees (QuadPrefixTree, PackedQuadPrefixTree under RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy)
bugs.title: QuadPrefixTree/PackedQuadPrefixTree with non-power-of-two world bounds put a point that lies on a grid line into a cell whose shape excludes it, so Intersects misses the document (deep trees throw InvalidShapeException)
bugs.summary: You index a point with RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy over a QuadPrefixTree (or PackedQuadPrefixTree) in a non-geo SpatialContext whose world bounds are not powers of two, such as Web Mercator's +/-pi*6378137, and the point lies exactly on a grid line (for example longitude 45 degrees projected, at y = 0) or on the world's east edge. You expect Intersects with that same point, or with a box whose edge passes through it, to find the document, because getCell is documented to return 'the cell containing point p' and the query error may only inflate a shape, never shrink it. Instead getCell chooses the cell by comparing the point with mid-points accumulated one way while QuadCell.makeShape rebuilds that cell's edges another way, the two floating-point results differ by one ulp, so the indexed cell's shape ends just short of the point, the query treats it as disjoint and returns 0 hits (and with the 50-level factory default a query for a point on the world's top edge throws InvalidShapeException).

bugs.area: spatial-extras / prefix trees (S2PrefixTree and S2PrefixTreeCell under RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy; Contains through ContainsPrefixTreeQuery)
bugs.title: S2PrefixTree: a Contains query whose shape is a point P misses a document indexed with that same point P when P lies on an S2 cell edge (the equator, an S2 face edge, (0,0)), because the query side follows every child cell that touches P while indexing puts P in one cell per level
bugs.summary: You index a document with point P through RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy over S2PrefixTree in the Geo3d spatial context and search with SpatialOperation.Contains and the same point P, expecting the document, because Contains is documented as the OGC 'Covers' predicate and its evaluate(P, P) is true, RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy builds a ContainsPrefixTreeQuery for it, a point query is resolved at full precision, and the geohash and quad trees do return the document. When P lies exactly on an S2 cell edge, for example Point(10, 0) on the equator, Contains finds 0 documents while Intersects finds 1. Indexing puts P in one cell per level (S2PrefixTree.getTreeCellIterator, from S2CellId.fromLatLng), but at query time S2PrefixTreeCell.getNextLevelCells has no point case and returns every child cell that touches P (2 on an edge, 4 at (0,0)), and ContainsPrefixTreeQuery requires the document to be in all of them.

bugs.area: spatial-extras / prefix trees: PackedQuadPrefixTree point-to-cell lookup (RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy and CompositeSpatialStrategy point queries)
bugs.title: PackedQuadPrefixTree in a geo context indexes a point at longitude +180 under the -180 edge cell, but point queries look in the +180 edge cell, so RPT and CompositeSpatialStrategy Intersects/Contains with that same point miss the document
bugs.summary: You index a point at longitude +180, for example Pt(180, 10), with RecursivePrefixTreeStrategy over PackedQuadPrefixTree(SpatialContext.GEO, 8) and query Intersects or Contains with that same point; the document must match, since a point intersects and contains itself and the prefix-tree approximation may only add matches (SpatialArgs: the error 'should not shrink' the shape). Instead the query returns 0 hits, and so does CompositeSpatialStrategy's Intersects: indexing keeps the first cell in Z order whose rectangle relates to the point, and a geo rectangle treats +180 as -180, so the point is stored in the cells at the -180 edge, while the point query's cell lookup (PackedQuadPrefixTree.getCell, a mid-point walk since LUCENE-8755 in 8.3.0) sends x=+180 to the cells at the +180 edge. The same point at -180, QuadPrefixTree, and a rectangle query touching +180 still find the document.

bugs.area: spatial-extras / PointVectorStrategy (Intersects and IsWithin rectangle queries: makeWithin x filter)
bugs.title: PointVectorStrategy misses a point at longitude +180 or -180 when a rectangle query that does not cross the dateline has its edge on that meridian with the other sign (-180 vs +180)
bugs.summary: You index a point with PointVectorStrategy in the default geo context and search it with SpatialOperation.Intersects or IsWithin and a rectangle that does not cross the dateline but has one edge on the antimeridian, expecting the point to be found whenever spatial4j's relate, which defines these predicates, says it is inside (in geo, -180 and +180 are the same meridian). Instead a point stored at x=+180 is missed by a box whose west edge is -180 (Pt(180,0) with rect(-180,-170,-10,10): 0 hits, oracle 1), and a point at x=-180 by a box whose east edge is +180 (Pt(-180,0) with rect(170,180,-10,10)). BBoxStrategy and both prefix-tree strategies in the same module return the hit; PointVectorStrategy.makeWithin filters x with one plain DoublePoint range [minX, maxX] for every non-crossing box, so +180 and -180 are different values to it.
bugs.introduced_commit: 6f1fde90512 (branch_4x, svn r1381280; trunk equivalent 1db287ce640, svn r1381230), 'LUCENE-4351 Update to Spatial4j 0.3' (issue apache/lucene#5417), by dsmiley, no PR (SVN + JIRA patch era) [exec]. Behavioural introduction: the commit changed no line of the x filter; it bumped spatial4j 0.2 to 0.3. spatial4j 0.2 normalized longitude +180 to -180 in makePoint/makeRect and its relate treated the two values as different, so the plain range agreed with the oracle; from 0.3 on, +180 is kept and relate treats +/-180 as one meridian. Code origin [read]: the plain x range dates from the module import 66a852234d4 (LUCENE-3795, 2012-02-20); the current crossing/non-crossing shape of makeWithin is from LUCENE-4389 'Fix TwoDoubles dateline support' (#5455; trunk 922c7316d81, branch_4x ed444bdac7d, 2012-09-15), which handled only boxes that cross the dateline

bugs.area: spatial-extras / prefix trees (DateRangePrefixTree date parsing: parseCalendar, also reached through NumberRangePrefixTree.parseShape for single dates and range bounds)
bugs.title: DateRangePrefixTree.parseCalendar (and parseShape) rejects day 32 but accepts a day that its month does not have (2014-11-31, 2014-02-30, 2013-02-29) and silently rolls it into the next month, so the range [2014-11-01 TO 2014-11-31] also matches December 1st
bugs.summary: You parse a date such as 2014-11-31, or a range such as [2014-11-01 TO 2014-11-31], with DateRangePrefixTree.parseCalendar or parseShape and expect a ParseException, which the parser has given since LUCENE-8640 for day 32, month 13, hour 25 and minute 60. Instead the day is checked only against 1..31 and set on a lenient java.util.Calendar, which moves it into the next month when the fields are read: 2014-11-31 becomes 2014-12-01, 2014-02-30 becomes 2014-03-02, and the range parses to [2014-11 TO 2014-12-01], so an Intersects query on a NumberRangePrefixTreeStrategy index also returns a document dated 2014-12-01.
bugs.introduced_commit: bb267a143e009f7b1375f7fa9755b76fcc82ec4f (trunk, svn r1600555, 'LUCENE-5648: DateRangePrefixTree and NumberRangePrefixTreeStrategy', author GitHub dsmiley; branch_5x got it through the bulk backport 55594bad9b0, LUCENE-5944, 2014-09-18; no PR, svn era, JIRA LUCENE-5648 is now GitHub #6710): the parser set the parsed day on a lenient Calendar from the start, at first with no field validation at all (day 32 and month 13 rolled over too). The specific inconsistency, day 32 rejected but a day past the month's end rolled over, dates from 8e69d12dd7e2b6d2341322e4ac7e5c33b789507a ('LUCENE-8640: date range syntax validation', committed by GitHub mkhludnev, 2019-01-26; backports d482312b854 branch_8x and 62ee5df5e17 branch_7x; issue #9686; the contributed PR apache/lucene-solr#538 was closed and the change committed directly), which added parseAndCheck with fixed per-field bounds (day 1..31) and no month-length check [read]. bugs.area: core document / LatLon distance sort (LatLonPointDistanceComparator competitive bounding box, Rectangle.fromPointDistance pad)
bugs.title: LatLon distance sort from a pole origin: the competitive bounding box (7 cm margin) rejects documents that tie with the queue bottom near the opposite pole, so the secondary SortField is skipped and top-N and searchAfter results are wrong
bugs.summary: You index two points about 45 cm from the north pole with LatLonDocValuesField and sort with Sort(LatLonDocValuesField.newDistanceSort("p", -90, 146.5868...), new SortField("tie", INT)); both documents report the same distance (2.0015113815150492E7 m) and search(n=2) correctly returns [1, 0], the tie broken by "tie". You expect search(n=1) to return that head, doc 1, and one-hit searchAfter pages to return [1, 0]. Instead search(n=1) returns doc 0 and the pages return only doc 0: once doc 0 is the queue bottom, the comparator's pruning box (radius = the bottom's sloppy distance + 7 cm) leaves out doc 1, whose exact distance near the antipode exceeds that sloppy distance by more than 7 cm, so compareBottom returns -1 instead of 0 without computing doc 1's equal key and the secondary sort never runs.

bugs.area: core document + geo / LatLon box queries (the newBoxQuery/newSlowBoxQuery 90/180 special case vs Rectangle2D.create and LatLonShapeBoundingBoxQuery)
bugs.title: LatLonPoint and LatLonDocValuesField box queries at exactly latitude 90 (box lat 90..90) or longitude 180..180 match nothing through newBoxQuery/newSlowBoxQuery but match the edge point through the Rectangle2D-based paths of the same field, so one point is reported as neither INTERSECTS nor DISJOINT (8.8.0 to main)
bugs.summary: You index one point at (90, 0) with LatLonPoint (stored at the top encoded latitude, 89.99999995809048) and query the box lat 90..90, lon -180..180 through LatLonPoint.newGeometryQuery, expecting the point to be either INTERSECTS or DISJOINT and every box path of the field to agree. Instead INTERSECTS, which newGeometryQuery routes to newBoxQuery and its deliberate MatchNoDocsQuery for minLatitude == 90, matches 0 docs; DISJOINT, which goes through Rectangle2D.create (commented 'behavior of LatLonPoint.newBoxQuery' but copying only the dateline part of that special case, then rounding the box up onto the top row with a saturating encodeLatitudeCeil), also matches 0; WITHIN, INTERSECTS(box, box), LatLonPointQuery and LatLonShape.newBoxQuery match 1. LatLonDocValuesField's slow queries behave the same, a box lon 180..180 over a point at (0, 180) gives the same pattern, and upstream's own equivalence assertion (BaseLatLonPointTestCase.testBoundingBoxQueriesEquivalence: count(newBoxQuery) == count(LatLonPointQuery INTERSECTS)) fails for this box, 0 vs 1.
