bugs.area: search / CachingCollector first pass and score-caching replay (CachingCollector, CachingCollectorManager)
bugs.title: CachingCollector (and CachingCollectorManager) never calls LeafCollector#finish on the collector it wraps, nor on the second-pass collector when it replays cached scores, so finish-dependent collectors such as FacetsCollector silently report no hits
bugs.summary: You wrap a FacetsCollector, or any collector that does its per-segment work in LeafCollector#finish, in a CachingCollector or CachingCollectorManager so you can run the query once and replay the hits later, or you replay a score-caching cache into such a collector, and you expect the same facet counts as a plain IndexSearcher search. Instead the collector reports no hits: CachingCollector's per-leaf wrapper overrides finish for its own bookkeeping and never passes the call on, and the score-caching replay never calls finish at all, although the no-score replay does. In the repro a query that matches 20 documents gives 0 matching docs, with no error unless assertions are enabled.

bugs.area: grouping / GroupReducer and SecondPassGroupingCollector (second-pass per-group collectors)
bugs.title: SecondPassGroupingCollector and GroupReducer never call LeafCollector#finish on the per-group leaf collectors, so a custom GroupReducer whose collector does its per-segment work in finish (for example a stock FacetsCollector per group) silently sees no documents
bugs.summary: You write a GroupReducer that gives each group its own FacetsCollector (or any collector that compiles a segment's results in LeafCollector#finish), run it through SecondPassGroupingCollector, and expect each group's collector to see the documents of its group, as GroupReducer's javadoc says and as a plain IndexSearcher search would give. Instead every group's FacetsCollector reports no documents, with no error: GroupReducer.setNextReader replaces each group's leaf collector on every segment without calling finish on the previous one, GroupReducer has no finish hook, and SecondPassGroupingCollector does not override finish, so IndexSearcher's per-leaf finish reaches only the outer collector. In the repro 5 documents in 2 segments are routed to groups a (3) and b (2), yet both groups report 0 hits; with assertions enabled FacetsCollector throws AssertionError on the second segment instead.

bugs.area: grouping / GroupReducer and SecondPassGroupingCollector (second-pass per-group collectors)
bugs.title: GroupReducer lets one group's CollectionTerminatedException escape SecondPassGroupingCollector, so IndexSearcher ends the whole segment and every other group silently misses its remaining documents in that segment
bugs.summary: You write a GroupReducer whose per-group collector needs only the first documents of its group in a segment (for example a stock TopFieldCollector in index order with a hit threshold of 1, which then throws CollectionTerminatedException, as collectors may), run it through SecondPassGroupingCollector, and expect every group's collector still to see the documents of its own group, as GroupReducer's javadoc says and as MultiCollector does for its children. Instead GroupReducer.collect does not catch the exception, SecondPassGroupingCollector passes it on, and IndexSearcher ends the segment for the whole second pass, so all the other groups silently miss their remaining documents in that segment. In the repro one segment holds docs 0-2 in group a and docs 3-4 in group b: group a's collector stops on doc 1, group b reports no hit instead of doc 3, and the second pass counts 2 of 5 documents.

bugs.area: codecs / vectors (flat scalar-quantized format: byte kNN and byte similarity search)
bugs.title: The flat scalar-quantized vectors format (Lucene104ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat) accepts BYTE vector fields but its byte search is a no-op, so unfiltered byte kNN and byte similarity queries return no hits
bugs.summary: You index a BYTE vector field with Lucene104ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat, a registered stand-alone flat (brute-force) format that accepts BYTE fields without error and searches its FLOAT32 and FLOAT16 fields by scoring every vector, and expect a byte kNN query to return the k nearest documents. Instead the reader hands byte searches to the raw flat reader, whose search method does nothing, so an unfiltered KnnByteVectorQuery returns 0 hits and ByteVectorSimilarityQuery.Adaptive with threshold 0 matches 0 of 10 documents, with no error. The same kNN query with a term filter that matches every document returns the exact top 3, because the filtered path falls back to exact search when the reader returns too few hits.

bugs.area: grouping / range group selectors (LongRangeFactory and DoubleRangeFactory, used by LongRangeGroupSelector and DoubleRangeGroupSelector)
bugs.title: Grouping LongRangeFactory and DoubleRangeFactory give the last range below max the full width, so its reported group bounds run past max and overlap the range for values >= max
bugs.summary: You group documents with new LongRangeFactory(10, 10, 25), meaning buckets 10 wide starting at 10 and everything at or above 25 in one bucket, and expect what the javadoc says: [10, 20), a shorter final bucket [20, 25), and [25, MAX). Instead the value 22 is labelled LongRange(20, 30) while 27 is labelled LongRange(25, MAX), so the two reported ranges overlap; each group holds the right documents, but a range query built from the label [20, 30), the way Lucene's own selector tests rebuild a group, also returns the document with value 27 from the other group. DoubleRangeFactory behaves the same, because both getRange methods set the bucket's upper bound to its lower bound + width and never cap it at max.

bugs.summary: You group documents by a double field with new DoubleRangeFactory(0, 0.1, 10), buckets 0.1 wide, and expect each group's DoubleRange label to contain the values grouped under it, because DoubleRange is documented as [min, max). Instead the value 0.6 is grouped under DoubleRange(0.5, 0.6), which excludes 0.6, and 1.7 under DoubleRange(1.7000000000000002, 1.8000000000000003); 27 of the 100 values 0.0, 0.1,..., 9.9 lie outside their own label, adjacent labels leave gaps (no label contains 0.6) or overlap, and a range query built from a label misses or picks up documents (values 0.55, 0.6, 0.65 form a group DoubleRange(0.5, 0.6) of 2 documents whose label matches 1). The cause is that getRange picks the bucket with Math.floor((value - min) / width) but computes its bounds separately as min + bucket * width and then that + width, and the three roundings disagree near boundaries; group membership itself stays consistent.

bugs.area: grouping / range group selectors (DoubleRangeFactory, used by DoubleRangeGroupSelector)
bugs.title: Grouping DoubleRangeFactory gives the below-min group the lower bound Double.MIN_VALUE (4.9E-324, the smallest positive double) instead of the most negative value, so that group's DoubleRange label does not contain its own members
bugs.summary: You group documents by a double field with new DoubleRangeFactory(-10, 5, 10), meaning buckets 5 wide from -10 to 10 and every value below -10 in one bucket, and expect the bucket returned for -20 to be a [min, max) range that contains -20, the way LongRangeFactory returns [Long.MIN_VALUE, -10). Instead DoubleRangeFactory returns DoubleRange(4.9E-324, -10.0): it uses Double.MIN_VALUE as the lower end, and Double.MIN_VALUE is the smallest positive double, not the most negative one, so the range is inverted and holds none of its members (with min > 0 it leaves out 0.0 and every negative member). Each group still holds the right documents, but its reported bounds are wrong, and a range query built from them, the way Lucene's own selector tests rebuild a group, finds none or only some of the group's documents.

bugs.area: document / range fields (DoubleRange, FloatRange, their doc-values fields; facet range-on-range)
bugs.title: DoubleRange and FloatRange accept the bounds [0.0, -0.0] and store them inverted, so range queries silently miss such documents and contradict each other (WITHIN [0,0] but not INTERSECTS [0,0])
bugs.summary: You index a DoubleRange or FloatRange with min 0.0 and max -0.0 (Java's negative zero, numerically equal to 0.0); the constructor accepts it, as it accepts [0.0, 0.0], so you expect queries to treat it as the point zero, or else an IllegalArgumentException like the one thrown for every other min > max pair. Instead Lucene stores the bounds in its sort order, where -0.0 is below 0.0, so the stored range is inverted: the document matches newWithinQuery [0,0] and newIntersectsQuery [-1,1] but not newIntersectsQuery [0,0] or newIntersectsQuery of its own bounds. The same happens with the doc-values slow intersects query and range-on-range facet counts, and a query with bounds [0.0, -0.0] misses a document [0.0, 0.0] that newContainsQuery with the same bounds matches.

bugs.area: facet / range facet counts (DoubleRange bounds and values converted to sortable longs in DoubleRangeFacetCounts, against DoubleRange.accept and getQuery)
bugs.title: DoubleRangeFacetCounts orders -0.0 below +0.0 while DoubleRange.accept and getQuery treat the two zeros as equal: a document holding a zero of the opposite sign at an inclusive zero bound (for example -0.0 in [0, 1]) is matched by the range's own drill-down but not counted, and the accepted range [+0.0, -0.0] makes counting throw
bugs.summary: You count range facets over a double field with DoubleRangeFacetCounts and a range that starts at an inclusive 0.0, such as new DoubleRange("[0, 1]", 0.0, true, 1.0, true), and some documents hold -0.0 (Java's negative zero, which ordinary arithmetic such as Math.ceil(-0.25) or -1 * 0.0 produces). You expect the count to include every document the range accepts, because DoubleRange.accept and the range's own drill-down query getQuery compare with primitive >= and <=, treat -0.0 as equal to 0.0, and match those documents. Instead the counter converts bounds and values with NumericUtils.doubleToSortableLong, where -0.0 sorts below +0.0, so those documents are silently left out of the count (likewise +0.0 at an inclusive -0.0 upper bound), and the range [+0.0, -0.0], which the DoubleRange constructor accepts, makes DoubleRangeFacetCounts throw IllegalArgumentException 'matches nothing'.

bugs.area: facet / range, rangeonrange and facetset (exclusive-bound adjustment of double and float ranges: range.DoubleRange, rangeonrange.DoubleRange, facetset.DimRange.fromDoubles/fromFloats)
bugs.title: Facet DoubleRange, range-on-range DoubleRange and DimRange.fromDoubles/fromFloats do not exclude an exclusive bound that is an infinity: the empty ranges (+Inf, +Inf] and [-Inf, -Inf) are accepted and match the +Infinity / -Infinity documents instead of matching nothing
bugs.summary: You build a facet range with an exclusive bound that is an infinity, for example new DoubleRange("> +Inf", Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY, false, Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY, true), meaning 'value > +Infinity', or the mirror [-Inf, -Inf) 'value < -Infinity'. No double is greater than +Infinity, so you expect a range that matches nothing, rejected with IllegalArgumentException 'matches nothing' as the class does for other empty ranges and as LongRange and DimRange.fromLongs do for an exclusive Long.MAX_VALUE bound. Instead the constructor makes the bound inclusive with Math.nextUp (or Math.nextAfter / Math.nextDown for the max), which leaves an infinity unchanged, so the range becomes [+Inf, +Inf]: DoubleRangeFacetCounts counts and the drill-down query matches every +Infinity document, and the copies in rangeonrange.DoubleRange and DimRange.fromDoubles/fromFloats count the same documents.

bugs.title: DoubleDocValuesStats and SortedDoubleDocValuesStats (lucene/misc) return mean = NaN instead of +/-Infinity when any value is collected after an infinite value, so the mean of {+Infinity, 1.0} is NaN while the mean of {1.0, +Infinity} is +Infinity
bugs.summary: You collect statistics for a double doc-values field with DocValuesStats.DoubleDocValuesStats (or SortedDoubleDocValuesStats) and expect mean, documented as 'the mean of all values of the field', to be +Infinity for the values {+Infinity, 1.0}: that is sum/count, and it is what java.util.DoubleSummaryStatistics, the oracle of the upstream test, returns. Instead mean is NaN, because the running update mean += (val - mean) / count computes Infinity - Infinity as soon as the running mean is infinite and another value arrives; {+Infinity, +Infinity} also gives NaN, while sum and max report +Infinity. The answer depends on document order ({1.0, +Infinity} gives +Infinity) and, since 10.5.0, on the searcher: with an executor and one segment per slice, DocValuesStatsCollectorManager rebuilds the mean from the sums and returns +Infinity.

bugs.area: benchmark / quality (utils.SubmissionReport, the TREC run-file writer used by QualityBenchmark and QueryDriver)
bugs.title: SubmissionReport writes scores of 1000 or more with a grouping comma ("1,200.5000") into the TREC run file that QueryDriver documents as the submission file for trec_eval, so trec_eval reads such a score as 1.0 and ranks those hits wrongly
bugs.summary: You evaluate search quality with lucene/benchmark's SubmissionReport, for example through QueryDriver, whose usage text calls the output the 'submission file for trec_eval', and expect the score column of each TREC run line (qid Q0 docno rank score tag) to be a plain number. SubmissionReport formats scores with NumberFormat.getInstance(Locale.ROOT) and never turns grouping off, so a hit scoring 1200.5 is written as '1,200.5000'. trec_eval reads that column with C atof, which stops at the comma and returns 1.0, and then re-sorts the run by the parsed score, so a run [1200.5, 900.25] is evaluated as [900.25, 1.0], with the top hit moved down, and the reported metrics are silently wrong.

bugs.title: QualityStats.average(stats).getPrecisionAt(n) is not the mean per-query precision at n when n is above the mean result count: the mean that average stored is replaced by a second extrapolation (mean P@10 0.4 instead of 0.6)
bugs.summary: You evaluate search quality with QualityBenchmark, average the per-query results with QualityStats.average(stats) and ask the average for its precision at 10, expecting the mean of the per-query P@10 values (which, like trec_eval's P_10, already count missing ranks as non-relevant). If the queries returned different numbers of results and their mean is below 10, getPrecisionAt(10) ignores the correct mean that average stored and extrapolates again from the precision at the mean result count: with setMaxResults(10), a query whose 10 hits are all relevant (P@10 = 1.0) and a query whose only 2 hits are relevant (P@10 = 0.2) give 0.4 instead of 0.6. bugs.area: facet / taxonomy facets (TopOrdAndFloatQueue order of float-valued child labels in getTopChildren: float association and value-source facets)
bugs.title: Float taxonomy facets: if one child label aggregates to NaN, getTopChildren can return a lower-valued label in place of a higher one (a=5, b=NaN, c=10 gives top-1 [a]), because TopOrdAndFloatQueue compares values with < and >; a regression in 9.11.0 from #12966
bugs.summary: You aggregate a float weight per taxonomy label (FloatAssociationFacetField, or a DoubleValuesSource such as the expression clicks / impressions) and call getTopChildren(k), documented to return 'the topN child labels'. If one label's value is NaN (a=5, b=NaN, c=10), getTopChildren(1) returns [a (5.0)] although c=10 outranks a, and getTopChildren(2) returns [b (NaN), c (10.0)], so the top-1 is not even in the top-2, whatever rank NaN should get. TopOrdAndFloatQueue.OrdAndFloat#lessThan compares with < and > and otherwise falls back to the ordinal, so NaN ties with every value, the order is not transitive and the heap keeps the wrong labels; #12966 (9.11.0) let NaN-valued labels into this queue and, in the same change, ordered dims with the NaN-safe Float.compare.

bugs.area: grouping / function grouping (core util.mutable: MutableValueFloat and MutableValueDouble equality)
bugs.title: MutableValueFloat and MutableValueDouble equals compare with ==, so a NaN value is not equal to itself and grouping by a float or double function puts NaN documents into empty groups (released versions) or throws IllegalArgumentException (main)
bugs.summary: You group search hits by a float or double function, for example new DoubleFieldSource("v") or a 0/0 division, and some documents have the value NaN; you expect them to form one NaN group, because MutableValueDouble's own hashCode (doubleToLongBits) and compareTo (Double.compare) treat every NaN as one value. Instead equalsSameType compares with ==, under which NaN is not even equal to itself, so on released versions every NaN document becomes its own group, each such group comes back with 0 documents and the NaN documents drop out of the grouped hit count. On main the same search fails with IllegalArgumentException 'group values differ across shards', because the result merge compares the NaN group value with itself.

bugs.title: Taxonomy Facets#getAllDims sorts float-valued dims with a NaN-unsafe < / > comparator, so one dim whose value is NaN puts the other dims out of value order, breaks the documented rule that getTopDims equals the first entries of getAllDims, and with 32 or more dims can make getAllDims throw 'Comparison method violates its general contract!' If one dim's value is NaN (dims a=1, b=NaN, c=2), getAllDims can return [a=1.0, b=NaN, c=2.0], with a ahead of c, while getTopDims(1, 10) returns [b=NaN]; with 32 or more dims, getAllDims can instead throw IllegalArgumentException 'Comparison method violates its general contract!' from List.sort. bugs.area: spatial3d / geom circles (GeoStandardCircle cut plane and SidedPlane sidedness, behind Geo3DPoint.newDistanceQuery and GeoCircleFactory.makeGeoCircle)
bugs.title: Geo3D circles with a radius between about 2e-5 m and 12 cm take the inside of their cut plane from the sign of rounding noise, so Geo3DPoint.newDistanceQuery with such a radius can match every point document on the planet
bugs.summary: You build a Geo3D distance query with a very small radius, for example Geo3DPoint.newDistanceQuery with 1.24 cm, and expect it to match only points near the centre, or to be rejected as too small. The circle's cut plane passes within about r^2/2 of the circle's centre (here about 2e-18), far below double rounding, and SidedPlane takes the plane's inside from the sign of evaluate(center), which at that size is rounding noise. When the noise has the wrong sign the circle is the whole planet minus a speck, and the query silently returns every indexed point: in the repro, all 3 documents thousands of kilometres away.

bugs.area: search / phrase queries (SloppyPhraseMatcher repetition groups: gatherRptGroups, non-multi-term branch)
bugs.title: A sloppy PhraseQuery in which two different terms each repeat (for example "a b a b"~1) misses documents of a segment, exact-phrase matches included, when the segment's first candidate document has two of those terms stacked at one position, because SloppyPhraseMatcher builds its repetition groups once, from that document, by position instead of by term
bugs.summary: You index text into a field whose analysis can put two words at one position (for example an index-time synonym) and search with a sloppy phrase such as "a b a b"~1, in which two different words each repeat; you expect every document within the slop, and certainly every document that holds the exact phrase, to match, whatever other documents share its segment. SloppyPhraseMatcher works out which phrase positions repeat each other only once per segment, on the first candidate document, and groups them by equal position in that document rather than by term, so when that document has a and b stacked at one position both words land in one group and the matcher then asks for more occurrences than exist. That document and later documents of the segment are missed with no error: in the two-document repro the plain document 'a b a b' matches with slop 0 but not with slop 1, while the same document indexed alone matches with slop 1.

bugs.area: search / phrase queries (SloppyPhraseMatcher repetition groups: gatherRptGroups same-offset exclusion, collide, advanceRepeatGroups, sortRptGroups tie order)
bugs.title: A sloppy PhraseQuery or MultiPhraseQuery with two entries at one position that a third entry pulls into the same repetition group misses documents its exact (slop 0) form matches, and for MultiPhraseQuery one unchanged query matches on some evaluations and misses on others, because SloppyPhraseMatcher checks its 'same offset is not a repetition' rule only pairwise and breaks equal-offset ties in HashSet order
bugs.summary: You build a sloppy phrase query by hand with two entries at the same position, for example PhraseQuery a@0 a@1 a@1 (the second 'a' added twice at position 1), and expect slop 1 to match everything slop 0 matches and the query to give the same answer every time it runs. SloppyPhraseMatcher's rule that two entries from one query position are not repetitions of each other is checked only pairwise, so a third entry (a@0) pulls both into one repetition group and the matcher then forces them onto different document positions: the document 'a a' matches with slop 0 but not with slop 1 to 4. For MultiPhraseQuery the same collision is resolved in HashSet iteration order, because groups are sorted by offset only, so the one immutable query (a|b)@0 b@2 a@2 ~2 on one unchanged reader matches the document a@0, a@1 with b@1 stacked, a@2 in about half of 200 evaluations and misses it in the rest, with no error.
bugs.introduced_commit: c54608b60dc6fb3e451dd1d3c430cf42c38f5fb5 (trunk r1173961, 2011-09-22, LUCENE-3215 'SloppyPhraseScorer sometimes computes Infinite freq', apache/lucene#4288; branch_3x backport a398352a0cbc09542c07a64ba5b35569f13ea77d, r1174002, same day) for the PhraseQuery manifestation: the rewrite replaced the pairwise conflict check that LUCENE-3068 (3.2.0) had made skip equal-offset pairs with repeat chains that test the equal offset only against the chain's first PP. The MultiPhraseQuery nondeterminism came with LUCENE-3821 (apache/lucene#4894, still open; branch_3x cf54f6523f9a50cc92c46f89ae84667a764f6cc3, r1299077, 2012-03-09; trunk 187bfe2ebc4555e93b71d6fe463d14d1a3b45932, r1299112, 2012-03-10), which brought HashSet<PhrasePositions> back for multi-term repeat groups with an offset-only sort. git blame on main attributes the grouping-loop lines (SloppyPhraseMatcher.java:565, 570-572) to c54608b60dc and lesser, collide, advanceRepeatGroups, sortRptGroups and most of gatherRptGroups to 187bfe2ebc4. bugs.area: search / IndexSearcher#count (two-clause term-disjunction shortcut, GITHUB#13036) under IndexSearcher#setTimeout
bugs.title: IndexSearcher#count on a two-term disjunction over-counts, even above maxDoc, when the searcher timeout fires while the intersection is counted
bugs.summary: You set a timeout with IndexSearcher#setTimeout and call IndexSearcher#count on a query like `a OR b`, where term b matches far fewer documents than term a, on an index without deletions. When the timeout fires you expect a partial count, at most the number of matching documents, which is what every other count and collect path returns under the same timeout (and what this path returned up to 9.9.2). Instead count returns count(a) + count(b) minus a cut-short count of `a AND b`, which is too high (1041 for a 1000-document index with 955 matches when the deadline has already passed) and gets smaller, not larger, when the timeout fires later; timedOut is true.

bugs.area: search / kNN query rewrite (AbstractKnnVectorQuery optimistic re-entry pass) under the IndexSearcher timeout
bugs.title: A multi-segment kNN query's optimistic second pass, when cut short by the IndexSearcher timeout, replaces the hits a complete first pass already found, so a later timeout can return fewer or farther hits than an earlier one, down to 0 hits
bugs.summary: You set a timeout with IndexSearcher#setTimeout and run a kNN query on an index with several segments; Lucene searches every segment once and, if that first pass completed, searches the segments that supplied the best hits a second time to improve the answer. You expect a timeout to give you the partial results found so far ('Return partial results only when timeout is met', AbstractKnnVectorQuery.java:296), so hits that the complete first pass already found are kept. Instead, when the timeout fires during the second pass, each re-entered segment's cut-short second-pass result (usually empty) replaces its first-pass hits, so the query keeps fewer or farther hits than a slightly earlier timeout would have given, down to 0 hits (IndexSearcher#count goes 6 -> 0 when one more timeout check is allowed).

bugs.area: index / doc values (single-valued SortedSetDocValues view, DocValuesRangeIterator)
bugs.title: SingletonSortedSetDocValues.intoBitSet does not refresh its cached ordinal, so nextOrd returns an earlier document's ordinal and DocValuesRangeIterator.forOrdinalRange can return extra hits on single-valued segments
bugs.summary: You take the SortedSetDocValues of a segment whose documents have at most one value each (DocValues.getSortedSet and LeafReader#getSortedSetDocValues then return a single-valued wrapper), call intoBitSet(upTo,...), and read nextOrd for the document the iterator now sits on; or you pass that view to DocValuesRangeIterator.forOrdinalRange on a skip-indexed field and load the matches in bulk. You expect nextOrd to describe the current document, as after the nextDoc loop that the intoBitSet javadoc says it behaves exactly like, and the range iterator to mark only documents whose value is in range. Instead the wrapper's intoBitSet moves the inner iterator without refreshing its cached ordinal, so with two documents a and b nextOrd on doc 1 returns a's ordinal, and forOrdinalRange for [b, b] also marks doc 8192, whose value is a.

The visible forOrdinalRange extra hit also needs the SortedSetDocValues factory (#15989) and the batched sorted-set range path (#16172), both first released in 10.5.0; they rely on the intoBitSet contract that #14618 broke and are not themselves the defect [read]

bugs.area: codecs / doc values (Lucene90 sparse multi-valued sorted-numeric rangeIntoBitSet)
bugs.title: Sparse multi-valued SortedNumericDocValues#rangeIntoBitSet
bugs.summary: On a default-codec index with docs {0: [1,3], 1: no value, 2: [5,7]} in a multi-valued numeric doc-values field, you call advanceExact(1) on the field's SortedNumericDocValues (it returns false) and then rangeIntoBitSet(1, 3, 1, 3, bits, 0) on the same iterator. You expect no bit, because neither doc 1 nor doc 2 has a value in [1, 3], and that is what the method's documented per-document default returns from the same state. Instead the codec's override evaluates doc 1 with doc 0's values and marks it (in a DENSE block it uses the next valued document's values), and when no earlier document has values ({0: no value, 1: [1,3], 2: [5,7]}, advanceExact(0) then rangeIntoBitSet(0, 3, 1, 3,...)) it throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index -1.

bugs.area: index / MultiDocValues merged norms view (also the merged reader passed to MergePolicy.OneMerge#reorder)
bugs.title: MultiDocValues norms view (also the merged reader passed to MergePolicy.OneMerge#reorder): advance(target) returns a document before target when target's segment has no norms for the field, so queries over that view can return duplicate or non-matching hits
bugs.summary: You read the norms of a multi-segment index as one merged iterator (MultiDocValues.getNormValues(reader, "body"), or LeafReader#getNormValues on the merged reader that IndexWriter hands to a custom OneMerge#reorder), where doc 0's segment has the text field "body", docs 1-2 sit in a segment without it and doc 3's segment has it again, and call advance(1) on a fresh iterator. You expect 3, the first document at or after the target that has a norm, as the DocIdSetIterator#advance contract says and as the merged numeric doc-values view of the same index returns. Instead advance(1) returns 0, a document before the target, because advance falls back to nextDoc before it records which segment comes next, so nextDoc restarts from the first segment; queries over that view inherit the backward step (FieldExistsQuery with intra-segment partitions returns [0, 0, 0, 3] instead of [0, 3], and a conjunction can return a document that fails one of its FILTER clauses).

bugs.title: SortedDocValues#ordinalRangeIntoBitSet's default implementation, called after advanceExact(d) returned false, reads ordValue for doc d, which has no value, so it marks d using a neighbouring document's ordinal (or throws EOFException)

bugs.title: SlowCodecReaderWrapper's KnnVectorsReader.getVectorCount (new in 10.6.0) returns the vector count of the SegmentReader under every FilterLeafReader/FilterCodecReader layer instead of the wrapped view's, so it disagrees with get*VectorValues(field).size of the same reader (6 instead of 3 for a view that exposes 3 of 6 vectors), and it throws NullPointerException for a vector field that the view adds

Instead seekExact("b") returns false, seekCeil("b") throws EOFException (or, in a segment whose terms file is larger than about 7 KB, returns NOT_FOUND with a made-up term) and next after a24 throws, because seekExact(ord) loads only the target block and deliberately leaves the enum unpositioned, while the TermState seek's 'already on this term' shortcut marks it positioned anyway, so the next call reuses parent frames that were never loaded.

bugs.area: memory / MemoryIndex stored fields (StoredFieldVisitor protocol)
bugs.title: MemoryIndex's StoredFields.document offers the visitor fields that have no stored value and asks needsField only once per field name instead of once per stored value, so LazyDocument fails with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException or silently loses values, and per-value NO/STOP decisions are ignored
bugs.summary: You add a document with an indexed-only field body (TextField, Store.NO) and a stored field tag with two values t1, t2 to a MemoryIndex and read it through storedFields.document(0, visitor), with a visitor that records its needsField calls or with LazyDocument's lazy-loading pattern from TestLazyDocument, expecting what an IndexWriter index gives for the same document: one needsField(tag) per stored value, never a question about body, and the lazy values tag=t1, tag=t2. Instead MemoryIndex asks about body, which has no stored value, asks about tag only once and then delivers both values on that single YES, because its loop calls needsField once per field name before it checks whether the field has stored values. bugs.area: search / IndriAndQuery (clause Occur handling in matching and explain)
bugs.title: IndriAndQuery accepts MUST, FILTER and MUST_NOT clauses without complaint but ignores them when matching (it always matches the union of all clauses), while its explain does read MUST/FILTER, so it explains some of its own hits as non-matches
bugs.summary: You build an IndriAndQuery from BooleanClauses with Occur values other than SHOULD, for example [MUST f:a, FILTER acl:x] or [SHOULD f:a, MUST_NOT f:secret], which the public constructor accepts, and run it. You expect either the meaning that BooleanClause.Occur documents (the same clauses in a BooleanQuery give {0, 2} and {0, 1}) or a rejection, and in any case an explain that agrees with the hits. Instead IndriAndWeight builds one disjunction over all clauses whatever their Occur, so MUST and FILTER clauses do not restrict ({0, 1, 2, 3}), a MUST_NOT clause adds the very documents it names ({0, 1, 2}; a lone MUST_NOT clause returns exactly them), and IndriAndWeight.explain, which does treat MUST/FILTER clauses as required, explains such hits as non-matches.

bugs.area: store / NRTCachingDirectory (commit durability: IndexWriter.startCommit, SegmentInfos.prepareCommit/finishCommit)
bugs.title: NRTCachingDirectory.sync creates a commit's cached segment files in the underlying directory after the commit's directory fsync, so an OS crash right after the segments_N rename can leave a newest commit whose files are missing and an index that will not open
bugs.summary: You index through NRTCachingDirectory (for example new NRTCachingDirectory(FSDirectory.open(path), 5.0, 60.0), the class javadoc's own example), call IndexWriter.commit, and the machine crashes during that commit. You expect what Lucene's commit protocol and LUCENE-8048 are built for: after the crash the index opens to the previous commit or to the new one, because SegmentInfos.prepareCommit fsyncs the directory before the commit is published by renaming pending_segments_N to segments_N. Instead the newly flushed segment files are still in NRTCachingDirectory's RAM cache at that directory fsync; NRTCachingDirectory.sync creates them on disk only afterwards and fsyncs their bytes but never the directory, so the rename can become durable before the new files' names do, and in that crash state every open fails (CorruptSegmentInfoException: segment info file _1.si cannot be read), while the same steps on a plain FSDirectory open fine.

bugs.area: index / commit protocol failure cleanup (SegmentInfos.finishCommit, IndexWriter.finishCommit and rollback)
bugs.title: If Directory.rename(pending_segments_N, segments_N) throws after it took effect, the failed commit leaves the new segments_N in the index (SegmentInfos.finishCommit deletes only pending_segments_N), and IndexWriter then deletes files that this newest segments_N references, so DirectoryReader.open and a new IndexWriter fail until the file is removed by hand (every release since 5.0.0; the rename-branch residual of LUCENE-9477)
bugs.summary: You commit through a Directory whose rename(pending_segments_2, segments_2) creates segments_2 and then throws an IOException; commit throws, the writer stays open (the failure is not tragic), and you expect the index to still be the last good commit segments_1, which is what LUCENE-9477 made Lucene do when the directory sync right after the rename fails. Instead SegmentInfos.finishCommit deletes only pending_segments_2, so segments_2 stays in the directory unknown to the writer; as soon as a merge removes the segments it references (a merge that finishes during the commit's fsync, or any merge before the writer is closed or rolled back) the writer deletes their files, and DirectoryReader.open, and after a restart a new IndexWriter, fail with CorruptSegmentInfoException '_1.si cannot be read' although segments_1 and its files are intact. Without a merge, rollback or close deletes the failed commit's files before the stray segments_2 with no directory fsync in between, so a process kill or OS crash in that window leaves the same unopenable index.

If that later filter adds an attribute the tee did not have yet, for example PorterStemFilter adding KeywordAttribute for a stemmed field next to an unstemmed sink field, the sink lacks it, because its attributes are a cloneAttributes snapshot taken when it was created, and its restoreState throws IllegalArgumentException ('State contains AttributeImpl of type...KeywordAttributeImpl that is not in in this AttributeSource') on the first token, so addDocument rejects the document. bugs.title: Loading some well-formed hyphenation grammars (e.g. the current TeX Afrikaans patterns) throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, because TernaryTree.insert(char, int, char) sizes its node arrays with strlen(key) instead of strlen(key, start)
bugs.summary: You load a well-formed FOP-format hyphenation grammar with HyphenationCompoundWordTokenFilter.getHyphenationTree (or HyphenationTree.loadPatterns, or the factory's hyphenator file) and expect it to load, as the TernaryTree javadoc's 'room for about 65000 nodes' suggests. For some grammars, for example the current TeX Afrikaans patterns or the repro's 1,310 random 4-8-letter patterns, loading instead throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 2048 out of bounds for length 2048 from TernaryTree.insert, called by compact during trimToSize. The cause: insert(char key, int start, char val) reserves room for strlen(key) + 1 nodes counted from index 0 instead of from start, and its only caller with start > 0, compact, passes a key array whose index 0 is an empty string, so it reserves one node and a multi-node insert that crosses the 2048-node block boundary writes past the arrays; with strlen(key, start), the bound the String overload already uses, every failing grammar loads with all values right.

bugs.area: analysis-common / hunspell WordStorage (dictionary word hash table)
bugs.title: Hunspell Dictionary fails to load with 'Too many collisions' when its entry count is a multiple of 961, because WordStorage takes the raw String.hashCode modulo the table size (for example the en_US dictionary plus a 300-word custom list)
bugs.summary: You load a Hunspell dictionary, for example the stock en_US dictionary plus a custom list of 300 words through HunspellStemFilterFactory's documented dictionary="en_US.dic,custom.dic" pattern, and expect it to load as it does with 299 or 301 custom words. Instead the Dictionary constructor throws RuntimeException 'Too many collisions. Try a larger Dictionary#hashFactor (now 1.0). If this doesn't help, please report this to dev@lucene.apache.org', so the analyzer cannot be built. WordStorage puts every word into slot Math.abs(String.hashCode % tableSize) with tableSize = entry count x hashFactor (default 1.0); when that size is a multiple of 961 = 31*31, the slot of a short word depends almost only on its last two letters (31^2 divides every earlier term of the unmixed radix-31 hash), so short words with a common ending (six-letter '-er' words in en_US) pile into a few slots and one exceeds the hard limit of 20 entries.

bugs.area: suggest / ternary search tree suggester (TSTLookup.build: rebuild failure atomicity and rebuild consistency)
bugs.title: TSTLookup.build empties its tree before it reads the new input but resets its count only after the input is sorted, so a rebuild that throws while the input is read or sorted leaves a lookup that suggests nothing while getCount and store/load still report the previous build; lookups made while a rebuild reads its input also find nothing
bugs.summary: You build a TSTLookup from {foo/10, bar/5}, rebuild it from a dictionary whose stream throws IOException after its first line, catch the exception and keep using the lookup. You expect either the previous build (lookup('fo') returns foo and getCount 2), which FSTCompletionLookup, WFSTCompletionLookup and AnalyzingSuggester keep after the same failed rebuild, or an empty lookup with getCount 0. Instead lookup('fo') returns nothing while getCount still returns 2, and store+load carry that state into a new lookup, because build replaces the tree with an empty one before it reads and sorts the input and resets the count only after that; for the same reason a lookup made while a rebuild is still reading its input finds nothing.

bugs.title: NearestFuzzyQuery (used by KNearestFuzzyClassifier) computes idf from reader.numDocs (live documents) and reader.docFreq (which still counts deleted documents), so when deleted documents that are not yet merged away make up most of the index the idf is negative and rewrite throws 'boost must be a positive float' (released since 8.0.0)

Instead both throw IllegalArgumentException 'boost must be a positive float, got -0.25276297'. bugs.area: queries / MoreLikeThis boosted query construction (MoreLikeThis.createQuery boost normalisation)
bugs.title: MoreLikeThis with setBoost(true) divides every term's score by the lowest selected score, so a selected term that scores 0 (a TFIDFSimilarity whose idf is 0, such as the textbook log(N/df) for a term in every document) makes like throw 'boost must be a positive float, got NaN' (8.0 and later) or build NaN and Infinity boosts (4.10 to 7.x)

You expect a query with finite, non-negative boosts: the same call works with setBoost(false), and BoostQuery accepts a boost of 0. Instead createQuery divides each term's score by the first score popped from its ascending queue, which is the lowest selected score (0 here), so the zero-score term's boost is 0/0 = NaN and like throws IllegalArgumentException 'boost must be a positive float, got NaN' on 8.0 and later, or builds the query with NaN and Infinity boosts on 4.10 to 7.x.

bugs.area: suggest / analyzing infix suggester (AnalyzingInfixSuggester NRT add/update/refresh after build; inherited unchanged by BlendedInfixSuggester [read])
bugs.title: AnalyzingInfixSuggester.ensureOpen publishes its new IndexWriter before the SearcherManager opened on it and does not undo that when the manager cannot be opened, so refresh refreshes the manager over build's closed writer and throws AlreadyClosedException
bugs.summary: You build an AnalyzingInfixSuggester with the default closeIndexWriterOnBuild=true, add a suggestion and call refresh, and you expect the addition to become visible, as the add/update javadoc says, or at worst refresh to be the no-op its own comment describes. The first add after build runs ensureOpen, which assigns the writer field before it installs the SearcherManager opened on that writer, and refresh (no lock) reads writer != null as 'the current manager is live', so in that gap it refreshes build's old manager, whose writer is closed, and throws AlreadyClosedException 'this IndexWriter is closed'. The gap is transient when refresh runs on another thread during that first add (or, contested, during a rebuild), and permanent after one IOException while ensureOpen opens the manager: writer stays set, no later add repairs it, and every refresh fails until build or a reopen.

It made build close its writer by default while leaving the SearcherManager opened on that writer installed, added refresh's 'writer != null' gate, and so made the first add after build reopen a writer through ensureOpen. The writer-before-SearcherManager order and the missing rollback in ensureOpen are older (LUCENE-5889 / #6951, 4a485d68771 on trunk and e4731cf8a36, first released in 5.0.0) but could not reach a closed writer before 6.4.0. bugs.title: Monitor.match can throw NullPointerException while queries are being registered (or while a read-only Monitor refreshes), because QueryIndex keeps its per-reader term filters in a plain HashMap that the searcher refresh and reader-close listeners modify while match threads read it without a lock
bugs.summary: You share one Monitor between threads: some threads call Monitor.match on documents while another registers new queries, and each register commits and opens a new query-index searcher, which the Monitor's design for searches during commits allows. bugs.area: suggest / analyzing suggester (AnalyzingSuggester.build and getCount, inherited by FuzzySuggester)
bugs.title: AnalyzingSuggester and FuzzySuggester getCount counts analyzed paths instead of entries when the analyzer produces a token graph (synonyms, word-delimiter graphs), and store/load persist the inflated count
bugs.summary: You build an AnalyzingSuggester or FuzzySuggester from the two entries 'fast car' and 'red car' with an analyzer whose synonym rule maps fast to {fast, quick}, and you expect getCount to return 2, because Lookup#getCount is documented as 'the number of entries the lookup was built with'. bugs.area: highlighter / UnifiedHighlighter passage selection (FieldHighlighter.highlightOffsetsEnums passage-queue sizing; maxPassages is never range-checked by UnifiedHighlighter.highlightFieldsAsObjects)
bugs.title: UnifiedHighlighter with maxPassages = Integer.MAX_VALUE throws a message-less IllegalArgumentException for every document that has a match (FieldHighlighter sizes its passage queue with Math.min(64, maxPassages + 1), which wraps)
bugs.summary: You ask the UnifiedHighlighter for at most Integer.MAX_VALUE passages, meaning 'no limit', and expect the same snippet that 1000 or Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1 gives (or, if the value is not allowed, an IllegalArgumentException that says so). Instead, for every document that has a match, FieldHighlighter.highlightOffsetsEnums sizes its passage queue with Math.min(64, maxPassages + 1); the + 1 wraps to Integer.MIN_VALUE, Math.min returns it, and the java.util.PriorityQueue constructor throws an IllegalArgumentException with no message. With per-field counts such as {1, MAX_VALUE} the field that asked for one passage loses its snippet too, because the whole call throws.

bugs.area: search / TermInSetQuery visitor (consumeTermsMatching automaton supplier over the util/automaton string-union builder's 1000-byte term limit), reached from highlighter / UnifiedHighlighter without WEIGHT_MATCHES
bugs.title: TermInSetQuery#visit gives QueryVisitor an automaton supplier that throws IllegalArgumentException when any term is longer than 1000 bytes, so UnifiedHighlighter without WEIGHT_MATCHES fails on such a query
bugs.summary: You search with a TermInSetQuery of the two terms 'short' and a 1001-byte term on a field indexed with offsets, get the hit, and highlight it with a UnifiedHighlighter built with withWeightMatches(false), expecting 'a short text', which is what the documented equivalent (a ConstantScoreQuery over a BooleanQuery of SHOULD TermQuery clauses) gives. Instead highlight throws IllegalArgumentException 'This builder doesn't allow terms that are larger than 1000 UTF-8 bytes', and any QueryVisitor that asks the query for its automaton gets the same exception. For more than one term TermInSetQuery#visit hands visitors a supplier that builds Automata.makeBinaryStringUnion over all terms, and that builder rejects terms longer than Automata.MAX_STRING_UNION_TERM_LENGTH (1000 bytes, a guard for its recursive construction), although the query itself accepts such terms and searches with them.

GITHUB#12320 (52ace7eb3564 on main, 349b458e8895 on branch_9x, 2023-06-02, author gsmiller, first released in 9.7.0) moved the supplier to Automata.makeBinaryStringUnion, so since 9.7.0 the limit is the string-union builder's 1000-byte term limit from LUCENE-8429 (d78feb22361, 2018) [read]; the bug was kept, only the message changed.

bugs.area: highlighter / TermVectorLeafReader (LeafReader over one document's term vectors; LeafMetaData invariant)
bugs.title: TermVectorLeafReader.getMetaData always throws IllegalArgumentException ('minVersion must be set when createdVersionMajor is >= 7'), so a TermVectorLeafReader cannot be searched with a Sort, wrapped in a ParallelLeafReader or copied with addIndexes
bugs.summary: You build a TermVectorLeafReader over one document's term vectors (new TermVectorLeafReader(field, terms), the public helper that 'wraps a Terms with a LeafReader') and use it like any other LeafReader, expecting getMetaData to return metadata with no index sort, as MemoryIndex's in-memory reader does. Instead getMetaData throws IllegalArgumentException('minVersion must be set when createdVersionMajor is >= 7') on every call, because it passes minVersion=null together with createdVersionMajor=Version.LATEST.major, a combination the LeafMetaData constructor rejects. So a field-sorted search (even with Sort.RELEVANCE), new ParallelLeafReader(reader) and addIndexes(SlowCodecReaderWrapper.wrap(reader)) all fail; a plain relevance search without a Sort works.

bugs.title: QualityQuery.compareTo is not a total order when numeric and non-numeric topic ids are mixed (ints compared as numbers, everything else as strings), so TrecTopicsReader and Trec1MQReader.readQueries, and with them QueryDriver, can throw IllegalArgumentException 'Comparison method violates its general contract!'
bugs.summary: You read a TREC topics file with TrecTopicsReader or Trec1MQReader (as QueryDriver does) whose ids are mostly numbers but include a few sub-topic ids such as 1a or 10.1, or a few digit-only ids larger than Integer.MAX_VALUE, and expect the topics back sorted by id, as the readers' '// sort result array (by ID)' comment says. Instead QualityQuery.compareTo compares two int ids as numbers and every other pair as strings, which forms cycles (2 < 100 as numbers, 100 < 1a and 1a < 2 as strings), so Arrays.sort can throw IllegalArgumentException 'Comparison method violates its general contract!' (the repro: ids 1..111 plus 1a, 20a, 64a and 99a, each listed after its parent); when the sort does not detect the cycle, the topics come back in an order that depends on the file order. Separately, the int branch returns n - nOther, which overflows for extreme ids such as 2147483647 vs -1 (this needs a negative id).
bugs.introduced_commit: 98fa2d898d18, LUCENE-836 'Add support for search quality benchmarking' (migrated as apache/lucene#1911; SVN era, no PR): added QualityQuery.compareTo (n - nOther when both ids parse as int, else String.compareTo) and TrecTopicsReader's Arrays.sort(qq) under '// sort result array (by ID)'. Trec1MQReader, with the same Arrays.sort(qq), came in 9e65cd554f2 (LUCENE-1116, apache/lucene#2193), before 2.3.0 was tagged. Later edits to compareTo are cosmetic: a0776e5cd0a (2009, compareTo(Object) to compareTo(QualityQuery)), e2f54df3ca7 (2012, @Override), 7f8b7ffbcad (2021, reformatting), 2971f311a2b and ba7f659b1d8 (2021, 2025, catch-variable form). bugs.area: misc / index: BpVectorReorderer merge-time reordering (BPReorderingMergePolicy) over core / index: SortingCodecReader vector views
bugs.title: addIndexes of a SortingCodecReader (including the reader that BPIndexReorderer.reorder returns) into a writer that uses BPReorderingMergePolicy with BpVectorReorderer throws UnsupportedOperationException, because SortingCodecReader's vector views do not support copy
bugs.summary: You pass a SortingCodecReader, for example the reader that BPIndexReorderer.reorder returns or SortingCodecReader.wrap(reader, docMap, null), to IndexWriter#addIndexes on a writer whose merge policy is BPReorderingMergePolicy with a BpVectorReorderer, and expect the documents to be added and reordered, as they are for plain segment readers and as the same policy does with the postings BPIndexReorderer. Instead addIndexes throws UnsupportedOperationException and adds nothing: the policy reorders addIndexes as a forced merge, BpVectorReorderer's per-thread state calls copy on the input's float vector values, and SortingCodecReader's vector views throw from copy (with several such readers in one call the throw comes through SlowCompositeCodecReaderWrapper's merged copy). Making copy work is not enough on its own: BpVectorReorderer then treats the sorting view's ordinals as doc order, so the reordering is silently applied in the wrong doc space.
bugs.introduced_commit: 02a09f6ab124e994fd1af42965617c8b5ec67bcc, apache/lucene#14097 'HNSW BP reordering' (by msokolov, merged to main 2025-01-07, milestone 11.0.0, never backported): it added BpVectorReorderer, whose PerThreadState constructor calls vectors.copy (BpVectorReorderer.java:110, unchanged since), and let BPReorderingMergePolicy take any IndexReorderer [exec]. Precondition, not the failure by itself: SortingFloatVectorValues.copy and SortingByteVectorValues.copy throw UnsupportedOperationException since 6053e1e3137 (apache/lucene#13779, 2024-09-28, a deliberate partial implementation; first released in 10.0.0); the float16 view's throw came with bfe5c847d3c (#16383, 2026-07-27, main only).

bugs.area: misc / index tools (MultiPassIndexSplitter.split, output IndexWriterConfig); IndexWriter.addIndexes field-role checks
bugs.title: MultiPassIndexSplitter builds every output part with a bare IndexWriterConfig and accepts no config, so it cannot split any index that uses soft deletes (7.4.0+) or has a parent field (9.10.0+): split and its command line throw IllegalArgumentException before any part gets a document
bugs.summary: You split an index with MultiPassIndexSplitter, for example one written with IndexWriterConfig#setSoftDeletesField("soft") and a single softUpdateDocument call, or one written with IndexWriterConfig#setParentField("_parent"), and expect it to split like any other index: the split javadoc says the source 'can have deletions, can have multiple segments (or multiple readers)', and the only documented limitation is that document blocks may be broken up. Instead split opens every part's IndexWriter with new IndexWriterConfig(null), which names no soft-deletes or parent field and cannot be replaced by the caller, so IndexWriter.addIndexes rejects the input's field infos with IllegalArgumentException ('this index has [soft] as soft-deletes already but soft-deletes field is not configured in IWC', or 'can't add field [_parent] as parent document field; this IndexWriter has no parent document field configured') and nothing is split.

bugs.area: join / ToParentBlockJoinSortField string sort (ToParentDocValues missing-child ordinals, since #15727)
bugs.title: ToParentBlockJoinSortField on a STRING field with max-child selection and childMissingValue=STRING_LAST throws IndexOutOfBoundsException when a parent has children both with and without the field
bugs.summary: You sort parent documents by a string field of their children, descending, with new ToParentBlockJoinSortField("s", STRING, reverse=true, null, SortField.STRING_LAST, parents, children) (or the 8-argument form with reverseChildren=true), and expect the search to return the parents with children that lack the field sorted as missing-last, because the javadoc lists STRING_LAST as a legal child missing value that 'participates in the min/max selection among siblings'. Instead, as soon as the search collects a parent that has one child with the field and another child without it, it throws IndexOutOfBoundsException from the doc-values terms dictionary (Lucene90DocValuesProducer$TermsDict.seekExact via ToParentDocValues$SortedDVs.lookupOrd), with -ea and -da. The cause is that the block-join wrapper reports 'a missing child, sorted last, won the max' as the ordinal Integer.MAX_VALUE, and the string comparator TermOrdValComparator treats every ordinal other than -1 as a real one and looks it up.

bugs.area: codecs / HnswBitVectorsFormat x index / IndexingChain aborting-exception classification
bugs.title: A float vector field routed to HnswBitVectorsFormat is rejected inside an aborting step of the indexing chain, so the one rejected document closes the IndexWriter and rolls back every document added since the last commit
bugs.summary: You use HnswBitVectorsFormat, which accepts only byte vectors, and by mistake add a document with a float vector field (KnnFloatVectorField) that is new to the index. You expect addDocument to reject that one document with IllegalArgumentException and the writer to stay open, as the format's own test TestHnswBitVectorsFormat#testFloatVectorFails expects the exception and as happens for the same codec's dimension limit and for a vector dimension mismatch. Instead the check sits in KnnVectorsWriter#addField, which IndexingChain calls after registering the field and treats as an aborting step, so the exception also becomes the writer's tragic exception: IndexWriter closes itself, the next call throws AlreadyClosedException, and the documents added since the last commit are gone (the repro ends with 1 committed document instead of 3).

bugs.area: index / IndexingChain inversion with custom term frequencies (TermVectorsConsumerPerField, FreqProxTermsWriterPerField) x aborting-exception classification
bugs.title: A document rejected for a custom TermFrequencyAttribute on a field with term-vector positions or offsets, postings positions or DOCS-only postings is rejected inside an aborting step of the indexing chain, so it closes the IndexWriter and rolls back every change since the last commit
bugs.summary: You index a document whose analysis chain sets a custom term frequency (TermFrequencyAttribute, for example DelimitedTermFrequencyTokenFilter with a token like 'red|2') on a field that also stores term-vector positions or offsets, indexes postings positions (a default TextField), or is DOCS-only and repeats the term. You expect addDocument to reject only that document with its usual IllegalArgumentException or IllegalStateException and the writer to stay open, as it does for the neighbouring offset checks and for the duplicate-term check that #15584 made non-aborting. Instead the four checks run inside termsHashPerField.add, which IndexingChain treats as aborting, so the rejection also becomes the writer's tragic exception: IndexWriter closes itself, the next call throws AlreadyClosedException, and everything since the last commit is lost (the repro ends with 1 committed document instead of 3).
bugs.introduced_commit: d276acfbbcb8ea6124fe486e35cea9eb928e4702, 'LUCENE-7854: enable indexing custom term frequencies' by mikemccand (JIRA-patch workflow, issue migrated to #8905; no GitHub PR), which created TermFrequencyAttribute together with all four rejection checks: TermVectorsConsumerPerField.getTermFreq (term-vector positions, term-vector offsets), FreqProxTermsWriterPerField.getTermFreq (postings positions) and the !hasFreq check in FreqProxTermsWriterPerField.addTerm (DOCS-only, repeated term) [read]. All four run inside termsHashPerField.add, which DefaultIndexingChain already wrapped as aborting in the parent commit (catch (Throwable th) { throw AbortingException.wrap(th); }), and LUCENE-5987 (5.0.0) had made aborting exceptions close the writer; LUCENE-8205 later replaced AbortingException.wrap with onAbortingException with identical behaviour [read]. The defect is the placement of the checks, present since the feature was created; isolation is by API absence (the probe cannot compile on 6.6.0 or 6.6.6, TermFrequencyAttribute being the only missing symbol)

bugs.area: analysis / hunspell (Stemmer affix removal)
bugs.title: Hunspell COMPLEXPREFIXES: after removing the second prefix the Stemmer keeps removing prefixes, so words with three prefixes are accepted and a zero-length prefix recurses until StackOverflowError (also in HunspellStemFilter, where it closes the IndexWriter)
bugs.summary: You load a hunspell dictionary that sets COMPLEXPREFIXES (twofold prefix stripping, meant for morphologically complex right-to-left languages) and chains prefixes through continuation classes, and expect at most two prefixes per word, as hunspell(5), C Hunspell and Lucene up to 9.4.2 do. Instead, after removing the second prefix the Stemmer goes on removing prefixes: with prefixes a, b, c chained on root x, the three-prefix word cbax is accepted by spell and stemmed to x, and with a zero-length prefix that only passes on a flag (PFX A 0 0/B), the same prefix is removed again and again without shortening the word, so spell("bbx"), getRoots("bx") and HunspellStemFilter throw StackOverflowError. Inside IndexWriter.addDocument that Error closes the writer, and every later addDocument throws AlreadyClosedException.

bugs.area: spatial3d / Geo3DPoint polygon and shape queries (Geo3DUtil.fromPolygon, PointInGeo3DShapeQuery, PointInShapeIntersectVisitor)
bugs.title: Geo3DPoint.newPolygonQuery turns a degenerate polygon (for example three vertices on the equator) into an empty GeoCompositePolygon that is meant to match nothing, but every search with the query throws NullPointerException; Geo3DPoint.newShapeQuery with an empty GeoCompositePolygon fails the same way
bugs.summary: You build Geo3DPoint.newPolygonQuery from an org.apache.lucene.geo.Polygon that Polygon accepts but whose vertices all lie on one great circle, for example lat {0,0,0,0} and lon {0,1,2,0}, and expect a query that matches nothing: Geo3DUtil.fromPolygon recognizes the polygon as degenerate ('// Polygon is degenerate') and deliberately replaces it with an empty GeoCompositePolygon. Instead every search with the query throws NullPointerException ('Cannot invoke Double.doubleValue because the return value of XYZBounds.getMinimumX is null'), because the empty shape adds nothing to its XYZBounds and the PointInShapeIntersectVisitor constructor unboxes the null bounds. Geo3DPoint.newShapeQuery with an empty GeoCompositePolygon fails the same way, while LatLonPoint.newPolygonQuery returns 0 hits for the same Polygon and newLargePolygonQuery rejects it with IllegalArgumentException when the query is built.

bugs.area: spatial3d / Geo3DDocValuesField outside-distance sort fields (Geo3DPointOutsideSortField equality)
bugs.title: Geo3DPointOutsideSortField.equals casts its argument to the sibling class Geo3DPointSortField, so comparing two distinct outside-distance sort fields on the same field (directly, through Sort.equals, or in a HashMap keyed by Sort) throws ClassCastException instead of returning true or false
bugs.summary: You build the same outside-distance sort twice, for example Geo3DDocValuesField.newOutsideDistanceSort("loc", 10, 20, 1000, PlanetModel.WGS84), and compare the two with equals, with Sort.equals, or by looking one up in a HashMap keyed by Sort, and expect true (or false for two different shapes), which is what the inside-distance sort gives. Instead equals throws ClassCastException ('Geo3DPointOutsideSortField cannot be cast to class Geo3DPointSortField'): the method was copied from the sibling class Geo3DPointSortField and still casts to that class right after checking that both objects are Geo3DPointOutsideSortField, so the cast can never succeed. bugs.area: misc / store DirectIODirectory (direct-I/O merge buffers)
bugs.title: DirectIODirectory accepts a mergeBufferSize that is not a multiple of the file system block size, and then every direct-I/O read fails, so merges hit a tragic exception; a size below the block size can also give a zero-capacity write buffer (BufferOverflowException, or writeBytes making no progress)
bugs.summary: You create DirectIODirectory(FSDirectory, mergeBufferSize, minBytesDirect) with a mergeBufferSize that is not a multiple of the file system block size (for example 100000, or 4 * 4096 + 100, on a 4 KiB-block file system) and expect merges to read and write through direct I/O as usual, because the constructor documents the value only as 'Size of buffer to use for merging' and accepts any int. Instead every fresh top-level DirectIOIndexInput fails on its first read with IllegalArgumentException 'Negative position' or IOException 'Channel position... is not a multiple of the block size', so a merge that reads through direct I/O fails while opening its segment readers and IndexWriter closes on a tragic exception (the index on disk stays intact, but the error sometimes surfaces as CorruptIndexException); with a size below the block size, some fresh outputs throw BufferOverflowException on the first writeByte and writeBytes on such an output loops without progress. The cause is that the direct buffers are aligned slices whose capacity is always a block multiple (and can be 0), while DirectIOIndexInput starts its file position at -mergeBufferSize and then advances it by the buffer's capacity, so the first read lands at -(mergeBufferSize mod blockSize) or at blockSize - (mergeBufferSize mod blockSize).

It created DirectIODirectory with aligned-slice buffers (capacity a block multiple,:233 and:372-376) while the top-level input kept starting at filePos = -bufferSize (:342) and fill advances by buffer.capacity (:497), and it deleted the predecessor NativeUnixDirectory's constructor check 'mergeBufferSize must be 0 mod ' + ALIGN (added by 005fec5a58e, LUCENE-2795, 2012; that check tested a single bit). None of the 15 later commits to the file changes the start position or the capacity step, or validates the size; the defect was in the class's first version

bugs.area: queries / function queries (ValueSource context map under concurrent search)
bugs.title: FunctionQuery, FunctionRangeQuery and ValueSource sort fields share one non-thread-safe context map across the slices of an executor search, and scale (ScaleFloatFunction) writes to it during the search, so when that write grows the map the search throws NullPointerException or silently returns different scores

bugs.area: queries / payloads (SpanPayloadCheckQuery.toString, reached from SpanWeight.explain)
bugs.title: SpanPayloadCheckQuery.toString and IndexSearcher.explain throw NullPointerException when payloadToMatch contains a null entry, although the matcher accepts null as 'no payload at this position' and the query searches and counts correctly (since 5.4.0, LUCENE-6716)
bugs.summary: You build a SpanPayloadCheckQuery over the span 'a b' with payloadToMatch = [null, 'p'], meaning that 'a' must have no payload and 'b' the payload 'p'; the matcher supports exactly this (a null entry matches a position without a payload, a non-null entry never does), and the search finds the document. You expect toString to print the query and IndexSearcher.explain to explain the hit. Both throw NullPointerException ('Cannot read field "bytes" because "termText" is null'), because toString hands every entry, null included, to Term.toString(BytesRef), and explain builds its description from the query string.

bugs.area: search / CachingCollector replay (CachingCollector, CachingCollectorManager)
bugs.title: CachingCollector#replay (and CachingCollectorManager#replay) lets a CollectionTerminatedException from the second-pass collector escape to the caller instead of ending only that leaf as IndexSearcher does, so replaying into an early-terminating collector, such as a TopFieldCollector sorted by the index sort, throws
bugs.summary: You run a query once through a CachingCollector (or CachingCollectorManager) and then replay the cached hits into a second-pass collector, expecting the same result as running that collector through IndexSearcher. When the second-pass collector stops a segment early by throwing CollectionTerminatedException, which is how LeafCollector#collect documents early termination and what a stock TopFieldCollector sorted by the index sort does once a segment has more than 1000 hits, IndexSearcher simply moves on to the next segment, but replay lets the exception escape to the caller, without a stack trace. Catching it around replay is no workaround: the later segments are never replayed, so in the repro the top 10 come back as [1000..1009] instead of [0..9].

bugs.area: index / IndexingChain per-field schema validation (FieldSchema)
bugs.title: A rejected document leaves its doc-values skip index type in the field's per-document schema state, so later valid documents with that field are rejected until the in-memory segment is flushed
bugs.summary: You index a document in which field f carries a skip-indexed doc-values field (for example SortedDocValuesField.indexedField, new in 10.0), IndexWriter correctly rejects it with IllegalArgumentException because f is already indexed without doc values (or because another field of that document is invalid), and you keep adding documents that have f without doc values. You expect only the bad document to be rejected, as for any non-aborting exception, and the next valid documents to be accepted, as they are when the rejected document used doc values without a skip index. Instead every later document with f and no doc values in the same in-memory segment is rejected ("doc values skip index type: expected 'NONE', but it has 'RANGE'", or "field 'f' cannot have docValuesSkipIndexType=RANGE with doc values type NONE") until the next flush, because IndexingChain.FieldSchema.reset clears the per-document doc-values type but not the skip index type, so the rejected document's RANGE is left behind.

bugs.area: index / IndexingChain per-field schema validation (frozen-FieldType cache) x columnar addBatch
bugs.title: IndexWriter#addBatch marks the frozen FieldType of an earlier rejected document as validated, so later documents with that type skip the per-field schema check (a wrong-dimension vector is stored truncated)
bugs.summary: You add a document whose 8-dimensional KnnFloatVectorField (built from one shared frozen FieldType) does not match the field's 4 dimensions, and Lucene correctly rejects it; you then index an IndexWriter#addBatch with a 4-dimensional vector column for the same field and add the same kind of 8-dimensional document again. You expect the same IllegalArgumentException, because Lucene requires a field to keep the same data structures in every document and checks each document against them. Instead the batch marks the rejected document's FieldType as already validated, so until the next flush every document with that FieldType instance skips the check: the 8-dimensional vector is accepted and stored as its first 4 values (CheckIndex clean), and a SORTED value for a NUMERIC doc-values field fails with ClassCastException instead of the schema error.
bugs.introduced_commit: 3d895681557 (#15990 'Add experimental columnar indexing api', by Tim-Brooks, merged 2026-05-14; 10.x backport #16066, 3ec3bff01b1): its processBatch calls PerField.trySetValidatedFrozenFieldType although it never sets candidateFieldType, so it promotes a candidate that an earlier rejected document left behind [exec]. The reported same-segment form first fails at 1a6f4040dc6 (#16219 'Allow multiple addBatch columns per field name', by Tim-Brooks, 2026-06-14; 10.x ae74896dd37), which made processBatch reset the field schema and validate through initAndValidateFields, on top of 3ca085e1c77 (#16171 'Address frozen FieldType cache never recovering after type switch', by neoremind, 2026-06-13; 10.x eccb3394382), which made PerField.reset record a candidate for every document and promote it after every successful check [exec]. The cache itself is 9e1c6a37c6e (#15886, 2026-04-07) and is not affected without addBatch [read].

bugs.area: core / document: LatLonPoint distance feature query (dynamic pruning through setMinCompetitiveScore)
bugs.title: LatLonPoint.newDistanceFeatureQuery can skip a competitive document under top-k pruning: computeMaxDistance returns the lower end of its 1 m binary search, and the pruning box built from that radius adds only a 7 cm pad
bugs.summary: You index points with LatLonPoint plus LatLonDocValuesField and run searcher.search(LatLonPoint.newDistanceFeatureQuery("loc", 1, 0, 0, 1000), 1), expecting the closest document, because Scorable#setMinCompetitiveScore lets a scorer skip only documents that score below the threshold and Lucene's own TestLatLonPointDistanceFeatureQuery asserts that pruned (TOP_SCORES) and unpruned (COMPLETE) top-k agree for this query. Instead, once a document 999.999 m due north (score 0.50000024) fills the queue, a document 999.803 m due north (score 0.5000492) is never visited and the farther one is returned. The scorer turns the threshold into a radius with a binary search that stops when the interval is 1 m wide and keeps the lower end (999.729 m, although every distance up to 999.999 m still competes), and the box it then searches adds only 7 cm to that radius, so competitive documents just beyond the box edge are dropped.

Not a regression

bugs.area: queries / FunctionScoreQuery block-max pruning (#16431)
bugs.title: FunctionScoreQuery scores negative values as 0, but its block-max bound stays negative, so top-k search skips competitive documents
bugs.summary: You index a numeric doc-values field with a skip index (NumericDocValuesField.indexedField("delta", v)) and search BooleanQuery(SHOULD FunctionScoreQuery(MatchAllDocsQuery, DoubleValuesSource.fromLongField("delta")), SHOULD TermQuery(body:b)) for the top hit, expecting the same hit as an exhaustive search, because FunctionScoreQuery documents that a negative value simply scores 0 (MIGRATE.md, LUCENE-7996). Instead, with 5,000 documents where doc 0 has delta 1, all others have -1000, and only doc 4999 matches body:b, TOP_SCORES and the plain IndexSearcher.search(q, 1) return doc 0 (score 1.0) instead of doc 4999. The cause is that the scorer's getMaxScore returns innerMaxScore * valueMaxScore * boost without the clamp at 0 that score applies, so a block of negative values reports a bound of -1000 for documents that all score 0, and MaxScoreBulkScorer skips windows that hold competitive documents.

bugs.area: queries / function queries (ValueSourceScorer behind FunctionRangeQuery, LUCENE-7996 non-negative score rule; the hit loss surfaces in core WANDScorer)
bugs.title: FunctionRangeQuery scores a document with its raw, possibly negative, function value although LUCENE-7996 forbids negative scores and FunctionQuery over the same source clamps them to 0; since 10.1.0 a matching document whose value is -Infinity can then disappear from the top-k results of a minimumShouldMatch >= 2 BooleanQuery
bugs.summary: You index a document with DoubleDocValuesField("d", -5.0) and search new FunctionRangeQuery(new DoubleFieldSource("d"), -10.0, 10.0, true, true), expecting a non-negative score, because since LUCENE-7996 (8.0) scorers must not produce negative scores and FunctionQuery over the same source scores that document 0. Instead it scores -5.0 (-Infinity and NaN become -Float.MAX_VALUE), because ValueSourceScorer.score returns the raw value and LUCENE-7996 clamped FunctionQuery, BoostedQuery and FunctionScoreQuery but not this scorer. Since 10.1.0 this also loses hits: with minimumNumberShouldMatch = 2 over SHOULD clauses FunctionRangeQuery(d, open range), body:a and body:b (sparse term clauses; also dense ones since 10.5.0), a matching document whose value is -Infinity is missing from search(q, 10), whose totalHits says '3 hits' while count(q) is 4, because WANDScorer rejects a candidate whose scaled score is below the initial minimum competitive score of 0.

bugs.area: search / function scoring (DoubleValuesSource skip-index score bounds for FunctionScoreQuery block-max pruning)
bugs.title: DoubleValuesSource.fromDoubleField/fromFloatField declare their raw IEEE-bit decoders INCREASING, so on a skip-indexed raw-bits field one NaN makes a block's score bound NaN (FunctionScoreQuery under TOP_SCORES then silently drops the true top hit) and all-negative blocks get inverted bounds
bugs.summary: You index doubles as raw IEEE bits in a NUMERIC doc-values field with a skip index (NumericDocValuesField.indexedField('rating', Double.doubleToRawLongBits(v))) and search BooleanQuery(SHOULD FunctionScoreQuery(MatchAllDocsQuery, DoubleValuesSource.fromDoubleField('rating')), SHOULD TermQuery) for the top hit, expecting the same top hit as an exhaustive search (a NaN value simply scores 0, as upstream TestFunctionScoreQuery#testNaN expects). Instead, with 5,000 docs valued 0.5, one NaN at doc 4500 and 50.0 at doc 4999, TOP_SCORES returns doc 1 (score 4.19) instead of doc 4999 (score 50). The cause is that fromDoubleField declares Double::longBitsToDouble INCREASING, so a block's maximum is read as the decoded largest raw long: NaN's raw bits are above every number's, giving a NaN bound, and negative values are in reverse raw order, so a block holding {-1.0, -2.0} reports getMaxScore -2.0 and getMinScore -1.0.

bugs.area: search / function scoring (DoubleValues.withDefault score bound for FunctionScoreQuery block-max pruning, #16431)
bugs.title: DoubleValues.withDefault's getMaxScore returns the wrapped source's bound, which does not cover missingValue, so a FunctionScoreQuery over such a source can silently drop the true top hit under TOP_SCORES
bugs.summary: You write a DoubleValuesSource that returns DoubleValues.withDefault(DoubleValuesSource.fromLongField("price").getValues(ctx, scores), 100) over a price field indexed with a skip index (NumericDocValuesField.indexedField), and search BooleanQuery(SHOULD FunctionScoreQuery(MatchAllDocsQuery, thatSource), SHOULD TermQuery(tag:t)) for the top hit, expecting the document without a price (which scores the default 100) to win, as it does in an exhaustive search. Instead, with 12,288 documents (prices i % 10, doc 0 = 50, doc 9000 without a price), the plain IndexSearcher.search(q, 1) returns doc 0 (score 50.0018) instead of doc 9000 (score 100). The cause is that withDefault.getMaxScore returns the wrapped source's bound, the skip-index block maximum, which counts only documents that have a value (9 in doc 9000's block), although withDefault itself produces missingValue (100) for documents without one, so pruning skips the block that holds the true top hit.

bugs.title: DoubleValuesSource rounds the skip-index block bound to the nearest float, so with a boost FunctionScoreQuery's max score can be one ulp below a real score and top-k search returns the wrong top hit
bugs.summary: You index a long counter with the doc-values skip index (NumericDocValuesField.indexedField('count', v)) and search BooleanQuery(SHOULD BoostQuery(FunctionScoreQuery(MatchAllDocsQuery, DoubleValuesSource.fromLongField('count')), 1.5f), SHOULD TermQuery(body:b)), expecting the same top hit as an exhaustive search. Instead, with 5,000 docs where doc 0 holds 2^24 and doc 4999 holds 2^24 + 1, the pruned search (TOP_SCORES, which plain IndexSearcher.search(q, 1) also uses) returns doc 0 (score 25165824) instead of doc 4999 (score 25165826). The cause is that the block bound is the decoded block maximum cast to the nearest float (2^24 + 1 becomes 2^24) and FunctionScoreQuery multiplies that rounded float by the boost, so the block's bound (25165824) is one float step below the score it must cover and the block is skipped; ordinary doubles do the same (0.065 with boost 1.1 scores 0.0715 under a bound of 0.071499996).
bugs.introduced_commit: 0d4f93a9ff93ccc396c1323f26416b57d8dc08d9 on main (apache/lucene#16431 'Enable Block-Max WAND dynamic pruning for FunctionScoreQuery via DocValuesSkipper (+422% QPS)', by rajat315315 with uschindler as co-author, related issue #16429, merged 2026-08-22) [exec]; it added both halves of the mismatch, the nearest-float cast of the decoded skipper bound and the float product innerMaxScore * valueMaxScore * boost, while score has returned (float) (value * boost) from the exact double since LUCENE-7996 (a8a63464e7d, 2017), which was harmless while the bound was +Infinity; the silent wrong top hit of the tested query became reachable end to end with #16697 (d150ba27d11, by easyice, 2026-10-09), which fixed a separate advanceShallow defect that made that query throw first and kept the cast [exec]

bugs.area: codecs / legacy scalar-quantized vectors (util/quantization ScalarQuantizer, backward-codecs Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsReader)
bugs.title: On main, a 9.x/10.x int7/int4 scalar-quantized segment whose vectors are all identical (stored quantiles equal) is decoded with the min == max widening that #14049 added, not the quantizer that wrote it, so its vectors read 127 (int7) or 15 (int4) units lower in every dimension and exact matches score about 0 and rank last (unreleased, 11.0 only)
bugs.summary: You index a field with the Lucene99 HNSW scalar-quantized format (int7, EUCLIDEAN) on 10.3.2 or 9.12.3, one segment holds only documents whose vector is [1,1,1,1], so the writer stores the quantiles (1, 1) and every code 0; you then open the unchanged index on main and search for [1,1,1,1]. Every release reader tested (9.9.2 to 10.5.2) decodes code 0 as 1.0, as the ScalarQuantizer formula for the stored quantiles says, and ranks those exact matches first with score 1.0. On main the reader rebuilds the quantizer through the min == max widening added by #14049, decodes those vectors as [-126,-126,-126,-126], and the exact matches score 1.5e-5 and rank last behind a document with half the similarity; int4 fields decode 15 units low, and DOT_PRODUCT and COSINE exact matches score 0.0.
