bugs.area: search / similarities (LMDirichletSimilarity)
bugs.title: LMDirichletSimilarity accepts mu = 0, but then every document scores 0: log(1 + tf/(mu*P)) + log(mu/(dl+mu)) becomes +Infinity + -Infinity = NaN, and the 'score > 0' clamp turns NaN into 0
bugs.summary: You configure LMDirichletSimilarity with mu = 0, which both constructors accept ('must be a non-negative finite value') and which upstream's TestLMDirichletSimilarity uses as its 'minimum value'. You expect documents that contain the query term more often than the collection model predicts to get a positive score and be ranked, as they are for every mu > 0 down to Float.MIN_VALUE, where the score already equals its finite mu -> 0 limit log(tf/(dl*P)). Instead score computes log(1 + tf/0) + log(0/dl) = +Infinity + -Infinity = NaN, the 'score > 0 ? score: 0' clamp returns 0.0, and every hit scores 0.0, so the best match can come back last; explain shows 'Infinity = term weight' and '-Infinity = document norm' under a 0.0 total.
bugs.introduced_commit: cfaf91c73981 (LUCENE-2959 / #4033, svn r1169470: the merge of the flexscoring branch into trunk, from JIRA patches, no PR) [read]. The two pieces were written on the flexscoring branch, which is not on main's ancestry: the two-log formula in 8f73f80d1d7 (LUCENE-3220 / #4293, 2011-07-15; mu = 0 gave NaN) and the clamp in 93bf76506b4 (LUCENE-3357 / #4430, 2011-08-20; it turned that NaN into 0). 42717d5f4bb (LUCENE-7997 / #9045, 2017-10-24, first in 8.0.0) added the 'non-negative finite value' check, which admits mu = 0, and the mu = 0 test case, and kept both logs and the clamp. Not a regression.

bugs.area: misc / similarities (SweetSpotSimilarity hyperbolicTf helper)
bugs.title: SweetSpotSimilarity.hyperbolicTf returns max instead of about min for frequencies far below xoffset, because its NaN fallback is right only for the Math.pow overflow above the midpoint, so a hyperbolic-tf subclass is not monotone in freq and ranks a document with one occurrence above one with hundreds
bugs.summary: You subclass SweetSpotSimilarity so that tf returns hyperbolicTf(freq), as its javadoc suggests, call setHyperbolicTfFactors(0, 2, 10, 400) and search, expecting the documented curve min+(max-min)/2*(tanh((freq-xoffset)*ln(base))+1): a tf near min (0) for frequencies far below the midpoint 400, rising to max (2) above it. Instead hyperbolicTf returns the maximum 2.0 for every frequency from 1 to 91 and drops to 0.0 at 92, so a document that contains the term once outranks an equally long one that contains it 400 times. Far below the midpoint Math.pow(base, xoffset - freq) overflows to Infinity (once xoffset - freq exceeds about 308 at base 10, about 2705 at the default base 1.3), the ratio becomes NaN, and the guard 'return Float.isNaN(result) ? max: result', which is right only for the overflow above the midpoint, returns max.

bugs.area: document / FeatureField sigmoid scoring (FeatureField.SigmoidFunction behind newSigmoidQuery; the same arithmetic is copied in queries / intervals IntervalScoreFunction.SigmoidFunction behind the 4-argument IntervalQuery constructor)
bugs.title: FeatureField.newSigmoidQuery (and the IntervalQuery sigmoid) return NaN scores when pivot^exp overflows or underflows a double, for pivot and exp values the factories accept
bugs.summary: You rank documents with FeatureField.newSigmoidQuery (or IntervalQuery's pivot-and-exponent constructor) and pick a steep exponent with a large or tiny pivot, values the factory accepts because it only requires both to be positive and finite. You expect the documented score weight * S^exp / (S^exp + pivot^exp), a number between 0 and weight that equals weight/2 at S = pivot. Instead SigmoidFunction precomputes pivot^exp as a double, which becomes +Infinity or 0 for such parameters, so scores come out as Inf/Inf or 0/0 = NaN: with pivot 2^20 and exponent 60 every document scores NaN; since 10.2.0 NaN hits rank ahead of correctly scored ones, so the best document can come last, and on 9.x (assertions off) TopDocs even returns placeholder hits with doc id 2147483647.
bugs.introduced_commit: 710993435f365fce44a60b7c498ce6af8327f92c (master) / 70cc7b68783b313a845996dac9e28c3ea6ad61e3 (branch_7x, the copy that shipped first, in 7.4.0): 'LUCENE-8197: Efficient integration of static scoring factors.' by jpountz, a JIRA patch with no pull request (the issue is now #9244). The commit created FeatureField; its SigmoidFunction already precomputed pivotPa = Math.pow(pivot, a) and scored (float) (weight * (1 - pivotPa / (Math.pow(f, a) + pivotPa))), and newSigmoidQuery already accepted every finite pivot > 0 and exp > 0, so no earlier version of the code was correct [read]. bugs.area: document / FeatureField score functions (SaturationFunction and SigmoidFunction behind newSaturationQuery and newSigmoidQuery); queries / intervals IntervalScoreFunction (IntervalQuery's default saturation scoring and its pivot and pivot-plus-exponent constructors)
bugs.title: FeatureField saturation and sigmoid queries and IntervalQuery scoring compute w*(1 - k/(S+k)) instead of the documented w*S/(S+k) (and the same rewrite for the sigmoid), so documents whose value is far below the pivot score exactly 0.0 or tie with documents that have different values
bugs.summary: You rank with FeatureField.newSaturationQuery, whose javadoc says it 'will score documents as weight * S / (S + pivot)' (newSigmoidQuery and IntervalQuery's scoring state the same kind of formula), a value that is positive and grows with S, so a document with a smaller feature value should score lower but above 0. The code instead computes weight * (1 - pivot / (S + pivot)) (and 1 - k^a / (S^a + k^a) for the sigmoid) so that rounding cannot make scores decrease, and when S is far below the pivot the sum S + pivot rounds to almost exactly the pivot and the subtraction cancels. With pivot 1000 a document with S = 1e-5 scores exactly 0.0 while explain prints 'computed as w * S / (S + k)', with the library's default pivot 199 adjacent pairs of distinct stored values tie, and IntervalQuery gives intervals 1,000,000 and 1,030,000 positions wide the same score and a 2^25-wide interval 0.0.
bugs.introduced_commit: 710993435f365fce44a60b7c498ce6af8327f92c on master / 70cc7b68783b313a845996dac9e28c3ea6ad61e3 on branch_7x (the copy that shipped in 7.4.0): 'LUCENE-8197: Efficient integration of static scoring factors.' by jpountz, committed from a JIRA patch with no pull request (the issue is now #9244). It created FeatureField with SaturationFunction already returning weight * (1 - pivot / (f + pivot)) and SigmoidFunction (float) (weight * (1 - pivotPa / (Math.pow(f, a) + pivotPa))), under the comment that the value 'should be f / (f + k)' and is rewritten 'to make sure it doesn't decrease with f in spite of rounding', so no earlier version was correct. bugs.area: search / similarities (PerFieldSimilarityWrapper, Similarity#computeQueryTermWeight) and BooleanQuery duplicate-clause rewrite
bugs.title: PerFieldSimilarityWrapper does not forward Similarity#computeQueryTermWeight, so a BM25Similarity or StableTflSimilarity k3 (query-term saturation) setting silently has no effect behind a per-field wrapper
bugs.summary: You configure BM25Similarity with its opt-in k3 parameter (new BM25Similarity(1.2f, 0.75f, true, 7f)), whose javadoc promises that a term repeated in a query is weighted ((k3 + 1) * qtf) / (k3 + qtf) instead of linearly, and you install it through a PerFieldSimilarityWrapper, the documented way to use per-field similarities, even one whose get returns that same instance for every field. You expect the query 'apple apple' to score as it does with the bare BM25Similarity, where BooleanQuery's duplicate-clause rewrite gives (body:apple)^1.7777778. Instead the rewrite asks the wrapper, which does not forward Similarity#computeQueryTermWeight and inherits its linear default, so the query becomes (body:apple)^2.0 and the document scores 0.63013375 instead of 0.5601189; StableTflSimilarity's k3 is ignored the same way.

bugs.summary: You turn on BM25's opt-in k3 parameter (new BM25Similarity(1.2f, 0.75f, true, 8f), or StableTflSimilarity with k3), whose javadoc promises that a term repeated in a query is weighted ((k3 + 1) * qtf) / (k3 + qtf) instead of linearly, and you search with a BooleanQuery that repeats a SHOULD term, for example QueryBuilder.createMinShouldMatchQuery('body', 'a b', fraction). bugs.area: core index / DOCS_AND_CUSTOM_FREQS (termdoc) field length vs term statistics; search similarities (BM25, SimilarityBase)
bugs.title: DOCS_AND_CUSTOM_FREQS fields (10.5.0+): the norm length counts terms but sumTotalTermFreq and totalTermFreq sum the custom frequencies, contradicting the FieldInfo#isTermDocField, IndexOptions and FieldStats javadocs and putting BM25's dl and avgdl in different units
bugs.summary: You index two documents, 'a|5 b|5' and 'a|5 b|5 c|5 d|5', into a field with IndexOptions.DOCS_AND_CUSTOM_FREQS (DelimitedTermFrequencyTokenFilter, a TextField type with norms). Lucene stores their lengths as term counts, 2 and 4. FieldInfo#isTermDocField says such frequencies count as 1 'for statistical and scoring purposes', and FieldStats says sumTotalTermFreq 'is also the sum of each document's field length'. So you expect sumTotalTermFreq to be 6 and BM25's average length to be 3. Instead, sumTotalTermFreq and totalTermFreq sum the custom values (30), and BM25 explains dl=2.0 against avgdl=15.0. Each document's length is compared with an average inflated by the mean custom value, which quietly weakens length normalisation.
bugs.introduced_commit: 5158a52a082b842c29918c8b955323d2a0848eb5. This is apache/lucene PR #15584, 'Compute 'length' of fields with custom term frequencies as docFreq', by msokolov, merged into main on 2026-04-24; it fixes #11086 (LUCENE-10048). It was backported to branch_10x as 3a55cc9ac5e96e39a75e837e326085c5efdc894d, and the 10.5.0, 10.5.1 and 10.5.2 tags contain that commit. The PR added three things together: IndexOptions.DOCS_AND_CUSTOM_FREQS with its javadoc, FieldInfo#isTermDocField with its javadoc, and the IndexingChain branch that adds 1 per term to the field length. Postings keep the custom value, so totalTermFreq and sumTotalTermFreq still sum it. bugs.area: search / AutomatonQuery RAM accounting (NFARunAutomaton lazily built DFA states; LRUQueryCache RAM budget)
bugs.title: AutomatonQuery.ramBytesUsed is computed once at construction, so a query that runs on an NFA (WildcardQuery and RegexpQuery by default on main, opt-in NFA queries since 10.0.0) under-reports the DFA states it builds while searching, and an LRUQueryCache can hold far more heap than its RAM budget
bugs.summary: You run a WildcardQuery or RegexpQuery whose automaton is not deterministic, for example '*a?????????' or 'a*b??????????', and expect its ramBytesUsed to estimate the heap the query holds, which is what the Accountable javadoc says and what LRUQueryCache uses to stay within maxRamBytesUsed. On main such a query runs on an NFARunAutomaton that builds DFA states lazily during the search and keeps them on the query object, but AutomatonQuery stored ramBytesUsed in a final field when it was constructed, so after one search the value is 40x to 310x too small (5,674 bytes reported vs 228,680 retained; 6,714 vs 2,081,152). An LRUQueryCache with a 1 MiB budget then keeps 4 such queries as keys that retain 2.7 to 7.4 MB while it accounts about 36 KB in total and evicts nothing; the matching documents are correct.
bugs.introduced_commit: c972c6a7754e9ff1f838ed72ff09e7def00be5f8, apache/lucene#225 'LUCENE-10010 Introduce NFARunAutomaton to run NFA directly' (zhaih, merged 2021-12-20): CompiledAutomaton began wrapping non-deterministic automata in an NFARunAutomaton that determinizes lazily and keeps its states for the life of the query, while AutomatonQuery kept the construction-time 'private final long ramBytesUsed; // cache' field added by LUCENE-8855 (a76c962ee61f, 2019-06-26, first released in 8.2.0; harmless while a CompiledAutomaton was always an immutable DFA) [read]. Default-path exposure on main only: 650684e6b440 (apache/lucene#15939, RegexpQuery(Term) no longer determinizes, merged 2026-04-12) and 86593e51b28d (apache/lucene#15961, WildcardQuery(Term) no longer determinizes and NFA-backed queries get value equality, so fresh per-request queries share one cache key, merged 2026-04-19) [exec]

bugs.area: spatial3d / PointInGeo3DShapeQuery RAM accounting (Accountable#ramBytesUsed; core LRUQueryCache RAM budget)
bugs.title: Geo3DPoint polygon and path queries report a constant 592-byte ramBytesUsed regardless of shape size, because PointInGeo3DShapeQuery prices its GeoShape as a 256-byte unknown object, so LRUQueryCache can hold many times its maxRamBytesUsed (since 8.2.0)
bugs.summary: You filter with a Geo3DPoint polygon or path query, for example newLargePolygonQuery with 2,000 edges or newPathQuery with 200 points, and expect its ramBytesUsed to estimate the heap it holds, which is what Accountable promises and what LRUQueryCache charges against its maxRamBytesUsed budget. Instead PointInGeo3DShapeQuery.ramBytesUsed passes the shape and its bounds to RamUsageEstimator.sizeOfObject, which prices every object that is not Accountable (no GeoShape is) at a fixed 256 bytes, so every such query reports 592 bytes whatever its size: 4.9x too low for an 8-edge polygon, 47x for 99 edges, about 2,300x for the 2,000-edge large polygon (1,360,960 bytes retained). An LRUQueryCache with a 1 MiB budget therefore keeps 8 such filters that retain 10.9 MB, accounts about 6 KB for them and evicts nothing; the hits are correct.

Not a regression of later work: no GeoShape class has ever implemented Accountable

bugs.area: join / JoinUtil numeric query-time join RAM accounting (PointInSetIncludingScoreQuery, Accountable#ramBytesUsed; core LRUQueryCache RAM budget)
bugs.title: PointInSetIncludingScoreQuery.ramBytesUsed leaves out its per-value score list, so scoring numeric JoinUtil joins (ScoreMode Max, Min, Avg, Total) under-report their heap (1.5x-2.4x on 9.11.0 and later, 6.2x or more in 8.2.0-9.10.0) and LRUQueryCache under-charges them (since 8.2.0)
bugs.summary: You build a numeric query-time join with JoinUtil.createJoinQuery(fromField, multipleValuesPerDocument, toField, numberType, fromQuery, fromSearcher, ScoreMode.Max) (or Min, Avg, Total) and expect its ramBytesUsed to estimate the heap the query holds, which is what Accountable promises, what LRUQueryCache charges against maxRamBytesUsed, and what the string-field scoring join (TermsIncludingScoreQuery) and the ScoreMode.None numeric join (PointInSetQuery) do. Instead the PointInSetIncludingScoreQuery it returns adds up only its base object, field, from-query and packed join values, and leaves out aggregatedJoinScores, the FloatArrayList with one float per join value that its constructor fills: with 100,000 join values it reports 304,248 bytes while it retains 710,632 (2.3x; 1.5x-2.4x depending on how compactly the keys prefix-code), against 303,272 vs 304,544 for ScoreMode.None. A query cache holding such a join as a filter charges it the same low number (304,408 bytes charged, 710,632 retained), so the cache can hold up to about 2.5 times its budget in these keys; the matching documents are correct.

bugs.area: queries / function queries (FunctionScoreQuery, FunctionMatchQuery, FunctionRangeQuery and FunctionQuery QueryVisitor traversal of DoubleValuesSource/ValueSource; consumer: IndexSearcher's cumulative clause limit)
bugs.title: IndexSearcher's cumulative maxClauseCount check never counts a query held by a values source (FunctionScoreQuery.boostByQuery's boost query, DoubleValuesSource.fromQuery, QueryValueSource): the function queries' visit stops at the source and each embedded query is checked alone with a fresh budget, so the total number of executed clauses is unbounded
bugs.summary: You search FunctionScoreQuery.boostByQuery(in, boostMatch, 2f), where in and boostMatch are each a 600-term disjunction (1,200 term clauses that all run), with the default maxClauseCount of 1024. You expect TooManyNestedClauses, which you do get for a BooleanQuery holding the same clauses (even when half of them are scoring-only SHOULD or MUST_NOT clauses), because the check counts 'total clauses cumulatively in all of its children' and LUCENE-8811 made it cumulative so that splitting clauses over sub-queries no longer bypasses it. Instead the search runs with correct hits: FunctionScoreQuery.visit visits only `in`, FunctionMatchQuery, FunctionRangeQuery and FunctionQuery.visit call visitLeaf(this), DoubleValuesSource and ValueSource have no visit hook, and the embedded query is rewritten later with searcher.rewrite, which checks it alone with a fresh count; FunctionScoreQuery(fromQuery), FunctionMatchQuery(fromQuery) and FunctionQuery/FunctionRangeQuery over QueryValueSource behave the same.

bugs.area: grouping / GroupingSearch two-pass caching x search / CachingCollectorManager (new in 10.6.0) under a concurrent IndexSearcher
bugs.title: GroupingSearch.setCaching / setCachingInMB limit is applied per slice since #16247 (10.6.0 release-candidate regression): with an IndexSearcher that has an executor, a query matching more documents than the limit is replayed from per-slice caches holding up to slices x limit instead of being purged and re-run (results unchanged)
bugs.summary: You enable caching for a grouped search with GroupingSearch.setCaching(600, true) (or setCachingInMB) and search through an IndexSearcher that has an executor, and expect what the unchanged javadoc says and what 10.5.2 and a sequential searcher do: the cache holds at most the limit, and when the query matches more it is purged and the second pass re-runs the query. Instead, since #16247 GroupingSearch hands the limit to the new CachingCollectorManager, which applies it to each slice separately, so with 1000 matching documents over 2 slices each slice cache stays under 600, the caches hold all 1000 documents, and the second pass is replayed (the query runs once instead of twice). Results are the same; what breaks is the documented memory bound and the replay decision, and the cache can reach (number of slices) x limit.

bugs.area: misc / memory-accounting bitset collector (MemoryAccountingBitsetCollector, MemoryAccountingBitsetCollectorManager, CollectorMemoryTracker) under IndexSearcher slicing
bugs.title: MemoryAccountingBitsetCollector sizes each collector's bitset to the doc-id span of its slice, so under concurrent search a slice whose segments are not adjacent in doc-id order allocates, and charges to the memory tracker, bits for the segments that other slices search
bugs.summary: You search with MemoryAccountingBitsetCollectorManager and a CollectorMemoryTracker on an IndexSearcher built with an executor, and expect each slice's collector to allocate a bitset only for the segments it searches, as the manager's javadoc says ('each collector only allocates a bitset for the slices it processes'). Instead each collector sizes its bitset to the doc-id range from the first to the last segment of its slice, and the default slicing groups segments by size, not by doc-id order, so in an index whose segments are 10, 300,000, 10, 300,000 and 10 documents the slice of the three small segments allocates a bitset over 600,030 doc ids for its 30 documents. The search tracks 243,960 bytes against 159,480 for the same search without an executor, and a tracker limit of 161,528 bytes that the sequential search fits throws IllegalStateException 'Memory limit exceeded' with the executor; the matched documents are correct.

bugs.area: facet / range queries (LongRange/DoubleRange ValueSourceQuery and MultiValueSourceQuery QueryVisitor traversal; consumers: IndexSearcher's cumulative clause limit, QueryVisitor.termCollector, RamUsageEstimator.sizeOf(Query))
bugs.title: LongRange/DoubleRange#getQuery(fastMatchQuery,...) range queries report themselves as a leaf in visit and never visit their fast-match query, so IndexSearcher's maxClauseCount check never counts the fast-match query
bugs.summary: You build LongRange#getQuery(fastMatch, LongValuesSource) (or the DoubleRange or multi-valued overloads) with a fast-match query of 1,200 term clauses (two required 600-term disjunctions) and search it with the default maxClauseCount of 1024. You expect TooManyNestedClauses, which you do get when the same fast-match query is a sibling FILTER clause, because the check counts 'total clauses cumulatively in all of its children', Query#visit is documented to visit 'any child queries', and getQuery documents fastMatchQuery as 'a query to use as a filter'. Instead the search runs and returns the correct hits: ValueSourceQuery.visit and MultiValueSourceQuery.visit only call visitor.visitLeaf(this), so the fast-match query, which stays in the rewritten query and is executed as the approximation in createWeight, is seen by no clause check at all, and QueryVisitor.termCollector returns none of its terms.

bugs.area: spatial-extras / composite: CompositeVerifyQuery (Query#visit; consumers: QueryVisitor.termCollector and other visit-based term extraction, IndexSearcher's cumulative clause limit)
bugs.title: CompositeVerifyQuery.visit reports the whole query as a leaf and never visits the index query it rewrites and executes, so QueryVisitor term collection misses the index query's terms and IndexSearcher's cumulative maxClauseCount check does not count its clauses
bugs.summary: You wrap your own index query, for example TermQuery(body:a) or a 20-clause DisjunctionMaxQuery, in new CompositeVerifyQuery(indexQuery, shapePredicate), then collect its terms with QueryVisitor.termCollector or search it after IndexSearcher.setMaxClauseCount(8). You expect [body:a] and an IndexSearcher.TooManyNestedClauses error, because Query#visit is documented to 'recurse through the query tree, visiting any child queries', the wrapper rewrites its index query and runs it as the approximation that every hit must match, and the same 20 clauses as a bare query or as a sibling FILTER clause are rejected. Instead CompositeVerifyQuery.visit only calls visitor.visitLeaf(this): termCollector returns and the clause check counts the whole query as one clause, so the over-limit query runs (its hits are correct).

bugs.area: facet / sampling (RandomSamplingFacetsCollector.createSample, cross-segment bin carry-over)
bugs.title: RandomSamplingFacetsCollector never samples the first hit of a segment that starts mid-bin: createSample does not handle randomIndex == counter at the end of a segment, so a sampling bin that crosses a segment boundary loses its sample (or samples at a stale offset)
bugs.summary: You count facets with RandomSamplingFacetsCollector on a multi-segment index for a query with many more hits than sampleSize, and expect systematic sampling: one random hit out of every run of binSize consecutive hits, with a run that is cut by a segment boundary continued in the next segment, so every hit has about a 1/binSize chance to be sampled. Instead, when the hit picked for such a run is the first hit of the next segment, createSample leaves its carry-over state unset (it tests only randomIndex > counter and randomIndex < counter), so that run contributes no sample, or one at a stale offset, and the first hit of a segment that starts mid-bin is never sampled. Nothing fails; the sample and the amortized counts are just smaller than the reported sampling rate implies (4 hits in segments [1 | 3], sampleSize 2: half the seeds sample 1 hit instead of 2).

bugs.title: CheckIndex silently skips FLOAT16 vector fields: it reports 'OK [0 fields, 0 vectors]' and never runs checkFloat16VectorValues

bugs.area: index / CheckIndex concurrent segment check and exorcise
bugs.title: CheckIndex -exorcise with more than one thread (threadCount > 1, the default on multi-core machines, or checkIndex(onlySegments, executor)) writes the surviving segments in ascending file-size order instead of commit order, so the repaired index's segment order and relative document order depend on the thread count
bugs.summary: You repair an index that has a broken segment with CheckIndex -exorcise, or checkIndex followed by exorciseIndex, on a multi-core machine, where threadCount defaults to the number of cores. You expect the same repaired commit that a sequential run (-threadCount 1) writes: the documentation describes the thread count and the executor overload only as ways to speed up the check, and exorcise only as removing the broken segments. Instead the concurrent path collects the segment results in ascending file-size order (a sort added so that small segments print first) and exorciseIndex commits that list as it is, so the surviving segments, and with them the relative order of their documents, are permuted; an index written in insertion order comes back reversed, so Sort.INDEXORDER returns the newest documents first instead of the oldest.
bugs.introduced_commit: 424192e1704664dc0ebc55109feaad5990b945cb on main, 'LUCENE-9662: CheckIndex should be concurrent - parallelizing index check across segments (#128)' (apache/lucene#128 by GitHub zacharymorn, reviewed by dweiss, mikemccand and rmuir; issue LUCENE-9662 = apache/lucene#10701); 8.x backport 965b54ce3fd450dd42758244870b6228e1b5e5d4 on branch_8x (apache/lucene-solr#2567). It replaced the single commit-order loop that filled Status.segmentInfos and newSegments with a sequential branch (commit order) and a concurrent branch that sorts a copy of the commit by sizeInBytes and appends the results in that sorted order; exorciseIndex commits newSegments unchanged [read] [exec]. Follow-up 7f8607b59e034541d62687374b86197797a30a4f (#281) changed the default threadCount from min(cores, 4) to cores

bugs.area: grouping / collector managers (FirstPassGroupingCollectorManager, TopGroupsCollectorManager and BlockGroupingCollectorManager reduce through the cross-shard merges SearchGroup.merge, TopGroups.merge and TopGroups.mergeBlockGroups; GroupingSearch)
bugs.title: With an executor, grouped search breaks ties by slice number instead of doc ID, so tied groups and tied documents differ from sequential search
bugs.summary: You run a grouped search (GroupingSearch, or the grouping collector managers) on an IndexSearcher that has an executor, and several groups or several documents tie on the sort, for example because every hit scores 1.0. You expect the tie to be broken by doc ID, as Sort's javadoc says and as the same search without an executor does, so the top group and the top documents are the same either way. Instead the per-slice results are combined with merges written for real shards, which break ties by shard index, here the slice number: the search returns doc 1 instead of doc 0, or group g1 instead of g0, and the choice changes whenever the slicing changes.

bugs.area: search / SynonymQuery scoring (SynonymScorer.freq float sum) and its merged-impacts max-score bound
bugs.title: SynonymQuery adds up boosted term frequencies in float in heap order, so identical documents can score differently and explain can differ from the hit score; with more than 2^24 occurrences in one field a score can exceed getMaxScore
bugs.summary: You run a SynonymQuery with three or more boosted terms, for example Synonym(a^0.2, b^0.2, c^0.3) over four identical documents 'a b c' with the default BM25, and expect identical documents to score the same and explain to report the hit's score, because the query scores 'the sum of all term frequencies for the document'. SynonymScorer.freq adds boost * freq in float, in the order of the disjunction's topList, and that order depends on how the iterator reached the document, so the rounding differs: docs 0 and 3 score 0.038817033, docs 1 and 2 score 0.038817026, and explain(doc 1) reports 0.038817033. The same float sum can also round above the exact integer sum that the merged impacts use as the max-score bound once a field holds more than 2^24 occurrences of the terms: under ClassicSimilarity a document scores 1.032795 while getMaxScore is 1.0327948, and a pruned top-1 search returns a different document than an exhaustive one.

bugs.area: suggest / document (NRT) suggester (NRTSuggesterBuilder.finishTerm dedup bytes; NRTSuggester top-n search through Util.TopNSearcher; TopSuggestDocsCollector tie order)
bugs.title: Document suggester: which equal-score copies of one suggestion are returned depends on n (top-2 [2, 1] is not a prefix of top-3 [2, 0, 1]), because NRTSuggesterBuilder numbers the copies in java.util.PriorityQueue heap order instead of doc-id order
bugs.summary: You index three documents with the same suggestion 'c' and weights 1, 1 and 2 in one segment and call SuggestIndexSearcher.suggest(PrefixCompletionQuery 'c', n, skipDuplicates=false). For n=3 you get docs [2, 0, 1] (score, then the smaller doc id, as the collector's comparator orders them), so n=2 should return the first two, [2, 0]; it returns [2, 1]. NRTSuggesterBuilder.finishTerm numbers the copies of one analyzed form (its dedup bytes) by iterating a java.util.PriorityQueue, whose iterator returns heap-array order ([doc 2, doc 1, doc 0] here), and the per-segment TopNSearcher breaks score ties by those bytes and stops after n results, so for n=2 doc 0 never reaches the collector.

bugs.title: StandardTokenizer and UAX29URLEmailTokenizer with setMaxTokenLength(1) end the token stream at the first supplementary character (for example an emoji), so all later text of the field value is silently left out of the index
bugs.summary: You set maxTokenLength to 1 on StandardTokenizer (or StandardAnalyzer, UAX29URLEmailTokenizer, or a factory with maxTokenLength=1) and tokenize text that contains a code point above U+FFFF, for example 'ab U+10400 cd' or 'hello U+1F600 world'. You expect what the setter documents, that too-long tokens are chopped and emitted as multiple tokens, so the words after that character are still tokenized and end reports the input length as the final offset. Instead the 1-char scan buffer cannot hold the surrogate pair, the scanner's refill reports end of input at a token start, and the stream stops: [a, b] with final offset 3 of 8, [h, e, l, l, o], and nothing after the character is indexed.

Instead the IndexWriter constructor throws: IndexFileDeleter passes every pending deletion, unfiltered, to inflateGens, which treats any name that does not start with segments or pending_segments as a segment file, so with -ea it fails the assertion 'wtf? file=snapshots_0' (or 'wtf? file=app-notes.txt'), and with -da app-notes.txt gives NumberFormatException 'For input string: "pp-notes" under radix 36'. With -da the snapshots_0 case opens, but the writer names its next segment _napshott: the segment counter jumps to 1 + Long.parseLong("napshots", 36), which is cosmetic.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter commit (merge-on-commit under commitLock, SerialMergeScheduler, tragic-event rollback)
bugs.title: With SerialMergeScheduler, a merge that fails while another thread's commit waits to run its merge-on-commit merges deadlocks both threads forever (commit holds commitLock and waits for the scheduler's monitor; the failing merge holds that monitor and its tragic rollback waits for commitLock), and the writer can no longer be closed (since 8.6.0; with default merge-on-commit settings since 9.3.0)
bugs.summary: You configure IndexWriter with SerialMergeScheduler and keep merge-on-commit on (the default since 9.3); one thread calls commit while another thread's addDocument runs a merge, and that merge fails, for example because the disk is full. You expect IndexWriter to close itself on the tragic merge failure and both calls to return with an exception, as they do with ConcurrentMergeScheduler or with merge-on-commit off. Instead commit holds IndexWriter's commit lock while it waits to enter SerialMergeScheduler's synchronized merge method, and the failing merge thread, still inside that method, waits for the commit lock in the tragic rollback, so both threads hang forever and the writer cannot be closed.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter close (waitForMerges, ConcurrentMergeScheduler, tragic merge failure)
bugs.title: IndexWriter.close never returns when a background merge fails while a forced-merge cascade merge is still pending (forceMerge(n, false), then close): the tragic rollback is skipped because close is already closing, getNextMerge refuses the pending merge once the tragedy is set, and waitForMerges never checks the tragedy (since 9.3.0)
bugs.summary: You start a background forced merge with forceMerge(1, false) and then call close, and you expect close to commit and return, or, if a merge fails, to throw and leave the writer closed, as its javadoc says. Instead, if one merge fails (for example disk full) just after another forced merge finished and queued the next round, close waits forever in waitForMerges: the failure does not roll the writer back because close is already closing, since 9.3.0 IndexWriter refuses to start any pending merge after such a failure, and the wait loop never looks at the failure. The write lock stays held and a rollback from another thread blocks as well; only interrupting the closing thread ends the wait.

(#921)' by jpountz (issue #11116, approved by s1monw). bugs.area: monitor / ParallelMatcher worker lifecycle (Monitor#match)
bugs.title: Monitor's ParallelMatcher starts blocking worker tasks in its constructor that only finish releases: a Monitor#match that fails before finish (an exception such as TooManyClauses from the presearcher, or a rejected submit) leaves its workers parked on the executor forever, and an executor that runs a worker on the calling thread (CallerRunsPolicy on a saturated pool) makes Monitor#match hang
bugs.summary: You match documents with Monitor#match using ParallelMatcher.factory(executor, matcher, threads), for example on Executors.newFixedThreadPool(threads), and you expect what the default serial matcher does: Monitor#match returns the matches or throws, and leaves nothing running on your executor. Instead the ParallelMatcher constructor submits `threads` workers that only finish can release, so when the match throws before finish (here IndexSearcher.TooManyClauses from the presearcher for a document with terms in 1,025 fields used by registered queries, the same exception the serial matcher throws) the workers stay parked forever and the next valid match on the same pool never returns. A rejected submit leaks the already-accepted workers the same way, and with CallerRunsPolicy on a saturated pool the calling thread runs a worker itself and Monitor#match never returns.

bugs.area: monitor / bulk query loading (ConcurrentQueryLoader worker error handling)
bugs.title: ConcurrentQueryLoader workers exit at the first exception from Monitor.register and are never replaced, so once every worker is gone add blocks forever and close never gets to report the IOException
bugs.summary: You bulk-load standing queries into a Monitor with the documented pattern, loader.add(q) in a loop inside try-with-resources, and Monitor.register fails inside the loader's worker threads, for example because the query index cannot fsync or create a file. You expect the load to stop and close to throw the IOException, which the loader records for exactly that purpose. Instead each worker leaves its loop at its first failure and is never replaced, so once every worker is gone nothing drains the bounded queue: the next add calls block in LinkedBlockingQueue.put forever, close is never reached and the error is never reported (repro: 1 worker, queue size 4, one simulated fsync failure; add is still blocked 30 s later).
bugs.introduced_commit: 251dbe7cea8126cb7ecadc921ba444c63d06c618 (main, 2019-06-13, 'LUCENE-8766: Add monitor subproject', by GitHub romseygeek), with the branch_8x twin b8773d13ad8e249a045862249bf476c30a444461 shipped in 8.2.0 (git diff of ConcurrentQueryLoader.java between the two is empty); submitted as apache/lucene-solr#648, which GitHub shows closed unmerged because the code was committed directly; JIRA LUCENE-8766 (migrated as #9811). [read]. Not a regression. The structure (IOException caught outside the worker loop, blocking put in add) predates Lucene: it is in the donated Luwak library from its commit 100c318d9e (2015-10-09), where a per-query error type was still caught inside the loop; the port dropped that inner catch, so any exception from register now ends a worker [read].

bugs.area: monitor / read-only query index (ReadonlyQueryIndex background refresh)
bugs.title: A read-only Monitor's background refresh stops for good after one run throws an unchecked exception, and no error is reported
bugs.summary: You open a read-only Monitor over a query index that a writable Monitor updates, and count on its background thread to pick up the writer's changes at the configured purge frequency, which the upstream test TestMonitorReadonly.testReadonlyMonitorGetsRefreshed asserts. You expect a failed refresh run to be reported through MonitorUpdateListener.onPurgeError and the next run to try again, as the writable Monitor's purge task does. Instead the read-only task catches only IOException, so one unchecked exception (for example from an onPurge listener that throws once, or a ConcurrentModificationException when a listener is added while a run is calling the listeners) escapes the scheduled task, the executor silently cancels every later run, and the Monitor keeps matching its old query set with no error.

bugs.area: facet / taxonomy (SearcherTaxonomyManager.getRefCount and tryIncRef; the misuse guard in core ReferenceManager.acquire)
bugs.title: SearcherTaxonomyManager.acquire spins forever at 100% CPU, instead of throwing the LUCENE-5436 IllegalStateException, when the current pair's taxonomy reader was closed outside the manager
bugs.summary: You use SearcherTaxonomyManager and, through a bug in your own code, call decRef or close on the taxonomy reader of a pair you acquired (for example by wrapping pair.taxonomyReader in try-with-resources), then release the pair as usual. Since LUCENE-5436 (4.7.0) the next acquire is meant to detect such an outside reference-count change and throw IllegalStateException, which is what SearcherManager and the index-reader half of the same pair do. Instead acquire retries forever in a busy loop, because SearcherTaxonomyManager.getRefCount reports only the index reader's count, so the guard never sees that the taxonomy reader is closed; only closing the manager ends the loop, with AlreadyClosedException.

bugs.area: util / OfflineSorter concurrent sort (partitionsInRAM permits on a rejected submit)
bugs.title: OfflineSorter loses a partitionsInRAM permit whenever its ExecutorService rejects a partition-sort task, so a later sort on the same sorter waits forever even though the executor is idle (released since 6.6.0)
bugs.summary: You give OfflineSorter your own bounded thread pool, one sort fails with RejectedExecutionException because the pool was full (or shut down), and you expect the same sorter to work again once the pool is idle, since every other exception path gives the partition's partitionsInRAM permit back. Instead the permit that readPartition took for the rejected partition is never released (only the task's finally block releases it, and a rejected task never runs; the semaphore belongs to the sorter instance), so with maxPartitionsInRAM = 1 the next sort on that sorter waits forever in Semaphore.acquire with an idle executor (executed: 'sort did not return within 20 s; waiting for a partition permit: true; executor active=0 queued=0'). With maxPartitionsInRAM = k each rejection costs one permit and after k rejections every later sort hangs; with a shut-down executor, a call that should fail fast with RejectedExecutionException waits instead.

bugs.area: classification / ConfusionMatrixGenerator (classifier evaluation utility)
bugs.title: ConfusionMatrixGenerator never cancels a classification that exceeded its 5 s limit, so later documents queue behind it on the single worker thread and are also counted as timed out
bugs.summary: You evaluate a classifier with ConfusionMatrixGenerator.getConfusionMatrix and one document's classification is slow (more than about 10 s) or hangs. You expect, as the code's own comment ('fail if classification takes more than 5s') and its skip-and-continue timeout branch intend, that only that document counts as a timeout and the other documents are still classified and counted. Instead the timed-out classification is never cancelled and keeps the generator's only worker thread, so the next documents wait behind it, their own 5 s waits expire while they are still queued, and they are dropped too: with a hung first document 0 of 2 instantly classifiable documents are counted (empty matrix, average time Infinity), with a 12 s one 1 of 2.

bugs.area: search / ControlledRealTimeReopenThread (NRT generation tracking: close, the HandleRefresh refresh listener, waitForGeneration)
bugs.title: ControlledRealTimeReopenThread.close never unregisters its refresh listener, so one later refresh of the still-open ReferenceManager overwrites the Long.MAX_VALUE 'closed' generation and an untimed waitForGeneration on the closed instance can block forever
bugs.summary: You use a ControlledRealTimeReopenThread with a SearcherManager, close the reopen thread (for example at shutdown), the application refreshes the still-open manager once more, and a request thread that still holds the closed instance calls waitForGeneration(gen) for its own new change. You expect the call to return, because close sets the searching generation to Long.MAX_VALUE 'so any waiting search threads will return', the method's @return says it returns when 'this instance was closed', and a wait with no refresh in between does return at once. Instead the HandleRefresh listener that the constructor registered on the manager is never removed, so that one refresh writes the writer's generation back over Long.MAX_VALUE, and the untimed wait blocks until some later refresh covers gen, which never comes once the manager is closed; only an interrupt releases the thread.
bugs.introduced_commit: 7b90561178d5ab8ca5a165e8f7a3a1e0da48b205 (trunk, svn r1478438; branch_4x 79ee60d41bcc, svn r1478446, the commit the 4.4.0 release contains), 'LUCENE-4967: move NRTManager entirely into a reopen thread so it can interact with any ReferenceManager' by mikemccand (JIRA LUCENE-4967, now #6031, no pull request; its comments do not discuss close semantics or listener removal) [read]. It replaced NRTManager, whose refresh hook kept the closed generation ('if (searchingGen != MAX_SEARCHER_GEN)', LUCENE-3776, 9da52f43527; the sentinel itself from LUCENE-3528, 57461996e2f), with a listener on an external manager that has no such guard; the history does not show whether dropping the guard was deliberate. LUCENE-9304 (18af6325ed9, lucene-solr PR #1427, 8.6.0) moved the generation capture into beforeRefresh, which changed the hang from permanent to 'until the next refresh that covers the target'

bugs.area: util / automaton (RegExp, Operations.repeat; reached from RegexpQuery and the classic and flexible query parsers)
bugs.title: RegExp builds an automaton that doubles with every stacked '+' ('ab' followed by n '+' gives 2^n+2 states for the 3-state language ab+), a 10.0 regression that exhausts a 1 GB heap at about 20 '+'
bugs.summary: You build a RegexpQuery for 'ab' followed by n '+' (directly, or by typing /ab+++.../ into the classic or flexible query parser) and expect a tiny automaton, because '+' means one or more occurrences, so the language is just ab+ (3 states, which is what 9.12.3 builds for any n). Instead the automaton doubles with every '+' (2^n+2 states: 16,386 at n=14, 262,146 at n=18), because RegExp turns each '+' into Operations.repeat(a, 1), which is built as a followed by a* and so copies a, and since 10.0 nothing minimizes in between; with a 1 GB heap about 20 '+' (a 22-character regexp) end in OutOfMemoryError while the query is still being constructed. Stacked {1,} and nested ((x)+)+ double the same way; stacked '*' and '?' do not.
bugs.introduced_commit: 84e4b85b094ccf2dc248ad90a302307d3618b81e, LUCENE-10010 'don't determinize/minimize in RegExp' (PR #513, by rmuir; JIRA LUCENE-10010 is GitHub issue #11049, still open) [exec]. It removed MinimizationOperations.minimize after every RegExp parsing step and the REGEXP_REPEAT_MIN size pre-check ((numStates - 1) * min > determinizeWorkLimit -> TooComplexToDeterminizeException). The two pieces that now double were already there and stayed harmless while every step was minimized: parseRepeatExp maps '+' to makeRepeat(e, 1) (unchanged since the 2010 import b679816a7001), and Operations.repeat(a, count) concatenates count copies of a with repeat(a) (be3cca1e4440 / ba56e757045b, 2014)

bugs.area: queryparser / classic (generated JavaCC parser QueryParser.jj and QueryParserBase.parse)
bugs.title: Classic QueryParser.parse (and its MultiFieldQueryParser, ComplexPhraseQueryParser and ExtendableQueryParser subclasses) throws StackOverflowError instead of the documented ParseException on deeply nested groups (about 2,650-3,700 levels, 5-7 KB of query text, on a 1 MB thread stack)
bugs.summary: You parse a valid query with many nested groups, for example "(".repeat(d) + "a" + ")".repeat(d), with the classic QueryParser.parse(String), which documents '@throws ParseException if the parsing fails' and already turns the generated lexer's TokenMgrError (a java.lang.Error) and clause-limit hits into ParseException, and you expect the query (here just f:a) or a ParseException. Instead the generated recursive-descent grammar calls Query -> Clause -> Query once per '(' with no depth bound, the thread runs out of stack, and java.lang.StackOverflowError escapes parse. On a cold JVM about 2,650 levels (5,331 chars) are enough at -Xss1m and about 5,900 on the 2 MB aarch64 default stack, while the same 100,000-level input parses to f:a on a 256 MB stack.
bugs.introduced_commit: bd3948c539ec1065db8b05b433ea55dbf844ff27 ('Initial revision', 2001-09-18, svn r149570: the import of the pre-existing Lucene CVS tree, committed by Jason van Zyl; the code predates the import; no issue, patch or PR). Both halves are in this first commit: the grammar 'Clause::= ["+", "-"] [<TERM> ":"] ( <TERM> | "(" Query ")" )' generated as Query -> Clause -> '<LPAREN> q=Query(field) <RPAREN>' -> Query with no depth bound, and a parse(String) that catches nothing. The current contract (parse documents and throws only ParseException, converting the lexer's TokenMgrError) took its form in 1a39c55c4c4 (2003-11-13, 'only throw ParseException from parse methods'), after LUCENE-14 (#1092) and 2a96b329a81 (2002-05-06); neither it nor any later commit catches StackOverflowError or bounds the depth. Not a regression. [read]

bugs.area: queryparser / simple (SimpleQueryParser.parseSubQuery / consumeSubQuery recursion)
bugs.title: SimpleQueryParser.parse throws StackOverflowError on deeply nested parentheses, because parseSubQuery and consumeSubQuery recurse once per '(' with no depth bound, although the parser is meant to do its best with any human-entered text
bugs.summary: You give SimpleQueryParser, the parser meant for raw human-entered text, a query with many balanced nested groups, for example "(".repeat(d) + "a" + ")".repeat(d), and expect a Query: its class javadoc says a person can type whatever they want and the parser will do its best to interpret it no matter how poorly composed, parse(String) declares no exception, and at small depths the same input parses to the plain TermQuery f:a. Instead parseSubQuery calls consumeSubQuery for every '(' and consumeSubQuery calls parseSubQuery again on the inner text, one frame pair per level with no depth bound, so a few thousand to about 25,000 levels (about 500 on a 256 KB stack), depending on stack size and JIT state, exhaust the thread stack and java.lang.StackOverflowError escapes parse. The clause limit does not help, because the nested groups collapse to a single clause.

bugs.area: queryparser / xml (CoreParser, QueryBuilderFactory and SpanQueryBuilderFactory with the compound and span builders, DOMUtils)
bugs.title: XML query parser: CoreParser.getQuery(Element) and getSpanQuery(Element) on any JDK, and plain CoreParser.parse(InputStream) on JDK 21 (the 10.x minimum, including the 10.6.0 RC), throw StackOverflowError instead of the declared ParserException on deeply nested queries (on a 1 MB thread stack about 3,000 nesting levels: about 180 KB of nested BooleanQuery XML or 51 KB of nested SpanOr; every release since 1.9.1)
bugs.summary: You give the XML query parser a well-formed query whose elements nest a few thousand levels deep, for example <BooleanQuery><Clause occurs="must"> repeated 3,000 times around one <TermQuery> (about 180 KB; enough on a 1 MB thread stack, while the 2 MB aarch64 default needs 5,000 or more levels), which the shipped DTD allows ('queries/filters of an arbitrary depth and complexity') and which parses fine at 40 levels, and you expect a Query or the ParserException that CoreParser.parse(InputStream), getQuery(Element) and getSpanQuery(Element) declare. Instead java.lang.StackOverflowError escapes, because each compound builder (BooleanQuery, DisjunctionMaxQuery, ConstantScoreQuery and the span builders) calls back into QueryBuilderFactory or SpanQueryBuilderFactory once per nesting level and nothing counts the depth or turns the Error into a ParserException. Whether the plain text path fails depends on the JDK, not on Lucene: JDK 21, the minimum for 10.x including the 10.6.0 RC, has no XML element-depth limit by default and overflows, while JDK 25 (main's minimum) rejects more than 100 nested elements with a ParserException; the DOM entries overflow on every JDK.

bugs.area: queryparser / surround (generated JavaCC parser, QueryParser.jj)
bugs.title: Surround QueryParser.parse throws StackOverflowError instead of its declared ParseException on deeply nested groups (as few as about 740 levels, about 1.5 KB of query text, on a 1 MB thread stack)
bugs.summary: You call the surround parser's documented entry point QueryParser.parse(String), which declares only ParseException and already turns the lexer's TokenMgrError (an Error) into a ParseException, on a valid query with many nested groups, for example "(".repeat(d) + "a" + ")".repeat(d) or a long chain of "(a OR " groups, and expect a query or a ParseException. Instead the generated recursive-descent grammar, which spends seven frames per "(" (FieldsQuery -> OrQuery -> AndQuery -> NotQuery -> NQuery -> WQuery -> PrimaryQuery -> FieldsQuery) and has no depth bound, runs out of stack and java.lang.StackOverflowError escapes parse, so a caller that handles ParseException gets an undeclared Error. On a 1 MB thread stack as few as about 740 nested groups (1,473 chars) are enough on the first deep parse, and an 800-term chain of parenthesised binary ORs (7,884 chars, under the module's 1024-basic-query limit) fails even after JIT warm-up.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter addIndexes(Directory...) and the writer-wide field registry (FieldInfos.FieldNumbers)
bugs.title: A failed addIndexes(Directory...) leaves the incoming fields registered in the writer's field schema, so getFieldNames lists them and later valid documents that use those names differently are rejected until the writer is reopened
bugs.summary: You call IndexWriter#addIndexes(Directory...) with an index whose first field a_new is new to the destination and whose field z_conflict clashes with the destination's schema; the call correctly throws IllegalArgumentException and adds no segment, as its javadoc promises ('either no indexes will have been added or they all will have been'). You expect the writer to be as it was before the call, so that a later document can use a_new with any schema, as it can after the writer is reopened and after the same failure in addIndexes(CodecReader...). Instead the writer keeps a_new registered with the incoming schema, because addIndexes(Directory...) registers each incoming FieldInfo in the writer-wide FieldNumbers map while it iterates and its failure path only deletes the copied files: getFieldNames lists a_new although no segment has it, and a document with NumericDocValuesField('a_new') is rejected ('cannot change field "a_new" from index options=DOCS to inconsistent index options=NONE') until the writer is reopened.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter doc-values updates and the writer-wide field registry (FieldInfos.FieldNumbers)
bugs.title: A rejected IndexWriter#updateDocValues call (an index-sort field, SORTED or SORTED_SET doc values, or a bad later field in the same call) first registers a never-seen field as doc-values-only, so later legal documents that index that field are rejected until the writer is reopened
bugs.summary: You call IndexWriter#updateDocValues (or softUpdateDocument(s) / tryUpdateDocValue) with a field that no document has used yet, and the call is correctly rejected with IllegalArgumentException, for example because the field is part of the index sort or because SORTED and SORTED_SET doc values cannot be updated. bugs.area: index / IndexWriter addIndexes(CodecReader...) failure path (AddIndexesMergeSource queue, SerialMergeScheduler)
bugs.title: A failed addIndexes(CodecReader...) leaves its unstarted merges in the writer-wide addIndexes queue, so the next addIndexes call runs them on the earlier call's readers and fails with AlreadyClosedException if those readers were closed
bugs.summary: You call addIndexes(CodecReader...) with a merge policy that turns the readers into several merges and with SerialMergeScheduler, and the first merge fails (for example disk full); the call throws, adds nothing, and the writer stays open and not tragic. You expect that failed call to be over, so you close its readers and later call addIndexes with other, valid readers, which should merge exactly those readers. Instead the failed call's unstarted merges are still in the writer's shared addIndexes queue, so the next call runs them first and throws AlreadyClosedException 'this IndexReader is closed', leaving its own merge queued in turn, so later calls keep failing this way until rollback or close; if you kept the old readers open, the next call silently runs the stale merge and writes a segment that is never used.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter addIndexes(CodecReader...) (writer-wide AddIndexesMergeSource queue, SerialMergeScheduler)
bugs.title: With SerialMergeScheduler, a valid addIndexes(CodecReader...) call can run a concurrent call's queued merge on its own thread and fail with that merge's exception, discarding its own completed merge
bugs.summary: Two threads call addIndexes(CodecReader...) on one IndexWriter configured with SerialMergeScheduler; call A's source is corrupt (or hits a read error) and call B's source is valid. You expect A to fail with its own exception and B to add its documents, as happens in either serial order and with the default ConcurrentMergeScheduler, because IndexWriter is documented as safe for concurrent calls to any method and each addIndexes call already rethrows the failures of its own merges. Instead B, which holds the scheduler, runs A's queued merge on its own thread after finishing its own, receives A's exception (for example CorruptIndexException 'checksum failed (hardware problem?)' naming A's source file), deletes its own completed merge and adds nothing, while A throws the same exception.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter addIndexes(CodecReader...) entry check vs deleteAll (abortMerges)
bugs.title: addIndexes(CodecReader...) throws AlreadyClosedException 'this IndexWriter is closed' on an open writer when it overlaps a deleteAll that is waiting for a running merge to abort, although deleteAll's javadoc says such callers may receive MergeAbortedException
bugs.summary: One thread calls deleteAll on an IndexWriter while a merge is running, and another thread calls addIndexes(CodecReader...) on the same writer. You expect the overlapping call either to succeed or to fail with MergePolicy.MergeAbortedException, as deleteAll's javadoc says for concurrent addIndexes(CodecReader) callers and as most such overlaps do. Instead, when the call reaches its entry check while deleteAll is waiting for the running merge to abort, it throws AlreadyClosedException 'this IndexWriter is closed. Cannot execute addIndexes(CodecReaders...) API' although the writer is open: isOpen is true, deleteAll returns normally and the next addIndexes call on the same writer succeeds.

bugs.area: core / search: TermInSetQuery equality (MultiTermQuery rewrite methods); consequence in index / IndexWriter delete-by-query buffering
bugs.title: TermInSetQuery.equals/hashCode ignore the rewrite method, so set queries that match different documents compare equal, and IndexWriter's delete-by-query buffer then applies only one of them
bugs.summary: Since 9.6.0 TermInSetQuery is a MultiTermQuery whose rewrite method decides which documents it matches and how it scores, but its equals/hashCode still compare only the field and terms: new TermInSetQuery("f", [a]) equals SortedSetDocValuesField.newSlowSetQuery("f", [a]) although on a field with only doc values they match 0 and 1 documents, and on an ordinary field new TermInSetQuery("f", [a, b]) equals its TopTermsScoringBooleanQueryRewrite(1) variant although they match 2 and 1 documents. You expect queries that match different documents to be unequal, as PrefixQuery, AutomatonQuery, FuzzyQuery and TermRangeQuery are when only the rewrite method differs. Instead anything keyed on the un-rewritten query treats the two as one: IndexWriter.deleteDocuments with both queries in one flush window applies only the first, so a doc-values delete silently does not happen, or a document added in between is deleted although no call matched it.

bugs.area: queries / intervals (PayloadFilteredTermIntervalsSource equality; IntervalQuery dedup and cache keys)
bugs.title: Intervals.term(term, payloadFilter) sources compare equal whatever their payload filter, so Intervals.or/ordered/unordered, BooleanQuery rewrite and the query cache merge sources that match different positions
bugs.summary: You index a field with a payload at each position and build two sources on the same term with different payload filters, for example a@0 = Intervals.term("a", payload is 'pos: 0') and a@1 = Intervals.term("a", payload is 'pos: 1'), which on their own match different documents. You expect Intervals.or(a@0, a@1) to match both sets, ordered(a@0, a@1) to match the document 'a a', FILTER a@0 + FILTER a@1 to match only that document, and a query cache to keep the two queries apart. Instead PayloadFilteredTermIntervalsSource.equals/hashCode compare only the term, so the two sources are equal: or keeps one of them, ordered and unordered become 'a@0 twice' and match nothing, the two FILTER clauses collapse into one (extra hits), MUST a@0 + MUST_NOT a@1 is rewritten to MatchNoDocsQuery, and a cached searcher returns the first filter's hits for the second, all with no error.

bugs.area: join / JoinUtil numeric score join (PointInSetIncludingScoreQuery equals/hashCode)
bugs.title: Numeric score joins (JoinUtil numeric overload, PointInSetIncludingScoreQuery) compare equal when only their per-value join scores differ, so DisjunctionMaxQuery keeps only one of two such joins and BooleanQuery merges them, returning wrong, clause-order-dependent scores
bugs.summary: You build two numeric score joins with JoinUtil.createJoinQuery("fromId", false, "toId", Integer.class, fromQuery, searcher, ScoreMode.Max), one over from-index A and one over from-index B; both collect the join value 7 and score the to-document 0.3648 and 0.4311, and you expect DisjunctionMaxQuery([qa, qb], 0) to give the maximum 0.4311, as the string-key joins over the same data do. Instead qa.equals(qb) is true with equal hash codes, because PointInSetIncludingScoreQuery's equals/hashCode compare the score mode, to field, from query and collected join values but not the per-value scores (aggregatedJoinScores) or multipleValuesPerDocument, so DisjunctionMaxQuery keeps one of the two equal disjuncts (it rewrites to '(toId:{7} | toId:{7})') and scores 0.3648. The same happens with one from searcher and two from fields whose value sets coincide, where the result then depends on clause order, and BooleanQuery SHOULD(qa) SHOULD(qb) is folded into one boosted clause that loses the second join's scores.

bugs.area: expressions / JavascriptCompiler code generation (boolean operators on long-typed operands: bitwise and shift results, hex and octal literals)
bugs.title: Expressions: !, &&, || and ?: keep only the low 32 bits of a bitwise/shift result or hex/octal literal, so a non-zero value such as 1 << 32 or 0x100000000 counts as false
bugs.summary: You compile a Lucene expression that tests a high bit of a long field, such as '(flags & 0x100000000) ? 10: 1' over a NumericDocValuesField with flags = 2^32 + 1, and expect 10, because 'flags & 0x100000000' evaluates to 4294967296 and '(flags & 0x100000000) != 0' is 1. Instead you get 1: the compiler asks for the operand of !, &&, || and ?: as a 32-bit int and narrows a long-typed operand (the result of & | ^ ~ << >> >>>, or a hex/octal literal) by keeping only its low 32 bits, so every non-zero value whose low 32 bits are zero counts as false. The same number is true when written as the decimal literal 4294967296, as a variable or as '((1 << 32) + 0)', but false as '0x100000000' or '(1 << 32)'.

bugs.title: Doc-values range queries from *RangeDocValuesField.newSlowIntersectsQuery base equals/hashCode on the caller's min/max arrays but match the bounds copied at construction, so queries built from reused arrays compare equal while matching different ranges
bugs.summary: You build a doc-values range query with, for example, IntRangeDocValuesField.newSlowIntersectsQuery(field, min, max), then write new values into the same min and max arrays and build a second query, as a loop that ORs several ranges through one scratch array pair does. bugs.area: search / kNN query execution (DocAndScoreQuery public factory, new in 11.0 via #16686; Weight#count and DocIdSetIterator contracts)
bugs.title: DocAndScoreQuery.createDocAndScoreQuery (public on main since #16686) keeps repeated doc ids: a document listed twice is counted and returned twice, and a repeated first document of a segment is iterated by the previous segment as doc id == maxDoc (a deleted or MUST_NOT-excluded document comes back, or a search with deletions or a doc-values sort throws)
bugs.summary: You build a query with the public DocAndScoreQuery.createDocAndScoreQuery from a TopDocs that lists some document twice, for example the concatenated, score-sorted results of two KnnFloatVectorQuery searches that both found it, and you expect what the javadoc promises, a query that 'matches exactly the documents in topK', so each document is counted and returned once. Instead every entry is kept: for 4 documents found through both fields IndexSearcher#count and totalHits are 8, each hit comes back twice and the leaf iterator returns 1 1 2 2 3 3 4 4. When the repeated document is the first document of a segment (docs [64, 64, 65] with segment 1 starting at 64), Arrays.binarySearch in findSegmentStarts can land on the later copy, so segment 0's iterator returns doc 64, which equals its maxDoc: a plain search then throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from the live docs when segment 0 has deletions, a doc-values sort throws or sorts the document by another document's value, and when segment 0 has no deletions the document is returned even if it is deleted or excluded by a MUST_NOT clause.

The mechanism itself (copy every entry after the doc-id sort; Arrays.binarySearch at each docBase in findSegmentStarts) dates from 624560a3d70 (LUCENE-9614, msokolov, 2021-08-13, first released in 9.0.0) [read] and was harmless while only Lucene's duplicate-free internal callers could reach it.

bugs.area: search / kNN query rewrite (AbstractKnnVectorQuery#mergeLeafResults extension point, optimistic re-entry pass) and DocAndScoreQuery max score
bugs.title: AbstractKnnVectorQuery#mergeLeafResults is documented to return hits in any order, but rewrite reads the k-th score from the last entry and DocAndScoreQuery the max score from the first, so an override that only reorders the hits changes the results
bugs.summary: You subclass KnnFloatVectorQuery and override mergeLeafResults, whose javadoc says it returns 'index-level kNN results (no constraint on their ordering)' and is 'useful for reading and / or modifying the final results', so that it returns exactly the default merge's hits in another order (same documents, same scores). You expect the same search results as the stock query. Instead rewrite takes the k-th score from the last entry and DocAndScoreQuery the max score from the first, so with doc-id order a top-1 search for the kNN query OR a 0.5-boosted term returns doc 0 (score 0.51) instead of the exact match, doc 200000 (score 1.0), and on a 10-segment index the k = 50 query re-enters no segment and returns farther documents (first differing doc 16000 instead of 19950).

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter statistics (soft deletes)
bugs.title: IndexWriter#hasDeletions ignores committed soft deletes in segments the writer has not pooled, so a writer reopened on an index whose only deletions are soft deletes (or one that took such segments through addIndexes(Directory)) answers false, and true once an NRT reader is opened
bugs.summary: You configure a soft-deletes field, soft-delete a document (softUpdateDocument, or updateDocValues on that field), commit, close, and open a new IndexWriter on the index; you expect hasDeletions to return true, because its javadoc says 'Returns true if this index has deletions', IndexWriterConfig#setSoftDeletesField says a soft-deleted document 'is treated as if it has been hard-deleted through the IndexWriter API', and the same writer's getDocStats reports maxDoc 3 and numDocs 2. Instead it returns false, with -ea and -da, until DirectoryReader.open(writer) puts the segment into the reader pool; after that the same call on the unchanged index returns true. The loop over committed segments uses SegmentCommitInfo#hasDeletions (delGen != -1, hard deletes only), while the buffered and pooled branches of the same method count soft deletes; the one-line fix is info.getDelCount(softDeletesEnabled) > 0.

bugs.area: highlighter / UnifiedHighlighter builder and highlight flags (UnifiedHighlighter.evaluateFlags(Builder) never reads Builder.flags)
bugs.title: UnifiedHighlighter.Builder#withFlags is silently ignored: the highlighter always takes its flags from the four boolean builder options
bugs.summary: You build a UnifiedHighlighter with Builder#withFlags(EnumSet.of(MULTI_TERM_QUERY)), whose javadoc says the set 'will override' the four boolean builder options, and expect it to behave like the same flags chosen through those options: for a PhraseQuery 'alpha beta' on 'alpha beta. alpha gamma.' that gives 'alpha beta. alpha gamma.'. Instead the constructor's evaluateFlags(Builder) tests the highlighter's own flags field, which is still null at that point, rather than the builder's, so the set passed to withFlags is never read: getFlags returns the defaults [PHRASES, MULTI_TERM_QUERY, PASSAGE_RELEVANCY_OVER_SPEED, WEIGHT_MATCHES] and the phrase is highlighted strictly as 'alpha beta. alpha gamma.'. Every set is ignored the same way, including the empty set (a PrefixQuery is still highlighted), with or without assertions.

bugs.title: KatakanaRomanizer.romanize(CharsRef) ignores CharsRef.offset, so a CharsRef that is a slice of a larger char is romanized from chars[0, length) instead of the slice (latent: Lucene's own JapaneseCompletionFilter always passes offset 0)

bugs.area: analysis-common / util OpenStringBuilder (public char-buffer helper; in-tree users KStemmer and HTMLStripCharFilter)
bugs.title: OpenStringBuilder.write(OpenStringBuilder arr) copies as many chars as this builder's own length instead of arr's length, so it appends nothing, appends chars from arr's buffer past arr's end (NULs or stale earlier content), or throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
bugs.summary: You append one OpenStringBuilder to another with dst.write(src) and expect dst to grow by src's contents, as it does with dst.append(src) and with every other write overload of the class. Instead the method copies dst's own length worth of chars out of src's buffer: an empty dst gets nothing (writing "lucene" gives ""), "hello" plus "ab" gives "helloab" followed by 3 NUL chars, a src that was reset and refilled with "q" leaks its earlier content ("1234" becomes "1234qECR"), and a dst longer than src's backing array throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The cause is one token: write(OpenStringBuilder arr) calls write(arr.buf, 0, len) (OpenStringBuilder.java:140), where len is the receiver's field, not arr.len.

bugs.area: spatial-extras / spatial4j bridge to spatial3d (Geo3dDistanceCalculator.within, the default DistanceCalculator that Geo3dSpatialContextFactory installs)
bugs.title: Geo3dDistanceCalculator.within returns the opposite of 'distance <= limit' for every finite distance, so the default distance calculator of the Geo3d spatial context answers every within call backwards
bugs.summary: You create a spatial context with Geo3dSpatialContextFactory and ask its distance calculator whether the point (1, 0) is within 10 degrees of (0, 0), with ctx.getDistCalc.within(from, 1, 0, 10), and expect true: distance returns 1.0 degree, and the spatial4j DistanceCalculator contract says within is true when the distance is <= the limit. Instead it returns false, and within(from, 50, 0, 10) returns true although the distance is 50 degrees. The method body is 'return (distance < distance(from, toX, toY));', the exact negation of the contract, so every answer with a finite distance is inverted, including within(p, p, 0).

bugs.area: spatial3d / geom distance styles (Vector.normalDistance[Squared]; DistanceStyle.NORMAL and NORMAL_SQUARED point-to-point distances in GeoCircle and GeoPath)
bugs.title: geo3d NORMAL and NORMAL_SQUARED point distances are wrong on WGS84 and other ellipsoids because Vector.normalDistance assumes a unit-length vector, so the NORMAL distance from a point to itself is up to about 0.0045 planet units (0.00165, about 10.5 km, at latitude 0.3 rad) instead of 0
bugs.summary: You build a geo3d circle or path on PlanetModel.WGS84 (or call Vector.normalDistance or DistanceStyle.NORMAL.computeDistance on two GeoPoints) and ask for the NORMAL or NORMAL_SQUARED distance, which Vector's javadoc defines as 'the normal (perpendicular) distance to a vector described by a vector taken from the origin', and expect 0 for a point and itself and about 7.85e-6 planet units for a point 50 m from a circle's centre. Instead both come out as 0.00165 (about 10.5 km) at latitude 0.3 rad, because Vector.normalDistanceSquared projects onto the receiver with t = dotProduct(v) and never divides by |this|^2, which is exact only for unit vectors, while WGS84 surface points have lengths between about 0.998 and 1.0011. The same offset enters every NORMAL and NORMAL_SQUARED circle and path distance on non-spherical planet models, with no error; on SPHERE the values are exact.

It added PlanetModel and WGS84, so surface points stopped being unit vectors, and made GeoPoint.arcDistance divide by both magnitudes, but left Vector.normalDistance[Squared] unchanged. The unit-length formula itself dates from the sphere-only first geo3d check-in bde056c7632 (LUCENE-6196, #7258, 2015-04-13; evaluate renamed to dotProduct in c561d376bc4, 2015-05-01), where every point the library built was a unit vector; the public DistanceStyle.NORMAL / NORMAL_SQUARED came with LUCENE-6578 (#7636; 688c67f8ff2 trunk, 780e4040238 branch_5x, 2015-07-01). bugs.area: spatial3d / geom path distances (GeoStandardPath component tree: PathSegment, BaseSegmentEndpoint, PathNode; DistanceStyle aggregation forms)
bugs.title: GeoPath.computeDistance with DistanceStyle.LINEAR_SQUARED or NORMAL_SQUARED on a path of width > 0 (GeoStandardPath) returns the fourth power of the distance instead of its square for points inside a path segment, because the segment's result is converted back from aggregation form twice (regression since 9.5.0)
bugs.summary: You build a path with GeoPathFactory.makeGeoPath and a width > 0 and call computeDistance with DistanceStyle.LINEAR_SQUARED (or NORMAL_SQUARED), expecting the square of the LINEAR (or NORMAL) path distance, which is what DistanceStyle's 'convert to aggregation form, aggregate, convert back' contract gives and what end-cap points, the zero-width path and Lucene 9.4.2 return. For a point inside a path segment you get the square of that value instead: 0.00803 rather than 0.0896 for a point whose LINEAR distance is 0.299, so the value jumps about 6x across a segment's end cutoff plane and can rank a farther point ahead of a nearer one. The cause is a leftover conversion from the 2022 path refactor: PathSegment.distance already converts its result back from aggregation form, and GeoStandardPath.distance converts the component tree's result back a second time.

bugs.area: spatial3d / geom path distances (GeoDegeneratePath, the zero-width path; DistanceStyle aggregation forms)
bugs.title: On a zero-width geo3d path (GeoDegeneratePath), computePathCenterDistance with DistanceStyle.LINEAR_SQUARED or NORMAL_SQUARED returns the unsquared distance and computeOutsideDistance returns the fourth power, instead of the squared distance, because the 2022 path refactor converted the path components to aggregation form but not the two places that combine them (regression since 9.5.0)
bugs.summary: You build a zero-width path with GeoPathFactory.makeGeoPath(planetModel, 0, points) and call computePathCenterDistance or computeOutsideDistance with DistanceStyle.LINEAR_SQUARED (or NORMAL_SQUARED), expecting the square of the LINEAR (or NORMAL) distance, which is what DistanceStyle's 'convert to aggregation form, aggregate, convert back' contract gives, what the same path with width 1e-6 returns and what Lucene 9.4.2 returned. Instead, for a point 0.01 rad beside the path, computePathCenterDistance returns about 0.01 (the unsquared distance) and computeOutsideDistance returns about 1e-8 (the fourth power) where about 1e-4 is expected. The cause is an incomplete edit in the 2022 path refactor: GeoDegeneratePath's components now return the square root (the aggregation form of the squared styles), but computePathCenterDistance never squares the minimum back, and PathSegment.outsideDistance still returns the plain square, which outsideDistance then squares a second time.

bugs.area: analysis-common / synonym.word2vec (Word2VecSynonymProvider.getSynonyms search size; Word2VecSynonymFilterFactory validation)
bugs.title: Word2VecSynonymFilterFactory accepts any positive maxSynonymsPerTerm, but Word2VecSynonymProvider sizes its HNSW search as maxSynonymsPerTerm + 1 with no clamp to the model size, so very large values (Integer.MAX_VALUE, where the + 1 overflows) make every in-model token throw IllegalArgumentException or OutOfMemoryError
bugs.summary: You configure Word2VecSynonymFilterFactory with maxSynonymsPerTerm=2147483647 (Integer.MAX_VALUE), which its validation accepts ('must be a positive integer greater than 0'), to keep every synonym above minAcceptedSimilarity, and you expect those synonyms or a rejection at configuration time. The analyzer builds, but Word2VecSynonymProvider.getSynonyms passes maxSynonymsPerTerm + 1 (int arithmetic) as topK to HnswGraphSearcher.search, which wraps to Integer.MIN_VALUE, so the first token with a model vector throws IllegalArgumentException 'initialCapacity must be > 0 and < 2147483630; got: -2147483648' from TernaryLongHeap (on 9.7.0 to 10.3.2: 'maxSize must be > 0...' from LongHeap). Because the search size is never clamped to the model size and the search allocates its queues of topK entries up front, values close to Integer.MAX_VALUE fail the same way and values from roughly heap-bytes/16 up (1e8 at a 1 GiB heap) throw OutOfMemoryError, even for a 3-term model.

bugs.area: core / search: TopDocs.merge paging window (mergeAux; score, Sort and tie-breaker overloads)
bugs.title: TopDocs.merge(start, topN,...) returns a page of null ScoreDocs, with no error, when start + topN overflows int (for example start = 1 and topN = Integer.MAX_VALUE meaning 'no limit')
bugs.summary: You merge two shards' results (5 hits in total) with TopDocs.merge(1, Integer.MAX_VALUE, shards) to get every hit after the first, and expect the 4 remaining hits in score order, the same as TopDocs.merge(1, 4, shards) returns. Instead you get an array of length 4 in which every entry is null, and no exception: merge adds start + topN in int, the sum wraps to a negative number, and the loop that copies hits never runs. The Sort and tie-breaker overloads behave the same way; start + topN = 2^31 - 1 still works and 2^31 fails.

bugs.area: search / HNSW
bugs.title: Concurrent HNSW build retries a lost entry-node promotion with the wrong query vector
bugs.summary: You build or merge HNSW graphs with more than one merge worker. You expect each node's neighbours to be scored against that node's vector. Instead, when an entry-node promotion is lost to another worker and retried, the shared scorer is not reset, so wrong scores are stored and the persisted topology changes.

bugs.area: codecs / merge instances
bugs.title: Merge instances re-open segment files by name, so merging an old reader after a name reuse can copy another segment's data
bugs.summary: You keep an old NRT reader open, roll back writers until a later writer reuses its segment name, and then merge that reader, for example with addIndexes(CodecReader...). You expect the merge to copy the old reader's own stored fields and vectors. Instead its merge instance opens the file again by name and copies the newer segment's data, silently (CheckIndex on the target is clean) or, for compound files of another layout, with a loud exception.

bugs.area: store / FSDirectory pending deletes (delete retry vs. the createOutput/rename revive, thread safety)
bugs.title: FSDirectory: a pending-delete retry running on one thread can delete a file that another thread has just re-created (createOutput) or renamed onto the same name, so a file that was written and closed successfully silently disappears
bugs.summary: On a file system that refuses to delete open files (Windows, or a virus scanner), you delete a file that a reader still holds open, so FSDirectory keeps it as a pending delete; after the reader closes, one thread re-creates that name with createOutput (or renames another file onto it), writes and closes it, while another thread makes any mutating call on the same directory, for example sync of an unrelated file. You expect the new file to stay, like any file that was created, closed and never deleted. Instead the other thread's pending-delete retry, which copied the pending set before the revive, deletes the new file: listAll no longer lists it and openInput fails (on main under the test framework's WindowsFS: 'x was created and closed successfully but is gone: [other]').
