bugs.area: core / util QueryBuilder token boosts on stacked tokens (newSynonymQuery; BoostAttribute from DelimitedBoostTokenFilter and weighted synonyms; reached through the classic and simple query parsers)
bugs.title: QueryBuilder hands a token boost (BoostAttribute) above 1 or equal to 0 on a word that shares its position with a synonym straight to SynonymQuery, which throws IllegalArgumentException, so every query containing that word fails, while the same weight on a word without a synonym works
bugs.summary: You configure weighted synonyms ('leopard, panthera|1.5') or let users type boosts ('leopard|2'), and expect QueryBuilder to apply the weight, as it does for a word without a synonym: 'lion => simba|1.5' gives (body:simba)^1.5 and 'tiger|2' gives (body:tiger)^2.0. But when the boosted token shares its position with another token, QueryBuilder.newSynonymQuery passes the raw boost to SynonymQuery.Builder.addTerm, which accepts only (0, 1], so building the query throws IllegalArgumentException 'boost must be a positive float between 0 (exclusive) and 1 (inclusive)' and QueryParser.parse('spotted leopard') fails with it instead of returning a query or a ParseException. Weights in (0, 1] work on both paths; whether 1.5 or 0 works depends only on whether the analyzer stacked the token.
bugs.introduced_commit: 663611c99c7d48dd31d53ea17644fcecd5e0fad7 '[SOLR-12238] Synonym Queries boost (#357)' (apache/lucene-solr#357; SOLR-12238 and LUCENE-9171 = apache/lucene#10211; branch_8x backport 2752d50dd1dc, same day) [read]. It made QueryBuilder read BoostAttribute, wrap an unstacked token's boost in a BoostQuery and pass a stacked token's boost unchanged to SynonymQuery.Builder.addTerm, whose (0, 1] check comes from LUCENE-8652 (d8cfeba912ea, 2019-03-11, first released in 8.1.0; not a defect on its own, because QueryBuilder passed no boosts before 8.5.0)

bugs.area: analysis-common / synonym (SolrSynonymParser; SynonymGraphFilterFactory and SynonymFilterFactory, format solr)
bugs.title: SolrSynonymParser rejects a whole synonyms file because one line holds only spaces or tabs, although its javadoc says blank lines are comments (ParseException 'Invalid synonym rule at line N', every release since 3.4.0)
bugs.summary: You load a synonyms file such as 'couch, sofa', then a line holding three spaces or a tab, then 'big, large', and expect it to parse, because the SolrSynonymParser javadoc says 'Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are comments'. Instead the whole file is rejected with ParseException 'Invalid synonym rule at line 2': the parser skips a line only when it has zero length (or starts with '#'), so the whitespace-only line is parsed as a rule whose single term trims to the empty string, which the analyzer step rejects. A truly empty line parses fine, and so did whitespace-only lines in the Solr loader this format came from before 3.4.

bugs.title: MappingCharFilterFactory throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException ('Index 256 out of bounds for length 256') when a mapping rule's source or target is longer than 256 characters, because it unescapes every rule string into a fixed char[256] buffer, so the analyzer cannot be built
bugs.summary: You configure the mapping char filter with a mapping file that contains one rule whose source or target is longer than 256 characters, for example "abc" => "<257 x>" or a long boilerplate phrase mapped to "", and expect the factory to build the map (NormalizeCharMap.Builder accepts such strings when called directly, and no limit is documented) or to reject the rule with an IllegalArgumentException that names it, as it does for other bad rules. Instead MappingCharFilterFactory.inform throws java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 256 out of bounds for length 256 from parseString, which copies each unescaped rule string into a fixed 256-character instance buffer without a bounds check. A 256-character string still works, and the limit counts characters after unescaping (256 \uNNNN escapes, 1536 raw characters, pass).

bugs.area: util / sorters (Sorter heap sort, IntroSorter's depth fallback)
bugs.title: Sorter.heapChild overflows int, so IntroSorter's heap-sort fallback compares a negative slot outside [from, to) when 2*to - from > 2^31 (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from ArrayUtil.introSort on a legal array slice)
bugs.summary: You sort a legal slice with IntroSorter, for example ArrayUtil.introSort on the last 1,000 elements of an array of length ArrayUtil.MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH (or a slice of more than 2^30 elements starting at 0), and the element order makes IntroSorter give up on quicksort and fall back to heap sort. You expect the slice [from, to) to be sorted using only slots inside it. Instead Sorter.heapChild computes 2*(i - from) + 1 + from in int, which wraps to a negative number for a node that has no child, siftDown's 'leftChild < to' check lets it through, and compare is called with a negative slot, so the array-backed sort throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException ('Index -2147482757 out of bounds for length 2147483631').

bugs.title: JapaneseCompletionFilterFactory upper-cases the default mode name instead of the configured value, so mode="query" is rejected with IllegalArgumentException while the sibling JapaneseTokenizerFactory accepts lower-case modes (minor consistency defect; no javadoc promises case-insensitive values)

bugs.summary: You call SimpleWKTShapeParser.parse("MULTIPOINT ((1 2), (3 4))"), the Simple Features WKT form in which each point of a multipoint sits in its own parentheses, and expect double {{1, 2}, {3, 4}}, because the class says it parses WKT in compliance with ISO/IEC 13249-3:2016 and it already accepts MULTIPOINT ((1 2)) and the bare legacy form MULTIPOINT (1 2, 3 4). bugs.area: suggest / spell: SpellChecker.indexDictionary (n-gram spell index build, failure cleanup)
bugs.title: SpellChecker.indexDictionary never closes or rolls back its IndexWriter when the build throws, so the spell index stays write-locked and every later indexDictionary, clearIndex or IndexWriter on it in the same JVM fails with LockObtainFailedException until the JVM restarts
bugs.summary: You build a spell index with SpellChecker.indexDictionary and the build throws, for example because the word-list file is not valid UTF-8, has a line longer than 32766 bytes, or its reader hits an I/O error; you fix the input and call indexDictionary or clearIndex again. You expect the retry to work, because the failed call should close or roll back the IndexWriter it opened. Instead indexDictionary closes its writer only on the success path, so the writer, which the caller cannot reach, keeps the spell index's write lock, and every later write to that index in the same JVM throws LockObtainFailedException 'Lock held by this virtual machine' until the JVM restarts.

bugs.area: index / deletion policies (PersistentSnapshotDeletionPolicy save-file failure handling)
bugs.title: After one failed fsync of its save file, PersistentSnapshotDeletionPolicy's next fault-free snapshot or release fails with FileAlreadyExistsException on its own leftover file: persist leaves the complete snapshots_N behind when Directory.sync throws and does not advance its generation, while snapshot and release undo their change in memory
bugs.summary: You call PersistentSnapshotDeletionPolicy.snapshot (or release), fsync of the new save file snapshots_N fails once, the call throws and the policy undoes the change in memory; you expect the next call, with no fault, to work. Instead persist has left the complete snapshots_N in the directory (its delete-on-failure block covers only creating and writing the file, not the sync) and has not advanced its generation, so the next snapshot or release writes the same name and fails with FileAlreadyExistsException; that call's cleanup deletes the leftover, and the call after it works. Secondary, contract open: a policy re-opened before that next call adopts the leftover, so a snapshot that threw is in effect and a release that threw has taken effect.

bugs.area: index / IndexWriter commit failure path (prepareCommit, IndexFileDeleter reference counts, merge-on-commit)
bugs.title: A commit that fails before startCommit (merge-on-commit setup, doAfterFlush, the merge scheduler or the event listener) keeps references on all of its files, so the still-open writer never deletes them, not even on rollback or close
bugs.summary: You call commit and it throws a non-tragic exception early, for example an IOException while Lucene opens the small segments it merges as part of the commit (on by default), or from your MergePolicy.findFullFlushMerges or doAfterFlush override; the writer stays open, as Lucene intends. You expect the writer to delete the files of that failed commit once they are no longer needed: after later merges and commits, on deleteUnusedFiles, on rollback (whose javadoc says it removes any temporary files) or on close. Instead prepareCommit has already taken a reference on every file of the commit and releases it only if startCommit fails, so these files keep a positive reference count and stay on disk until a new IndexWriter opens the directory.

bugs.title: OfflineSorter.sort with an ExecutorService runs its failure cleanup before the partition-sort and merge tasks it already submitted have finished, so each task still queued or running leaves a temp file (prefix_sort_N.tmp) behind that nothing deletes (released since 6.6.0)
bugs.summary: You give OfflineSorter your own ExecutorService so it sorts partitions in parallel, and when sort fails (an I/O error, a truncated input file, or an interrupt of the sorting thread) you expect it to delete every temp file it created, as it does without an executor and as its own code comment says ('So we can remove any partially written temp files on exception'). bugs.summary: You call WordBreakSpellChecker.setMaxEvaluations(n), documented as 'the maximum number of word combinations to evaluate', and then suggestWordCombinations, and you expect at most n combined-term lookups and so at most n suggestions. Instead the limit cuts off only the rest of the one left term at which the counter first equals n, and every later left term is evaluated in full: with every 2-6 letter run of 'abcdef' indexed, the query [a, b, c, d, e, f], maxChanges=5 and maxEvaluations=1, 11 of the 15 combinations are evaluated and returned, and maxEvaluations=0 evaluates all 15. Nothing is thrown and the work stays bounded by the number of terms times maxChanges; only the configured cap is not applied.

bugs.area: core / index (ParallelLeafReader and ParallelCompositeReader stored fields, StoredFieldVisitor protocol)
bugs.title: ParallelLeafReader stored fields ignore StoredFieldVisitor.Status.STOP: the later parallel readers still offer and deliver fields after the visitor answered STOP
bugs.summary: You split a document over two lockstep indexes (title in index A, price in index B), open them as a ParallelLeafReader, and load the document with a StoredFieldVisitor that answers STOP at title and YES otherwise, expecting the visit to end at title, as STOP promises ('stop processing any other fields for this document') and as a single index holding the same document does. Instead the second parallel reader still asks needsField(price) and delivers price=42 after the STOP, because ParallelLeafReader.storedFields.document hands the visitor to each parallel reader in turn and never checks its answer. ParallelCompositeReader builds ParallelLeafReaders, so it behaves the same.

bugs.area: queries / spans: SpanMultiTermQueryWrapper top-N rewrite methods vs the core IndexSearcher clause limit
bugs.title: SpanMultiTermQueryWrapper's top-N span rewrites (TopTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite, FrequentTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite) do not cap their size at IndexSearcher#getMaxClauseCount, so a span-wrapped FuzzyQuery that works unwrapped throws TooManyNestedClauses
bugs.summary: You wrap new FuzzyQuery(term, 2, 0, 2000, true) in SpanMultiTermQueryWrapper (for example to use it inside a SpanNearQuery) and search an index where more than 1024 terms are within two edits. FuzzyQuery documents that a maxExpansions above IndexSearcher#getMaxClauseCount is replaced by the limit, and the span top-N rewrites say they 'will not overflow the boolean max clause count', so you expect the same capped expansion the plain FuzzyQuery gets (it runs with 1024 terms). Instead the span rewrite keeps up to maxExpansions terms (TopTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite.getMaxSize returns Integer.MAX_VALUE, and FrequentTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite sizes its queue with the caller's size only), and IndexSearcher.rewrite throws IndexSearcher$TooManyNestedClauses ('maxClauseCount is set to 1024').
bugs.introduced_commit: 53f56fb7ad44afab9c78fab2e89737438093247f (LUCENE-8811 'Move max clause checks to IndexSearcher', apache/lucene#9855, committed by romseygeek with patches by atris, 2019-06-26, first released in 9.0.0) is where the failure starts: IndexSearcher.rewrite began to count every clause of the rewritten query with a QueryVisitor, span terms included, and the commit did not touch SpanMultiTermQueryWrapper. The missing cap it exposes is older: TopTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite.getMaxSize returning Integer.MAX_VALUE and the mapping of a TopTermsRewrite (FuzzyQuery's) to new TopTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite(size) come from ac71ebc23716 (LUCENE-2754, apache/lucene#3828, uschindler, 2010-11-14; 3.x backport 7d137513808), written when SpanOrQuery had no clause limit (sibling comment 'we accept all terms as SpanOrQuery has no limits', 1d0515124e2, LUCENE-2757). The FrequentTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite half is 156fb97fd33 on main and 3572e2c03f0 on branch_10x / branch_10_6 (apache/lucene#16484, 2026-08-18, unreleased). [read]

bugs.area: queries / spans (SpanMultiTermQueryWrapper.FrequentTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite queue sizing; core ScoringRewrite creates the top-level builder before collecting terms; util PriorityQueue pre-allocates maxSize + 1 slots)
bugs.title: SpanMultiTermQueryWrapper.FrequentTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite (new in 10.6.0) sizes its priority queue from maxSize before collecting any term, so maxSize >= 2147483631 (for example Integer.MAX_VALUE as 'no limit') makes every rewrite throw IllegalArgumentException, and a large maxSize allocates a (maxSize + 1)-slot array on every rewrite
bugs.summary: You wrap a PrefixQuery in SpanMultiTermQueryWrapper, call setRewriteMethod(new FrequentTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite(Integer.MAX_VALUE)), whose javadoc promises only that it 'keeps at most maxSize terms' (ranked by document frequency instead of boost, unlike TopTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite), and expect it to keep all 3 matching terms, as TopTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite(Integer.MAX_VALUE) does on the same index. Instead the constructor accepts the value and every search then throws IllegalArgumentException 'maxSize must be >= 0 and < 2147483631; got: 2147483647', because getTopLevelBuilder returns PriorityQueue.usingComparator(maxSize, order) and ScoringRewrite.rewrite calls it before it collects any term, so the internal queue pre-allocates maxSize + 1 slots (or rejects a size it cannot allocate) instead of being sized by the terms actually found; for the same reason a large legal cap such as 2^26 allocates about 268 MB per rewrite for 3 terms. Sizing the queue lazily, by min(maxSize, collected terms), as the sibling TopTermsRewrite does with a growing queue, fixes both and leaves every result unchanged.
bugs.introduced_commit: 156fb97fd33d8f2039309381ccaca4a6a7e59e14 on main, 'LUCENE-6513: Add FrequentTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite' (apache/lucene#16484, author dsmiley; the feature request is #7571): it added the class with getTopLevelBuilder { return PriorityQueue.usingComparator(maxSize, order); }, so the defect was born with the API [read]. On branch_10x and branch_10_6: the cherry-pick 3572e2c03f0 plus 2bcbe3d82ed (#16532, dweiss, 'Fix API only available on main'), which replaced usingComparator with new PriorityQueue<>(maxSize) { lessThan } and kept the eager sizing. The older ingredients are unchanged: ScoringRewrite has created its builder before collecting terms since at least 2015, PriorityQueue has pre-allocated maxSize + 1 slots and rejected sizes >= ArrayUtil.MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH since at least 2018 (4c646dab3fb), and TopTermsRewrite has used Math.min(size, getMaxSize) with a growing queue since 2010. The introducing commits were not built (disk rule); git diff 156fb97fd33..a9779ef3c193 is empty for the five relevant files, and 2bcbe3d82ed..4ae946e5a9b differs only by diamond-operator edits (#16592) [read]

bugs.area: util / BytesRefArray (iterator(Comparator) with a null comparator)
bugs.title: BytesRefArray.iterator(Comparator) throws NullPointerException for a null comparator once the array holds 2 or more values, instead of iterating in append order as its javadoc says (regression since 8.5.0, LUCENE-9228)
bugs.summary: You append two or more values (for example c, a, b) to a BytesRefArray and call iterator((Comparator<BytesRef>) null), expecting the values back in append order, as the method's javadoc promises ('Otherwise the order is the same as the values were appended') and as Lucene 8.4.1 and earlier do. Instead the call throws NullPointerException ('Cannot invoke Comparator.compare... because this.val$cmp is null', from StringSorter$1.compare via BytesRefArray.sort), because the method now always sorts with the given comparator; with 0 or 1 values, or with the no-arg iterator, append order still comes back. The one-line fix restores the pre-8.5 null check ('return iterator(comp == null ? null: sort(comp, false));'); a maintainer may instead prefer to correct the javadoc.

bugs.area: geo / XY shapes (XYPolygon winding order, Tessellator.tessellate(XYPolygon), XYShape.createIndexableFields and createDocValueField)
bugs.title: XYPolygon evaluates its winding sum in float, so valid polygons with large finite coordinates (differences of about 1.8e19 or more) can get the wrong winding order, and XYShape rejects them as 'Unable to Tessellate shape'
bugs.summary: You build an XYPolygon with large but finite float coordinates, which the constructor accepts (any finite float), for example the triangle (0,0), (2^66,2^66), (2^67,2^66), and index it with XYShape.createIndexableFields; you expect it to index exactly like the same triangle at scale 1, because multiplying every coordinate by a power of two is exact and changes neither the shape nor its orientation. The constructor computes the winding sum with float products, which overflow to Infinity once coordinate differences reach about 1.8e19; Infinity minus Infinity is NaN, and a NaN sum is labelled CW. The Tessellator then links the ring the wrong way round, finds no ear to cut, and rejects the valid polygon with 'Unable to Tessellate shape. Possible malformed shape detected.'
bugs.introduced_commit: 0c09481374cab029d57b0f9b45994822c0dcd39b (master; LUCENE-8632 'New XYShape Field and Queries for indexing and searching general cartesian geometries', nknize, apache/lucene-solr#726, migrated issue apache/lucene#9678; branch_8x backport 81c88e2df30428f61fad6129525d839c57e08504, shipped in 8.2.0 in the lucene-sandbox module) [read]. The float arithmetic came from the PR-internal commit 4d0c96f40b8dd9d2f5c2bb2112e55a81dd47e1cd ('change XYPolygon and XYLine API to accept floats instead of doubles', 2019-06-26): it turned the constructor parameters into float, which shadow the double fields, while the loop kept reading the parameters; at its parent 1c982b90199 the sum was computed in double, and the PR was squash-merged, so no mainline commit had the double version. Later commits kept the expression: 4a54ffb553a (LUCENE-9218, 8.5.0) made the fields float, 2d6ad2fee6d (LUCENE-9570) only reformatted the two lines. No build at 0c09481374c or its parent was made (the API does not exist before it).

bugs.area: core / geo (Rectangle.fromPointDistance circle bounding box, used by LatLon distance and Circle queries)
bugs.title: Rectangle.fromPointDistance throws 'invalid longitude NaN' for some legal circles whose edge stops just short of a pole, so LatLon distance queries on them fail with IllegalArgumentException
bugs.summary: You run LatLonPoint.newDistanceQuery("p", 0.43945312499999994, 0, 9958692.080819247), a valid centre and a finite, non-negative radius whose circle stops about 7 cm short of the north pole, and expect it to match the two indexed points inside the circle. Instead IndexSearcher.count throws IllegalArgumentException 'invalid longitude NaN; must be between -180.0 and 180.0' from Rectangle.fromPointDistance, and LatLonDocValuesField.newSlowDistanceQuery throws the same when it is built. The bounding box computes asin(sin(r) / cos(lat)) without a clamp, and SloppyMath.cos, which is not monotone across its lookup-table switches, makes the quotient 1.0000000000000002 although its exact value is below 1, so asin returns NaN.
bugs.introduced_commit: 92b659ab9e1a (trunk) / 3a189ff68dec (branch_5x, shipped in 5.5.0): LUCENE-6908 (migrated as #7966) by nknize, which replaced StrictMath.asin/sin/cos with SloppyMath in the non-pole branch deltaLon = asin(sin(radDistance) / cos(radLat)) and added sin(a) = cos(a - pi/2) [read]. The unclamped quotient itself is older (d369057766ae, LUCENE-6780, 2015-10-21, sandbox, StrictMath trig), but that form threw for no input in the bounded scans. Later commits moved or renamed the code and kept the formula: 665041c52f08 (LUCENE-6997, to lucene-spatial), ce3114233bdc (LUCENE-7123, GeoUtils.sloppySin), 6c219e99e4b / 951563aa427 (LUCENE-7163, core Rectangle.fromPointDistance, 6.1.0) and 3fcc87752a42 (#14516, renamed to SloppyMath.sin, 10.3.0); 045659533cd (LUCENE-7147, the 7 cm pad, 6.1.0) only moved the witness radius. Never clamped: not a regression

bugs.area: spatial3d / geom path distances (GeoStandardPath and GeoDegeneratePath PathSegment foot selection; Geo3DDocValuesField.newPathSort)
bugs.title: geo3d path distance methods (GeoStandardPath, GeoDegeneratePath) and Geo3DDocValuesField.newPathSort throw RuntimeException "Can't find world intersection" for a point inside the path that sits at the edge of the 1e-12 tolerance band of a segment's cutoff plane
bugs.summary: You build a geo3d path (GeoPathFactory.makeGeoPath, or the path of Geo3DDocValuesField.newPathSort) and ask for the distance of a point that the path reports as inside it, expecting a number (GeoDistance.computeDistance documents a distance, or +Infinity outside the shape). Instead, when the point sits at the very edge of the 1e-12 tolerance band of a segment's cutoff plane, the call throws RuntimeException("Can't find world intersection..."): on the unit sphere a point 3.4e-6 rad beside a path of width 1e-4 and 1e-12 rad past its middle point throws instead of returning about 0.1000034, the same happens for a zero-width path's nearest and centre distance, and a 500 km path sort whose middle point sits at a stored document's decoded longitude makes IndexSearcher.search throw. The cause: the segment's tolerant section test accepts the point, then the same tolerant test rejects both rounded perpendicular feet of the point on the path, and the code throws instead of picking one.
bugs.introduced_commit: 688c67f8ff22b72b9df4ed2f92d26b909563b2b1 on trunk (svn r1688545) and its branch_5x backport 780e4040238713c2ff85c4b981cbc6b80aa4094f (svn r1688546), 'LUCENE-6578: Geo3D: compute the distance from a point to a shape' (JIRA LUCENE-6578, now apache/lucene#7636; svn era, no pull request; committed by dsmiley, CHANGES credits DaddyWri (Karl Wright) and David Smiley). It added computeDistance and PathSegment.pathDistance with findIntersections, a strict 'within both cutoff planes' choice of the foot and the else-throw, while SidedPlane.isWithin already accepted points up to MINIMUM_RESOLUTION outside a plane. The same block was later copied into nearestPathDistance and pathCenterDistance (LUCENE-7962, #9011, 2017-09), into GeoDegeneratePath (LUCENE-7955, #9004, 2017-09) and into pathDeltaDistance (LUCENE-8039, #9087, 2017-11-08); the user-facing newPathSort came with LUCENE-7212 (#8267, 2016-05). bugs.area: index / IndexWriter doc-values updates
bugs.title: IndexWriter accepts doc-values updates of the reserved parent field; with index sorting and document blocks this leaves a segment that fails CheckIndex, or an index whose merges fail
bugs.summary: You use index sorting with a parent field (IndexWriterConfig#setParentField) and document blocks, and call IndexWriter#updateNumericDocValue or #updateDocValues on that parent field, for example to give a child document a parent mark or to set a parent's mark to null. You expect the call to be rejected with IllegalArgumentException, as IndexWriter rejects doc-values updates of index-sort fields and any document that contains the parent field ('is a reserved field'), or else the index to stay valid. bugs.summary: You load a Hunspell dictionary with a compound rule such as 'CHECKCOMPOUNDPATTERN o /X z' (a simplified compound form whose second part may begin with anything: hunspell(5) allows empty beginchars with a flag and an optional replacement) and call Hunspell.spell("foz"), and expect true or false; C Hunspell 1.3.2 and 1.7.2 both say false. Instead, with assertions enabled, spell and suggest throw java.lang.AssertionError from WordStorage.lookupWord ('assert length > 0'). The cause: checkCompoundPatternReplacements expands the final 'z' to 'o' plus empty beginchars and puts the break right after 'foo', but never checks that a second part remains, so checkCompoundsAfter looks up a second part of length 0; with -da that lookup finds nothing and spell returns false for the repro.
bugs.introduced_commit: d0ae2bd2b9c9, LUCENE-9717 'Hunspell: support CHECKCOMPOUNDPATTERN' (apache/lucene-solr#2280, by donnerpeter; issue apache/lucene#10756), the root cause: it added checkCompoundPatternReplacements ('int breakPos = pos + pattern.endLength') and 'remainingLength = word.length - breakPos' in checkCompoundsAfter with no check that a second part remains [read] [exec]. Silent at that commit, because the FST lookup returns no entry for an empty word. Made visible as an AssertionError by LUCENE-9825 (4842e0c9cab, 2021-03-05, by donnerpeter, apache/lucene-solr#2459, issue apache/lucene#10864), which added WordStorage.lookupWord with 'assert length > 0' and reached main through the merge f5012a4cdaf (apache/lucene#2, 2021-03-10) [exec]. Reached 8.x through the branch_8x backport c6b964a1157 (apache/lucene-solr#2499, LUCENE-9687). Both steps predate every release, so it is not a regression of a released version
bugs.introduced_date: 2021-02-03 (root cause, silent); 2021-03-10 (AssertionError visible on main); 2021-05-28 (8.x backport with both)

bugs.area: misc / BP merge-time reordering (BpVectorReorderer centroid arithmetic)
bugs.title: BpVectorReorderer scales a zero DOT_PRODUCT/COSINE centroid by 1/sqrt(0), so a split whose vectors cancel out gets a NaN centroid: with assertions on, reordering fails and a reordering merge closes the IndexWriter; with assertions off, that split is silently not refined
bugs.summary: You index DOT_PRODUCT or COSINE float vectors and reorder them with BpVectorReorderer, by calling computeDocMap or by merging through BPReorderingMergePolicy, for example 64 legal unit vectors where docs 0..31 alternate (1,0) and (-1,0) and docs 32..63 are (0,1); you expect a valid reordering, as for any other legal vectors. Instead the half whose vectors cancel out sums to the zero vector, computeCentroid normalizes it by 1/sqrt(0) = Infinity and the centroid becomes NaN. With assertions on, VectorUtil.dotProduct then fails with 'AssertionError: not finite: NaN from <[1.0, 0.0],[NaN, NaN]>' and the merge path closes the IndexWriter; with assertions off nothing throws, but the NaN biases leave that split in doc-ID order.
bugs.introduced_commit: 02a09f6ab124 (#14097 'HNSW BP reordering' by msokolov, main) [exec]; the finite-result assertion in VectorUtil.dotProduct predates the class (071461ece541, #12281, 2023-06-13; #15213 only added the 'not finite' message); not a regression: the class has had this behaviour since it was added
bugs.first_affected_version: unreleased (main only, 11.0.0-SNAPSHOT; CHANGES.txt lists GITHUB#14097 under 11.0.0 and no release tag contains BpVectorReorderer)
bugs.affected_versions: main from 02a09f6ab124 (2025-01-07) through ea57360912ed (2026-10-24) [exec]; upstream main cf398bfb142c (2026-10-26) still has the unguarded line [read]; open PR #15430 (moves the class to core) copies it [read]. bugs.area: search / TopDocs.merge tie breaking (score and Sort merges with a custom tie breaker)
bugs.title: TopDocs.merge with a custom tie breaker fails an assertion (only with -ea) when the tie breaker returns 0 for tied hits from two different shards at the same rank
bugs.summary: You merge per-shard results with TopDocs.merge(start, topN, shardHits, tieBreaker), or the Sort overload, and pass a valid Comparator<ScoreDoc> tie breaker that ignores the shard, for example one that compares doc ids only; two shards each have a hit with the same score (or sort value) at the same rank and the same local doc id. You expect both hits back, since the method accepts any custom tie breaker and its helper documents that a 0 from the tie breaker falls back to hit indices. Instead, with assertions enabled, the merge throws AssertionError at TopDocs.java:88 ('assert first.hitIndex != second.hitIndex'), because that check assumes a tie can only come from the same shard while the merge queue only ever compares hits of different shards; with -da both hits are returned.

bugs.area: util / PriorityQueue (sift-down; base class of HitQueue and FieldValueHitQueue)
bugs.title: PriorityQueue.downHeap computes the child index i << 1 in int, so a queue holding 2^30 or more elements throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from updateTop, pop or insertWithOverflow and is left with one element lost and another duplicated
bugs.summary: You fill a Lucene PriorityQueue with 2^30 + 1 elements, a size its constructor accepts (any maxSize below ArrayUtil.MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH), and call updateTop, pop or insertWithOverflow; you expect the usual log(size) sift-down and the new least element back. Instead, when the sift-down reaches node 2^30, the child index i << 1 wraps to Integer.MIN_VALUE, the negative index -2147483647 passes the 'k <= size' check, and the call throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException after children were already moved up, so the queue has lost the element being sifted and holds a second copy of another. A queue of 2^30 - 1 elements works; exactly 2^30 already fails for updateTop.
bugs.introduced_commit: bd3948c539ec1065db8b05b433ea55dbf844ff27 'Initial revision' (2001-09-18, svn r149570, the repository's first commit: the import of the existing code base, with no issue or pull request) [exec]; reachable within the documented capacity since 2e082f2f008 (2003-09-11, svn r150020, 'Added insert(Object) method to PriorityQueue class', which changed the heap size from 2 * maxSize + 1 to maxSize + 1 and documented maxSize as the capacity; CHANGES 1.3 RC2 item 5) [read]. Not a regression: later changes to downHeap (generics LUCENE-1935 698b73e2ae1, start index LUCENE-6066 ef3a99b385f, LessThan interface #14873 39549329509, visibility #15493 dea98efd5e2, whitespace) left the index arithmetic alone, and each new sift-down entry point (insertWithOverflow 2.3.0, updateTop 2.9.0, addAll's heapify 9.2.0 #770) inherited it
bugs.introduced_date: 2001-09-18 (bd3948c539e; the code may be older, its pre-import history is not in the repository); reachable within the documented capacity since 2003-09-11 (2e082f2f008)

bugs.area: util / FixedBitSet (approximateCardinality)
bugs.title: (Latent) FixedBitSet.approximateCardinality returns a negative value for bit sets of 2^31-63 bits or more, because its scale factor 64 * numWords overflows int
bugs.summary: You create a FixedBitSet of 2^31-63 to 2^31-1 bits (for example new FixedBitSet(Integer.MAX_VALUE), a legal length: the class javadoc points to LongBitSet only for more than 2.1B bits), set some bits and call approximateCardinality; you expect a non-negative estimate of the number of set bits, as BitSet documents ('an approximation of the cardinality of this set'). Instead it returns a negative number (-2147418112 with all 2^31-1 bits set, -64 with a single set bit), because the scale factor (interval / rangeLength) * numWords / maxWord is computed in int and its product 64 * numWords wraps to Integer.MIN_VALUE once the set has 2^25 words; new BitDocIdSet(bits) then throws IllegalArgumentException 'cost must be >= 0'. No Lucene code path builds a bit set that long (doc-ID sets stop at IndexWriter.MAX_DOCS = 2^31-129 bits), so only external code that uses FixedBitSet directly over another int domain is affected.
bugs.introduced_commit: ca73ed1c2842 (LUCENE-10311, apache/lucene#710 'Make FixedBitSet#approximateCardinality faster (and actually approximate).', author jpountz, merged on main 2022-03-03; branch_9x backport bb10e62dff88, same date) replaced the inherited exact BitSet default with the sampled estimate and wrote the overflowing line [read]; later commits in the same series did not touch the overflow: ae16917c1de (#724, rewrote the sampling loop with Long.bitCount) and e999056c19d (dweiss, 2022-03-09, 'avoid division by zero on small sets', changed numWords < interval to <= in the same method)

bugs.area: util / RamUsageEstimator
bugs.title: RamUsageEstimator.sizeOfCollection adds the assumed backing-array bytes in int arithmetic, so a collection of 536,870,908 or more elements (268,435,453 with 8-byte references) gets a size estimate that is a multiple of 4 GiB too low, and negative when the elements add little
bugs.summary: You ask RamUsageEstimator.sizeOfCollection (or sizeOfObject) for the size of a very large list, for example Arrays.asList(new Object[536870908]). You expect a size in bytes that is at least the 2,147,483,648 bytes of its backing array, which shallowSizeOf(Object) reports correctly. Instead the method adds the array header and the per-element references in int arithmetic, which wraps, so it returns -2,147,483,616; in general the estimate is too low by a multiple of 2^32 bytes from 536,870,908 elements on (268,435,453 with 8-byte references), and it is negative only when the elements' own sizes add little.

bugs.title: (Latent) MonotonicBlockPackedWriter writes a block whose values end close to Long.MAX_VALUE with too few bits, so MonotonicBlockPackedReader returns wrong values: min + (long) (avg * i) overflows in flush
bugs.summary: You write a block of non-negative, increasing longs with MonotonicBlockPackedWriter, for example {1, Long.MAX_VALUE}, and read it back with MonotonicBlockPackedReader. You expect the same values back: the writer is documented as 'A writer for large monotonically increasing sequences of positive longs' with no upper bound, and flush says 'adjust min so that all deltas will be positive'. bugs.area: index / sorted-set doc values terms enum (SortedSetDocValuesTermsEnum, the default SortedSetDocValues#termsEnum)
bugs.title: The default SortedSetDocValues terms enum casts the ordinal to int in seekExact(long) and seekExact(term, TermState): on a view with more than 2^31 values a seek by ordinal throws, and from 2^32 values on it can silently land on the wrong term
bugs.summary: You take the terms enum of a sorted-set doc-values view with more than 2^31 distinct values (for example MultiDocValues.getSortedSetValues over a very large multi-segment index), position it on a term with seekCeil, keep ord or termState, and later return with seekExact(ord) or seekExact(term, state); you expect to land on that term again, because sorted-set ordinals are longs and termsEnum is documented to support ord and seekExact(long). Instead seekExact(long) stores '(int) ord' (SortedSetDocValuesTermsEnum.java:69), so for ordinals from 2^31 to 2^32-1 it asks the values for a negative ordinal and throws, and for 2^32+5 it silently positions on ordinal 5 and returns that term, with -ea and -da. seekCeil, seekExact(BytesRef), next and ord use long arithmetic and are correct; the fix is to drop the cast.

It created SortedSetDocValuesTermsEnum as a copy of SortedDocValuesTermsEnum and widened currentOrd from int to long, but kept 'currentOrd = (int) ord;' in seekExact(long). Reached trunk through the merge b44aa618348 (r1447999) and branch_4x through bb1f4d0c61b (r1448085), both 2013-02-20; the line never changed afterwards [read]

bugs.area: codecs / BufferingKnnVectorsWriter flush-time vector values (KnnVectorValues.ordToDoc and getAcceptOrds)
bugs.title: BufferingKnnVectorsWriter hands writeField vector values whose ordToDoc(ord) returns ord, which is wrong for sparse fields and, with an index sort, for every field (latent: no shipped writer calls it)
bugs.summary: You build a vector codec on BufferingKnnVectorsWriter and, in writeField, ask the flush-time vector values which document a vector ordinal belongs to (ordToDoc, or getAcceptOrds, which is built on it), expecting what the javadoc promises, 'the docid of the document indexed with the given vector ordinal'. Instead the buffered values answer ordToDoc(ord) = ord, which is right only when every document has a vector and there is no index sort: for a field that documents 0, 2 and 3 have, ordinals 1 and 2 map to documents 1 and 2 instead of 2 and 3, so a getAcceptOrds filter that accepts only document 2 accepts document 3's vector and one that accepts only document 3 accepts none; under a reversing index sort even a dense field's ordinals map to themselves instead of to their documents' sorted positions. Iteration (nextDoc, index, vectorValue) stays correct, nothing throws, and FLOAT32, BYTE and FLOAT16 behave the same.

bugs.area: util / HNSW graph node iterators (HnswGraph.NodesIterator, DenseNodesIterator)
bugs.title: HnswGraph.DenseNodesIterator.consume (the level-0 node iterator of every HNSW graph) does not advance its cursor, so draining level 0 in chunks with consume returns the first chunk forever and a nextInt after consume starts again at node 0 (latent: Lucene itself never calls consume on level 0)
bugs.summary: You take the level-0 node iterator of an HNSW graph (getNodesOnLevel(0), a DenseNodesIterator over the node ids [0, size)) and read it in chunks with consume(buf), expecting each call to hand out the next block of ids, as the javadoc ('Consume integers from the iterator') and the two sibling iterator classes do. Instead DenseNodesIterator.consume copies the block but never moves its cursor, so every call returns the same first block, hasNext stays true and the loop never ends; a nextInt after consume also starts again at 0. Lucene's own code never calls consume on level 0, so indexes and search results are not affected.

bugs.area: index / doc values and norms flush with index sorting (NumericDocValuesWriter.SortingNumericDocValues)
bugs.title: With an index sort, the flush-time iterator that IndexWriter hands to a doc-values or norms consumer for a numeric field that every document has ends intoBitSet(upTo >= maxDoc) on docID == maxDoc instead of NO_MORE_DOCS, so a custom consumer that bulk-loads it and loops until NO_MORE_DOCS never finishes (latent: Lucene's own consumers skip the bulk load for such fields)
bugs.summary: You sort an index at flush and every document in the segment has a given numeric doc-values field (or norms, or a single-valued SortedNumericDocValuesField); a custom DocValuesFormat or NormsFormat consumer bulk-loads the iterator it gets at flush with intoBitSet(maxDoc) or intoBitSet(NO_MORE_DOCS) and expects it to end on NO_MORE_DOCS, as the reference loop in the intoBitSet javadoc does. Instead NumericDocValuesWriter.SortingNumericDocValues sets the right bits but leaves docID at maxDoc, a position the docID contract never allows, so a consumer that loops until NO_MORE_DOCS never ends; fed to IndexedDISI.writeBitSet it fails the flush with an AssertionError (-ea) or keeps writing empty-block headers until the output fails (-da). Lucene's own consumers never bulk-load a field that every document has, so stock indexes and search results are not affected.

bugs.area: index / doc values flush (DocValuesWriter Buffered*DocValues iterators handed to DocValuesConsumer)
bugs.title: The flush-time doc-values iterators that IndexWriter hands to a DocValuesConsumer move only their doc-ID cursor in intoBitSet, so values read afterwards belong to earlier documents (NUMERIC, BINARY, SORTED, SORTED_NUMERIC, SORTED_SET; latent: Lucene's own consumers never read values after intoBitSet on the same iterator)
bugs.summary: A custom doc-values codec receives, at flush, the iterator over a field's buffered values; it calls nextDoc, bulk-loads the next documents into a bit set with intoBitSet, and then reads the value of the current document, expecting what the documented nextDoc loop gives. Instead the five flush-time iterators (one per doc-values type) move only their doc-ID cursor in intoBitSet, so the value read belongs to an earlier document, and every later value of the field in that segment stays shifted by the same number of documents (doc 2 reports doc 0's value, doc 3 reports doc 1's). Lucene's own doc-values consumer never reads values after intoBitSet on the same iterator, so indexes written by stock Lucene are correct.

bugs.area: codecs / SimpleText points format (SimpleTextBKDReader.SimpleTextPointTree#clone)
bugs.title: SimpleText points: PointTree.clone shares a saved split-value array with the tree it was cloned from, so moving one tree corrupts the node bounds the other reports
bugs.summary: You index points with the SimpleText codec, take a PointTree from PointValues.getPointTree, clone it and keep moving both the clone and the original, and expect each tree to report the bounds of its own current node, as PointTree#clone promises ('the current node becomes the root of the new tree') and as the default points format does. Instead SimpleTextPointTree.clone copies the reference to the original's saved split-value array for the current level, so a move of one tree overwrites the bound that the other tree restores when it moves back up: after tree.moveToChild, tree.moveToParent, clone = tree.clone, clone.moveToChild, tree.moveToChild, tree.moveToSibling, clone.moveToParent, the clone at its root reports max 0 instead of 2047 for the values 0..2047. Any traversal that prunes on those bounds can then miss or wrongly include cells; no in-tree query moves trees this way.

bugs.area: analysis-common / synonym.word2vec (Word2VecSynonymFilter minAcceptedSimilarity javadoc vs Word2VecSynonymProvider threshold test)
bugs.title: Word2VecSynonymFilter documents minAcceptedSimilarity as a cosine similarity, but Word2VecSynonymProvider compares it with the normalised score (1 + cosine) / 2, so the effective cosine cutoff is 2m - 1 (the default 0.8 accepts cosine 0.6, 0.5 accepts orthogonal terms, values below 0.5 accept negatively correlated terms); documentation defect, the javadoc fix is the default proposal
bugs.summary: You build Word2VecSynonymFilter with minAcceptedSimilarity 0.8 (the factory default), whose only documentation says it is the 'minimal value of cosine similarity between the searched vector and the retrieved ones', so you expect only model terms at cosine 0.8 or more as synonyms. Word2VecSynonymProvider compares the threshold with the DOT_PRODUCT score of the unit-length model vectors, which is (1 + cosine) / 2, so the real cosine cutoff is 2m - 1: at 0.8 a term at cosine 0.65 is emitted, at 0.5 an orthogonal term (cosine 0) is emitted, and at 0.2 a term at cosine -0.5 is emitted. The authors' intent points to the score scale (the factory accepts only (0, 1]), so the fix is a javadoc clarification, not a code change.

bugs.area: monitor / batch matching: Monitor.match(Document) and DocumentBatch (documentation)
bugs.title: Monitor.match(Document) does not document that a batch is matched as one index, so queries whose rewrite or statistics depend on the index (top-N multi-term rewrites incl. the default FuzzyQuery, CommonTermsQuery, MoreLikeThisQuery) can match a document differently in a batch than alone
bugs.summary: You register queries with a Monitor and match documents in batches with Monitor.match(Document), which the package javadoc offers as an alternative to matching them one at a time with Monitor.match(Document) and whose only documented batch caveat is that filter-field values must agree. Each registered query is in fact rewritten and run once over one small index that holds the whole batch, so a query whose rewrite or statistics depend on the index can give a document a different answer than it gets alone: a default FuzzyQuery('abcdef') matches 'abcdxy' alone but not in a batch with 50 documents that each hold a closer term, and a CommonTermsQuery that matches 'ab' alone matches neither copy in a batch of two copies of 'ab'. This is the designed behaviour (a plain IndexSearcher over an index of the same documents returns the same result), but neither Monitor.match(Document) nor the package documentation says that a batch is matched as one index, so users cannot tell that a document's matches can depend on its batch.
bugs.introduced_commit: 251dbe7cea81 on master ('LUCENE-8766: Add monitor subproject', romseygeek; LUCENE-8766 = apache/lucene#9811, review in apache/lucene-solr#648, committed directly) and its branch_8x copy b8773d13ad8e. That commit added Monitor.match(Document) building one DocumentBatch.MultiDocumentBatch (IndexWriter.addDocuments, commit, forceMerge(1), one leaf) with one IndexSearcher for all candidate queries, and the package-info text that offers single and batch matching side by side with only the filter-field batch caveat [read]. The batch-as-one-index design is older than Lucene (the predecessor project's 2015 batching API, whose public DocumentBatch javadoc said a multi-document batch is held in an in-memory directory; in Lucene the class became package-private without that javadoc) [read]. The documentation gap is as old as the API; not a regression.

bugs.area: queries / intervals (Intervals.within / Intervals.notWithin and their javadoc; queryparser fn:within / fn:notWithin docs)
bugs.title: Intervals.within and notWithin are documented as opposites, but a multi-position source interval only partly inside the n-position window around the reference matches neither (documentation / API-contract defect)
bugs.summary: You index 'the new york times' and run within(phrase(new, york), 1, times) and notWithin(phrase(new, york), 1, times), and you expect exactly one of them to match, because the javadoc says within returns source intervals that 'appear within a set number of positions' of the reference and notWithin those that 'do not appear within' it, and the fn:within / fn:notWithin docs give both the same 'maximum positions' parameter. Instead neither matches: within keeps an interval only if all of it lies inside the window [r.start-n, r.end+n] (here [2,4]), while notWithin drops it if any part touches that window, so 'new york' at [1,2], which touches the window without lying inside it, is in neither result (within needs n = 2 for a phrase directly next to the reference). In the same way, on 'new york' both within(phrase(new, york), 0, york) and notWithin(phrase(new, york), 0, york) return nothing, and no doc says that a partly-near interval matches neither.

bugs.area: core / search similarities (MultiSimilarity: undocumented norm ownership, inherited getDiscountOverlaps)
bugs.title: MultiSimilarity does not document that only sims[0] computes the field norm, so the other sub-similarities' index-time norm settings (discountOverlaps, a computeNorm override) are silently ignored and the array order decides the stored norm, and its inherited getDiscountOverlaps always returns true (documentation defect; on one index the score is an exact sum in either order)
bugs.summary: You combine two sub-similarities in a MultiSimilarity, for example BM25 with discountOverlaps=true and BM25 with discountOverlaps=false, and use it for indexing and searching; the javadoc says only that it 'will sum the scores of the provided sims' (CombSUM), so you expect both sub-similarities' settings to count. In fact computeNorm returns sims[0].computeNorm(state), so only the first sub-similarity writes the field's single norm and every sub-scorer decodes that norm: the second one's discountOverlaps (or its own computeNorm encoding) is silently ignored, swapping the array order changes the stored norms and therefore the scores (0.7534208 for [discount, noDiscount] vs 0.6862843 for [noDiscount, discount] in an independent repro), and the inherited getDiscountOverlaps returns true even when sims[0] counts overlap tokens. The single norm is the intended one-norm-per-field design and on any one index the score is an exact sum in either order; what is missing is the documentation (and a correct getter), so the fix is a javadoc sentence, optionally plus passing sims[0].getDiscountOverlaps to the super constructor.

Later commits on the line only changed the signature (98e59fceeec LUCENE-3687; 8ef98119381); it has always delegated to sims[0], and no javadoc ever mentioned the norm. Part 2 (getDiscountOverlaps always true): 7c056ab88c7589a0d103fd4c372ac7677515691d on main and 1b38d5dec85d on branch_9x, apache/lucene#13757 (cpoerschke, co-author rmuir), which added the final getter and Similarity -> this(true) while MultiSimilarity's 2011 constructor calls the implicit super [read]. bugs.area: analysis-common / ConcatenateGraphFilter and ConcatenateGraphFilterFactory (maxGraphExpansions javadoc); also suggest / CompletionAnalyzer
bugs.title: ConcatenateGraphFilter, its factory and CompletionAnalyzer misdocument maxGraphExpansions: the javadoc promises a TooComplexToDeterminizeException when the token graph has more than maxGraphExpansions paths (and 'no limit on graph expansions' for CompletionAnalyzer's 1- and 3-argument constructors), but the code silently keeps the first maxGraphExpansions paths (default 10000) and also uses the same value as the determinize work limit, so it can throw for a graph with fewer paths than the limit (documentation defect; the truncation is intended)
bugs.summary: You set maxGraphExpansions on ConcatenateGraphFilter (or its factory), or use CompletionAnalyzer's 1- or 3-argument constructor, and expect what the javadoc says: a TooComplexToDeterminizeException when the token graph has more than that many paths, and, for CompletionAnalyzer, no limit at all. Instead the filter silently emits only the first maxGraphExpansions paths (a 4-path synonym graph at limit 3 gives 3 tokens and no error; CompletionAnalyzer keeps 10000 of 16384 paths), and because the same number is also passed to determinize as its work limit, a 2-path graph at limit 3 throws. Silent truncation is the suggester's deliberate design (LUCENE-4971), so the fix is to correct the javadoc, not the code.

In XML the backslashes stay literal, and since 9.0.0 RegExp deliberately rejects a backslash before a letter other than s, S, w, W, d, D (LUCENE-9370, MIGRATE.md), so building the factory throws IllegalArgumentException 'invalid character class \116'; on 6.5 to 8.x the same pattern was accepted but split on the letters t, r and n instead. bugs.area: suggest / spell (JaroWinklerDistance threshold)
bugs.title: JaroWinklerDistance.setThreshold javadoc says 'Set to a negative value to get the Jaro distance', but a negative threshold adds the Winkler bonus to every pair (the same as threshold 0); only a threshold of 1 or more gives plain Jaro; documentation defect, the javadoc fix is the default proposal
bugs.summary: You want the plain Jaro similarity from JaroWinklerDistance, so, as the setThreshold javadoc says ('Set to a negative value to get the Jaro distance'), you call setThreshold(-1) and expect getDistance("martha", "marhta") to return the Jaro value 0.9444. Instead it returns 0.9611, the Jaro-Winkler value: getDistance skips the Winkler bonus only when the Jaro value is below the threshold, which never happens for a negative threshold, so every pair gets the bonus, exactly as with threshold 0. bugs.area: codecs / term vectors (Lucene90TermVectorsFormat.tvd file-format javadoc vs Lucene90CompressingTermVectorsWriter / Reader)
bugs.title: The file-format javadoc of the default term-vectors format (Lucene90TermVectorsFormat) contradicts the.tvd bytes in three places: the Flags bit meaning is inverted, FieldNums are called delta-encoded but are the plain field numbers, and AvgCharsPerTerm is called absent without positions but is written whenever a field has offsets (documentation defect; the writer and reader agree)
bugs.summary: You decode a.tvd chunk of the default term-vectors format by following its javadoc, which says the Flags Bit is 1 when all fields of the chunk have the same options, that FieldNums is a delta-encoded list, and that AvgCharsPerTerm is absent unless some field has both positions and offsets. The writer does the opposite on all three: it writes 0 for 'same options' (then one flag per distinct field) and 1 otherwise, it stores the plain sorted field numbers (fields 1, 3, 6 are stored as 1, 3, 6, which summed as deltas give 1, 4, 10), and it writes one AvgCharsPerTerm value per distinct field whenever any field has offsets, so a parser built from the text misreads the chunk. Lucene's own reader matches the writer, so nothing breaks at runtime; only the documentation is wrong, and it has been since it was written in 2013.

bugs.area: queries / spans: SpanMultiTermQueryWrapper equality (span rewrite methods); consequence in index / IndexWriter delete-by-query buffering
bugs.title: SpanMultiTermQueryWrapper.equals/hashCode ignore the span rewrite method (since 5.5.0), so wrappers that match different documents compare equal and IndexWriter's delete-by-query buffer keeps only one of two such deletes
bugs.summary: You build new SpanMultiTermQueryWrapper(new PrefixQuery(f:aa)) twice and call setRewriteMethod(new TopTermsSpanBooleanQueryRewrite(1)) on one of them, so on a 6-document index one wrapper matches all 6 documents and the other matches 1, and you expect the two to be unequal, as two PrefixQuery objects that differ only in their rewrite method are. Instead equals and hashCode compare only the wrapped PrefixQuery, so the wrappers are equal with equal hash codes. IndexWriter buffers delete-by-query calls in a HashMap keyed by the query, so deleteDocuments(top1) followed by deleteDocuments(all) in one flush window keeps only the first and commits with 5 of the 6 matching documents still live, and in the other order a document added between the two calls is deleted although no delete issued after it matches it.

bugs.area: util / automaton (RegExp, Operations.concatenate; reached from RegexpQuery and the classic and flexible query parsers)
bugs.title: RegExp builds about n^2/2 transitions for a run of n repeated nullable atoms (a.*.*...b, a(x?)^n b, [a-z]*, (bc)?), and on main RegexpQuery keeps that automaton: a 2,002-character regexp of language a.*b holds 502,502 transitions and 170 MB (10.5.2: 4 states, 7 KB)
bugs.summary: You build a RegexpQuery, directly or by typing /regexp/ syntax into the classic or flexible query parser, for a regexp with a long run of the same nullable atom, for example 'a' followed by 1,000 copies of '.*' and then 'b', and expect an automaton about as small as its language a.*b (4 states, which is what 10.5.2 keeps and what WildcardQuery builds for a run of '*' since #16382). Instead Operations.concatenate gives every accept state a link to each following piece for as long as those pieces accept the empty string, so the run gets about n^2/2 transitions (502,502 here), and on main, where RegexpQuery no longer determinizes (#15939), the query keeps that automaton: ramBytesUsed 170 MB, about 3 s to build, and OutOfMemoryError under a 1 GB heap from about 4,000 characters. The same happens for x?, x*, [a-z]*, (ab)*, (bc)? and [^x]*; search results are always correct, and released versions pay the quadratic cost only while building (OutOfMemoryError at about 12,000 characters under 1 GB, or a TooComplexToDeterminizeException for 447 'x?' in a row).

bugs.area: core / search (MultiPhraseQuery.Builder input validation and MultiPhraseQuery.toString)
bugs.title: MultiPhraseQuery.Builder does not validate an empty Term: it throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at the first position but accepts one at later positions, and toString of the accepted query then throws, which also breaks explain and the 'indexed without position data' error
bugs.summary: You build a phrase with MultiPhraseQuery.Builder and pass an empty Term for one position, for example the terms of a prefix expansion that found nothing (the class javadoc's 'microsoft app*' recipe); add(Term) documents the array as a disjunction, so you expect an empty position to match nothing, or the Builder to reject it with IllegalArgumentException. At the first position Builder.add throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (it reads terms[0].field, MultiPhraseQuery.java:127), while at any later position the array is accepted and search correctly returns 0 hits, but toString throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (terms[0].text,:345). So logging the query fails, IndexSearcher.explain throws for a BooleanQuery or IndriAndQuery that holds it (BooleanWeight.java:99 and:103, IndriAndWeight.java:88), and on a field indexed without positions the documented IllegalStateException becomes that exception, because its message prints the query (:255-262).

Inherited from PhrasePrefixQuery (15bbd8def83, 2002-07-18, first released in 1.3, same defect [exec]). The Builder API named in the title arrived with LUCENE-7064 (#8120, 40aab73a4c9, 2016-03-03, 6.0.0), which moved the unchanged add body into Builder.add. Not a regression.

bugs.area: queryparser / flexible core: QueryNodeProcessorPipeline (java.util.List views and default methods)
bugs.title: QueryNodeProcessorPipeline's listIterator/subList views, and replaceAll / Collections.replaceAll built on them, put processors on the pipeline without its QueryConfigHandler, so the flexible query parser silently skips point, boost and default phrase slop handling or throws NullPointerException
bugs.summary: You customise a flexible query parser pipeline, for example StandardQueryParser's, by inserting or replacing a processor through the pipeline's java.util.List API: pipeline.listIterator then add or set, subList(..).set, pipeline.replaceAll or Collections.replaceAll. You expect the processor to receive the pipeline's QueryConfigHandler, as it does with add(k, p) or set(k, p), because the class says it 'takes care of setting this QueryConfigHandler on all processor on pipeline'. Instead those paths write through the private ArrayList's own views and leave the processor with a null handler, so a replaced PointQueryNodeProcessor turns n:5 into a TermQuery that finds 0 of 1 matching documents, a replaced BoostQueryNodeProcessor drops field boosts, and most other stock processors throw NullPointerException at parse.
bugs.introduced_commit: 6f66858572c0aa9528e5b1e6999c945db5712fce (trunk r1024402, 'LUCENE-1937: add methods to manipulate QueryNodeProcessorPipeline elements', patch by Adriano Crestani, committed by Robert Muir; JIRA patch workflow, no GitHub PR; migrated as apache/lucene#3012); branch_3x backport 2ab3fc4ba40bcdd239d49bbac1b4d2539198170c (r1024405), the commit released in 3.1.0. bugs.area: suggest / document (NRT) suggester: CompletionWeight#scorerSupplier vs the Weight/ScorerSupplier contract and IndexSearcher#searchLeaf
bugs.title: CompletionWeight returns a non-null ScorerSupplier whose bulkScorer is null, so IndexSearcher#search of a CompletionQuery throws NullPointerException on a segment the query cannot match (regression in 10.0 from #13408)
bugs.summary: You index suggestions with SuggestField and run a PrefixCompletionQuery through IndexSearcher#search with a CollectorManager of TopSuggestDocsCollector, on an index where one segment has no document with the suggest field (or where the query's filter matches no document of a segment). You expect the same suggestions as SuggestIndexSearcher#suggest (3 in the repro), because Weight#scorerSupplier 'must return null if the scorer is null' and IndexSearcher then skips that segment, as 9.12.3 does. Instead CompletionWeight returns a non-null ScorerSupplier whose bulkScorer returns null, and IndexSearcher#searchLeaf throws NullPointerException ('Cannot invoke BulkScorer.score(...) because "scorer" is null'; with a timeout set, Objects.requireNonNull in TimeLimitingBulkScorer throws it first).
bugs.introduced_commit: ddf538d43e94a814f783fcc40728ee45038a03a1 (apache/lucene#13408 'Move bulkScorer from Weight to ScorerSupplier', by jpountz, approved by mikemccand; main only, milestone 10.0.0): it made Weight#bulkScorer a final helper, moved CompletionWeight's three 'return null' paths (no terms, no FST, MatchNoBits filter) from its overridden Weight#bulkScorer, which IndexSearcher null-checked, into ScorerSupplier#bulkScorer, and changed IndexSearcher to null-check only the supplier. Precondition: 838b23ebed1a (apache/lucene#13319 'Make Weight#scorerSupplier abstract, Weight#scorer final', by iamsanjay, merged by jpountz, 2024-05-14) added the 'It must return null if the scorer is null' rule and gave CompletionWeight its always-non-null supplier, harmless until #13408. bugs.area: queryparser / flexible core (QueryParserHelper; inherited by StandardQueryParser and PrecedenceQueryParser)
bugs.title: Flexible query parser: QueryParserHelper.setQueryNodeProcessor(null) throws NullPointerException, although its javadoc says null is allowed and means no query-node processing (StandardQueryParser and PrecedenceQueryParser inherit the setter; every release since 2.9.0)
bugs.summary: You call setQueryNodeProcessor(null) on a StandardQueryParser, a PrecedenceQueryParser or any QueryParserHelper to switch off the optional query-processing phase, as the method's javadoc allows ('The argument can be null, which means that no processor will be used to process the query node tree'). You expect the parser to go on parsing without processing, as it does when the null processor is passed to the QueryParserHelper constructor. Instead the setter always throws NullPointerException, because it stores the argument and then calls setQueryConfigHandler on it without the null check that the constructor, setQueryConfigHandler and parse all have.

bugs.area: suggest / document (NRT) suggester: CompletionScorer under IndexSearcher's windowed execution (setTimeout, intra-segment partitions)
bugs.title: CompletionScorer silently ignores the BulkScorer [min, max) window instead of rejecting it, so a CompletionQuery run through IndexSearcher#search with a timeout (even one that never fires) or with intra-segment partitions returns repeated suggestions and drops others
bugs.summary: You run a CompletionQuery through IndexSearcher#search with a TopSuggestDocsCollector (for example suggestSearcher.search(query, collector)) on a searcher that has a timeout set, even one that never fires, or that splits a segment into intra-segment partitions. You expect the same top suggestions as SuggestIndexSearcher#suggest, or a loud error if this path is unsupported, because BulkScorer#score must score only the documents in [min, max) and a timeout that never fires must not change results. Instead CompletionScorer runs its whole-segment top-N lookup again on every window or partition, so the top suggestions come back several times and lower ones are dropped (500 suggestions, n=5: [499, 499, 498, 498, 497] instead of [499, 498, 497, 496, 495]; one suggestion returned 5 times; partitions: [499 x5]), while the total says EQUAL_TO and timedOut is false.
bugs.introduced_commit: be4d58c7740bea4e797eb1acff6355eb260e7c93 (trunk, 'LUCENE-6459: add common suggest API for document based NRT suggester', patch by Areek Zillur, committed by mikemccand; JIRA LUCENE-6459, migrated as apache/lucene#7518; no PR, SVN era), released through the branch_5x backport 380bb29f39595de1c3947075296d1d0a36f02fd8 [read].
